| state | `te_seabed_holder` | its owner when last recorded (the Strategic Reserve's `st_res_hub_holder` pattern) |
| country | `te_seabed_unbuilt_<basin>` | entitled and unused |
| country | `te_seabed_held_<basin>`, `te_seabed_ent_<basin>`, `te_seabed_w_<basin>` | records in its states, entitlement, claim weight, at the last sharing |
| country | `te_seabed_wait_<basin>` | without the technology: its share above its holdings, waiting for it (no claim; absent for a claimant); `te_seabed_wpart` flags, during the pass, a coastal country that only waits (`te_seabed_waits`) |
| country | `te_seabed_policy`, `te_seabed_policy_prev` | 1 Scientific Survey, 2 Sponsor Contractors, 3 Unilateral Licensing; absent = 1, never seeded, so a winner inherits the nation's choice |
| global | `te_seabed_regime` | 1 Open, 2 Regulated, 3 Scramble; absent = Open. The UN hook writes it |
| state | `te_seabed_unb_snap1`, `te_seabed_unb_snap2` | licences on its unbuilt levels at the last two first-sharings of a year (the holding fee's grace) |
| country | `te_seabed_floor_<basin>`, `te_seabed_fz_<basin>` | Sponsor's floor (set at the year's first sharing), and what the sharing froze it at (max(held, floor), scaled to fit) |
| country | `te_seabed_relinq_<basin>` | flag: relinquished, weight 0 there until Claim Again |
| country | `te_seabed_sh_<basin>`, `te_seabed_shleft_<basin>` | held as the sharing counts it (a lease's licences go to its lessor, a pact's to the subject), and what the leases left to shift |
| country (lessee) | `te_seabed_lease_src_<basin>`, `te_seabed_lease_n_<basin>`, `_built_<basin>`, `_unused_<basin>` | its lease there: the lessor, the total, licences built on it, unused leased claims (part of unbuilt) |
| country | `te_seabed_subj_unused_<basin>`; on a subject `te_seabed_pass_unused_<basin>`, `te_seabed_pass_built_<basin>` | claims its subjects passed it, unused (part of unbuilt); a subject's own share of those, and the licences its overlord built on them |
| country | `te_seabed_policy_changed`, `te_seabed_policy_cost_cached`, `te_seabed_fee_cached` | the month of the last policy change (the lock; absent = free), and the two modifiers' multipliers |
| country | `te_seabed_queued_<basin>`, `te_seabed_lic_now_<basin>` | licences on its queued levels (distant ones first) and all its licences, by basin, monthly |
| country | `te_seabed_need_navy_<basin>`, `te_seabed_coast_<basin>`, `te_seabed_ports_<basin>`, `te_seabed_coast_all`, `te_seabed_dr_<basin>` | the "+1 licence" readout (-1 full, -2 no weight) and its inputs (coast counted with unincorporated states at half), yearly; `te_seabed_coast_states_<basin>` every coastal state there, which the Free hover lists |
| player | list `te_seabed_rk_list_<basin>` | on each player, the basin's other claimants' capitals, largest share first, rebuilt at every sharing (`te_seabed_rank_list`; audit SEA-3, 2026-10-27). It replaced the six global seats `te_seabed_rk_<basin>_<n>`, `te_seabed_rk_more_<basin>` and the players' `te_seabed_rkcap_*`, which the sharing removes from an older save |
| global | `te_seabed_last_sharing_month` | the panel's "as of" |
| global | `te_seabed_world_wait_<basin>` | the shares waiting for countries without the technology (the pool hover; their weight is in `te_seabed_world_w_<basin>`) |

**Room**, read live (`te_seabed_room`): the unbuilt shares, summed, less the levels not yet recorded. One national number; the gate reads no basin.

**A level is recorded as soon as it is queued** (its building's `level_after_queued_constructions`), not when finished. The spec's room already counts queued levels, so this is the same accounting one step earlier, and it closes the leak a sharing that shrinks an entitlement would otherwise open under levels being built. A cancelled construction gives its licence back at the next recording.

**Recording, monthly** (`te_seabed_record_country`, monthly country pulse; also for every participant at the start of the yearly pass): first every coastal state gives back licences above its levels to its owner's shares, distant basins first; then each level without a record takes one from the owner's unbuilt share, the state's own basin first, else the basin with the most; a distant licence swaps for a local one whenever the owner has local share to spare; every coastal state is restamped. A level its own stamped owner can't pay for **waits unrecorded** (pending): it is a level the owner queued past its room through the gate's second branch (below), its room stays below 0, and it takes a licence when a share pays for one. Only § 2.4's three cases are recorded in their own basin **against no share** (counted in `te_seabed_noshare_<basin>`): a state with no stamp (an old save's first recording, a split's new state, the rule switched back on, which clears the stamps so its levels are grandfathered as § 2.9 says), and a holder gone when its state changes hands.

**On a change of owner** (`te_seabed_on_state_owner_change`): unrecorded levels are recorded against the stamped holder (against no share if there is no stamp or the holder holds no state any more; waiting for the new owner's share if the holder exists but can't pay), the records stay on the state for the new owner, and the stamp names the new owner. Unverified: that a state keeps its variables across the change (self-check `seabed_licence_follows_state`).

**The yearly sharing** (`te_seabed_yearly_pass`) runs from the global `on_monthly_pulse` once a year (the first monthly pulse of a new year) and in the month after a new claimant appears (`te_seabed_reshare`), so a country that has just researched Abyssal Plain Mining need not wait for January. Global scope computes every weight before any pool is shared, whatever order the country pulses run in. Order: the year's first sharing is noted (`te_seabed_first_sharing_of_year`, cached as `te_seabed_first_of_year`); state basins (every coastal country's); the regime hook; every participant (claimants, and holders without the technology) records, and the coastal countries with no other part are flagged `te_seabed_wpart` (they only wait); on the year's first sharing the holding fee's snapshots (`te_seabed_take_snapshots`); held, then the leases' and pacts' shift (`te_seabed_lease_shift_held`), and on the year's first sharing Sponsor's floors (`te_seabed_set_floors`); weights; each pool, its floors fitted first (`te_seabed_fit_floors`); stale shares off for countries that no longer take part; the leases settled (`te_seabed_settle_leases`) and subjects' claims passed (`te_seabed_pass_subject_claims`); a non-claimant's policy back to Survey (its lock cleared); Unilateral relations (only on the year's first sharing, `te_seabed_relations_year`); world totals; the rivals' ranks (`te_seabed_rank_basin`); the floor self-check. A civil war's end (`on_civil_war_won`) also asks for a sharing: a winning revolution keeps its own variables, so its shares were the rebel claimant's.

- **Weight** (`te_seabed_compute_weights`, § 2.3; seabed claims spec § 5.1): home basin (coastal states there, an unincorporated one counting `te_seabed_uninc_coast` = 0.5 in both counts) `(2 × states + port levels + navy × states ÷ all coastal states) × policy factor`; elsewhere `0.05 × navy × policy factor`. Policy factor ×0.75 / ×1 / ×1 (Survey's was ×0.25 until 2026-10-27), and `te_seabed_latent_factor` (0.75) in its place without the technology (`te_seabed_claim_factor`), for a holder and a country that only waits alike; navy ×2 under Unilateral Licensing or the Scramble (not stacked). The navy is `te_seabed_navy_effective`, naval power projection ÷ `te_seabed_power_projection_scale` (300, about an era-11 ship's power projection, a first estimate; seabed claims spec § 6.1), read as a value behind the once-a-game `seabed_power_projection` self-check (fallback `navy_size`); the "+1 licence" readout stores the navy needed in those units and shows it × the scale. +5 Southern with `te_antarctic_station`; 0 Southern for `te_seabed_southern_barred` (holdings grandfathered).
- **Sponsor's floors** (`te_seabed_set_floors`, `te_seabed_fit_floors`; seabed claims spec § 2.2): at the year's first sharing a claimant on Sponsor Contractors, outside a Scramble, stores per basin its holdings (`te_seabed_sh_<basin>`) plus `floor(0.75 × own claims)` (`te_seabed_own_claims_<basin>`: leased and subject-passed claims are never protected; Southern: holdings where barred) and that protected part `P` alone (`te_seabed_fprot_<basin>`); every sharing that year freezes it at `max(held, min(floor, held + P))` instead of held (building on claims keeps the floor; a licence lost mid-year adds no protection), a mid-year one honouring the stored floor (void off Sponsor, in a Scramble, for a non-claimant, `te_seabed_floor_void_<basin>`). Floors that don't fit beside the holdings are scaled down by one factor; holdings are never touched. A floor may spill into a Regulated pool's reserved half (the pioneer investors).
- **Water-filling** (`te_seabed_share_basin`): a real `while` until no country is newly frozen; a country holding at least its tentative entitlement is frozen at its holdings, or its floor if more. Whole licences rounded down, leftovers by largest remainder (`ordered_country` on the fractional remainder), so the pool is fully shared; unbuilt = entitlement − `te_seabed_sh_<basin>` for a claimant (without the technology: entitlement = holdings, the rest `te_seabed_wait_<basin>`, unbuilt 0), leased and passed claims re-divided with the rest.
- **Regulated:** the pool is a reserved half (rounded down; claimants passing `te_seabed_reserved_half_eligible`) and an open half (everyone), water-filled together: a country's tentative entitlement is its share of each half it claims in; a frozen country's holdings come off the two halves in proportion to its two tentative shares (all off the open half without a reserved share); a half driven below zero by grandfathered holdings takes the deficit from the other. Licences carry no half. This keeps Σ entitlements = the pool (or the frozen holdings if more) with nothing to store, and a party holding more than its reserved share spills into the open half instead of starving the other parties. A reserved half that no active country is eligible for joins the open half (`te_seabed_share_fold_unclaimed`), so every pool is fully shared; an eligible party without the technology is active, so the half waits with it.

**Leases** (seabed claims spec § 4; model § LEASES). Five directed articles, Lease <Basin> Seabed Claims (`te_seabed_lease_<basin>`, `can_be_enforced`, one template): the source leases N of its own claims in the basin to the target, N being the lease's total (licences built on it plus its unused claims). The hook dispatches: `te_seabed_lease_start` marks the lessee and the hidden `te_seabed.1` a day later reads the article's lessor and quantity from its treaties, then moves up to N of the lessor's own claims (`te_seabed_lease_enter`). A level the lessee records takes its own claims first, then subject-passed ones, then leased ones (`te_seabed_lease_consume`, the end of the recording). At the sharing a lease stands while an in-force article from the recorded lessor names the lessee and both claim (`te_seabed_lease_shift_basin`, `te_seabed_lease_stands`); its licences, at most the lessee's holdings, count as the lessor's. The sharing re-divides leased claims, and `te_seabed_settle_leases` tops a standing lease back up to N less its licences from the lessor's own claims, unless the lessee relinquished the basin. An ended lease's licences go on charging the lessor (`te_seabed_lease_past_<basin>`) while both take part (review C2: else ending and re-signing moves their cost onto third parties), and the record then admits a new lease from that lessor only; it clears when one side stops taking part. An in-force article never taken up (a start event that didn't run, an enforced lease) is adopted at the sharing. AI: offer claims above a year's building pace (`te_seabed_ai_lease_spare_<basin>`), request in a home basin when room is at most 5 and Tech-Critical Metals sell above base (`te_seabed_ai_lease_request_value_<basin>`).

**Administer Seabed Claims** (§ 5.2; model § SUBJECTS): an overlord's pact with a direct subject (Raise Payments' shape without its DLC gate, not on protectorates or personal unions, +0.10 liberty desire, −1 relations a day, overlord only). A lease with no total in the same two counters, kept on the subject: at entry (`accept_effect` → `te_seabed_pact_start`) and after every sharing (`te_seabed_pass_subject_claims`) the subject's own claims pass to the overlord (`te_seabed_pass_basin`), and the licences the overlord builds on them count as the subject's holdings at the sharing (`te_seabed_pact_shift_basin`), so the pair never takes a third party's share. The counters charge the overlord named in `te_seabed_pass_to`, and go on charging it after the pact ends while both take part (review C2), so ending and taking the pact again moves nothing onto a third party; only another overlord's pact starts them afresh. The pact is the record of whether claims pass (`te_seabed_pact_stands`: `has_diplomatic_pact`, `is_direct_subject_of`); when it ends, the passed claims return through the next sharing.

**Long-Haul Seabed Operations** (`te_seabed_long_haul`, `building_throughput_add = -0.25`): a building modifier on the state's Deep-Sea Mine (owner, 2026-10-27; it was a state modifier on `building_ocean_mine_throughput_add`, a type still registered for the blockade fallback), applied from `on_monthly_pulse_state` with multiplier = the state's share of distant licences, kept in the state variable `te_seabed_long_haul_x` and read as `root.var` (a building has no variables), its one refresh site. The refresh also removes a state copy an older save carries. Monthly, not yearly as the spec drafted: the records it reads move at the monthly recording, so a swap lifts the penalty within a month.

**Blockades** (seabed claims spec § 6.2): `building_ocean_mine` is `city_type = port`, the field every blockade-affected vanilla building shares, so a blockade cuts its throughput as it does a fishing wharf's (up to `BLOCKADE_THROUGHPUT_IMPACT_SCALING` = 75%). Unverified: `docs/testing/global-commons-playtest.md` item 28 names the fallback, a state modifier `te_seabed_blockaded` scaled by blockade level.

**The rush, announced** (seabed claims spec § 7): the event `te_seabed.3`, The Seabed Rush Begins, once a game from `te_seabed_global_monthly` to every player, the month the first claimant appears and before its first sharing (an old save past its first sharing sets `te_seabed_rush_announced` silently; the claimant is kept in global `te_seabed_first_claimant`), standing in for `headlines_tech_abyssal_plain_mining` while the rule is on (`common/on_actions/headlines.txt`); then feed notifications (`common/messages/te_global_commons_seabed_messages.txt`, none to decentralized countries): `te_seabed_new_claimant_notice_<basin>` from `te_seabed_claimant_notices` (yearly pass step 7c) to every player with a share there since an earlier sharing and coast on the basin (`te_seabed_coast_<basin>` > 0), when a country's `te_seabed_ent_<basin>` first passes 0 (country flag `te_seabed_claimed_<basin>`; the first sharing to run it only marks, `te_seabed_claimed_seeded`); `te_seabed_basin_full_notice_<basin>` from `te_seabed_world_totals` to every player with a share there or coast on it, when the world's records reach the pool, re-armed below it (global `te_seabed_full_<basin>`). Both are in the message group `te_seabed_notification_group`, so Message Settings can mute them.

**Policy** (`te_seabed_set_policy = { POLICY = n }`, the one change): sets `te_seabed_policy_prev`, then `te_seabed_policy` and `te_seabed_policy_changed` (the month), rebuilds the influence modifier, then calls the UN hook. The cost (seabed claims spec § 2.3) is a unit modifier (`te_seabed_policy_sponsor_cost` / `_unilateral_cost`, `country_influence_cost_add = 1`) applied with multiplier `var:te_seabed_policy_cost_cached`: Sponsor `50 + 0.5 × own unused claims` (`te_seabed_sponsor_cost_value` over `te_seabed_protected_claims`, uncapped; leased and passed claims cost nothing, as nothing protects them), Unilateral `1.5 ×` that, at least 150. The monthly pass re-adds it when the figure moves. **The lock** (§ 2.4): any change holds the policy 60 months (`te_seabed_policy_locked`); Unilateral opens sooner when a country sharing a home basin switched to it after our last change (`te_seabed_unilateral_answer_open`), Survey while influence is in deficit (`te_seabed_influence_deficit`); the buttons and the AI read `te_seabed_can_choose_*`. **Relinquish / Claim Again** (`te_seabed_relinquish`, `te_seabed_claim_again`, per basin, from the panel): claims to 0, floor to 0, weight 0 there until Claim Again; never sets `te_seabed_reshare`. **The holding fee** (§ 2.1): `te_seabed_holding_fee_modifier` (`country_expenses_add`, Budget Breakdown: United Nations), refreshed monthly by `te_seabed_fee_refresh` with multiplier = 2% of a level's base output value a week × the licences on levels already unbuilt at the last two first-sharings of a year (`te_seabed_fee_base`); a Law of the Sea party under the Regulated regime's fee joins the royalties' weekly total. Unilateral claimants that both have incorporated coast in a basin lose 10 relations a year, half from each side, on the year's first sharing only. The weights follow at the next sharing; the influence from the day of the change.

**AI** (`te_seabed_ai_choose_policy`, `on_yearly_pulse_country`, AI claimants only, never a revolution's side): holds the highest score of `te_global_commons_seabed_ai_values.txt` (header table), with a stay bonus. Building needs no AI code: the engine's builder obeys the gate.

**The gate** (`te_seabed_gate`, read from `building_ocean_mine`'s `possible` beside `is_coastal`): with the rule on, the owner's room above 0, or at 0 in a state with a level already under construction (the Solar Power Receiver's form, so construction under way isn't halted by its own queued level); two information lines say which licence the next level takes. The second branch can't tell re-checking a queued level from queueing one more, so at room 0 it lets one extra level in. Recorded against no share, that level would put room back to 0 and the branch would let another in every month (review H1: 124 Arctic records against a pool of 100 in two years); waiting unrecorded, it holds room below 0 and shuts both branches. Every room read sits behind a cheap test (the unbuilt sum, or a mine under construction here), since `te_seabed_room` walks every building of the owner's coastal states.

**Display.** The **Seabed** tab of the Timeline Extended window (`gui/te_seabed_widgets.gui`, layout A; the window's fifth tab, after the Colonial Empire, open once the country has taken part in a sharing): an overview of six boxes two to a row (room to build and at home; our licences, built and queued, the holding fee; long-haul; unused claims and what next January can take; policy and its lock; regime and ITLOS party), the three short policy buttons, the Ocean Basins table (all five: Free, a stacked pool bar of our built and queued licences, our claims, rivals' licences and rivals' claims (the dark rest, with the shares waiting for countries without the technology, which the hover lists apart), Weight, the "+1 licence" readout `te_seabed_readout`), each basin opening onto its claimants in columns (flag, name, Mines, Claims, Weight: a datamodel of the player's `te_seabed_rk_list_<basin>`, each item a capital read through `State.GetCountry`; `TE_SELF_CHECK seabed_claimant_list` once a game) with our own row's Relinquish / Claim Again, and How Seabed Licences Work (collapsed). Fonts in `te_seabed_fontsize_*` (17 / 20 / 16); `test_seabed_layout.py` holds every fixed cell to its longest text. The State Panel's **Seabed Licences** tile (§ State Panel GUI Enhancements).

**The UN's hooks** (bodies in the UN layer, below): `te_seabed_reserved_half_eligible`, `te_seabed_itlos_party`, `te_seabed_southern_barred` (country triggers, `common/scripted_triggers/te_seabed_un_hooks.txt`); `te_seabed_un_update_regime` (no scope, at the start of each sharing) and `te_seabed_un_on_policy_change` (country, after both policy variables are set; reached with ROOT = the country from the buttons and the AI, and with no ROOT from the yearly pass's reset of a non-claimant), in `common/scripted_effects/te_seabed_un_hooks.txt`. The UN layer reads `te_seabed_held_<basin>` and `te_seabed_policy`.

**Self-checks** (`docs/testing/global-commons-playtest.md`): `seabed_cap` (each yearly pass after the first: each basin's records within last year's ceiling plus what was recorded against no share since, no monthly recording grandfathering a stamped state since (the H1 leak's signature, which the no-share count would otherwise absorb), and no participant leaving a level unlicensed while it holds share; levels waiting past room are counted, not BROKEN; OK once, BROKEN each failing year) `seabed_licence_follows_state` (the first watched state to change owner: its records and stamp read back inside the hook and a month later) and `seabed_floor_fits` (after a sharing in which a floor protected something: every basin's entitlements within its pool, or its holdings if more).

**Tests.** `test_seabed_basins.py` (every coastal state and sea region mapped, file current), `test_seabed_allocation.py` (the model over random worlds in every regime; `WaitingShareTest`: a lone first mover gets only its weighted share and can't lock a basin, the reserved half waits for an eligible party without the technology, a waiting share is never a claim; builders using both gate branches with construction finishing and cancelled: no basin over its pool where nothing is grandfathered, a level unlicensed only while its owner has no share left, an over-pool basin never grows, a far power's share is small, the Southern bar; `UnderConstructionBranchTest` reproduces the review's H1 leak with the old rule and holds the pool with the new), `test_seabed_script.py` (the script's constants, call order, gate and contract against the model), `test_seabed_loc.py` (no "recorded" in seabed player text; the panel's keys), `test_seabed_layout.py` (the panel's widths and structure). The model also covers the floors, Relinquish (never pays), the fee's grace and the "+1 licence" readout (`FloorTest`, `RelinquishTest`, `FeeTest`, `ReadoutTest`: the readout is a sufficient figure, the exact need between it for the entitlement and for one more).

## Global Commons: the UN layer

The UN's part of the Global Commons (`docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-16-global-commons-design.md` §3, §4, §6.5): the Law of the Sea's seabed terms, the Antarctic research station and the Antarctic Treaty, and the Moratorium on Destructive Anti-Satellite Tests. The seabed licences, basins, pools and the seabed policy are the seabed system's (its section beside this one); the strike and the debris index are the space race's. The UN details (docket items, vote sites, the registry) are in `journal_entry_systems.md` § United Nations, "The Global Commons".

**Files:** `common/script_values/te_global_commons_un_values.txt` (every figure), `common/scripted_triggers/te_global_commons_un_triggers.txt`, `common/scripted_effects/te_global_commons_un_effects.txt` (every writer), `common/static_modifiers/te_global_commons_un_modifiers.txt`, `common/decisions/te_global_commons_un_decisions.txt`, `common/on_actions/te_global_commons_un_on_actions.txt`, `common/messages/te_global_commons_un_messages.txt`, `events/te_global_commons_un_events.txt` (the self-check), the two conventions' sites in the UN files, and the hooks: `common/scripted_triggers/te_seabed_un_hooks.txt` + `common/scripted_effects/te_seabed_un_hooks.txt` (the seabed allocation calls them), `common/scripted_triggers/te_asat_un_hooks.txt` + `common/scripted_effects/te_asat_un_hooks.txt` (the anti-satellite strike calls them). Tests: `test_global_commons_un.py`, `test_un_convention_registry.py`.

### The interface with the seabed and debris systems

| Name | Kind | Written by | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `te_seabed_regime` | global var: 1 Open, 2 Regulated, 3 Scramble (absent = Open) | `te_seabed_un_update_regime`, once a year at the start of the seabed allocation | the allocation (reserved half, navy ×2), royalties, Our Obligations |
| `te_seabed_itlos_party` | trigger (country) | here | the allocation, the Seabed section's party status |
| `te_seabed_reserved_half_eligible` | trigger (country) | here | the allocation's reserved half |
| `te_seabed_southern_barred` | trigger (country): an Antarctic Treaty party | here | the allocation (Southern entitlement 0, built levels grandfathered) |
| `te_seabed_un_on_policy_change` | effect (country), after `te_seabed_policy` / `te_seabed_policy_prev` are set | here | called by the seabed policy's change |
| `te_seabed_policy`, `te_seabed_held_<basin>`, state `te_seabed_basin` | country / state vars | the seabed system | here, every read guarded |
| `te_antarctic_station` | country var | the station decisions here | the seabed allocation's +5 Southern weight |
| `te_asat_moratorium_party` | trigger (country) | here | the strike (twice the infamy and the case) |
| `te_asat_un_on_strike` | effect (the striker; `scope:te_asat_target`) | here | called by the strike |
| `te_asat_last_strike_month`, `te_asat_strikes_total`, `modifier:country_orbital_debris_removal_add` | globals; a country modifier | the debris system | here, guarded |

### Mechanics

- **Regimes.** Open while the Law of the Sea is not in force, its seabed terms are asleep (nobody has Abyssal Plain Mining, `te_seabed_terms_awake`) or the UN rule is off; Scramble while two or more great powers hold Unilateral Licensing; Regulated otherwise. A Scramble returns to Regulated 24 months after fewer than two remain (`te_seabed_scramble_return_month`, read at the yearly pass, so two passes). Each change of regime is a notification to every country with Abyssal Plain Mining.
- **Party status.** Ratified (the member modifier or its mirror), not on Unilateral Licensing, and not cooling off: a party that switches to Unilateral Licensing while the convention governs the seabed (in force and awake, the live condition `te_seabed_itlos_governs`, not the stored regime, so nobody slips out between a vote and the next pass) pays 10 infamy, 5 standing and 10 defiance once (`te_seabed_defected`); leaving Unilateral Licensing for either lawful policy starts `te_seabed_party_cooldown_end` (60 months). Under the Scramble a defection still costs, since the convention still governs; royalties and the reserved half are suspended.
- **Royalties.** A party under Regulated pays `te_seabed_ocean_mine_levels × te_seabed_royalty_per_level` a week (4% of 44,700, the base method's proposed output value at base prices: 1,788), billed as dues are (`te_seabed_royalty_modifier` × `var:te_seabed_royalty_cached`, refreshed monthly, one site). The monthly global pulse sums them into `te_seabed_royalties_weekly`; `un_dev_fund_pot_weekly_value` adds it while the World Development Fund stands and `un_budget_weekly_value` otherwise. Budget Breakdown: United Nations.
- **The station.** A decision for any country with Space Exploration under the Global Commons rule. +2% research speed, +25 innovation cap, upkeep 0.1% of GDP a year with a floor of 1,000 a week (Budget Breakdown: Space Race). `var:te_antarctic_station` is the truth; `te_antarctic_station_refresh` rebuilds both modifiers monthly.
- **The Antarctic Treaty.** Raised by a country's first station (docket item 15). Parties: +2% prestige (×E), no new Southern licences, +3% research with a station (regime term ×E), +0.25 Policy at ×1 (`te_antarctic_policy_refresh`). Denounced by decision (10 infamy, 5 standing, 10 defiance, `te_antarctic_denounced` until a new treaty); lapses monthly-checked when two great powers outside it hold Southern licences.
- **The Moratorium.** Raised by a destructive anti-satellite strike (docket item 16, `un_dkt_asat_pending`); the striker is not offered it for two years. Parties: +5% prestige (×E); the strike reads `te_asat_moratorium_party`; once a year a party with a removal method books 0.25 × weight to Delivery (reason 40).
- **Rules.** The station and the treaty need the Global Commons rule (`has_game_rule = global_commons_enabled`); the moratorium the space race rule; all UN business the UN rule (the regime is Open without it).
- **Revolutions.** Everything that must survive is a variable or a convention's mirror; the royalty, station, upkeep and Policy modifiers are derived monthly. `je_immediate_reset_audit` has nothing to flag: nothing here runs in an `immediate`.

## Wonder Buildings (Construction Site Pattern)

> **Full design document:** `docs/vanilla/wonder_buildings_reference.md`

The seven **megaprojects** use a two-phase construction pattern: a buildable construction site becomes the completed building through a scripted effect. (The ordinary wonders in `common/buildings/wonders.txt` are built through the normal construction queue and are not covered here.) All seven are era-12 technologies; their sites and buildings live in `common/buildings/extra_buildings.txt`.

| Megaproject | Tech | Max level | Completed building does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Space Elevator | `space_elevator` | 20 | 1M `launch_capacity` per level, `country_space_race_progress_add` |
| Orbital Solar Collector | `space_based_solar_power` | 10 | an orbital hub: each level opens 3 `building_solar_receiver` slots (`country_solar_receiver_max_level_add`); the ground receivers produce the electricity |
| Orbital Battlestation | `orbital_weapon_platforms` | 5 | country-wide unit offense/defense/morale and nuclear-defence chance; no goods output |
| Antimatter Containment Facility | `antimatter_production` | 10 | each level opens 5 slots (`country_antimatter_facility_max_level_add`) for `building_antimatter_engine` and `building_antimatter_warhead_plant` |
| Mind Upload Nexus | `mind_backups` | 5 | digital assets, services, tourism and fine art output, research speed; under the Demographics rule's Full setting both follow the uploaded minds it hosts (§ Demographics, Uploaded minds) |
| Nanofabrication Center | `molecular_assemblers` | 10 | `advanced_materials` output, lower space race risk |
| Consciousness Network | `telepathic_communities` | 10 | state infrastructure, tax capacity and institution impact, bureaucracy; a mode group picks Open (SoL, innovation, influence) or Social Control (authority, less turmoil; unlocked by the laws that disallow Open) |

- **Construction effect:** `generic_wonder_construction_base = { WONDER = <name> MAX_LEVEL = <n> }` in `common/scripted_effects/extra_effects.txt`, called through one named wrapper per megaproject (`space_elevator_construction`, …). Each megaproject's `<name>_on_action` runs it from `on_monthly_pulse_state` (`common/on_actions/extra_on_actions.txt`). On completion it removes the site and creates the building at level 1, or raises it one level up to the cap; a site can't be placed once the building is at its cap.
- **Construction progress:** each month, `building_annual_<name>_progress / 12`, and nothing while the site has a goods shortage. The PM puts that modifier in `workforce_scaled`, so it already scales with staffing and progress is linear in occupancy; until 2026-10-01 the tick multiplied by `occupancy` again, so a half-staffed site ran at a quarter speed. The site's `<name>_progress` modifier mirrors the state's `<name>_progress_var` (`multiplier = root.var:…` from the state pulse). Speed PMs set the annual progress: paused 0, slow 0.25, medium 0.5, fast 1.0 (about 4 / 2 / 1 years at full occupancy).
- **Custom modifier types:** `building_annual_*_progress` and `building_total_*_progress` (script_only) in `megastructure_progress_modifier_types.txt`.

## Grand Monuments (Political Instrument)

A government raises a Grand Monument to what it stands for, and the next government deals with its legacy. Design: `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-09-27-grand-monument-rework-design.md`; plan: `docs/superpowers/archive/plans/2026-09-27-grand-monument-rework.md`. v2: `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-05-grand-monuments-v2-design.md`, plan `docs/superpowers/archive/plans/2026-10-05-grand-monuments-v2-phases-1-3.md`. Built: phase 1 (1,000 construction a level; vanity and Rededicate a tenth), phase 2 (commissions, names, typed names) and phase 3 (the monument policy; the owner swapped it ahead of the 1836 monuments). Phase 4 is built too: the 23 landmarks standing in 1836 (design `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-12-grand-monuments-landmarks-design.md`, plan `docs/superpowers/archive/plans/2026-10-11-grand-monuments-landmarks.md`), and since 2026-10-12 nineteen more where Europe's looting took place (the Parthenon, the Obelisks of Karnak, the royal palaces of Benin and Kumasi, the Bukgwan Victory Stele, the Imperial City of Huế, Persepolis, the Red Fort, Great Zimbabwe, the Royal Palaces of Abomey, Klungkung Palace, the Uffizi, the Capitoline Museums, Bodrum Castle, the Temples of Baalbek, Palmyra, Xanthos, the Mesha Stele and the Arch of Ctesiphon) with the ten trophies already abroad in 1836 (design `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-12-grand-monument-loot-and-1836-trophies-design.md`). Commissions became **opportunities** on 2026-10-12 (spec `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-12-grand-monument-opportunities-design.md`): no downsides, every one from a moment, completion gives 5 grandeur (a free rebuild 5 levels taller until the ageing rework), the approval and a ten-year boon. Since 2026-10-16 a monument is **frozen at dedication and grows grander with age**, new levels in its state found a monument beside it, and a monument beside another carries its own dedication (spec `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-16-grand-monument-ageing-design.md`, plan `docs/superpowers/archive/plans/2026-10-16-grand-monument-ageing.md`; § Ageing below). Phase 5 is built too: trophies (design `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-12-grand-monument-trophies-design.md`). Since 2026-10-16 **unique dedications** (*signatures*: a unique dedication layered on one of the twelve, for landmarks, for the monument that completes certain opportunities, and phase 6 rebuilt as historical opportunities; spec `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-16-grand-monument-signatures-design.md`; § Unique dedications below) are built, with the first six historical opportunities. **Add a dedication:** add its row to `DEDICATIONS` in `test_grand_monument_registry.py`; the failures are the checklist. **Add an opportunity's moment (with its boon), a form, namesake or policy:** its row in `COMMISSION_SOURCES`, `FORMS`, `NAMESAKES` or `POLICIES` in the same file. **Add a form or a style:** its row in `FORMS` or `BUILDING_SKINS` in the same file, then its picture: a new code at the end of its block in `PICTURES` (never renumber) and its entry in the icon pipeline's `gm_picture` category. **Add a landmark:** its row at the end of `LANDMARKS` in the same file (key, state, 1836 owner, dedication, form, stand-in picture, level); the failures list its seeding call, loc, name branches and picture line. Its picture takes the next code from 1,000,000 once drawn; until then it shows the stand-in's. **Add a trophy of 1836:** its row in `TROPHIES_1836` in `test_grand_monument_trophies.py` (landmark, origin and its 1836 owner, site and its holder, levels, share, year); a trophy with no standing monument of its own also needs a `LANDMARKS` row with `placed=False` (no seeding call, no level; its state and owner are its origin's), which it is rebuilt as when it goes home.

- **Files:** `common/buildings/grand_monuments.txt`, `common/production_methods/grand_monument_pms.txt`, `common/production_method_groups/grand_monument_pmgs.txt`, `common/scripted_triggers/monument_triggers.txt`, `common/scripted_effects/gm_effects.txt`, `common/script_values/gm_values.txt`, `common/static_modifiers/gm_modifiers.txt`, `common/journal_entries/je_grand_monuments.txt`, `gui/journal_entry_widgets/grand_monuments_widget.gui`, the state view's card in `gui/te_state_panel_widgets.gui` (`te_state_gm_card`, instanced from `gui/states_panel.gui`), `common/scripted_guis/gm_sguis.txt`, `common/customizable_localization/gm_custom_loc.txt`, `common/on_actions/monument_events_on_actions.txt`, `events/monument_events.txt`, `events/te_debug_monuments_events.txt`; the shared `common/scripted_triggers/te_heritage_triggers.txt`; `grand_monuments_rule` in `extra_game_rules.txt`. v2: `gm_commission_triggers.txt`, `gm_commission_effects.txt`, `gm_commission_values.txt`, `gm_name_triggers.txt`, `gm_name_effects.txt`, `gm_policy_triggers.txt`, `gm_policy_effects.txt`; trophies: `gm_trophy_triggers.txt`, `gm_trophy_effects.txt`, `gm_trophy_values.txt`, `gm_trophy_sguis.txt`, `gm_trophy_on_actions.txt`, `gm_trophy_custom_loc.txt`, `events/monument_trophy_events.txt`, `gui/gm_trophy_widgets.gui`, the treaty articles `118_return_cultural_property.txt` and `119_surrender_monument.txt`, and `test_grand_monument_trophies.py`; several monuments in one state: `gm_monument_effects.txt`, `gm_monument_triggers.txt`, `gm_monument_values.txt`, `gm_monument_sguis.txt`, `gm_monument_on_actions.txt`, the Also Standing Here section of the state card (`te_state_gm_beside`, in `gui/gm_trophy_widgets.gui`) and `docs/testing/grand-monuments-multiple-playtest.md`; archaeology: `gm_archaeology_effects.txt`, `gm_archaeology_triggers.txt`, `gm_archaeology_gate_triggers.txt`, `gm_archaeology_values.txt`, `gm_archaeology_sguis.txt`, `gm_archaeology_on_actions.txt`, `gm_archaeology_modifiers.txt`, `gm_archaeology_custom_loc.txt`, `events/archaeology_events.txt`, `gui/gm_archaeology_widgets.gui`, the treaty articles `120_archaeological_concession.txt` and `121_excavation_permit.txt`, `test_grand_monument_archaeology.py` and `docs/testing/grand-monuments-archaeology-playtest.md`; the typed-name carrier `common/company_types/gm_name_carrier_company.txt` with `common/buildings/gm_name_carrier.txt` and its PM/PMG; founding years seeded from `common/history/extra_history.txt`.
- **Grandeur and the curve.** A monument's grandeur is its starting grandeur plus its age grandeur (§ Ageing below); its size is its records (§ Construction sites below), never its building's level, and no script rebuilds a finished monument. Every effect grows in steps. National effects and interest group approval take the **doubling curve**, each step costing twice the grandeur of the last (`gm_curve_steps_f5` / `_f10`, eight terms; `gm_curve_next_*` for the JE's "next step"). Local effects (tourism, each dedication's and each signature's), prestige, cultural pull and Antiquity's pull take the **1/n curve** (owner, 2026-10-19: grandeur priced by world wealth can't be farmed, so they taper less): step n costs n first steps, so each step is worth 1/n of the first a point of grandeur and the effect grows about as √grandeur. Local effects use `gm_curve_steps_lin_f5` (thirty terms, the last ending at 2,325; `gm_curve_lin_steps`), capped per dedication by `gm_state_local_steps_one`'s `CAP` (War Memorial's conscription at `gm_local_cap_war_memorial` = 10 steps of +0.01, Stadium's turmoil at `gm_local_cap_athletic` = 5 steps of −10%; the rest `gm_curve_lin_steps`, after the policy factor); the national ones `gm_set_steps_lin_open`, a `while` with no end that also records the step's width (`gm_w_*`) for the bar. Each static modifier carries **one step** and the multiplier is the step count; `gm_step_*` script values mirror them for loc, pinned equal by the registry test.
- **Construction sites and recorded size (2026-10-18; spec `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-18-grand-monument-sites-and-world-wealth-design.md`, plans `docs/superpowers/archive/plans/2026-10-18-grand-monument-sites-plan-a.md` and `-plan-b.md`, code maps beside them).** A player builds and expands `building_grand_monument_site` (`grand_monument_site.txt`: one per state, `pm_grand_monument_site` does nothing, no upkeep, no effects, `gm_state_can_build_site` its gate, the AI's `ai_value`). `gm_state_count_site_levels` (from `gm_state_monthly` and the dedication) counts its new levels into `gm_site_counted` / `gm_site_grandeur`, each at the world-wealth rate of the month (`gm_world_rate_value`, below), with the grandeur they add on the vanity ledger in hard times; lost levels take their share. **The rate** (Plan B): `gm_world_rate` = `gm_world_gdp_1836` (402,500,000: `global_gdp_script_value` at a new game's first pass, February 1836, read by `gm_world_base` on 2026-10-25; the first figure, 334,000,000 summed from a save of 1836.1.20, read a sixth low) ÷ `global_gdp_script_value`, written each January by `gm_monument_monthly` and by `gm_world_rate_ensure` wherever none is; `gm_world_rate_value` reads it times `gm_level_grandeur_1836` (5, owner 2026-10-19), to the nearest 0.001 and at least 0.001, and `gm_world_wealth_factor` is 1 ÷ the stored ratio; `TE_SELF_CHECK gm_world_base` compares a new game's first pass with the constant. Shown on the site's card, once on the overview's last line, under the policy (`gm_je_world_rate`, `gm_world_wealth_factor` on hover; GM-5 of the 2026-10-27 GUI audit put it above Awaiting Dedication's rows, which hid it until the first site, so it moved on 2026-10-28) and in the site's build tooltip (`gm_site_rate_tt`, an `always = yes` custom tooltip in `possible`). What a monument means counts starting grandeur: opportunities (`gm_com_fit_grandeur`; `gm_com_levels_to_go` = the grandeur missing ÷ the rate, at most 100), vanity, trophy infamy (`gm_tr_infamy` on the grandeur taken), an anniversary's gift (a tenth of the starting grandeur); levels count what it cost (upkeep, Rededicate's 500 a level). The 1836 landmarks, the trophies abroad in 1836 and digs record their grandeur at `gm_level_grandeur_1836` a level, split by `gm_set_historical_grandeur` as if dedicated in the year they were built and aged since at 2% of the start a year for at most a century (owner, 2026-10-19): start = G ÷ (1 + 0.02 × min(years, 100)), age = the rest, so anything a century old in 1836 is a third start and two thirds age and ages no further (the Parthenon 16.7 + 33.3), the Brandenburg Gate (1791) 26.3 + 23.7; the year is each seed call's `BUILT` (negative before Christ; `BUILT` in `test_grand_monument_registry.py`), a dig site's stored as `gm_tr_built` (read by `gm_mon_built`, this year without one; seed round 3 gives it to sites seeded earlier) and split when it is placed or a partage piece is cut; landmarks and trophies already in a running save keep their old split; older saves' records count one a level. Dedicate (`gm_dedicate_sgui`, greyed while a level is under construction) opens the ceremony in mode site (`gm_ceremony_mode`); the answer (`gm_state_finish_site`, under a click guard) demotes a finished monument standing here (`gm_newcomer`: the grander swaps back from `.29` once the newcomer is settled), writes `gm_levels` / `gm_start_grandeur` from the site, removes the site and creates the finished `building_grand_monument` at level 1 with `activate_production_methods` and a `gm_restore_pm` fallback (`gm_site_created`), or switches the one standing. The finished type is `buildable = no`, `expandable = no`, `downsizeable = no`. Records: primary on the state (`gm_levels`, `gm_start_grandeur`, `gm_age`), beside on its container (`gm_tr_levels`, `gm_tr_start_grandeur`, `gm_tr_age`); a missing start reads as the levels (`gm_state_primary_start`, `gm_mon_start`). Takings, returns, digs, Pull Down beside and promotion change records only; the building is made only where none stands (`gm_state_tr_rebuild_from_moving`, `gm_state_raise_orphan`) and removed only when the last monument goes (`gm_state_tear_down`, `gm_state_tr_remove_whole`). A building lost while its records stand is put back at level 1 on `gm_dedication` (`gm_state_lost_building`, `.29`). Upkeep: none since 2026-10-23 (policy spec § 5): `gm_upkeep` on the building, multiplier `root.var:gm_upkeep_mult` = −1 (`gm_state_upkeep_mult`), cancels `pm_maintenance`'s level-scaled input; `pmg_maintenance` stays on the building. Rededicate asks first (`gm_rededicate_asking`, mode rededicate); the answer (`gm_state_apply_rededicate`) pays and halves the records; *Keep it as it is* changes nothing. Older saves: the first monthly pass marks unmigrated finished buildings `gm_premigration` (`gm_sites_marked`); `monument_events.32` (from the refresh, once nothing is under construction or pending) records a dedicated one at its levels and resets its building to 1 (levels finished above its record, `gm_mig_excess`, stand as a site), or makes an undedicated one a site at its level; every building script makes is `gm_migrated`, and until then a building pays its own level-scaled upkeep (`gm_state_upkeep_mult` is 0) and no merge resets it; `TE_SELF_CHECK monument_migrated`. Panels: `te_state_gm_site_card` and `gm_site_row` (Awaiting Dedication), Our Monuments lists finished ones (`gm_state_disp_listed`) but the contested, which Awaiting a Decision lists (GM-3, owner 2026-10-27), and the overview's Sites cell counts sites (`gm_disp_count_sites`, those ready `gm_disp_count_sites_ready`). `WalkedRefreshTests` pins that nothing the refresh calls makes or removes a building or container.
- **The dedication chain opens as popups (owner, 2026-10-19).** The ceremony (`monument_events.2`), the style (`.11`), the form (`.24`), the namesake (`.25`) and an opportunity's seized notice (`.28`) each define `is_popup = yes`, and every `trigger_event` that fires one says `popup = yes` (`DedicationPopupTests` pins both). Anniversaries (`.3`–`.10`, `.12`–`.15`) and the opportunity offer (`.21`) stay notification cards. The idiom: `docs/guides/event_creation_guide.md` § "Making an Event Open at Once". Play-test row: `docs/testing/grand-monuments-ageing-playtest.md` § Dedicate.
- **Landmarks** (phase 4, `gm_landmark_effects.txt`): placed once from `on_game_started_after_lobby` behind the rule. A landmark is its own skin (`landmark_<key>`) with one form, locked while it stands (`gm_state_is_landmark`): the style offer, the unveiling's default form and `gm_clear_state` (`KEEP_LANDMARK = yes` from Rededicate only) leave its skin, form and picture. Its historical name (`gm_namesake = landmark`, `gm_state_has_historical_name`) greys out Rename and Name It and survives a met commission; a rededication names it again, and `monument_events.25` offers the historical name back. The AI preserves a contested landmark at three times the weight. The Grand Opera House, Botanical Gardens and Grand Observatory methods carry no technology, so the engine can't switch a landmark off them; the ceremony checks it, and `gm_state_first_sight` sends a panel pick made without it to the ceremony (`gm_state_lacks_dedication_tech`). Debug: `te_debug_monuments.5`.
- **To History and the heritage landmarks (tourism heritage phases 2–3, 2026-10-25; spec `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-23-tourism-heritage-design.md` §§ 7, 9).** `pm_monument_historic` carries tourism, prestige and cultural pull and nothing else: no `gm_local_historic`, no national sum, no interest group, no anniversary, no signature. Timeless, so it always fits, `gm_state_changed_hands` never contests it, and with nothing to contest Pull Down and Rededicate never reach it; the ceremony doesn't offer it (a player-built monument would get prestige with no politics), and since construction sites no finished building stands undedicated for a panel pick but an older save's before its migration. 51 landmarks of 1836 are seeded on it with the others (`gm_seed_landmarks`, `DEDICATION = historic`, levels 3–15 by the base appeal each takes: 2 steps 3, 3 steps 6, 4 steps 10, 5 steps 15; Petra beside the Mesha Stele), and 14 buried sites come up on it when dug (`gm_arch_seed_site`'s `DEDICATION`). Each record list a dedication passes through names it (`gm_state_record_dedication`, `gm_state_mark_restore_pm`, `gm_state_restore_dedication`, `gm_tr_record_dedication`, `gm_state_stands_on_dedication`). Each has its own picture and trophy picture. A landmark added without one shows a stand-in, and `PLACEHOLDER_PICTURES` in the registry test and the backlog table in `docs/systems/grand_monuments_gui_icons.md` list it. `HistoryDedicationTests` pins the wiring and the policy weighting.
- **PMs carry only staff.** The dedication PMs keep the self-reference ratchet (see the file header) and `unscaled` employment; no `country_modifiers`, `state_modifiers` or goods. A building `create_building` makes starts on the dedication most of its owner's monuments carry, not on `is_default` (2026-10-08), unless `activate_production_methods` names one; the ratchet binds the panel only, `activate_production_method` passes it, and `gm_restore_pm` puts a recorded dedication back a pulse later (`gm_state_restore_dedication`). Since construction sites (2026-10-18) a finished building is always made on its dedication, so the engine's-copy repairs (`gm_state_reset_copied_dedication`, the panel-pick branch of first sight) are gone.
- **Where modifiers live.** Local effects (`gm_local_*`) are state modifiers refreshed by `gm_state_monthly` from `on_monthly_pulse_state`. National effects (`gm_national_*`, `gm_ig_approval_<ig>`) sit on `je:je_grand_monuments`, applied by `gm_country_refresh` with ROOT = the country (monthly, or `monument_events.20` after `on_law_activated`, `on_new_ruler`, `on_state_owner_change` and a finished level, whose ROOTs are not the country). A variable backing a multiplier is zeroed, never removed.
- **JE activation.** `is_shown_when_inactive` auto-activates the entry for new saves the moment a country owns a Grand Monument (gated on `grand_monuments_rule` too). Because a new auto-activating JE never reaches a save that predates it, `gm_country_refresh` also calls `add_journal_entry` explicitly whenever the rule is on, a monument is owned and the entry is missing, so old saves and any save where the entry lapsed pick it back up on the next monthly pulse.
- **Kinds and fit.** Regime (Crown, Republic, Revolution), ruler (Leader), faith (Shrine), timeless (the rest). Fit is read live each month (`gm_state_message_fits`). Records live on the **state** (buildings hold no variables): `gm_raised_by` (a bound monument fits only while that country owns it), `gm_honoree` / `gm_honoree_ig`, `gm_faith`, `gm_skin`. `gm_state_first_sight` writes them for panel picks and old saves; after that a missing record reads as "does not fit".
- **National totals** (`gm_compute_totals`): standing grandeur (every monument not contested: prestige, cultural pull), regime grandeur (fitting regime and ruler monuments: legitimacy), one per dedication with a national effect, and one signed total per IG (approvals minus oppositions, plus its ledger, minus contested monuments whose "new order" it is), each through the curve on its absolute value. `gm_zero_ledgers`: when the last monument is gone and every ledger is idle, the ledgers are zeroed before the pulse stops.
- **Contests** (`gm_check_contests`, skipped while the country has `te_cw_role`): a bound monument that stops fitting records `gm_base_ig` / `gm_supporter_ig` flags and becomes contested; one that fits again is restored. `gm_state_changed_hands` contests a conquered regime or ruler monument and makes a conquered shrine heritage; a monument already contested when its state changes hands is contested afresh for the new owner. The winner of a civil war adopts the loser's monuments (`gm_repair_after_civil_war`, in `te_civil_war_on_won`): while the loser still resolves it rewrites `gm_raised_by` / `gm_tr_raised_by` from the loser to the winner, on every state and on the `gm_monuments`, `gm_trophies` and `gm_shadows` containers, so a monument that reaches the winner later is already its own (the loser is deleted within about two weeks, #1136). A loser still alive, a secession that won, keeps its monuments except those in the winner's states. Choices: `gm_state_tear_down` / `_rededicate` (rebuilt at half level through the shared ladder, which runs to 200) / `_preserve`; each writes decaying ledgers (`gm_teardown_ledger`, `gm_ig_ledger_<ig>`), so nothing stacks. Players get `monument_events.16` (and `.17` per monument); the AI decides monthly. `building_grand_monument` is `downsizeable = no` (AI countries were demolishing monuments as pure upkeep), so these choices, trophies and commission rebuilds, all through `remove_building`, are the only ways one goes or shrinks. A monument that disappears some other way (a save from before the flag) while contested is recorded as torn down by its state pulse (`gm_state_record_teardown`, which also sets `gm_active`), and the JE's `invalid` also waits until no state still carries `gm_seen`, so that teardown is applied before the entry can go.
- **Skins** (`gm_skin`): faith skins by state religion, heritage skins by the language-reform revival partition (`te_heritage_<language>`, also called by `extra_law_events.25`), chosen in `monument_events.11`; `gm_inscription` names a revived language. The choice event is offered to players only; the AI keeps the most specific skin.
- **The dedication ceremony** (`monument_events.2`, a state event) starts through `gm_state_start_ceremony`, which sets what it asks about (`gm_ceremony_mode`): a construction site's dedication (a player's Dedicate button; the AI's from `monument_events.1` on a site's level and from the refresh, `gm_state_offer_missed_ceremony`, once nothing more is queued: `gm_state_ai_dedicates_now`), or Rededicate's (`gm_rededicate_asking`). The trigger reads the mode; an older save's undedicated monument with no mode is asked as before until its migration. *Let it stand as it is, for now* (`gm_state_ceremony_not_yet`) is the site's, weighted 0 for the AI; *Keep it as it is* is Rededicate's. Exactly one default is valid, by complementary triggers. The refresh path exists because five queued levels finishing on one day fired no `on_building_built` (2026-10-07, `scripting_best_practices.md`). `te_debug_monuments.3` asks to rededicate one of our three tallest monuments from the console.
- **Vanity backlash:** the construction site's monthly count (`gm_state_count_site_levels`) calls `gm_state_vanity_backlash_for` in hard times (`gm_country_hard_times`) with the grandeur it counted: radicals once a month, and that much on the linear `gm_vanity_ledger`.
- **Anniversaries:** `.3`–`.10`, `.12`–`.15`, dispatched by `monument_events_on_action` for a fitting monument of grandeur 3 or more; every option is positive, money the only cost.
- **NOT in `bg_monuments`, and that is load-bearing.** `tourism_bonus_from_monuments` and `cultural_pull_from_monuments` iterate `bg_monuments` and assume one-off wonders. `bg_grand_monuments` is a top-level group with no `parent_group`; Grand Monument cultural pull is `cultural_pull_from_grand_monuments` (standing grandeur through the 1/n curve with no ceiling, `gm_set_steps_lin_open`).
- **Panel** (`grand_monuments_widget.gui`, style pass 2026-09-29): three named roots, each a gated wrapper round a composer type, so the Timeline Extended window's tab reuses the sections. Container 1 holds the overview: four status cells (Upheld, Heritage, Undedicated, Contested; the middle two words are the concepts `concept_heritage_monument` / `concept_contested_monument`), lit while their live count (`gm_disp_count_*`) is above zero, and under them, only while `gm_hard_times_sgui` holds, the Hard Times icon over a red "Hard Times" in a fixed 480 column. The entry has no status description: its counts were the overview's. Container 2 holds National Effects (open, `gm_national_closed`), Awaiting Dedication (open, `gm_awaiting_closed`; only while `gm_disp_count_awaiting` > 0, § Dedicate below) and Our Monuments (open, `gm_monuments_closed`; the rows of monuments awaiting dedication are left to the section above it, `gm_state_disp_awaiting`). In National Effects each total shows only while in force, with an empty-state line gated on `gm_disp_national_any`, and each stepped total is a bar filled by `gm_disp_frac_*`, which is (2G − N + f) / (N + f) from its `gm_g_*` / `gm_n_*` pair on the doubling curve, and (G − N + W) / W with the step's width `gm_w_*` on the 1/n curve (prestige, cultural pull, Antiquity), with the grandeur and the next step on hover. Container 3 holds How Grand Monuments Work (collapsed, `gm_how_open`). Everything is display-only; `test_grand_monuments_layout.py` pins the order, the flags, the gates and each bar's f. The status and Hard Times icons are the mod's own, from PR #586 (`gfx/interface/icons/gm_icons/`, listed in `docs/systems/grand_monuments_gui_icons.md`).
- **Timeline Extended window (2026-09-30; not yet seen in game).** The same three composers also show on the *Grand Monuments* tab of the mod's own window (`gui/te_systems_window.gui`), under `datacontext = "[GetPlayerJournalEntry('je_grand_monuments')]"`, then a link back to the entry. The tab is greyed until the entry runs; its tooltip lists `gm_entry_unlocked` (owning a Grand Monument).
- **State view card (2026-10-09; not yet seen in game).** `te_state_gm_card`, a 530 px card under the tourism card, shown while `gm_status_code` is above 0 in any country's state. The row's status icon and word (`gm_row_status`), title (`gm_row_title` / `_named`), contest line and inscription, then Grandeur with a bar of its own step (the 1/n curve from the live level: `gm_state_disp_steps` mirrors `gm_curve_steps_lin_f5`, `gm_state_disp_next_step` ends step n at 5n(n+1)/2, `gm_state_disp_step_pct` is the step count's fraction), its tourism output (`gm_state_disp_tourism`; `gm_local_tourism` is `goods_output_tourism_mult` +0.10 a step since 2026-10-23, Ancestral Antiquity's +0.05 and the First Emperor's Army's +0.10, all output, as base appeal is) and its dedication's local effect (`gm_state_disp_local`, steps × `gm_step_local_<key>`), each from the steps `gm_state_monthly` last wrote and hidden at 0. Since the card shows them, `gm_local_tourism` and `gm_local_<dedication>` are left out of the state panel's modifier rows (step 6 of the dynamic-modifier pattern at the top). The local effect's name and format are the custom localization `gm_local_effect_label` / `_value`, one branch per dedication (`StateCardTests` in the registry test). Display only but for Dedicate (§ Dedicate below) and Carry It Off: the player's own state gets a goto, gated on `te_window_grand_monuments_tab_sgui`, that opens the Timeline Extended window on its Grand Monuments tab (two `onclick` lines: `te_systems_window_tab` to `grand_monuments`, then `com_open_window`). A construction site has its own card under it (`te_state_gm_site_card`, shown while `gm_state_disp_site` is 1): the levels built, the grandeur so far, whether levels are still being built, and our own site's Dedicate button.
- **Opportunities (2026-10-12; v2 §2's commissions reworked).** Players read "opportunity"; script keeps the `gm_com_*` names and files, because a save carries an open commission in them. One record per country in country variables (`gm_commission_effects.txt` header lists them); the asking group is a flag naming its type (a civil war's winner has other IG objects). Offered by `gm_com_send_offer` through `monument_events.21` (titled for the moment by `gm_com_occasion_name`; Seize is the default, Let It Pass costs nothing; the same event for the AI, `gm_com_ai_declines`), open in the JE's Opportunity section (Let It Pass, `gm_com_let_pass_sgui`), closed by `gm_com_fulfil` / `_miss` / `_lapse` / `_decline`, all through `gm_com_close`, which is `gm_com_clear` and nothing else: no cost and no cooldown anywhere. Progress is `gm_com_progress`, as v2: fitting grandeur of the dedication (in the fixed state, if any) above the baseline at seizing, floored at 0, checked by every `gm_country_refresh` (before the totals) and the monthly tick. **Moments** (`COMMISSION_SOURCES` in the registry test): the world pass `gm_com_world_on_action` (every country, monthly), in priority order: first sight (`gm_com_first_sight`, once per country: records great power status and the five technologies as seen, removes v2's promise ledger and cooldown, so 1836 and old saves bring nothing), the founding year, A New Order (regime edge), A New Reign (`gm_com_track_ruler` sees a ruler who is not last month's: Crown when crowned, else Leader; the new ruler is the namesake; none while `has_gov_regency`, since vanilla's `regency.1` adds the modifier and makes the regent ruler in one block, but the regent is still recorded, so the monarch who takes over when the regency ends is a new ruler), Among the Great Powers (once a game), A New Faith (`gm_com_faith_last`, not on a side in a civil war), the space firsts (orbit, Moon landing, lunar colony, Mars landing, interstellar probe; first sight sees those already won), the January centenaries, the five technologies (`gm_com_track_tech`: each civic-progress dedication's gate, the Gardens' moved to the Environmental Movement); plus `on_won_war` / `on_lost_war` and `on_character_death` (a ruler of 180 months), which offer at once, so a long reign's mausoleum takes the slot ahead of the successor's reign. Every rank (`gm_com_can_offer`; owner, 2026-10-12), but not while any state carries `gm_restore_pm`; `gm_com_time_months` 60 for a great power, 120 for a major one, 180 otherwise; the AI below major power lets them pass (`gm_com_ai_declines`). **Completion** gives three things: the asking group's ledger +15; a boon (`gm_com_grant_boon`: `gm_boon_<source>` = 120 months, counted down by `gm_tick_boons` in `gm_country_monthly`, the static modifier of the same name added to the JE by `gm_add_boons` while it runs; `gm_boons_idle` is part of `gm_ledgers_idle`, so the entry and the pulse stay); and the **gift**: `gm_com_fulfil` only marks the completing monument (`gm_gift`) and triggers `monument_events.26` (hidden state event), because the fulfilment runs inside the refresh that tooltips walk. `gm_state_gift_grandeur` removes the building and builds it again `gm_com_gift` (5) levels taller through the ladder (at most 200), keeping every state record; the rebuilt building starts on the engine's copy, so `gm_state_mark_restore_pm` records the dedication as `gm_restore_pm` and `gm_state_restore_dedication` (from `monument_events.1`, the refresh's state loop and `gm_state_monthly`) activates it until it reads back. While `gm_restore_pm` stands, no ceremony starts, no contest check and no picture update reads the monument. The AI queues the levels with `start_building_construction` in a `while` (at most 100, `gm_com_levels_to_go`), and `gm_com_monthly` queues what is still missing once no construction site stands; its ceremony at a monument that can answer the opportunity takes its dedication for certain. A Promise Kept is retired: `gm_national_promise` stays defined and removed for old saves. **Usability (spec §6):** Raise It (`gm_com_raise_sgui` → hidden `monument_events.27` → `gm_com_raise`, the levels still missing, `gm_com_levels_to_go`, queued where `gm_com_pick_build_state` puts them, the picker the AI's `gm_com_ai_queue` shares through `gm_com_queue_levels`); greyed while any of our Grand Monuments `is_under_construction` (script can't count queued levels) or for 7 days after a press (`gm_com_raise_pending`). Where it would build is `gm_com_build_where`, written by `gm_country_refresh` (`gm_com_update_build_where`) and never read back there. The offer's third option, Seize It and Start Building, is players only and does the same through `.27`. The ceremony's first option, As the opportunity asks (`gm_state_ceremony_offers_opportunity`, `gm_state_dedicate_as_opportunity_asks`), is the default while offered, swapping the default with a copy of the leave-it-undedicated option (`.2.a`) by complementary triggers. Completion for a player is `monument_events.28`, which names the monument and the boon from `gm_com_seized_state` / `gm_com_seized_source` (`gm_com_source_is` lets the boon custom loc read either); a notice (`gm_com_reminder_notice`) comes at 12 months left. The panel's Where line, the under-construction line (`gm_disp_com_building`) and the Counts toward the opportunity mark on rows and the state card (`gm_state_disp_com_counts`). Countries of 1836 have a founding year only from `gm_seed_founding_years`.
- **Names (v2 §3).** Records on the state beside `gm_skin` (`gm_name_effects.txt` header), all cleared by `gm_clear_state`. Forms by skin are `gm_state_form_fits_<form>` (the plan's Task 7 table fixes the spec's §3.2 draft; the five civic-progress dedications have their building's form, faith skins their building's name). The unveiling: `gm_state_offer_skins` → (players, more than one skin) `.11`, else `gm_unveil_pending` for the next refresh (the unveiling reads the production method the dedication has just activated, which may not be visible in the same effect) → `gm_state_unveil` sets the default form and namesake (the commission's when `gm_state_answers_commission`) → (players) `.24` form, only when the skin offers more than one → `.25` namesake; each event's default keeps what is set. A fulfilled commission renames the monument that completed it unless it was unveiled during that commission (`gm_unveiled_for_com`). Names print through `gm_monument_name_row` (`State`) and `gm_monument_name_evt` (`SCOPE.sState('monument_state')`): customizable-localization targets inherit the caller's context, so each pattern exists once per context. An option name loses the event's saved scopes inside a target, so `.25`'s keep option splices the `_evt` pattern keys itself, one triggered name per branch of the family. Old monuments are named by the refresh (`gm_state_name_if_unnamed`). Rename (`gm_rename_sgui`) reruns `.24`/`.25` for an upheld monument.
- **Pictures, forms and styles (2026-10-11; spec `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-11-grand-monument-pictures-design.md`).** Every monument is a dedication, a skin (players see *style*) and a form. `gm_picture_code` (state variable) numbers its picture: `gm_state_update_picture` (`gm_picture_effects.txt`; the style-and-form table is `gm_picture_from_look`, which a trophy runs too) sets it at the end of `gm_state_set_default_form`, `gm_state_take_commission_name` and `gm_state_unveil`, in `gm_state_choose_form` and on every refresh; `gm_clear_state` removes it, and `gm_disp_picture_code` reads 1 (the draped picture) while it is unset. The `gm_picture` type (`grand_monuments_widget.gui`) holds one icon per code, 96 px in the row and 120 px on the state card. Codes are append-only (`PICTURES` in `test_grand_monument_registry.py`); a pair with no picture of its own (an old generic Tower or Memorial) shows its skin's default form. The five civic-progress buildings take the heritage styles in `BUILDING_SKINS` (axis `flag:building_<key>`, `gm_state_choose_building_skin`), which change only the look: `gm_skin_name` gives them their building's name. The art is the pipeline's `gm_picture` category (framed, `building_icons`' frame). Over the picture, a grandeur frame by step (spec §3.5): `gm_disp_frame_tier` (0-5, the live level on the 1/n curve's first five step ends, 5, 15, 30, 50 and 75) shows one of `gm_pictures/frames/frame_tier_<1-5>.dds`, which `scripts/image_pipeline/gen_gm_grandeur_frames.py` draws by recolouring the pictures' own frame band. `te_debug_monuments.4` steps the tallest monument through every picture. The ceremony (`.2`) shows every gated dedication greyed (`show_as_unavailable`); the style choice (`.11`) highlights each option's own condition, its `gm_skin_axis` test in `hidden_trigger`.
- **Typed names (v2 §3.5).** Name It adds `company_gm_name_carrier` and a company slot, the row's naming line (`gm_naming_line`) opens the company-rename popup from its `_show` state and a 1×1 watcher sends `gm_name_use_sgui` when the company's name changes; the name is stored as the flag `gm_name` and the row title prints it straight (`gm_row_title_named`). `gm_name_carrier_close` ends a naming; `gm_name_sweep` closes one abandoned for a year (game time runs while the box is open; the clock restarts as the naming line appears), and the country pulse keeps running while `gm_naming_active` even with no monument left. A state that changes hands drops `gm_being_named`. Every `Var('gm_name_carrier')` read sits in the naming line. Keep `building_gm_name_carrier_anchor` forever: saves list it.
- **Monument policy (v2 §5; reworked 2026-10-23, spec `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-23-gm-policy-prestige-design.md`).** `gm_policy` flag (`gm_policy_effects.txt`): `open`, `ceremonial`, `culture` (the default: `gm_policy_is = { P = culture STANDARD = yes }`) and `education`, each the best at one thing. Factors after the curve (`gm_policy_scale_steps` in `gm_compute_totals`): `gm_policy_factor_culture` (×1.5 on `gm_s_culture` and Antiquity's `gm_s_sig_antiquity` under Cultural Promotion with `cultural_hegemony_enabled`) and `gm_policy_factor_prestige` (×1.5 on `gm_s_standing` under Cultural Promotion with the rule off, since pull then feeds nothing); `gm_policy_factor_tourism` (state scope, ×1.5 under Open), through `gm_state_sig_local_steps_one`'s `FACTOR`, on the two signatures whose local effect is tourism. **To History counts at half under every policy** (policy spec § 4.5; `gm_policy_history_weight` 0.5, `gm_policy_history_cut` the half left out): `gm_g_historic` (`gm_sum_historic`: To History primaries, those beside another and trophies of one held) comes off `gm_sum_venues` at half and off Public Education's input (`gm_g_education`, `gm_sum_education`, which its bar and hover read); Cultural Promotion's steps take `gm_policy_factor_culture_standing` and `gm_policy_factor_prestige_standing`, the factor less half its gain on To History's share of standing grandeur; a state's monument tourism takes `gm_policy_factor_tourism_here`, Open's gain likewise on `gm_state_historic_grandeur`'s share of `gm_state_grandeur` (×1.25 for To History alone). Antiquity keeps `gm_policy_factor_culture` and the signatures `gm_policy_factor_tourism` whole: no To History monument carries a signature. State Ceremonial adds before the curve: `gm_g_ceremonial` = `gm_g_venues` (`gm_sum_venues`: every monument not contested, heritage and held trophies included; `gm_state_counts_venue`, `gm_mon_counts_venue`) × `gm_policy_ceremonial_share` (0.25), into `gm_g_regime_in` and `gm_g_leader_in`, which the legitimacy and authority curves and their bars read. Public Education: `gm_national_education` (`state_education_access_add`, `gm_step_education`) on `gm_s_education`, standing grandeur on the open 1/n curve with a first step of 10, 0 under any other policy. No policy changes upkeep (there is none), ageing, the dedications' local effects or anniversaries. 60-month cooldown after any change but the first. Older saves: `gm_policy_migrate`, first in `gm_country_refresh`, drops a Mothballed or Standard flag, keeping the wait. AI each January (`gm_policy_ai_choose`). Self-check `gm_education_reaches_states` (`gm_policy_education_self_check`); in-game checks in `docs/testing/grand-monuments-policy-playtest.md`.
- **Trophies (phase 5, 2026-10-12).** A monument, or part of one, carried off: from a state the taker occupies in a war (`gm_state_tr_occupied_by`: at war with the owner, not its civil-war twin, and controlling half the state's provinces, read from `any_province = { percent >= 0.5 controller = X }` because what a state's own `controller` link returns is unread), from the taker's own unincorporated state holding a monument it did not raise (`gm_built_by`, written at first sight and by the ceremony), or by the treaty article `surrender_monument` (enforceable, so a war goal), which a draft lists only for a country with a monument it could give up (`gm_tr_country_has_takeable` in its `visible` and `possible`, owner 2026-10-23). The share is by form (`TROPHY_SHARES` in `test_grand_monument_trophies.py`): objects whole, pieces of structures 25%, tokens 10%, never a Grand Shrine; a piece is taken by the gift's rebuild run backwards (`gm_state_tr_remove_piece`, records kept, `gm_tr_cooldown` ten years), a whole monument's building goes and its records stay a month (`gm_carried_off`) so the notices can name it. A trophy is a parentless script container (`gm_trophy`, global list `gm_trophies`) with the monument's records and name (`gm_tr_*`, named by the container custom loc `gm_trophy_name` / `gm_trophy_title`); its holder is its site's owner and its claimant its origin's owner, read live. It counts for half its grandeur, levels and age (`gm_tr_grandeur`, written when it is made: a trophy does not age abroad), in `gm_sum_standing` and in the Armed Forces' total (`gm_tr_ig_share_<ig>`). The monthly pass (`gm_trophy_monthly`, `on_monthly_pulse`) repairs vanished states from their regions, runs the AI (brings home what it owns unless it carried it off itself, `gm_tr_taken_by` / `gm_tr_held_by_its_taker`, which stops an own-colony take from coming straight back; returns to allies and bloc partners; loots trophies on display) and rebuilds each country's `gm_trophies_held` / `gm_trophies_abroad` and each state's `gm_trophies_here` lists. The AI loots occupied monuments from each monument's state pulse (`gm_state_tr_monthly`, odds `gm_tr_ai_loot_chance`: law stances on Total War, Ethnostate and National Supremacy, unrecognized, tall; ×0.25 under UNESCO); a player occupier gets `monument_trophy_events.1` once per occupation. Consequences: infamy (`gm_tr_infamy`), relations −30, the victim's war support +10, radicals in an own state. Home again (`gm_tr_return_home`): a piece of the standing monument (same landmark, or neither names one) or of a secondary's landmark rejoins it through the rebuild (`gm_state_tr_receive` → `gm_state_tr_add_levels`); any other trophy with a monument standing becomes a secondary monument (§ Several monuments in one state); with none standing it is rebuilt with the trophy's records (`gm_state_tr_rebuild_from_moving`), `gm_seen` and `gm_ceremony_level` set and the dedication put back through `gm_restore_pm`; The Homecoming (`gm_boon_homecoming`, +5 legitimacy, 120 months, ticked by `gm_tick_boon`), never for the trophy's own taker. Ways home: Return It / Bring It Home (`gm_tr_return_sgui`), occupying the site (`gm_tr_take_site_sgui`), and the article `return_cultural_property`, listed only where the holder has one of the other side's trophies (its `visible` repeats `possible`, owner 2026-10-23). No taking or return runs where a tooltip walks the effect: clicks, the offer and the articles only order (`gm_state_tr_order_take`, `gm_tr_order_take_site`, `gm_tr_order_return`) and hidden events `monument_trophy_events.10`–`.13` do the work. Panels: the journal entry's Trophies and Held Abroad sections, Carry It Off on the monument row and state card, and the state view's Trophies on Display card (`gui/gm_trophy_widgets.gui`), which has three views chosen by buttons in its header and held in the client-side `gm_state_tr_view` (unset is Full; `short` is a line per trophy with the rest on hover; `collapsed` is the summary line alone, "N trophies, worth G grandeur to <holder>", read from `gm_state_tr_disp_here` and `gm_state_tr_disp_here_grandeur`, the sum of the trophies' `gm_tr_grandeur` that the monthly pass writes beside the count as `gm_tr_here_grandeur`); a trophy from a landmark shows its "Historical monument" line, its line of history on hover (`gm_tr_landmark_desc`). Every trophy row shows the picture of the monument it was taken from, a piece's too (2026-10-13): `gm_tr_update_picture` lends the trophy's `gm_tr_skin` / `gm_tr_form` / `gm_tr_landmark` under the state's names, runs the monuments' table (`gm_picture_from_look`, then `gm_state_picture_landmarks`) and stores `gm_tr_picture_code`, when the trophy is made or seeded and from the monthly pass; the `gm_tr_picture` type is `gm_picture`'s icons read through `gm_tr_disp_picture_code`, 96 px, no grandeur frame. A landmark's trophy also has a picture of its own, what was carried off on display in a museum room (2026-10-16): `gm_tr_picture_trophies` sets `gm_tr_trophy_picture_code` (2,000,000 + the `LANDMARKS` row, `TROPHY_PICTURES` in the registry test; 0 for none) at the end of `gm_tr_update_picture`, and the trophy rows' `gm_tr_trophy_picture` draws it over the monument's picture (a secondary monument's row doesn't). Debug: `te_debug_monuments.6`. **The trophies of 1836** (`gm_seed_trophies`, after the landmarks in `gm_landmarks_on_game_started_after_lobby`; debug `te_debug_monuments.5` option c): the Parthenon's marbles, the Rosetta Stone and Tipu's Tiger in London, the Kandyan throne at Windsor, the Dendera Zodiac, the Luxor Obelisk and the Venus de Milo in Paris, Baba Merzoug at Brest, the Piraeus Lion and the Horses of Saint Mark in Venice. `gm_seed_trophy` makes each as a taking does, with no consequences, and places nothing (logging `TE_MONUMENTS:`) when an owner proves wrong, one country owns origin and site, or the landmark's trophy already exists.
- **Several monuments in one state (2026-10-13; spec `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-13-multiple-monuments-per-state-design.md`, plan `docs/superpowers/archive/plans/2026-10-13-multiple-monuments-per-state.md`).** The engine allows one `building_grand_monument` a state: it stands at level 1 (§ Construction sites) and runs the **primary** monument's dedication; every other monument is a **secondary**. The primary stays on the state's own variables (`gm_skin`, `gm_form`, `gm_name`, ...: ~25 writers). A secondary is a parentless script container tagged `gm_monument`, in the global `gm_monuments`, which keeps a trophy's `gm_tr_*` records (so the trophy names, forms, parts and pictures serve it), with `gm_tr_levels` / `gm_tr_start_grandeur` its size and `gm_tr_origin` its state. The monthly pass (`gm_monument_monthly`) repairs a vanished state from its region and rebuilds each state's `gm_monuments_here`, each owner's `gm_monuments_held` and the counts, so a civil war's winner has its rows back; a return, a taking and a promotion keep the lists current at once. A secondary carries its own dedication's effects and contests (§ Ageing below); it counts in standing grandeur unless it is itself contested. **Returns** (`gm_tr_return_home`): a piece of the standing landmark rejoins it; any other trophy with a monument standing (or a building raised there today, `gm_tr_stands_apart`) is the *same container*, retagged `gm_monument` and moved from `gm_trophies` to `gm_monuments` (`gm_tr_become_monument`). **Taking** one (`gm_mon_take_sgui` → `gm_mon_tr_order_take` names it in the state's `gm_tr_take_target`; `monument_trophy_events.10` checks `gm_state_tr_takeable_secondary`; occupation only): by its form's share, whole it becomes the trophy again (`gm_mon_tr_take_whole`), otherwise a piece is a new trophy with its share of the records (`gm_mon_tr_take_piece`). The AI's one roll falls on one monument, each as likely (`gm_state_tr_ai_choose_target`). **The primary goes** (Tear Down, taken whole, or the building lost): the largest secondary rises into the building that stays (`gm_state_promote_secondary`, under a click marker; the pass promotes a state left with no building, and the building is made at level 1).
