Panels: the state view's monument card lists the others in a section of its own, full width under the picture and details (`te_state_gm_beside`), and Our Monuments has a second list. A landmark seeded in a state another already stands in is stood beside it (`gm_seed_landmark_beside`, `beside=True` in `LANDMARKS`; no row uses it yet). `gm_monument_self_check` logs `TE_SELF_CHECK` once a game for the one unverified engine fact (a cross-scope flag comparison); fallbacks and the in-game checks are in `docs/testing/grand-monuments-multiple-playtest.md`. The occupier's AI roll asks `gm_state_tr_any_takeable` (the primary, or a secondary beside a shrine); the player's offer event stays the primary's.
- **Ageing and monuments beside (2026-10-16; spec `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-16-grand-monument-ageing-design.md`; size from records since 2026-10-18).** **Values:** `gm_state_primary_levels` (`gm_levels`, else what the building holds for an older save's monument, `gm_state_built_levels`), `gm_state_primary_start` / `gm_mon_start` (starting grandeur, the levels when unrecorded), `gm_state_primary_age` (`gm_age`) and `gm_mon_age` (`gm_tr_age`); grandeur is starting grandeur + age (`gm_state_primary_grandeur`, `gm_mon_grandeur`; `gm_state_grandeur` is the whole state's). Trophy shares, Rededicate's cost and upkeep read levels; effects, sums, displays and frames read grandeur. **Ageing:** each month a dedicated, recorded monument that is not contested (`gm_state_ages`, `gm_mon_ages`; heritage ages) adds starting grandeur × 2 ÷ 1200 to its age (`gm_state_age_step`, `gm_mon_age_step`), the primary in `gm_state_monthly` before its steps, secondaries in `gm_monument_monthly`; trophies abroad never age. It stops at a century's worth (owner, 2026-10-19): each step is clamped to `gm_state_age_room` / `gm_mon_age_room`, twice the starting grandeur (`gm_age_cap_years` = 100 × 2%) less the age already there, so a monument stands at three times what it was dedicated with; anniversary and opportunity gifts (`gm_*_add_age` with their own amounts) are not clamped and may carry it past. A taking carries the levels' share of the starting grandeur and age (`gm_state_tr_start`, `gm_state_tr_age`, `gm_mon_tr_*`), a return brings them back, Rededicate halves them. A trophy counts abroad for half its grandeur. **A dedicated site beside a finished monument:** the answer demotes the primary into a `gm_monument` container (`gm_state_demote_primary`, every record in `CONTAINER_RECORDS`), marks the newcomer `gm_newcomer`, and once it is dedicated and named (`gm_state_newcomer_settled`) `.29` swaps the grandest secondary back in if it is grander (`gm_state_settle_newcomer` → `gm_state_swap_primary`: demote + `gm_state_raise_secondary`, its dedication back through `gm_restore_pm`). **Secondaries are whole monuments:** container twins of the fit, kind and IG-stance triggers (`gm_mon_message_fits`, `gm_mon_status_fits`, `gm_mon_approved_by_<ig>`, ...), `gm_mon_first_sight` for one with no raiser; the national sums, IG nets and counts walk `gm_monuments_held`; each dedication's local effect counts that dedication's grandeur in the state (`gm_state_local_steps_one`, `gm_local_steps_<key>`). Contests: `gm_mon_check_contest`, `gm_mon_changed_hands`; Pull Down and Rededicate order the work (`gm_mon_order_choice`) for the hidden `monument_events.30` (`gm_state_run_mon_orders`: every Pull Down at once, then one Rededicate by swap); Keep as Heritage runs at once (`gm_mon_preserve`); the sguis are `gm_mon_tear_down_sgui` / `_rededicate_sgui` / `_preserve_sgui`. **Opportunities** count the fitting dedication's starting grandeur (`gm_com_fit_grandeur`, `gm_mon_com_counts`), never age; the gift adds `gm_com_gift` to the completing monument's age. **Anniversaries** are held by every monument of grandeur 3+, those beside another too (`gm_country_holds_anniversary`; `gm_ann_pick` saves `monument_state` and, for one beside another, `monument_mon`; .12–.15 have a `_beside` text), and each one's option a adds a tenth of the monument's starting grandeur, at least 1, to its age (`gm_ann_add_age`). In-game checks: `docs/testing/grand-monuments-ageing-playtest.md`.
- **Dedicate (owner, 2026-10-18).** No ceremony asks by itself for a player's monument: it stands as a construction site as long as its owner likes (to pause, or to build a huge one over decades), and its Dedicate button (`gm_dedicate_sgui`, scope country, saved scope `gm_state`; `gm_dedicate_button` on the site's card, `te_state_gm_site_card`, and under the tab's Awaiting Dedication, `te_gm_sec_awaiting`, each row a `gm_site_row`) opens the ceremony, greyed while any of the site's levels are under construction, before its first level, while a ceremony asks, while a method is put back, or while the monument standing here is unveiled or named. The answer finishes the monument at the site's levels (§ Construction sites); more building is a new site. The AI has no button: its site's ceremony opens once nothing more is queued (`gm_state_ai_dedicates_now`) and it never picks *Let it stand as it is, for now*. Visibility comes from the state's own value and owner (`gm_state_disp_awaiting`), not `is_shown`: whether a saved scope reaches `is_shown` is thinly evidenced (gui gotcha #22).
- **A merged state keeps its monument (issue #936; records only since 2026-10-18, sites spec §3.7).** A state is a (region, owner) pair, and when one country comes to hold two parts of a region the engine merges them; the absorbed part's variables, where a primary's records live, are lost. Each month `gm_shadow_monthly` (from `gm_monument_monthly`) keeps a **shadow** of every recorded, dedicated primary: a `gm_shadow` container in the global `gm_shadows`, linked from the state (`gm_shadow`) and back (`gm_tr_origin`, `gm_tr_origin_region`), with the records a demotion copies (`CONTAINER_RECORDS`, mirrored set-or-remove by `gm_sh_mirror`), `gm_tr_levels` (its `gm_levels`) and its owner (`gm_sh_owner`). It is written only there and after a raise, and dropped at once wherever a state forgets its primary (`gm_clear_state`) or loses it whole (`gm_state_tr_remove_whole`). A shadow whose state is gone is an orphan (`gm_sh_is_orphan`); the pass hands its region to the hidden `monument_events.31`, and `.1`, `.29` and `gm_state_changed_hands` adopt first wherever `gm_state_merge_pending` holds (a finished building no record describes, or one above level 1, with an orphan in its region, `gm_state_orphan_in_region`). `gm_state_adopt_orphans` waits a day while a building in the region was made or removed today, repairs the orphaned monuments that stood beside first (`gm_mon_repair_origin`: the part with a recorded monument), then each orphan, landmarks first (`gm_sh_settle_one`), settles into the part of its region its last owner holds: onto a finished building no record describes (`gm_state_raise_orphan`), beside the monument there (`gm_sh_adopt_beside`), or raised into a new level-1 building where none stands; failing an owner's part, beside the most populous recorded part; else it is lost (`gm_sh_lost`, `TE_MONUMENTS:`). A finished building left above level 1 goes back to 1 on its recorded dedication (`gm_state_reset_building_level`; not before `.32` has migrated it). `TE_SELF_CHECK monument_merge_kept` reads once a game whether the first orphan was kept, and `monument_merge_level1` whether the reset building stands at 1 on its dedication. **A revolt keeps the monument whole (owner, 2026-10-18):** a finished building nothing records, from no older save (`gm_premigration`) and made by no script (`gm_migrated`), with no orphan in its region, is the engine's copy in a revolt's part of the state: `gm_state_stray_building`, removed by `.29`. The split-piece machinery of 2026-10-17 and the one-off repair (#936) are gone. In-game checks in `docs/testing/grand-monuments-ageing-playtest.md`.
- **Archaeology: buried sites (2026-10-14; spec `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-14-grand-monument-archaeology-design.md`, issue #939; MVP).** 50 monuments that lie buried until a country digs them (36 To the Nation, 14 To History since tourism heritage phase 3). A site is a `LANDMARKS` row with `buried=True` (rows 52–86: never seeded at the start, no owner of its own, a level of its own) and a parentless script container tagged `gm_site` in the global `gm_arch_sites`, made once and lazily by the monthly pass (`gm_arch_monthly`, `gm_archaeology_effects.txt`). It holds the monument it will be under a trophy's `gm_tr_*` records, so `gm_tr_landmark_name`, `_desc` and `gm_tr_part_name` name it with no new branch, and `gm_site_tech` / `_vector` / `_status` (1 buried, 2 known, 3 being dug, 4 unearthed) / `_sponsor` / `_method` / `_progress`. The ground is a state *region*, so a merge of split states (#936) cannot lose it. **Opening** needs the technology of the site held by a country that owns a part of the region (`gm_arch_has_gate_for`, read from the site's side with the country as its argument, one branch per technology in `gm_archaeology_gate_triggers.txt`): a `survey` site is open at once, an `incidental` one when a 1% monthly chance turns it up (`gm_arch_try_find`). A player who may dig a site is told once (`gm_arch_tell_found`, `gm_site_told` on the container): `arch_events.1`, *The Scholars Know Where to Look* for a survey site, *Something Under the Spade* for a chance find. Both it and the finished dig's `arch_events.2` (own, ruined, abroad, or the host's copy; `arch_events.3` merged in) name the place, the state, the find and a historical note from four loc lines per site (`gm_arch_site_<key>_place` / `_found` / `_dug` / `_history`), picked race-free by a saved scope named for the site (`gm_arch_ev_mark`, `scope:gm_arch_ev_<key>`, which is also the state the text names); `gm_arch_last` is gone. **The dig** runs in three methods (`gm_site_method`: Antiquarian at 4%, Systematic 2.5%, Forensic 3.5% a month, each needing Romanticism, Empiricism, Computer Networks); no slot cap. Its brake is one static modifier on `je:je_grand_monuments`, multiplied by the country's summed units (`gm_arch_pass`: `gm_arch_innovation_units`; `gm_arch_add_national` in `gm_apply_national_modifiers`): `gm_arch_diversion` (`country_weekly_innovation_add` only; the innovation *cap* is never touched, owner 2026-10-14). The MVP's `gm_arch_expense` (`country_expenses_add`, the Archaeological Digs row of the Budget Breakdown) is a retired stub since 2026-10-16: nothing adds it, and `gm_arch_remove_national` strips it from older saves. **Rework (2026-10-16, spec `2026-10-16-grand-monument-archaeology-rework-design.md`):** innovation is the only cost, never money (owner, 2026-10-16: the country pays for its innovation through its universities): 5 / 20 / 100 weekly innovation a dig by method (`gm_arch_innovation_<method>`; `gm_arch_site_innovation` for the row), and a player may launch one only while `country_innovation` is at least that (`gm_arch_spares_<method>`: the buttons, the find event's options, `arch_events.10`'s re-check); a site's months scale with `(levels + 5) / 15` (`gm_arch_size_factor`, `gm_arch_site_rate_<method>`), so 17–34, 27–54 and 20–39 months; the AI digs the grandest site waiting by the best method whose innovation it makes four times over (`country_innovation` against `gm_arch_ai_floor_<method>`, `gm_arch_ai_affords_<method>`, `gm_arch_start_affordable`). A sponsor that loses the ground suspends the dig with its progress kept (`gm_arch_suspend`). **Finishing** runs after the walk over the list (`gm_arch_done`, a temporary list: a container is not taken off the list it is walked in): `gm_arch_settle_levels` (Forensic +2; Antiquarian 35% to halve it, at least 3), then `gm_arch_place`, which sets the trophy's return records on the container and either builds the state's monument from them (`gm_state_tr_receive`, the container destroyed) or, with a monument standing, retags the same container `gm_monument` beside it (`gm_arch_stand_beside`, the lists of `gm_seed_landmark_beside`). Every order only marks the work and a hidden event does it (`gm_arch_order_launch` / `_suspend` → `arch_events.10` / `.11`, the trophies' shape). Panel: Archaeological Expeditions (`gui/gm_archaeology_widgets.gui`, after the Opportunity section; `gm_arch_closed`), rows from the country's `gm_arch_digging` and `gm_arch_available` lists, and `gm_arch_ai_decide` for the AI (8% a month, two digs at most, the best method it has). The journal entry's conditions and `gm_ledgers_idle` count a dig or an open site (`gm_arch_country_has_any`). **Pompeii** (row 87, rework § 5) is seeded already under way: `VECTOR = excavating` makes `gm_arch_seed_dig` start an Antiquarian dig by Campania's owner at 30% (`gm_arch_excavating_progress`); a game seeded before it gets it from the next monthly pass (`gm_arch_seed_round` against `gm_arch_seed_rounds`, raised with each row added later). **Foreign digs** (rework § 3): two directed state-input articles, `archaeological_concession` (sponsor needs Romanticism, 75 influence, enforceable; partage: half the levels to the sponsor's capital as a `gm_trophy` piece made from the site's records, `gm_arch_partage`, the rest standing in the host's state; a rock-cut site stays whole) and `excavation_permit` (Empiricism, 40 influence, friendly; the finds stay). Either way a sponsor left without a trophy gains `gm_arch_scholarship` (+10 prestige, +1 cultural pull, ten years). A draft lists either article only where the host has a site open to the sponsor (`gm_arch_country_offers_site` in `visible`, as in `possible`; owner 2026-10-23). The right is read live from the treaty (`gm_arch_state_conceded_to`, `gm_arch_may_dig_ground`; `LIVE` in `test_state_treaty_article_sync.py`); the dig state is the sponsor's own part first, then a conceded one (`gm_arch_save_dig_state`, `gm_site_terms`); `arch_events.12` refreshes the sponsor a day after a grant. **Deferred:** the political brakes and most speculative breakthroughs (the antiquity and archive dedications shipped as signatures, below). Debug: `te_debug_monuments.7`; in-game checks in `docs/testing/grand-monuments-archaeology-playtest.md`.
- **Unique dedications: signatures (2026-10-16; spec `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-16-grand-monument-signatures-design.md`).** A signature is a parent dedication plus two records, `gm_signature` / `gm_sig_parent` on a state and `gm_tr_signature` / `gm_tr_sig_parent` on a container (both pairs in `CONTAINER_RECORDS`, so every copy point carries them). The parent does everything (PM, fit, kind, contests, IG stances, opportunity progress); the signature adds a name and effects, and counts only on its parent (`gm_state_sig_on_parent`, `gm_mon_sig_on_parent`): nationally when upheld (`gm_state_sig_counts`), locally whatever the status, never on another dedication (dormant). Families (Antiquity, Archive, Throne, Royal Pantheon, Martial Glory, Liberty, Heroes) cover most landmarks; four one-offs count as their family too (`gm_sig_counts_as_<family>`). **Sums:** `gm_sig_compute_sums` (from `gm_compute_totals`, after the policy scaling) zeroes each `gm_g_sig_<key>`, walks the states once, `gm_monuments_held` once and `gm_trophies_held` once (a trophy at `gm_tr_grandeur` for its holder, whatever its government), then `gm_set_steps` F = 5 and `gm_policy_factor_standing`; each national static modifier (`gm_national_sig_<key>`, one step) goes on the JE with `gm_s_sig_<key>`; Antiquity's cultural pull is the script value `cultural_pull_from_antiquity`, on the 1/n curve with no ceiling (`gm_sig_set_steps_lin_open`; its +3 cap went 2026-10-19, owner: its monuments are a fixed list). Local ones (`gm_local_sig_<key>`) come from `gm_state_monthly` (`gm_state_sig_local_steps_one`) and show on the state card, so they are hidden from the panel's modifier rows. IG: `gm_state_sig_approved_by_<ig>` / `gm_mon_sig_approved_by_<ig>` in `gm_compute_ig` (only the Intelligentsia has a real branch). **Backfill:** `gm_sig_from_landmark` maps a landmark key to its signature and parent; it runs at seeding and from every refresh/monthly walk (`gm_state_sig_backfill`, `gm_tr_sig_backfill`), so old saves pick signatures up in a month. **Specials (§5):** `gm_com_fulfil` saves the granter, reads the source's special (`gm_sig_special_for_source`) and marks the completing monument with `gm_sig_grant` (a primary, written by `monument_events.26` through `gm_state_sig_take_grant`) or writes a secondary's records at once (`gm_mon_sig_take_special`); a monument that already carries one, or no monument, makes the country hold it (`gm_sig_held_<special>`, a count, variable so a civil war's winner keeps it). The ceremony offers a held special (`monument_events.2`, hidden options gated by `gm_state_ceremony_offers_special`, base AI weight 1000); `monument_events.28` names the grant or the hold (`gm_com_seized_special(_held)`); old saves get one held special per boon still running (`gm_sig_seed_monthly`, `gm_sig_seed_round` against `gm_sig_seed_rounds`). **Historical opportunities (§6):** source `historical`, `gm_com_track_historical` at the end of the world pass tries each row (`gm_com_try_historical`: once a game by a global flag, a forty-year window, `has_state_in_state_region`, a holder condition `gm_com_hist_cond_<cond>` re-checked by `gm_com_has_lapsed`, target the landmark's levels, `gm_com_time_months` × target ÷ 5); no boon; completion marks `gm_hist_become` and the completing monument becomes the landmark (`gm_state_become_landmark` / `gm_mon_become_landmark`: skin, form, namesake, picture, signature). Rows: `SIGNATURES` and `HISTORICAL_OPPORTUNITIES` in `test_grand_monument_registry.py`; **add a signature** with a `SIGNATURES` row, and its failures are the checklist. Debug: `te_debug_monuments.8`; in-game checks in `docs/testing/grand-monuments-signatures-playtest.md`.
- **Debug:** `event te_debug_monuments.1`; `event te_debug_monuments.2` (offer each opportunity's moment, complete (with the gift and boon) / run out / lapse the open one); `TE_MONUMENTS:` lines each month for players.

## Temporary Amendments (Sunset Clauses)

Three amendments can be attached **temporarily** (`add_amendment = { … timeout = <months> }`) as enactment concessions. The engine removes them when the timeout (counted from law activation) elapses and fires `on_amendment_timeout`, which `common/on_actions/amendment_on_actions.txt` routes to a follow-up event offering to make the clause permanent (re-add without `timeout`; `te_legitimacy_drain` + radicals) or let it lapse (Industrialist disapproval + a few capitalist radicals). Engine semantics and authoring rules: `docs/guides/scripting_best_practices.md` § Temporary amendments.

| Amendment | Delivery (DEBATE checkpoint) | cooldown / timeout (months) | Expiry event |
|-----------|------------------------------|-----------------------------|--------------|
| `amendment_env_grandfather_clause` (new; +5% pollution, +5% emissions, +2 Industrialist approval on `law_ministry_of_the_environment`; cancels one institution level) | `ministry_law_events.58` option a | 48 / 120 | `ministry_law_events.59` |
| `amendment_national_champion_exemption` | `extra_law_events.29` option e (option a remains the permanent variant) | 48 / 120 | `extra_law_events.85` |
| `amendment_corporate_data_exemption` | `extra_law_events.31` option e (option a remains the permanent variant) | 12 / 36 | `extra_law_events.86` |

The `has_amendment` guards on events 29/31/58 make the permanent and temporary variants mutually exclusive within one enactment. The expiry events re-derive `sunset_law` from `active_law:<lawgroup>` and `industrialists_ig` in `immediate`, and are not in any checkpoint pool. Deferred from issue #278: a financial-regulation phase-in (the three laws' penalties are structurally different — numeric, none, boolean lock) and a wartime rules-of-war clause (no per-country war-start on-action; would need a timeout on an already-active law).

## Amendment Petitions (`amendment_petition_events`)

Rare events in which an interest group asks for one of the mod's amendments on a law **already in force**, because the country's situation gives it a case. The enactment events (`extra_law_events.28`–`.34`, `.87`–`.90`, `te_fptp_events.2`, `inheritance_events.10`–`.13`, `te_judiciary_events.20`–`.22`, `ministry_law_events.58`) offer amendments only while a law is debated; these reach a law years after it passed. One event per amendment, two options: attach it (option a) or decline (option b, the default).

- **Files**: `events/amendment_petition_events.txt`, `common/scripted_triggers/amendment_petition_triggers.txt` (every `te_ap_*` trigger), `common/on_actions/amendment_petition_on_actions.txt`, loc in `te_events_l_english.yml`.
- **Frequency**: each event rolls on its own, from a named sub-action of `on_yearly_pulse_country` (`te_amendment_petition_<amendment>`) whose `random_events` pairs a no-event weight (`N = 0`, the `cultural_hegemony_events_on_actions.txt` idiom) with the event, the two summing to 1000. The event's weight is its yearly chance in tenths of a percent while the country qualifies (the Chance column below), and a country that doesn't qualify sees nothing however the engine treats a failing event. The chance follows how long the situation lasts: lasting ones (a multicultural population, a dominant governing group) roll every year they hold, so they roll low; a war or an election campaign rolls high. Every event's trigger also asks `te_ap_window_open`: each petition sets the country variable `te_ap_recent_petition` for five years in its `immediate`, whatever the answer, so a country sees at most one petition every five years. Each event also has its own 20-year cooldown (`very_long_modifier_time`), so a declined petition doesn't come back soon.
- **Law qualification**: `te_ap_law_ok_<amendment>` holds when a law the amendment allows is in force (the amendment's `allowed_laws`, restated; keep the two in step), the law doesn't carry the amendment yet, and no law of its group is being enacted (`te_ap_enacting_in_<group>` lists every law in the group, variants included; a law added to one of these groups belongs in its list). It is also each event's `cancellation_trigger`. The trigger restates the amendment's `possible` too, because `add_amendment` silently does nothing when `possible` fails.
- **Attachment**: `scope:petition_law` (saved from `active_law:<group>`) gets `add_amendment = { type sponsor = scope:petition_sponsor_ig cooldown = 60 }`: permanent, unrepealable for five years. No timeout: a timeout on an active law is unverified (§ Temporary Amendments).
- **Reactions**: option a gives the sponsor `ig_approval_positive_modifier` and the group that opposes the amendment `ig_approval_negative_modifier` (five years, decaying), plus radicals among the pops it hurts; option b gives the sponsor `ig_approval_negative_modifier` and radicals among its supporters or the pops it would have helped. AI weights favour accepting when the sponsor is in government or powerful, and declining when the opposing group is in government.

Option a's tooltip (`amendment_petition_events.10.a.tt`) says so.

- **Adding a petition** for a new amendment: a `te_ap_law_ok_<amendment>` trigger (and a `te_ap_enacting_in_<group>` list if the group is new), an event of the same shape, its own `te_amendment_petition_<amendment>` sub-action with a chance (`amendment_petition_on_actions.txt`), loc, the picture's `events` entry in `scripts/image_pipeline/event_image_prompts.py`, a row above and in the player guide's petition list (`docs/player_guide/20-appendix-reference-lists.md`).

## First Past the Post (`amendment_first_past_the_post`)

An amendment on the voting laws that squeezes party politics into two parties. It replaces vanilla's culture-hardcoded American two-party system (`usa_two_party_system`: −10 to five parties for any North American Yankee or Dixie country under Presidential Republic, +3 to the Liberals). Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-25-first-past-the-post-design.md`.

- **Files**: `common/amendments/te_first_past_the_post.txt`; `common/scripted_effects/te_fptp_effects.txt` (ranking, seed, `te_fptp_var`, self-check); `common/scripted_triggers/te_fptp_triggers.txt`; `common/script_values/te_fptp_values.txt` (the two join-weight sizes); `common/on_actions/te_fptp_on_actions.txt`; `events/te_fptp_events.txt`; the generated `common/parties/zz_te_party_join_weights.txt` (`scripts/generators/gen_party_join_weights.py`) and the mod's three party files; `amendment_petition_events.28`; the USA in `common/history/extra_history.txt`.
- **Amendment**: allowed on Landed, Wealth and Census Voting, Universal Suffrage and Anarchy (not Oligarchy, which grants no voting power). `country_legitimacy_ideological_incoherence_mult = -0.25` (the strongest vanilla law reduction) and `country_legitimacy_base_add = -5`. No parent law; `would_sponsor` is membership of one of the two largest parties (`te_fptp_major_member`) once those parties' groups hold 60%+ of the clout (`te_fptp_major_clout`), as the petition asks. Repealable at `legitimacy_to_repeal_amendment`; the AI never repeals it.
- **Join weights**: every party's `join_weight` gives one of the two largest parties `te_fptp_major_party_join_weight` (+5) and any other party `te_fptp_minor_party_join_weight` (−20), while the amendment is in force and two parties are marked. The bonus sits ahead of vanilla's party-size chain (×2 with at most one prior member for a group that isn't powerful, ×0.5 with two, ×0 with three or more; the mod's three parties have ×0.05 at three), so a party still fills up at three groups and a group's fit still picks its major; the penalty comes after every multiplier. So two major parties hold at most six groups between them, and a group that fits neither strongly stays out of parties. An `INJECT` into `join_weight` replaces vanilla's field, so the generator restates each vanilla party's whole block from the game files (dropping `usa_two_party_system`) — rerun it after a vanilla patch (`--check`). The revolutionary party is never ranked or injected.
- **Ranking**: `te_fptp_refresh_major_parties` on the monthly pulse of every country with a voting franchise (one that loses it drops its marks) orders the active parties by `te_fptp_party_clout` (the members' `ig_clout`) and marks the top two: `te_fptp_major_<party type>` on the country (`te_fptp_mark_major_party`, one branch per type; `te_fptp_party_is_major` reads them), `te_fptp_two_majors`, and `te_fptp_major_member` on each member group. Not inside `join_weight`, because all groups re-pick their parties together at a campaign's start. With fewer than two parties nothing is marked and the terms stay off. A new party type needs a line in the mark, clear and `te_fptp_party_is_major` lists and the two terms in its `join_weight` (`test_first_past_the_post.py` checks).
- **`te_fptp_var`** (country): the country holds first past the post. `te_fptp_track_held` sets it while the amendment is in force and removes it when the country sits on an allowed voting law without it (a repeal, a declined `.1`); on a law without elections it stays.
- **Ways in**: the USA's 1836 history (with the Democrats and Whigs pre-marked as its two majors, for the parties formed at game start); `te_fptp_seed`, once per country on its first pulse, for any country `te_fptp_seed_eligible` (vanilla's culture-term conditions plus an allowed voting law: the Confederacy, Texas, the USA in an older save), never for a revolution's rebels; `te_fptp_events.2` "The Winner Takes All" in `on_law_checkpoint_debate` while an allowed voting law is enacted in a country whose two largest parties hold 60%+ of the clout and no `te_fptp_var`; petition `.28`.
- **Changing the voting law**: amendments leave with their law, so `te_fptp_from_law_scope` (`on_law_activated`) fires `te_fptp_events.1` "Counting the Votes" when an allowed voting law arrives in a country with `te_fptp_var` and no amendment. Option a re-attaches it (default); option b adopts proportional representation and removes `te_fptp_var`. Sponsor: the strongest group in a major party; the strongest group outside them takes the other side's approval change.
- **Civil wars**: a revolution's winner continues the nation. The seed skips revolutionaries (`is_revolutionary`), so the winner inherits the nation's `te_fptp_seed_checked` and can't be handed back a repealed amendment; secessionists are seeded as new nations. `te_fptp_repair_after_civil_war` (in `te_civil_war_on_won`) fires `te_fptp_events.1` when the winner holds `te_fptp_var` (the merge hands it over) on an allowed voting law without the amendment, as a change of voting law does: the rebels hold the law they fought for from the outbreak, so no `on_law_activated` fires at the end.
- **Self-check**: `TE_SELF_CHECK OK|BROKEN fptp_major_parties`, once a game, the first time a country with three or more parties is ranked (two marked, no unmarked party larger than either marked one, compared pairwise, with a positive control that must be 1 or more so a comparison that didn't read can't pass; the second's clout above 0). Fallback for BROKEN: order by `momentum`. Play-test rows: `docs/testing/first-past-the-post-playtest.md`.

## Legislated Tax Code (`je_tax_code`, `te_tax_code_rule`)

**Experimental, default off.** Under the rule the five vanilla taxation laws cannot be enacted; every country holds the carrier `law_te_tax_code`, whose generated amendments set each rate, and taxes change only through a bill that interest groups must commit to, taking effect on the 1st of its month. The customs option legislates a market owner's tariffs too. AI countries legislate through the same commands (package 6, the schema's "AI legislation"): a staggered monthly step raises taxes on a fiscal-deficit streak, cuts them on a surplus streak, passes emergency bills, bargains with the same offers and keeps or renegotiates its promises; their tariffs stay native until the customs probe (P09b/P09c) decides the mechanism. The UI is the journal entry and the Budget panel's Tax Code tab.

The fourth setting, *Light Tax Code* (`te_tax_code_light`, gated by `te_tax_code_light_on`), keeps the vanilla taxation laws: each law caps every tax it levies at its very-high rate and every levied tax may be cut to nothing, and the player moves each rate a step at a time from the tab, at once, with no bills. The native tax level is the highest step any tax sits on (the tax-level buttons are greyed) and every tax below it carries a relief static modifier, so the country collects the code's rates; the taxed goods and tariffs stay native. Interest groups react to each change (the support model's material and ideology reasons for the step; a pleasing reaction counts half; ±10, fading 30% a month) and the view bands reward relief instead of judging a resembled law, since the engine already gives the enacted law's stance. AI countries keep choosing their tax level and their code follows it. Schema and sync: [`tax_code_schema.md`](tax_code_schema.md), "Light code"; design: `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-09-tax-code-light-design.md`.

- **Design of record**: [`tax_code_schema.md`](tax_code_schema.md): tokens and sentinels, the one collection writer, the scheduler, migration, civil wars, drift, the bill lifecycle and support model, offers, obligations, the economy snapshot and fiscal record, the panels and customs. Read it before touching any `te_tax_*` variable.
- **Engine capabilities and play-tests**: [`../testing/tax-code-capability-ledger.md`](../testing/tax-code-capability-ledger.md): what is verified in game and what is only read statically (row 29 lists the unproven engine forms the panels rely on), the items recorded for later, the evidence matrix and the known limitations. The play-test runbook is [`../testing/tax-code-playtest.md`](../testing/tax-code-playtest.md).
- **Spec and plan**: [`../superpowers/specs/2026-09-29-legislated-tax-code-design.md`](../superpowers/specs/2026-09-29-legislated-tax-code-design.md) and, for the AI and the release, [`../superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-03-tax-code-ai-and-release-design.md`](../superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-03-tax-code-ai-and-release-design.md); plans [`../superpowers/plans/2026-10-02-legislated-tax-code-tasks.md`](../superpowers/plans/2026-10-02-legislated-tax-code-tasks.md) and [`../superpowers/archive/plans/2026-10-03-tax-code-ai-and-release-tasks.md`](../superpowers/archive/plans/2026-10-03-tax-code-ai-and-release-tasks.md).
- **Generated files** come only from `scripts/generators/gen_tax_code.py` (`--check` in the tests; [`../auto_generated_files.md`](../auto_generated_files.md)). Tests: `test_tax_code_*.py`.

## Collective Governance (`law_direct_democracy`)

The governance principle `law_direct_democracy` is displayed as **Collective Governance**: no individual holds supreme executive power. The key is historical (the law was Direct Democracy) and kept because renaming a law breaks saves. Spec: `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-09-26-collective-governance-design.md`.

- **What it means depends on Distribution of Power**, expressed as one amendment on the law per group: the voting laws → *Direct Democracy* (the old referendum package, with a soft movement gate), Single-Party State → *Collective Leadership*, Technocracy → *Collegial Administration*, Anarchy → *Free Federation*, Oligarchy/Organic Regulation → *Patrician Council*, Algorithmic Governance → *Algorithmic Commons*. Autocracy can't hold the law. The law itself carries only the "no head" base (legitimacy from broad coalitions, less authority, slower enactment).
- **Soft movement gate (2026-10).** Direct Democracy and Free Federation used to carry `country_must_have_movement_to_enact_laws_bool`, which blocks every law no movement backs. Four mod law groups (Privacy Rights, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Consumer Protection, Urban Planning) have no movement stance at all, and the likeliest reading of "backs" is comparative (the movement rates the law above the current one), so under Anarchy the anarchist movement, already content, backs nothing and every law and exit needed a movement hostile to the regime. Both now carry a flat `country_law_enactment_success_add = -0.1` instead. A movement backing a law adds its support to the law's success chance natively (`LAW_ENACTMENT_MOVEMENT_SUPPORT_PASS_EFFECT = 1.0`; its activism can't drop below the 25% it needs while the law is enacted), so backed laws make up the 10% and unbacked laws pass slowly, or can't start under 11% success from the interest groups (`LAW_MIN_SUCCESS_CHANCE = 0.01`). Direct Democracy's +25% success went with the gate. Free Federation adds `state_loyalists_from_political_movements_mult = 0.5` (25% → 37.5% of a backing movement's supporters turn loyal on passage, `MOVEMENT_LOYALISTS_ON_APPROVED_ENACTMENT`) and `country_bolster_cost_mult = -0.5` (offsets Anarchy's −50% authority for bolstering). `test_no_movement_gate` keeps the bool off the law and every amendment. No modifier can make the gate per law: `political_movement_enact_support_mult` exists only in vanilla loc, and the movement-support defines are global.
- **Script-attached, never negotiated.** `te_refresh_collective_governance_amendment` (`collective_governance_effects.txt`) keeps exactly the matching amendment, derived from current laws on every call: the law's `on_activate` (hidden), `on_law_activated` (after the consistency cascade) and the monthly country pulse. The amendments' `possible` and `can_repeal` ask the same triggers (`collective_governance_triggers.txt`), so the player can't repeal the one their Distribution of Power calls for.
- **Preview:** the law's `on_enact` names the amendment the current Distribution of Power will give (the language-reform pattern).
- **Government types** (`timeline_extended_governments.txt`) run most specific first, because the first match wins: Noble Commonwealth (Oligarchy + Feudal Contracts) before Patrician Council, with `gov_collective_governance` as the catch-all. Algorithmic Commons comes before `gov_algorithmic_directorate`, which keys on Algorithmic Governance alone.
- **"Democracy" readings** (the liberal-democratic cultural-hegemony model, the referendum events `extra_law_events.24/.60/.84`) also require `collective_governance_is_popular`.
- **Every allowed Distribution of Power law must be holdable with it**, down the chain of laws it needs. Anarchy needs Cooperative Ownership, which vanilla unlocks only with Council Republic or Corporate State, so `common/laws/modified.txt` adds `law_direct_democracy` to its `unlocking_laws`. Before that, an anarchist Council Republic that enacted the law lost Cooperative Ownership to the consistency walk, then Anarchy, Collectivized Agriculture and Possession by Use. `test_gen_law_consistency.PrerequisiteHoldableTest` walks the chain for every law's prerequisites.
- **Adding a Distribution of Power law:** add it to its row of `EXPRESSIONS` in `test_collective_governance.py` (or add a row); the failures are the checklist.

## Bureaucracy Laws: Who Staffs the Administration (`law_contracted_administration`, `law_communal_administration`, `amendment_spoils_system`)

Beside vanilla's Hereditary, Appointed and Elected Bureaucrats and Automated Bureaucracy (next section), two human-staffed bureaucracy laws (`common/laws/extra_laws.txt`) and one amendment (`common/amendments/extra_amendments.txt`). Each law's identity is who staffs the Government Administrations: its own PM in vanilla's `pmg_government_administration_bureaucrat_professionalism`, which replaces Professional Bureaucrats while the law holds (`INJECT:pm_professional_bureaucrats` `disallowing_laws` lists all three mod laws), plus clout. They avoid Neocameralism's and Devolution's levers, so they stack with those laws without doubling up. Spec §7–12: `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-01-bureaucracy-laws-design.md`.

- **Contracted Administration** (Supply Chain Management; `unlocking_laws` Laissez-Faire or Interventionism; disallowed by Council Republic and Algorithmic Governance): capitalists +15% and bureaucrats −25% political strength, +25% institution size change speed, +5% institution bureaucracy cost (contract overruns), no Legislative Override Capacity. PM `pm_service_contractors`: 250 bureaucrats a level plus 20 Services, a local good, so a state with few Urban Centers pays more and can go short.
- **Communal Administration** (no technology; `unlocking_laws` Council Republic, Anarchy or Collective Governance; disallowed by Technocracy, Elder Council and Algorithmic Governance, Elected's vanilla exclusions plus machine rule): bureaucrats −25%, Trade Unions and Rural Folk +10% political strength, −5% movement radicalism, −10% tax capacity, −2 Legislative Override Capacity. PM `pm_recallable_delegates`: 250 bureaucrats and 250 clerks a level.
- **Progressiveness and the consistency walk.** Contracted is −2: below 0 keeps Appointed as Elected's fallback, and above −5 makes Appointed, not Automated (−10), Contracted's own (−5 ties and goes to the ideology tiebreak). Communal is 75, so a Council Republic or Collective Governance that loses Elected lands on Communal, and losing Communal falls back to Elected, else Appointed. Re-read `te_fix_inconsistent_lawgroup_bureaucracy` after changing any bureaucracy law's progressiveness or constraints.
- **Spoils System** (`amendment_spoils_system`): parent Appointed, allowed on Appointed and Elected (the US starts with Elected), −10% tax capacity, sponsor +15% political strength. Sponsored by IGs in government or led by a Jacksonian Democrat, and offered by `extra_law_events.87` ("To the Victor Belong the Spoils", debate checkpoint) while either law is enacted, sponsored by the governing IG with the most clout. Vanilla's `amendment_preserved_bureaucratic_caste` is the template and is left unchanged.
- **Adding a bureaucracy law:** `disallowing_laws = { law_algorithmic_governance }` (or machine rule evicts it), a progressiveness checked against the cascade, its PM in the professionalism group plus the `pm_professional_bureaucrats` INJECT, Appointed's two IG-shift `on_enact` tooltips, an inline Legislative Override Capacity value or a comment saying why none, ideology stances, loc, a law icon (a `law` entry in `scripts/image_pipeline/icon_prompts.py`), the player guide.

## Machine Administration and Machine Rule (`law_automated_bureaucracy`, `law_algorithmic_governance`)

Bureaucracy decides who administers the state; Distribution of Power decides who rules it. **Automated Bureaucracy** (Bureaucracy, Generative AI) hands administration to machines under human authority, and any government can hold it. **Algorithmic Governance** (Distribution of Power, Artificial Intelligence) hands the machines the authority itself. Spec: `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-01-bureaucracy-laws-design.md`. The human-staffed laws beside it are in the Bureaucracy Laws section above.

- **Automated Bureaucracy:** −20% institution bureaucracy cost, +50% institution size change speed, −25% bureaucrat and +15% engineer political strength, +1 Legislative Override Capacity. Progressiveness −10, so `gen_law_consistency` still moves a country that loses Elected Bureaucrats to Appointed. Its staffing is `pm_automated_casework` in vanilla's `pmg_government_administration_bureaucrat_professionalism`: 150 bureaucrats and 100 engineers a level instead of 500 bureaucrats, plus Digital Access and Digital Assets. That PM replaces Professional Bureaucrats while the law holds (`disallowing_laws` INJECTed on `pm_professional_bureaucrats`), as vanilla's Hereditary Bureaucrats PM does.
- **Install and lock.** Algorithmic Governance's `on_activate` enacts Automated Bureaucracy. Appointed and Hereditary Bureaucrats (and the Crownland Diets variant) get `disallowing_laws = { law_algorithmic_governance }` (`common/laws/modified.txt`), Contracted and Communal Administration carry it in their own definitions, and Elected needs a voting law, so Automated is the only valid bureaucracy law under machine rule. Don't put `unlocking_laws = { law_automated_bureaucracy }` on Algorithmic Governance: Distribution of Power is fixed before Bureaucracy in the consistency walk, so any bureaucracy change would evict the governing law, and old saves would lose it.
- **Algorithmic Governance** keeps no administrative effects. Its legitimacy is a flat `country_legitimacy_base_add = 70` on the law plus `algorithmic_mandate` (`sol_expectations_modifiers.txt`): +1 base legitimacy times `algorithmic_mandate_value`, which is 5 × the cached SoL expectations gap, capped at ±40. The base is there because every other Distribution of Power law carries legitimacy of its own (clout 25–120, votes 40–110, Elder Council a flat 20) and this one has no clout, votes or head-of-state term: with the mandate alone, a Presidential Republic on very low taxes sat at 42 (Unstable Government) with the mandate at its old +25 cap, and a first fix of base 50 with the cap unchanged still topped out at 92 there. Base plus cap is sized for headroom, not for the neutral case: 70 + 40 = 110 before taxes (`tax_modifier_*`: +10 very low, +5 low, 0 medium, −10 high, −20 very high), the head of state's group and timed modifiers. At the +40 cap a Presidential Republic reaches 100 through High taxes and 97 at Very High; at +25 (a gap of 5) it reaches 100 through Medium and falls to 92 and 82. A country on a steady standard of living sits near 70 plus those terms. The tooltip on enactment (`ALGORITHMIC_GOVERNANCE_TT_MANDATE`) explains the mandate and quotes the 5 and the 40; `test_algorithmic_mandate.py` pins them to the script value. The mandate is re-applied from `sol_expectations_monthly_on_action` right after the update caches the gap; that is its only refresh site, and the law's `on_deactivate` removes it. The gap is zero once expectations catch up, so the mandate pays for improvement and costs for decline, not for a level of wealth. Together with the doubled radicals and loyalists from SoL change, a falling standard of living is what threatens machine rule.
- **Events:** `society_technology_events.27` (Generative AI) and `post_scarcity_events.3` belong to Automated Bureaucracy. `extra_law_events.83`, the dispute over who has the last word, is Automated Bureaucracy's enactment event, and `.23`/`.59` fire for either law.

## Policing: Private Policing and Its Amendments (`law_private_policing`, `amendment_corporate_security_powers`, `amendment_civilian_police_oversight`, #628)

`lawgroup_policing` answers who provides ordinary enforcement, who pays and whom it answers to. Beside vanilla's No Police, Local Police Force (public constabularies under local notables), Dedicated Police Force and Militarized Police Force, the mod adds one law (`common/laws/extra_laws.txt`) and two amendments (`common/amendments/extra_amendments.txt`). Internal Security (regime protection) and Criminal Justice (punishment and rehabilitation) are separate groups. The group's and the four vanilla laws' descriptions are overridden in `localization/english/replace/` to say who pays and answers. Every effect is aggregate: coverage that follows money is modelled within states (strata standard of living) rather than as a per-state modifier, because every state has rich and poor districts (owner call). Spec, with the decision on every candidate in the issue: `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-04-policing-laws-design.md`.

- **Private Policing** (Computer Networks; `unlocking_laws` Laissez-Faire or Interventionism; disallowed by Council Republic). Keeps `institution_police` (displayed as Ministry of Public Safety) at −40% institution cost, vanilla Private Schools' and Private Health Insurance's value. Per investment level: upper strata +0.25 and middle strata +0.1 SoL, `state_turmoil_effects_mult` +0.05 (half the institution's own −0.1), `goods_output_services_mult` −0.01 (owners' funding: the guards are service workers, so Services buyers pay through prices; an investment-pool cut was rejected as too harsh on the corporate economies most likely to enact it). Flat: Trade Unions −10% political strength, Labor Movement pop attraction +15%, Legislative Override Capacity −0.5 (No Police's value). No IG clout bonus per level: the issue warned against moving Local Police's landowner bonus to the Industrialists.
- **Who favours it.** Only Corpocrat (strongly approve) and Corporate Rule (approve); `ai_will_do` needs a Corpocrat ruler (Neocameralism's rule). Market ideologies are left neutral. The disapproving vanilla ideologies are in `ideology_modifications.py` (`private_policing_*`). Every ideology with a Policing block states a stance on it (`ideology_lawgroup_audit`), and one the block is new to also states the four base-game police laws.
- **Consistency walk.** Progressiveness 25 equals Dedicated Police Force, so `te_fix_inconsistent_lawgroup_policing` moves a country that loses its market economy or becomes a Council Republic to Dedicated Police Force (nationalization; the shared institution keeps its investment), or No Police without Law Enforcement.
- **Corporate Security Powers:** parent Private Policing (so the same corpocrat-only stance), allowed on Local, Dedicated and Militarized Police Force; Corporate Charters and not Command Economy, Cooperative Ownership or Industry Banned; −10% police institution cost, Trade Unions −10%, Labor Movement +15%, sponsor +10% political strength. Sponsored by the Industrialists or any IG approving the parent, and offered by `extra_law_events.89` ("Guards at the Mill Gate", debate checkpoint) with the Industrialists as sponsor. Not allowed on Private Policing, which already delegates the whole force.
- **Civilian Oversight:** parent Guaranteed Liberties, allowed on Local, Dedicated and Private Policing (not Militarized); Civil Rights Movement; +10% police institution cost, Legislative Override Capacity −0.5, radicalism increases −10% for Second-Rate Citizen and Open Prejudice pops, turmoil effects −5%, sponsor +10% political strength. The 2026-10-17 rebalance replaced Civil Rights Movement pop attraction −15%, which worked against the reforming governments that adopt it (spec §3). Sponsored by the Intelligentsia or any IG approving the parent, and offered by `extra_law_events.90` ("Who Watches the Watchmen", debate checkpoint) with the Intelligentsia as sponsor.

## Inheritance: Who Inherits (`lawgroup_inheritance`)

Six laws answer one question, who inherits an estate; apart from each law's Wealth Concentration line (below), the group's systemic effects come from script rather than from the laws' modifier blocks. Spec, with the owner's decisions of 2026-10-08: `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-08-inheritance-laws-design.md`. Files: laws in `common/laws/extra_laws.txt` (the INHERITANCE block), amendments at the foot of `common/amendments/extra_amendments.txt`, `te_inheritance_values.txt` (script values), `te_inheritance_effects.txt`, `te_inheritance_triggers.txt`, `te_inheritance_modifiers.txt`, `te_inheritance_on_actions.txt`, `events/inheritance_events.txt`.

| Law (key) | Unlock | Concentration target | Own modifiers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Primogeniture & Entail (`law_primogeniture`) | start | 80 | tax capacity −10%, population bureaucracy cost −10% (the gentry sit as unpaid magistrates) |
| Customary Inheritance (`law_partible`) | start; GLOBAL default (`extra_history.txt`) | 50 | population bureaucracy cost −5%, tax capacity −5% (small: 281 countries start on it) |
| Forced Heirship (`law_equal_inheritance`) | Egalitarianism | 25 | Rural Folk +10%, tax capacity +10%, bureaucracy cost +5% |
| Freedom of Testation (`law_free_testation`) | start | 60 | capitalists' investment pool +10%, bureaucracy cost +5% |
| State as Universal Heir (`law_state_universal_heir`) | Command Economy | 0 | +200 authority, dividends efficiency +5%, Bureaucrats +10%, bureaucracy cost +5%, upper strata −20% and middle strata −10% investment-pool efficiency |
| Possession by Use (`law_non_inheritable_usage_rights`) | Cooperative Ownership | 0 | population bureaucracy cost −5%, Rural Folk and Trade Unions +10%, the same investment-pool cuts |

- **Balance (2026-10-09, owner's table).** Each law has an upside and a cost of its own, and none repeats what the score carries: radicals, qualifications and education access come from the state's score (`inh_concentrated_property`), so Primogeniture lost its radicals +10% and qualifications −10% and Forced Heirship its radicals −10% and education access +0.05 (`TestInheritanceBalance` pins it). Primogeniture's bureaucracy saving moved from institutions (−5% investment cost) to local administration (−10% population cost); Customary Inheritance gained a small pair; Freedom of Testation's litigation cost rose from 3% to 5%. State as Universal Heir and Possession by Use are unchanged.
- **Keys are historical.** Each old key kept its meaning (Partible → Customary, Equal Inheritance → Forced Heirship, Usage Rights → Possession by Use), so saves keep their laws. The two new laws come after the old four in file order (a law at the head of an existing group broke pre-change saves, #520); the defensive `te_repair_double_inheritance_law` (`te_old_save_repairs.txt`) clears any country left holding two. A pre-redesign save's Command-Economy holder of Usage Rights moves to State as Universal Heir through the monthly consistency walk, which now finds Possession by Use unlocked by Cooperative Ownership only.
- **Starting laws**: France Forced Heirship, Britain and Japan Primogeniture & Entail, the USA Freedom of Testation, everyone else (Russia included) Customary.
- **Progressiveness** shapes `te_fix_inconsistent_lawgroup_inheritance`: State as Universal Heir 50 and Possession by Use 60 fall to each other when the economic system allows, else to Forced Heirship (25, needs Egalitarianism), else Customary (10). Freedom of Testation is 5 so it is never that fallback.
- **`ideological_opinion_impact = 0.5`** (was 0): groups react to the law in force. France's Landowners now dislike Forced Heirship from 1836; balance item to check in play.
- **Wealth-concentration score** (`te_inh_concentration`, 0–100, concept `concept_inheritance_concentration`). Kept per state since the demographics census (§ Demographics): each state holds a score `te_dg_wc` and a target `te_dg_wc_target`, and `te_inh_concentration` is the national figure, the states' average weighted by where property is held (`te_demog_wc_national`, the one refresh site of the figure and of #822's modifiers). A state's target is the law's (`te_inh_law_amendment_target`: the table above plus Estate Duties −30, Birthright Endowment −20, Perpetual Trusts +30, Undivided Farm Succession +10, clamped 0–100; since 2026-10-21 50 plus each law's and amendment's `country_wealth_concentration_inheritance_add` line, the table's target less 50, so the law's and the amendment's tooltips show it, where only the laws' `on_enact` text had said it) plus land tenure, who owns the state's capital, its income inequality, the country's taxes on wealth, its economic laws and its return on capital against growth (r > g), clamped 0–100, or pinned at the state's score under continuity of title. Each state's yearly pulse (`te_demog_wc_state_yearly`, straight after its walk) closes 3% of the gap (half in ~23 years), takes up to 10 a year off the score at full devastation (10 × the state's 0–1 devastation) and takes the state's ownership shock. The shocks are listed in § Demographics, Wealth Concentration per state. The national refresh (at the yearly country pulse, and after any event shift or shock) reapplies the two country modifiers, which carry the political capture: `inh_great_fortunes` (multiplier (score − 50)/30 above 50, straight, 5/3 at 100: Aristocrats and Capitalists +20% clout and +0.3 bubble pressure a month at full) or `inh_dispersed_wealth` (full at 20, half the slope beyond, 4/3 at 0: Aristocrats and Capitalists −20%, bubble −0.4; the 2026-10-22 effects design, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-22-demographic-effects-impact-design.md`, sized by `banking_cycle_simulation.md` §27), reading `te_inh_great_fortunes_mult` / `te_inh_dispersed_mult`. The rest acts per state (below, and § Demographics, Wealth Concentration per state). `te_inh_yearly_update` keeps the old country-level drift (`te_inh_concentration_next`, 3% of the gap) only for a country with no scored state, such as a landless one. Game start: the hidden `inheritance_events.1` (`te_inh_game_start`; on_game_started has no ROOT for the multiplier) seeds every state at its own target, then the national figure, and clears the generation clock history set. A save from before the census starts each state from its owner's figure, or from its own target if the owner has none, at its first yearly pulse, so nothing drifts on load. The score and its target are shown in the law group's description, the concept and the Demographics tab's Wealth section.
- **Old Landowner clout, birth rate and migration** moved off the laws: the clout to the score, birth and migration to the rural modifiers.
- **Rural-scaled modifiers** (state, `te_inh_refresh_rural_effects`, the only refresh site, called by `te_demog_state_yearly` on the state's yearly pulse straight after the census walk): multiplier `te_inh_agrarian_share` = Peasants + Farmers over the state's population, read from the walk's `te_dg_agr_share` (the walk replaced the old `te_inh_agrarian_share_value` pop walk, so the mod walks pops once a year per state; London reads 0.174). Forced Heirship `inh_forced_heirship_rural` (birth −15%, migration quota −20% at full share; since phase 3 the birth line sits on the absorbed family too, as Primogeniture's does: outside Full the moved lines' pair applies it as Laws and Institutions, and under Full Family Limitation takes its place, § Phase 3: Family Limitation and Cultural Hegemony's drift); Primogeniture `inh_primogeniture_rural` (+10%, +20%; the birth line is on the absorbed family's script-only type, so outside Full the moved lines' pair applies it as Laws and Institutions, the rural refresh firing `te_demog_events.4` the same day, and under Full Late Marriage takes its place; a once-a-game `TE_SELF_CHECK` in `debug.log` says whether the engine scales the type, `docs/testing/demographics-playtest.md`); Undivided Farm Succession `inh_undivided_farm_rural` (migration +20%) replaces Forced Heirship's. The quota is symmetric, so scaling by rural share is what makes it a rural-exodus lever.
- **Amendments** (parents from other groups; ways in: debate events `inheritance_events.10`–`.13` in `on_law_checkpoint_debate`, petitions `amendment_petition_events.17`–`.20`). Estate Duties (`amendment_estate_duties`): parent Graduated Taxation, on the four private-estate laws, Political Agitation, not beside the Endowment, target −30 and no other modifier (no standing revenue, owner, 2026-10-08): the stronger leveller, since all the duty goes to the treasury. Perpetual Dynastic Trusts (`amendment_perpetual_trusts`): parent Laissez-Faire, Freedom of Testation only, Globalization, capitalists' investment pool +10%. Birthright Endowment (`amendment_birthright_endowment`): parent Old Age Pension, the four laws, Universal Basic Income, target −20 (its duty is set to pay the stakes), qualifications +10%, education access +5%, Laborers', Farmers' and Shopkeepers' investment pool +10%, bureaucracy cost +5% (an account for every young adult); it levies the duty itself, so it replaces Estate Duties. The swap adds the Endowment before removing the duty (`te_inh_swap_duties_for_endowment`), so whether `add_amendment` sees a same-block removal does not matter; `te_inh_tidy_amendments` drops a duty an IG left beside it. Undivided Farm Succession (`amendment_undivided_farm_succession`): parent Peasant Proprietorship, Forced Heirship and Customary, no unlock. The debate events offer to carry an amendment the outgoing law holds over to the incoming one (their `_carry` descriptions).
- **Generation events** (first wave): `.2` The Cadet Sons (Primogeniture), `.3` The Last Division (Forced Heirship, without the farm amendment; one option attaches it), `.4` The Founder's Will (Freedom of Testation; a foundation, −5 and ten years of schooling and innovation, a dynasty, +5 and ten years of capitalist investment, or the heirs go to court, −10, the deepest cut, and five years of dearer institutions), `.5` The Great Estates for Sale (an estate duty held 15 years, `te_inh_duty_years`; the state buys the land for smallholders, −10 and 5% of a year's income, or the market takes it, −2 and +3%, or working farms are exempted, +3). Each rolls 10% a year from its own sub-action, has a 25-year cooldown and waits for `te_inh_law_recent`, set for 20 years by every inheritance law's `on_activate`. Options that move the score call `te_inh_shift_concentration` inside a `custom_tooltip`. The second wave (spec § 11, 2026-10-25): `.14` The Hidden Estates (State as Universal Heir; audit, −3 and 100 authority fading, or look away, +5 and ten years of `inh_estates_overlooked`), `.15` The Empty Holding (Possession by Use; the commune reallocates, −2 and agriculture throughput −3%, or the family keeps it, +5 and +5%), both on the same clock; `.16` The First Cohort (the Birthright Endowment held 5 years, `te_inh_endowment_years`, 25% a year, once per tenure through `te_inh_first_cohort_paid`: schooling, businesses, or spent, +3).
- **Posthumous Title** (`.6`, Mind Backups or Biological Immortality, 20% a year, once per country, `te_inh_posthumous_decided`): recognise continuity of title (`te_inh_title_continuity` pins the target; `inh_continuity_of_title`, −10% innovation and qualifications; `.7` The Heirs Who Never Inherit five years later, with a reversal option) or declare legal death (`inh_legal_death_backlash`, Transhumanist movement +25% for ten years).
- **Wealth Concentration's state modifiers** (demographics spec §4.2, phase 2; `te_inh_refresh_wc_state_effects`, the only refresh site, called by `te_demog_state_yearly` straight after the state's drift, and at game start by the hidden state event `inheritance_events.8`, which `.1` fires for every state once they are seeded; ROOT is the state, so the multiplier reads its own score). Each reads the state's `te_dg_wc`: `inh_concentrated_property` (the high side, (score − 50)/30: Aristocrats' and Capitalists' investment pool efficiency +20%, political strength from wealth +20%, qualifications −20%, education access −0.10 at full), `inh_dispersed_property` (the low side, full at 20, 4/3 at 0: political strength from wealth −10%, qualifications +10%, education access +0.10, radicals −10%; no investment line, since small owners save too), `inh_land_hunger` (the high side × the agrarian share `te_dg_agr_share`: migration quota +30%, Land Reform movement support +25%, radicals +10%; a third modifier because a multiplier is one variable and the rural exodus needs both factors). The sizes are `demographics_effects.SIZES`, pinned by `test_demographics_registry.TestWealthSizes`. Multipliers `te_inh_wc_high_mult`, `te_inh_wc_low_mult`, `te_inh_land_hunger_mult` (state, never removed). A shift or shock made from country scope moves the scores at once and the state modifiers follow at each state's next yearly pulse. All five Wealth Concentration modifiers run under every Demographics rule setting (owner, 2026-10-09). The state's three, with the inheritance law's three rural ones, are listed in the state panel's Wealth Concentration tile and left out of its modifier rows (§ State Panel GUI Enhancements).
- **Revolutions**: the score and Posthumous Title flags are variables; `inh_repair_after_civil_war` (called from `te_civil_war_on_won`) copies the loser's over a revolutionary winner's own, with Wealth Concentration's land-law role and r > g's GDP baseline and growth average (`te_demog_wc_civil_war_inherit`: the winner continues the nation), and reapplies the country modifiers (the state modifiers are the states' and move with them), and `te_inh_apply_concentration_modifiers` restores `inh_continuity_of_title` while its flag holds.
- **Ideology stances** (`ideology_modifications.py`, P C F T S U): traditional SA N D D SD SD, moderate D N N SA SD SD, reform D A A N D D, bonapartist D N SA N D D, progressive (Proletarian) SD N A D A A, communist SD D N SD SA D, anarchist SD D N SD D SA. Hand-written blocks in `extra_ideologies.txt` name all six; Islamic Inheritance D A A D D D; the socialist, imperial-cult and theocratic custom-religion economies approve State as Universal Heir and disapprove Possession by Use. The reform movements (2026-10-22), each strongly against entail: liberal, liberal-republican and national-liberal SD N N A D D; radical SD N A D N D; socialist SD N A D A N; land reformer SD A A N D N. The AI weighs a law change by the movements that want it (`CHANGE_LAW_POLITICAL_MOVEMENT_FACTOR`, 1000 × support × radicalism), and before these only the traditionalist movements, which defend Primogeniture, held a stance; a movement's stance on each law in force also moves its radicalism (`MOVEMENT_RADICALISM_FROM_ACTIVE_LAW_STANCE`, −0.05 times its stance), so these four grow more radical under Primogeniture.
- **Enactment events** `extra_law_events.17`, `.53`, `.77` fire for Forced Heirship, Freedom of Testation, State as Universal Heir and Possession by Use.

## Rules of War (`lawgroup_rules_of_war`)

Five laws, one identity each (2026-10-09 redesign from a playtest: the old group was one dial at ×1/×2/×3, and the default was a pure malus). Laws in `common/laws/extra_laws.txt` (the RULES OF WAR header), AI trigger `te_row_serious_war` in `common/scripted_triggers/rules_of_war_triggers.txt`, strike bans in `nuclear_program_modifier_types.txt`, pins in `test_rules_of_war.py`. Every country starts on Traditional (`extra_history.txt`).

| Law (key) | Unlock | For | Signature | Other modifiers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total War (`law_total_war`) | Chemical Warfare (was Bombing Aircraft) | the nation mobilized | mobilization speed +25%, war-support loss from casualties −50% | kill rate +0.10, devastation +100%, battles ±25% war support, Ministry of War impact +25%, Foreign Affairs cap −1, reputation −10, anti-war +20%, escalation +25% both ways, UN −2; unlocks three PMs |
| Traditional (`law_traditional_rules_of_war`) | start | the soldier's code | morale loss −5%, army experience +25% | none |
| War Crimes Forbidden (`law_war_crimes_forbidden`) | Wargaming | the law of occupation | radicals from conquest −25% | devastation −25%, kill rate −0.05, Foreign Affairs impact +10%, reputation +2, escalation −10%, UN +0.5 |
| Humanitarian Regulations (`law_humanitarian_regulations`) | Nuclear Weapons | the trusted partner | recovery rate +10%, reputation +6 (the group's highest) | devastation −50%, kill rate −0.05, strategic strike ban, Foreign Affairs impact +25%, anti-war −10%, escalation −10%, UN +1 |
| Limited War (`law_limited_war`) | ICBMs | proportionality, limited aims | war goal maneuver cost +100% in plays it starts, infamy generation −25%, tactical strike ban, escalation −30% (the group's strongest) | battles −20% war support both ways, anti-war −20%, devastation −75%, kill rate −0.05, strategic strike ban, Foreign Affairs impact +25%, reputation +3, UN +1.5 |

- **Limited War prices aims, it doesn't ban them** (owner, 2026-10-09). Gating the subjugation war goals would need `REPLACE:` copies of vanilla war goal types (an `INJECT` can't add to a `possible` block vanilla declares; read for diplomatic actions, `scripting_best_practices.md` § "A second trigger block is rejected at load"), so the law raises `country_initiator_war_goal_maneuver_cost_mult` instead: war goals in plays it starts cost double, still conquerable but fewer at once. A cost increase can't go below zero; Aggressive Coordination's −0.3 (any tier) softens it. Defensive counter-goals are untouched.
- **No law closes a ministry.** Caps move by at most 1 (Ministry of War's law cap is 3, Foreign Affairs' 2). An impact multiplier scales the whole institution block, wage and goods costs included, so it is a mixed lever; only Total War's Ministry of War +25% and the humane laws' Foreign Affairs boosts use one.
- **Nuclear bans are law modifiers**: `country_strategic_nuclear_strikes_forbidden_bool` (Humanitarian Regulations, Limited War) and `country_tactical_nuclear_strikes_forbidden_bool` (Limited War), `script_only` booleans that show in the law tooltip. `nd_war_law_permits_strategic_strike` / `_tactical_strike` read them; `nd_war_law_exception` (struck, a covered country struck, or `nd_fighting_for_existence`) lifts either.
- **AI** (`ai_enact_weight_modifier` only; vanilla's `ai_will_do` is a hard veto): Total War +200 in a serious war (`te_row_serious_war`: at war with a major or great power, or `nd_fighting_for_existence`), −100 at peace; the other four +150 while a country at peace still holds Total War. Enactment time is the default, so a switch costs months, a law slot and the law-change approval swing.
- **Stances** (`ideology_modifications.py`, TW Trad WCF HR LW): aggressive SA A N D SD; traditional N SA N D D; moderate D N A N D; liberal (liberal, liberal_modern, market_liberal, humanitarian) SD D N SA SA; pacifist (pacifist, anarchist) SD D N A SA. The nuclear posture classes compare Total War with Limited War (`nd_stance_*`), so liberals keep Limited War at strongly approve. The six hand-written custom-religion outlooks in `extra_ideologies.txt` name all five.
- **Kept fixed by the redesign:** the UN Authority values (`test_un_policy_pillar.py`), the UN AI hooks (most reward Humanitarian Regulations), the amendments (No-First-Strike Pledge on Humanitarian Regulations / Limited War, Military Necessity Clause on War Crimes Forbidden / Humanitarian Regulations) and the enactment events `extra_law_events.10`, `.11`, `.32`, `.46`, `.47`, `.70`, `.71` (all a humane bill against military pushback).
- **Infamy on taking effect** (`te_row_charge_infamy`, `common/scripted_effects/rules_of_war_effects.txt`). Each law's `on_activate` passes its standing (Total War +25, Traditional 0, War Crimes Forbidden −10, Humanitarian Regulations −15, Limited War −20), and `change_infamy` moves infamy by the difference from `te_row_charged_standing` (`te_row_infamy_standing`, the standing last charged; 0 when unset; `common/script_values/rules_of_war_values.txt`): the full difference toward a looser law, `te_row_infamy_reduction_share` (0.9) of it, rounded toward zero, toward a stricter one. So a move there and back costs 1 to 5 infamy (owner, 2026-10-16: a loop must be a net loss) and cycling the restrictive laws can't wipe it; leaving Total War takes 22 of its 25 back. Rounding to nearest would make the five-point steps (War Crimes Forbidden ↔ Humanitarian Regulations ↔ Limited War) free to loop, since 0.9 × 5 = 4.5. No pulse resyncs the variable to the law in force: a country from an older save was charged nothing, and a resync would hand it a cut. Edge: a revolution that wins a different Rules of War law can leave the winner on the loser's standing (rebels start with no variables), at most 45 off. It renders in the enactment preview.
- **War-crime scandal** `social_tensions_events.7` fires at war under Total War, Traditional or War Crimes Forbidden; its reform option needs Traditional or War Crimes Forbidden (it had needed a humane law the trigger excluded, so it never appeared).

## Demographics (`demographics_rule`): the census (phase 1; phase 2 steps 1, 2 and 4; phase 3: event wave, late game and Family Limitation)

A yearly census of every state's people by single year of age and by sex, shown in a Demographics tab of the Population panel and a Demographics subtab of the state panel. It also keeps Wealth Concentration per state and computes the Gini and the national urban pattern. **From phase 2 step 4 the census sets each state's births and deaths** (under Full; § The census's births and deaths): the engine's events become the model's plus the terms added on top of the census (a state-wide one acting on the census's rate, a pop's own on its bare curve), and the ring follows what the engine did. The laws', technologies' and institutions' own birth and mortality lines are script-only and reach a state through the census or, without it, through Laws and Institutions (§ The census's births and deaths, "The moved lines"). **From phase 2 step 2 it sets each state's workforce too** (under Full): who is of working age and who works, with a pension setting, a pension bill and a health bill (§ Phase 2 step 2). Plan: `docs/superpowers/archive/plans/2026-10-10-demographics-phase2-engine-rates.md`. Two changes outside population ride with it: Wealth Concentration is now kept per state with four new target terms (a fifth, the economic laws, came with the phase 2 balance pass) (§ Wealth Concentration per state), and the tactical nuclear strike counts its soldiers among the dead. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-08-demographics-design.md` (§ numbers below are its sections); plan: `docs/superpowers/archive/plans/2026-10-08-demographics-phases-0-1.md`; engine evidence: `docs/testing/demographics-probe-results-2026-10-08.md`, and the engine's own births and deaths per pop: `docs/testing/demographics-growth-probe-results-2026-10-09.md`; harness results: `docs/testing/demographics-harness-2026-10-08.md`. The model, harness and spec corrections are PR 1 (#828); the census is PR 2 (branch `demographics-phase1`).

**Built (calibration step 2):** Late Marriage and Birth Spacing, two customs that lower children per woman (§ Late Marriage and Birth Spacing).

**Built with it:** Primogeniture's farm births under Full (the late-marriage spec's call 4; the late-marriage plan, Task 9, Plan A): Late Marriage takes their place.

**Built (phase 2 step 3a):** the Family Policy measures, their buttons in the tab's Family Policy section, their upkeep and terms, and the family laws' AI weights (§ Family Policy measures). The census reads the measures' six new types into its birth and sex-ratio terms (step 3b).

**Built (phase 3, 2026-10-12):** the national urban pattern's effects and the Plan a New Capital decision, under Full only (§ The urban pattern's effects and Planned Capital).

**Built (phase 3, 2026-10-19):** the per-state metropolitan share (spec §5.2), shown under Display only and Full, its effects under Full only (§ The metropolitan share).

**Not built yet.** Phase 2 steps 1 to 4 are built (step 2, the workforce, pensions and health costs, since 2026-10-12: § Phase 2 step 2), along with calibration steps 1–3. The step 4 conscription, youth-bulge and sex-balance effects were enabled under Full by the migrant booking (2026-10-12). **Release precondition (owner, 2026-10-10, amended): nothing changes outside Full.** Step 4 of the engine-rates plan edits no engine birth or mortality line: the lines the census absorbs stay on their laws, techs and institutions, and only M cancels them, under Full. Step 5, a retune of the global defines, is dropped (owner, 2026-10-10): it would change every game, census on or off. Its only job was to keep M small so the terms on top count at the right weight; if that ever matters, it is handled inside M under Full. Wealth Concentration's effects, split by scope, are built (§ Inheritance, the state modifiers). Phase 3's urban pattern and Planned Capital, event wave, late game, and Family Limitation and Cultural Hegemony's fertility drift are built; the per-state metropolitan share is built too (§ The metropolitan share). Wealth Concentration's remaining shocks, the r > g term and the Inequality effect are built (2026-10-19: § Wealth Concentration per state, § The Inequality effect). Internal Resettlement's programme profiles and the US frontier's 1836 start were built on 2026-10-19 (§ Internal Resettlement in the census, and the US frontier). Map modes stay blocked until a per-state source exists (the `te_map_mode_*` hijack is switched off, `docs/audits/open_issues.md`).

**The late game** (approved design, 2026-10-11; **built 2026-10-12**, § Phase 3: the late game): `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-11-demographics-late-game-design.md` scopes biological age, the pension age, fertility under life extension, who gets life extension, the pension and health costs and their display as one model, and lists what phase 2 must build now so its workforce, pension and health work reads age through calendar and biological clocks rather than a fixed 65.

**Uploaded minds** (the owner's calls of 2026-10-19; **built 2026-10-19**, § Uploaded minds): `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-16-demographics-uploaded-minds-design.md`. Under Full, in a country with Mind Backups and a Mind Upload Nexus, people in longevity care facing death from illness or old age upload instead, within the Nexus's capacity, into a pool of minds beside the census; the Nexus's output follows the minds it hosts; and Mind Backups' −50% restore reaches only those in care.

**Phase 2's consequences** (design, 2026-10-12; all four steps built): `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-12-demographics-phase2-consequences-design.md` designs the workforce, pensions and health costs, the Family Policy measures, conscription, the youth bulge and sex balance in four steps, and lists what changes outside Full (the base-law fixes only). Step 1, the late game's interfaces, changing no number, is built (§ Phase 2 step 1: the interfaces; plan `docs/superpowers/archive/plans/2026-10-12-demographics-phase2-interfaces.md`), and so is step 3a, the Family Policy measures without the census reading them (§ Family Policy measures). Step 4, conscription, the youth bulge and sex balance, is built (§ Phase 2 step 4: conscription, the youth bulge and sex balance; built from the spec, owner 2026-10-12); it shipped its three effects held back behind switches, and the migrant booking (2026-10-12; § The census, "Flows") turned them on. Step 2, the workforce, pensions and health costs, is built too (§ Phase 2 step 2).

### Game rule

`demographics_rule`: `demographics_full` (default), `demographics_display_only`, `demographics_disabled`, labelled Full / Display only / Disabled under the rule name "Demographics" ("Demographics (Experimental)" until 2026-10-25). Full by default since 2026-10-25 (owner); it was off by default from 2026-10-10 while the census was experimental. Every check is written positively through `te_demog_cohorts_run` (Full or Display only) and `te_demog_effects_run` (Full), the only reads of the rule, so a save from before the rule, which stores no value for it, reads as Disabled; a negated check would start the census in a running campaign (the tax code's rule, for the same reason). 1.2.0 is the first release to ship the census (owner, 2026-10-26); 1.1.8 was cut without it. A release that ships without the census runs `scripts/release/comment_out_census_inputs.py` on its release branch (never on `main`): it comments out every line that sets one of the census's script-only modifier types, which render on tech, law and institution tooltips although the engine never applies them, along with France's Family Limitation, phase 3's census line of it and the rule itself (`test_release_census_inputs.py`). Full applies the census's births and deaths terms (§ The census's births and deaths), which take over the absorbed lines while it is on; Display only and Disabled clear them at each state's next step, and nothing changes outside Full (owner, 2026-10-10). Disabled runs no cohorts and hides the tab and subtab. It does **not** stop the pop and building walks, Wealth Concentration, the war shock or the national figure: inheritance (#822) owns those and must keep working. No setting gates Wealth Concentration's five modifiers either, the two national ones or the three per state (owner, 2026-10-09). Keys: `rule_demographics_rule`, `setting_demographics_*` (and `_desc`) in `te_game_rules_l_english.yml`.
