### When it runs

| Pulse | Scope | Runs |
|---|---|---|
| `on_game_started` | hidden country event `te_demog_events.1` per country | `te_demog_country_game_start`: walk every state and, if the cohorts run, seed it (marked `te_dg_reseed`, since the seed is off the state's pulse), then the country's figures. Wealth Concentration's own seed is `te_inh_game_start` (`inheritance_events.1`), which then fires the hidden state event `inheritance_events.8` in every state for its three state modifiers |
| `on_yearly_pulse_state` (a different day per state across the year) | state | `te_demog_state_yearly`: walks, then inheritance's rural modifiers, then Wealth Concentration's drift and its state modifiers (`te_inh_refresh_wc_state_effects`), then (cohorts run) seed, skip or step (`te_demog_state_census`; while fast mode's clock runs, this pulse keeps only inheritance, Wealth Concentration and phase 3's two state checks below, and the first two only for a state the clock has walked (`te_dg_walk_pop`): one that appears between steps, a colony or a split, waits for its first). No census yet, a census more than a year old, an emptied ring, or a seed made off this pulse (`te_dg_reseed`: game start, the console's re-seeds): seed. A census exactly one year old: step, however far the state's people moved (owner, 2026-10-20; until then a move of more than 25% seeded again, on the premise of a state merged or split, and in the owner's 2057 game it fired only on migration). A second pulse in one year does nothing. Each pulse stores the state's provinces (`te_dg_provinces`, `te_demog_state_provinces`, a script value's `every_province`) and, when they changed since the last, logs `TE_INFO demog_province_change` with the old and new counts, the people at the last census and now, the owner and the state (`te_debug_demog_province_change`), so a play-test learns whether the engine merges or splits states; one province more in an unincorporated state (a colony growing) isn't logged, and the line changes no number. Then the on-action runs phase 3's urban-pattern refresh and the planned capital's check (`te_demog_up_state_refresh`, `te_demog_pc_state_check`), with ROOT the state. The metropolitan share moves first, before `te_demog_state_yearly`, on last year's walk (`te_demog_mt_state_update`, so the step's urban fertility term reads this year's share), and its two modifiers are refreshed last (`te_demog_mt_state_refresh`) |
| `on_monthly_pulse` (global, the 1st of each month) | none | Only while fast mode's clock runs (`te_demog_clock_tick`): every N months, advance the clock a year, fire `te_demog_events.2` in every state (walks, seed or step, the fast rate modifiers) and `te_demog_events.3` in every country a day later (its census, the speed modifier). See Fast mode below |
| `on_monthly_pulse_country` | country | `te_demog_country_monthly`: snapshot the owner's war dead (a rise only) into the year's total, whatever the rule; while the cohorts run, share the month's rise to the states at once (`te_demog_share_war_dead`). Then, under Full, `te_demog_ms_monthly`: the Crash Campaign ends itself once its five years have run ; under Full, `te_demog_wave_war_monthly`: the event wave's war tracker (§ Phase 3: the event wave) |
| `on_yearly_pulse_country` (each country on its own day) | country | `te_demog_country_yearly`: the war shock, then the year's war dead reset; the national Wealth Concentration, Gini and #822's modifiers (`te_demog_wc_national`); then (cohorts run) `te_demog_country_census`: sums, lists, urban pattern (with phase 3's largest city and strength, `te_demog_up_country`), trend flags, the player's outline, the history sample. Then, under Full, `te_demog_ms_yearly`: the Family Policy measures kept (their modifiers put back where the variable is set and the law allows them, the rest ended with a notice) and costed at this year's GDP, then the AI's choices ; then `te_demog_wave_yearly`: at most one yearly event on this census's figures (§ Phase 3: the event wave) |
| `on_acquired_technology` | country | `te_demog_wave_technology_on_action`: under Full, The Last Generation? at once when the country has Biological Immortality (besides the moved lines' refresh in each state, below) |
| `on_law_activated` | the law (its owner) | `te_demog_ms_law_on_action`: under Full, a Family Policy measure the law in force doesn't allow ends at once, with a notice (`te_demog_ms_law_check`) |
| `on_lost_war` | country on the losing side | `te_demog_wc_shock = { AMOUNT = -5 }` when the war cost it a war goal (`exists = scope:victim_of_wargoal`), whatever the rule |
| `on_monthly_pulse_country` (`te_demog_country_monthly_on_action`) | country | besides the war dead: Wealth Concentration's financial boom (`te_demog_wc_boom_check`) and land reform (`te_demog_wc_land_reform_check`), whatever the rule |
| `on_yearly_pulse_country` (`te_demog_country_yearly_on_action`) | country | first `te_demog_wc_growth_update` (r > g's inputs and term), then `te_demog_country_yearly`, whose national refresh reads them; whatever the rule |
| `on_state_owner_change` (`te_demog_wc_owner_change_on_action`) | the state | clears the ownership shock's stored share (`te_dg_wc_sown`), whatever the rule, beside the moved lines' refresh |

`te_inheritance_on_actions.txt` no longer has its own `on_yearly_pulse_state` hook. Three more hooks sit in other files: the known-kill sites (below), the banking crash and the hyperinflation crisis (`te_inflation.1`).

### The census

- **Ring.** Each census state keeps `te_dg_f<k>` and `te_dg_m<k>` for k = 0–299, the birth year mod 300 (300 one-year slots, women and men apart; 150 until issue #1075, § The ring's 300 years), plus a pool (`te_dg_pf`, `te_dg_pm`, mean age `te_dg_pa`) for ages 300 and over, and `te_dg_ring` (300) to say so. A slot nobody holds has no variable, and the step skips it. **People, not shares**: values are stored in units of 1e-5, and a one-year cohort of 90-year-olds is a share near 1e-5, so its deaths would round away. `te_dg_scale` ties the ring to the engine's population and is applied lazily at the next sweep, while the display bands and class sums are scaled at once.
- **Seed.** The state's own life table times a growth factor read from a table by net reproduction rate gives the stable structure of its rates (§2.6), scaled to `state_population`; the seed's raw ring (radix 100,000) is normalised to people in two multiplications (see `scripting_best_practices.md`, § Writing a Yearly Per-Age Model in Script). Every 1836 state is seeded at game start and seeded again at its first pulse, so its first step, a year after that, compares a year's population change with a year's natural change (a step on a census taken off the pulse would compare 12 to 24 months with one year, and read the difference as migrants). A state without a census, or with one more than a year old, is seeded at its pulse. The US frontier's 1836 seeds give its men the 1840 census's ratios by age (§ Internal Resettlement in the census, and the US frontier).
- **Step** (once a year per state): `te_demog_step_begin` (the year's rates into locals, then the flows) and `te_demog_step_run` (the sweep over the ring, then the year's totals and the scale). The sweep is two guarded passes in age order (generated, `te_demog_sweep`); each age takes its group's death probability from five causes (infection and hunger, work, accidents and violence, maternal, chronic and old age), each a base schedule times a multiplier from literacy, standard of living, technology, laws and institutions; the newborn enter at 0 from fertility (§2.3: wealth, then education, child survival and urban life lower the desired number, and the means to plan a family close the gap). Flows are applied by **rate age** (last year's age), so the war window (the conscription pool's ages, 20–39 until phase 3: phase 2 step 4) and the migrant classes use that age.
- **Flows** (§2.5). War dead: the monthly pulse sums each war's `num_country_dead` for the owner, keeps the positive change, and shares it at once among the states by soldiers; a state's step takes what gathered since its last step (`te_dg_war_in`), 95% men, from the conscription pool's ages (calendar 20 or more, biological 39 or less; the women's 5% from the women of those ages; phase 2 step 4, the consequences design §4.2), so the dead cover the same months as its population change (shared at the country's yearly pulse, a state stepping in October would read March's battle dead as emigrants, then as immigrants the next year). Known kills: nuclear strikes and Violent Hostility record their dead on the state (`te_demog_note_kills`); the tactical strike now tallies the soldiers' half too, so the figure `nuclear_weapon_events.5`/`.6` print rises. Since 2026-10-19 Internal Resettlement's deaths in transit are known kills too, booked by their programme's profile (§ Internal Resettlement in the census, and the US frontier). Migration is the residual: the population change less the engine's own natural change (under Full, the trapezoid's window, § The census's births and deaths), war dead, kills and, since 2026-10-19, Internal Resettlement's known moves, which are booked by their programmes' profiles instead. The natural change is estimated in the pop walk from each pop's curves × its own multiplier, `te_demog_pop_birth_mult` / `_death_mult`. Those take the state's read plus literacy, starvation, class and workplace terms, the workplace's group reads carrying working conditions at the building's scale (`gen_demographics.py`, `engine_rate_terms`; growth probe, `docs/testing/demographics-growth-probe-results-2026-10-09.md`; the table's constants on top counted it twice until the self-check `working_conditions_read`, 2026-10-17). The state read alone made Closed Borders countries read −6 per 1,000 a year as emigrants. A residual inside 0.3% of the population is model error and becomes 0; otherwise, however large (a move over 25% in a year re-seeded the state until 2026-10-20), it is shared over migrant classes by a profile built from the destination's jobs, women's share of its workers, transport and the origin's crisis (`te_demog_crisis`: devastation, turmoil and war). Transport is a census-only type on its carriers since 2026-10-19 (modifier-types stage 3), so its tooltip says what it does: **Families Among Migrants** (`state_family_migration_add`) adds to the family kind's weight, 0.2417 before it: Paddle Steamer and Railways +0.10, Combustion Engine +0.15 (`te_demog_tech_injections.txt`), Commercial Aviation and Jet Engine Technology +0.05 each (`era_6.txt`, `era_7.txt`; the aviation pair is new, owner 2026-10-19); it was a has_technology_researched ladder from `demographics_params.py`'s table, at the same values bar the aviation pair. The labour kind's women's share is 0.1 + 0.5 × the women's job share × women's share of the state's workers ÷ 0.5 (women working as much as men), within 0.1–0.6 (`te_dg_labour_f`). Women's share of the workers is the census's own count at the last count (`te_dg_fws_wk`), else, before a count, what the sexes' rates give equal numbers of women and men (`te_demog_women_worker_share`); it also splits work deaths and feeds Late Marriage. **Until 2026-10-25** the women's-rights laws carried their own share as **Women's Work Outside the Home** (`state_female_work_share_add`, 0.1 + 0.15 to 0.38), which the labour kind, Late Marriage and, outside Full, the work-death split read, and which over Protected Class's 0.48 added up to 0.2 to the family kind's weight. It duplicated the census's own count of women at work (the participation model already reads the same laws' women's-work lines), and the families' term had no ground: women who can move on their own account don't make families move more. The line and the term went (owner, 2026-10-25); the 0.0417 the term gave No Women's Rights stayed in the families' base, so a state under that law books families as before. **The booking keeps the structure plausible** (2026-10-12; `docs/testing/demographics-migrant-booking-2026-10-12.md`): the residual is the engine's own migration (a save's per-state weekly migration statistics agree with it, in starving states too), and the engine moves whole pops, which have no age or sex, so the profile is the census's overlay. Booked the same way every year it hollowed out states that lost 2–7% of their people a year for decades (Hill Punjab 2 men per 100 women by 1870, Hyderabad 45) and piled men up where they arrived (Durango 199). So a step's profile adds to a class and sex at most 5% of its people and takes at most 3% (`MIGRANT_CAP_IN`, `_OUT`); what is left over is booked at one flat rate over every class and sex, whole families (`te_demog_migrant_rates`, generated; `demographics_model.migrant_rates`). And the labour kind's women's share moves to 0.5 as the state's men per 100 women aged 20–59 fall from 95 to 91 (departures) or rise from 105 to 115 (arrivals) (`LABOUR_BALANCE_*`; `te_demog_labour_balance`, `labour_balance_weight`). Below the cap and outside the ramps the booking is the profile's, as before. Re-walked with the run's own residual (`demographics_harness.py rebook`), the 2026-10-12 run's states stay within 90–111 men per 100 women to 1901, against 2–225.
- **Figures.** Each state stores bands (5 years, 0–4 to 85+; `te_dg_bf<b>`, `te_dg_bm<b>`) and, where anyone is past them, the people past each of the pyramid's row starts past 85 (§ The ring's 300 years), median age, age shares, dependency ratio, sex balance, children per woman, life expectancy at birth and 65, infant mortality, births and deaths per 1,000, and net migration. The country's census sums the bands, weights the rates (children per woman by women aged 15–49, life expectancy by people), counts urban people (everyone outside a rural workplace, Peasants counting as rural) and sets primacy, the effective number of cities and the pattern (Primate 40% or more, Dominant 25%, Balanced 10%, Dispersed). The player's country alone also gets the outline (`te_dg_pjf<b>`, `te_dg_pjm<b>`): its bands carried twenty years ahead, five years at a time, on its own average rates with no migration.
- **Trend arrows.** Each state and country keeps `te_dg_prev_<name>` from a step; `te_dg_stepped` is 1 when the figures came from a step and `te_dg_trend_ok` is 1 only when this census and the one before were steps. The step and the seed say which ran (the local `te_dg_from_step`), and a country has stepped when any of its states has. Until 2026-10-16 the flag read births above 0, so a step with none looked like a seed: the late game's lost births (fixed the same day) froze those states' births and deaths terms, since `te_demog_rates_refresh` skips a seed. A seed writes no births or deaths, so the first step's arrows would compare with nothing: arrows start at the second step (in an 1836 start, the country's yearly census two or three years in). The panel draws an arrow only while `te_dg_trend_ok` is 1 and hides births and deaths per 1,000 while `te_dg_stepped` is 0.
- **Lists** on the country (variable lists the panel draws, `te_demog_country_lists`): `te_dg_states` (its census states, largest first by the people their own census counted, the figure each row shows, at most 40), `te_dg_states_top` (its first ten, the States section's rows until Show All; `te_dg_states_n` counts them all), `te_dg_cities` (its three census states of the largest cities by `state_city_size_rank`). The number of effective cities is the scalar `te_dg_n_cities`; the list keeps `te_dg_cities` because the engine may keep a variable and a list in one namespace. A revolution's winner inherits `te_dg_census_year` but no list, so the civil-war repair (`inh_repair_after_civil_war`) draws them again at once.
- **History.** `te_demog_history_record` keeps a yearly sample (median age, children per woman, life expectancy, Gini, Wealth Concentration; since issue #1029 also births, deaths and net migration per 1,000 from a stepped census, each cause's share of the deaths, and three marker pips: war dead, a famine month, a demographic event) in a container per year on `te_dg_hist` for countries `te_history_country_is_tracked` accepts (the player and major powers), at most 100 years. The first yearly census overwrites the game-start sample when both fall in the same year. A famine month (`te_demog_history_note_famine`, the monthly pulse) and an event of the wave (`te_demog_history_note_event`) note their year on the country, and a famine month or an event after the country's census marks the stored sample at once.

### Variable families

All census variables start `te_dg_` (short: there are about 345 on a state, and each name is in the save); effects, values and loc start `te_demog_`. The full inventory is the header of `te_demog_effects.txt`. In brief:

| Family | Scope | Variables |
|---|---|---|
| Walk (every year, whatever the rule) | state | `te_dg_walk_pop`, `_walk_pop_prev` (the walk before's, the AI's population trend), `_lit`, `_sol`, `_wtfr`, `_eb`, `_ed`, `_agr_share`, `_soldiers`, `_bureaucrats`, `_urban`, `_urban_share`, `_fjob_share`, people and incomes by wealth band `te_dg_gn<k>`/`te_dg_gy<k>` (k = 1–41, only the bands with people) and their layout `te_dg_gini_layout`, `_gini`, building levels by holder `_lv_priv/_self/_ctry/_own` |
| Ring and scale | state | `te_dg_f<k>`, `_m<k>`, `_pf`, `_pm`, `_pa`, `_scale`, `_raw`, `_people`, `_pop_last`, `_year`, `_provinces` (the provinces at the last census pulse, for the province line), `_ring` (the ring's years, 300; a census without it is on the 150-year ring and is re-filed at its next step) |
| Bands and classes | state / country | `te_dg_bf<b>`, `_bm<b>`; the people aged 100, 125, 150, 200, 250 and 300 and over, `te_dg_of<i>`, `_om<i>` (i = 1–6, only where anyone is; a country's `te_dg_cof<i>`, `_com<i>`), and where the pyramid splits 85 and over, `te_dg_pyr_top` and each row's people `te_dg_pxf<i>`, `_pxm<i>` (i = 0–6, on states and countries alike; issue #1075); migrant classes `_cf<c>`, `_cm<c>`; the conscription pool's sums `_fam`, `_faw` (phase 2 step 4: the men of calendar age 20 or more and biological age 39 or less, and the women of those ages; they replaced the 18–40 sums `_f1840`, `_m1840`, which a census removes) |
| Rates and figures | state | `te_dg_e0`, `_e65`, `_imr`, `_tfr` (realized, × (1 + bz)), `_tfr_model`, `_natural`, `_means`, `_desired`, the cause multipliers `_m_inf/_ext/_chr/_work`, `_median`, shares, `_dependency`, `_sex_balance`, `_cbr`, `_cdr`, with `te_dg_prev_<name>`; `te_dg_mig_rate` (net migration per 1,000), `te_dg_count_mi` (the month of the last count); deaths by cause `te_dg_dc_inf/_ext/_chr/_work/_mat/_ontop/_war/_kill`, `_dc_total`, `_dc_lead`, `_dc_fit` (issue #1029); `te_dg_pyr_max` (the pyramid's scale, stored at the census so the bars don't each read 36 bands a frame; a country's too) |

### Wealth Concentration per state

Spec §4.2. A state's target is `owner.te_inh_law_amendment_target` (the inheritance law and amendments, #822) plus eight terms (`te_demog_values.txt`), clamped 0–100. **The land, tax, economic, public goods and slavery laws' parts sit on the laws** (since 2026-10-17, so each law's tooltip says what it does), and so does the inheritance law and amendment term (since 2026-10-21, on the mod's own laws and amendments: § Inheritance): script-only types in `demographics_wealth_concentration_types.txt` (`country_wealth_concentration_inheritance_add`, `state_wealth_concentration_land_add`, `country_wealth_concentration_tax_add`, `country_wealth_concentration_economy_add`, `country_wealth_concentration_public_goods_add`, `country_wealth_concentration_slavery_add`), the vanilla laws' lines in `te_demog_wealth_law_injections.txt` (Graduated Taxation's in `te_tax_vanilla_law_gates.txt`, the one file the tax code lets INJECT the vanilla taxation laws; a script-only line changes no rate) and the antitrust and intellectual property laws' in `extra_laws.txt`. They are not census inputs (Wealth Concentration runs whatever the rule), so they sit outside `demographics_modifier_types.txt` and a release keeps them. The land, tax and economic values are the old `has_law` table's, and no group holds two of these laws, so no figure moves; the public goods and slavery values are new (2026-10-21):

- **Land tenure**: Serfdom and Manorialism +15, Tenant Farmers and the two Latifundias +5, Commercialized Agriculture 0, Peasant Proprietorship and Homesteading −10, Collectivized Agriculture −20, times the state's agrarian share. Each of the four variants carries its parent's value.
- **Ownership**: 40 × (private share of the state's capital levels − 0.65), capped ±20: +14 when everything is private, −20 at 15% private or less. **Centred on 0.65, the 1836 share measured on a save** (2026-10-09): large countries' capital is 55–65% private, because farms, mines and workshops their own workers hold read self-owned. The old centre of 0.9 (#833) held almost every country 10–17 points down for the whole game (72 of 285 countries sat at the −20 cap in 1836, and the 2062 observer save read −11 to −20), so it was re-centred (owner). Capital is the walk's private, cooperative and state levels; the ownership buildings (Manor Houses, Financial Districts, company headquarters) read self-owned and are left out, as Subsistence Farms (read private) and government-funded buildings are. A Construction Sector is not government-funded in this mod (`REPLACE:bg_construction` drops the flag), so a state-owned one counts as state capital: in a small country it can be most of the capital there is (owner: left as it is).
- **Income inequality**: 40 × (the state's shown Gini − 0.40), at most +15 (reached at 0.775), at least −4 (owner, 2026-10-10). On the computed figure that is 28 × (computed − 0.143): the centre is 1836's median state, so most of the 1836 world starts near 0 (Britain, shown 0.55: +6), and Britain's industrial peak in the runs sits near the cap.
- **Taxes on wealth** (country): Graduated Taxation −5; under the tax code, 20 × the enacted dividend rate (`te_tax_view_en_div_rate`) more; at most −10.
- **Economic laws** (country, `te_demog_wc_econ_term`, owner 2026-10-09): how freely capital compounds and combines. Laissez-Faire +10, Extraction Economy +5, Interventionism −5; Guilds and Chartered Monopolies and Freedom of Contract +5, Antitrust Enforcement (`law_trust_busting`) and Regulated Utilities −5; the other economic system and antitrust laws 0 (state and cooperative property already count in Ownership); at most ±15. Every 1836 country holds a 0 or +5 law in each group, so the start moves by 5 at most; scores then rise under laissez-faire capitalism and fall under regulation, the shape of the historical record (top-decile wealth shares rose to about 1910 and fell to the 1970s).
- **Public goods** (country, `te_demog_wc_public_term`, owner 2026-10-21): whether health care, schooling and ideas are provided or sold. Private Health Insurance, Private Schools and Terakoya (a variant, at its parent's value) +5, Public Health Insurance and Public Schools −5; Traditional IP Protection +5 and Strict IP Protection +10; every other health, school and IP law 0 (No Health System, Charity Hospitals, No Schools, Religious Schools, No IP Protection, Creative Commons, Open Source Innovation, State Intellectual Property: nothing is yet sold, or nothing yet provided). From −10 to +20 in all, with no clamp, since a cap below the sum would only clip a law added later. **A term of its own, not part of the economic laws':** that one is capped at ±15, and a Laissez-Faire country with Guilds or Freedom of Contract already sits on the cap, so Strict IP, which the AI weights toward laissez-faire countries, would have been a dead line for the countries most likely to enact it. Strict IP is the one law at +10 because its rents fall on every industry's ideas, where a health or school law touches one sector. The mod's IP laws carry the line in `extra_laws.txt`, the vanilla health and school laws in `te_demog_wealth_law_injections.txt`. Wired like the economic term: `te_demog_wc_target` adds `owner.te_demog_wc_public_term`, `te_demog_wc_national` stores `te_dg_wc_t_public` for the panel's bar, and `te_inh_concentration_target` shows a change at once (an old save without the variable shows none until its next yearly refresh). **Not measured on a save:** a country whose start history gives it one of the private or public health or school laws moves by up to 10 in 1836, and the repository holds no start history to count them, so re-read the 1836 calibration on a save.
- **Slavery** (country, `te_demog_wc_slavery_term`, owner 2026-10-21): property in people, the largest single asset a planter class held. Colonial Slavery (slavery in the colonies only), Legacy Slavery (the slaves already held, none added) and Debt Slavery +10; Slave Trade +5; Slavery Banned 0. 0 to +10, no clamp (one law of five). **What sets the order is how wide the ownership is, which the supply decides** (owner, from the economic-history literature on Brazil and the US South: Frank on Rio, Klein and Luna on Minas Gerais, Slenes on the post-1850 internal trade, Gavin Wright on the cotton South). An open trade keeps slaves cheap, so artisans, shopkeepers and small farmers own a few and the stock is widely held (Slave Trade +5); a closed supply makes the stock an appreciating asset that prices the small owner out and concentrates it (Legacy Slavery +10); debt bondage hands people to creditors (Debt Slavery +10); colonial export plantations, run for absentee owners, were the most concentrated of all (Colonial Slavery +10). The first version had it the other way round for Slave Trade, because it took vanilla's own severity (Slave Trade at −50 progressiveness, Landowners +50%) for a measure of concentration; it is not one. The sources give the direction, not the size, and the figures in the report the owner read were not all checked, so +5 against +10 is a judgement; a flat +10 on all four is the other defensible choice. **A term of its own:** under Public Goods a slavery law's tooltip would read "Public Goods", and in the economic laws' it would meet the ±15 cap that Laissez-Faire and Guilds already fill. **A flat national line, not weighted by a state's slaves**, as the tax, economic and public goods lines are: the census walk counts no slave share (`pop_type_percent_state` is a threshold trigger, not a value), so a Colonial Slavery country raises its home states' targets as much as its colonies' (its planters' fortunes were held at home, which is what makes that tolerable). Weighting it would take a slave sum in the pop walk (`te_demog_walks`, one more `is_pop_type` test per pop a year) and a state type read as the land term is. The same wiring as the public goods term, with `te_dg_wc_t_slavery`. **Not measured:** 1836 countries that start under a slavery law (several do) move by 5 to 10.
- **Return on capital against growth** (country, `te_demog_wc_rg_term`, owner 2026-10-19; Piketty's r > g): 2 × (the real policy rate − GDP growth averaged over about five years), in percentage points, at most ±5, and 0 until the country's banking cycle has started (`te_banking_cycle_running`). Stored at the yearly country pulse by `te_demog_wc_growth_update`, first in the yearly on-action, so the national refresh, the stored target and the panel read one figure all year: `te_dg_wc_gdp` (its own GDP snapshot; the monetary system's `te_mon_gdp_last_year` is rewritten by another yearly on-action in an undefined order), `te_dg_wc_states` (the states it held then, `te_demog_wc_state_count`), `te_dg_wc_g` (each year's growth in log points, taken in at a weight of 0.2: an exponential average with no ring buffer; every country keeps it, so it is warm when a cycle starts), `te_dg_wc_r` (the policy rate less headline inflation, `te_demog_wc_real_rate`, as the stance gap takes it) and `te_dg_wc_rg`. **Growth is in log points** (owner, 2026-10-20): 100 × ln of the year's GDP ratio (`te_demog_wc_log_growth`), so a fall and the recovery to the same GDP cancel (the samples of −50% then +100% net 0; in percent, −50 and +100 averaged up), and a normal year reads as percent (5% is 4.88); against the real rate, in percent. Script has no logarithm, so it is the atanh series 2(z + z³/3 + z⁵/5 + z⁷/7 + z⁹/9), z = (r − 1)/(r + 1), each odd power kept as 100 zᵏ for the fixed point: within 0.0002 log points for r from 0.5 to 2, 2% short at 0.1 or 10, rising with r throughout. **A territory jump takes no sample** (owner, 2026-10-20, in place of a ±10 clamp on each year): every year's growth counts, however large, except a year in which the country's states changed (or an old save's first, with no count) and its GDP moved more than a tenth (the ratio under 0.9 or over 1.1). That year folds nothing into the average but re-bases the GDP, so next year's growth is measured on the new land. A colony's year and a real boom count; a conquest's jump doesn't. A GDP of 0 or below, this year's or last, takes no sample either and is re-based. A won revolution's winner takes the loser's count with its GDP. **The hovers show a compound annual rate**, 100 × (e^(g/100) − 1) (`te_demog_wc_g_shown`, display only, by an eight-term series with every term positive; a negative g takes the reciprocal): a halving's average reads −50% and a doubling's +100%, where the log figure reads −69 and +69. r > g itself compares the log figure. **The rate is the real one** (the build's call on the owner's "policy rate"): the engine has no nominal prices, so GDP grows in real terms, and the nominal rate (median 9.6% in a 2055 save) put 55 of 84 running cycles at +5; on the real rate the same save's high-inflation countries sit at −5 (median inflation 22%), which is what inflation does to bond fortunes. In an 1849 save the 22 running cycles average about 0. Under the simplified banking setting `te_inflation` stays 0. **The real rate it reads moves with #1084** (owner, 2026-10-20: the monetary deficit term capped and the dial's reach raised): in a 2057 save 72 of 91 countries sat at the −5 floor, most of them high-inflation microstates; at the 3–4% inflation the fix aims for, the investigation put about 47 at −5 and 34 at +5, so any Wealth Concentration calibration done before it should be re-read.

Continuity of title pins the target at the score. Each state drifts 3% of the gap a year and loses up to 10 a year at full devastation (10 × its 0–1 devastation). The national figure is the states' average weighted by where property is held: each level of the ownership buildings and of self-owned buildings counts 1, and the country's state-owned levels are shared by the state's share of the country's bureaucrats × 0.1 (when the weights total under 1 the states weigh by people, and by 1 each if people total under 1 too). It is the one refresh site of `te_inh_concentration` and the two country modifiers (`te_demog_wc_national`), which also rewrites each scored state's target from the law and taxes as they stand, sets the term bars for the panel and the most and least concentrated state (each shown only while that state exists and is still the country's). The target the law tooltip, the concept and the panel show (`te_inh_concentration_target`) moves at once with a law, amendment or tax change: the stored target shifts by the change in the law, tax and economic-law terms since the refresh, which move every state alike, and the panel's bars for those three read them live. Under continuity of title a note under the bars says why they no longer add up to the target. Shocks (`te_demog_wc_jump` moves every scored state, `te_demog_wc_shock` also refreshes the national figure; a country with no scored state moves its own figure): a year at war −1 to every state, at most −10 until peace (`te_demog_wc_war_shock`, first in the yearly country pulse, once the year's war dead pass 0.2% of the population); a lost war that cost it a war goal −5 (`scope:victim_of_wargoal`: a co-belligerent that gave up nothing is spared); a winning revolution of the left (Council Republic or Trade Unions in government) −20, from `inh_repair_after_civil_war` reading `var:te_cw_rebels_won`; a banking crash −5 at both `banking_crisis_wave_crashed` sites; the hyperinflation crisis −5 when `te_inflation.1` fires (its `immediate`, so riding it out takes it again each time the crisis returns after its cooldown) and −5 more under its currency-reform option (owner, 2026-10-20), each said in the options' tooltips; land reform, −10 × each state's agrarian share, the month Peasant Proprietorship or Collectivized Agriculture replaces Serfdom or Tenant Farmers (each with its variants, `has_law_or_variant`, through `te_demog_wc_land_code`; compared with last month's law in `te_dg_wc_land`, so every way a law changes counts and no vanilla law carries an `on_activate`; Commercialized Agriculture in between breaks the chain. A won revolution counts too: the rebels store their own law through the war and a winner's variables take precedence, so `inh_repair_after_civil_war` gives the winner the old government's `te_dg_wc_land`, `te_dg_wc_gdp` and `te_dg_wc_g` (`te_demog_wc_civil_war_inherit`), and the next month compares the old law with the rebels'). Upward: the banking cycle's Frenzy +5, once a cycle (`te_demog_wc_boom_check`, monthly, marked in `te_dg_wc_boom`, which goes when the cycle falls below Boom; every crash lowers the cycle to 40 or less once its option lands, so a crash re-arms it, but not at the crash itself, when the cycle can still read Frenzy). And per state, the **ownership shock** (`te_demog_wc_ownership_shock`, in the state's pulse): when the state-owned share of its capital levels (the walk's `te_dg_lv_ctry` over the three, the ownership term's capital filter) moves 10 points or more since its last pulse, the score jumps half a point per point, at most ±10, up as the share falls and down as it rises, whatever caused it: a privatisation or nationalisation, or one side's capital growing or shrinking faster than the other's (the owner's rule measures the share, not transfers). Skipped in the first year a share is stored (`te_dg_wc_sown`), after a change of owner (`on_state_owner_change` clears it), and under 20 capital levels, which also clears it; a move of the state's people skips nothing (owner, 2026-10-20: capital levels don't move with people, so a migration jump makes no share change spurious; until then a move of more than 25% did, the census's old re-seed rule). The 20-level guard was the build's call and is kept on the owner's call of 2026-10-20: in the 1849 save 603 of 862 states held under 10 capital levels, where one state-owned port or railway level is 10 points or more; between saves of 2052 and 2054, 19 of 656 states with 20 levels or more moved 10 points. Plague (§4.2's events) is dropped.

**What it moves** (§4.2's table, phase 2). The national figure sets political strength through two country modifiers, `inh_great_fortunes` and `inh_dispersed_wealth`; each state's own score sets the rest in that state through `inh_concentrated_property`, `inh_dispersed_property` and, in farming states, `inh_land_hunger` (values and refresh in § Inheritance). A state well above its country's figure (a capital full of Financial Districts, a serf province) carries the costs of concentration while the country as a whole does not.

The Gini is the grouped Gini over 41 wealth bands at the income stand-in's knots (1 or less, 2–5, …, 191–195, 196 or more), shown as 1 − 0.7 × (1 − the computed Gini) (§4.1; owner, 2026-10-10: the computed figure is the game's own distribution; the shown one scales down the equality it sees for the spread inside each pop, X fitted to historians' 1836 estimates). The stand-in, spending per head from the buy packages, runs uncapped to the top wealth level (200, the mod's `NUM_WEALTH_LEVELS`): until 2026-10-10 it was flat from wealth 60 and the last band held everyone above, which read a 1953 Colombia at 0.71 against 0.81 pop by pop and would read any country whose people mostly sit above 60 at the 0.30 floor. The walk adds each pop to its band (`te_demog_gini_band_add`, five or six `wealth >` tests) and computes its income in the band's leaf: people ÷ 100,000 × the band's line, so income is summed in units of 100,000 and a country of 4×10^9 people all at wealth 200 (9.5×10^8 a head) fits the fixed point twice over (the generator asserts it). Each state keeps the bands it has people in (`te_demog_gini_band_store`: 5–11 bands on average, so fewer variables than the old 28 on average, though a state of the saves checked held up to 18) beside `te_dg_gini_layout`, and removes the rest and an old save's strata sums; the country adds only states whose layout is the current one (`te_demog_gini_band_add_state`, which counts them in `te_dg_g_states`), so a state carrying an older save's 14 bands is left out until its own pulse, and with none the country keeps its last figure; one generated formula (`te_demog_gini_from_locals`) takes the Gini over the bands in order, with no sort, each running share cut once and multiplied by the band's people before the one division by all people. Britain 1836 computes to about 0.35 and shows about 0.55; of the 1836 save only Bikaner (BIK), with 72 people above wealth 60, moved with the uncapped stand-in (+0.012). The checks behind it: `docs/testing/demographics-gini-check-2026-10-10.md` (with its high-wealth section); the harness's `gini` prints the band figure beside pop by pop, and `--shift N` moves every pop N levels up.

### The Inequality effect

Spec §4.1, §7 (owner, 2026-10-19), **under Full only**: relative deprivation. `te_demog_census_inequality` (`te_demog_inequality_modifiers.txt`, radicals from movements and socialist and labor movement support +10% a unit) at multiplier (the state's shown Gini − 0.45) / 0.20 + max(Gini − 0.70, 0) / 0.20, at least 0 and with no cap (owner, 2026-10-20; it was 0–1; the steep part and the movement lines are the 2026-10-22 effects design's): +10% at a Gini of 0.65, +12.5% at 0.70, +42.5% at 1 (`te_dg_ineq`). The owner: "Even 20%, while significant, can be countered by other policies (e.g. institutions)." The engine has no lower-strata radicals type (the radical types are `state_radicals_from_political_movements_mult`, the state-wide one Concentrated Property and the youth bulge take, and `state_radicals_and_loyalists_from_sol_change_mult`; the lower-strata standard-of-living expectation is an integer), so it takes the state-wide one. Crime is dropped: no engine quantity. The one refresh site, `te_demog_inequality_refresh` (`te_demog_wealth_effects.txt`), runs on the state's yearly pulse after Wealth Concentration's (`te_demog_state_yearly`), with ROOT the state, on the latest walk's `te_dg_gini`, and takes the modifier and its variable off outside Full. Shown Ginis in the saves: 1849 median 0.41, 170 of 862 states above 0.45 and 5 at 0.65 or more; 2054 median 0.64, 627 of 755 above 0.45 and 360 at 0.65 or more, where the old cap of +10% sat. So under Full it is a rich-industrial-state effect early and close to universal late, as the game's industrial Ginis climb faster than history's (§4.1). The Nation tab's `te_demog_census_*` family places it on states (`gen_nation_tab.py`). The state panel's modifier rows leave it out: it lists, with Youth Bulge, Fewer Men, More Men, the Longevity Gap, Metropolis, Dispersed Towns, Primate City and Provincial Neglect, in the Demographics subtab's Modifiers section (`te_state_demog_modifiers`; owner, 2026-10-21).

### Family Limitation

**Natural fertility** (phase 2 step 4) is a third fertility type but not part of the means: `state_natural_fertility_mult`, on the women's-rights laws at vanilla's own birth lines re-centred on No Women's Rights (owner call (d), 2026-10-10: Women in the Fields −15%, Women Own Property −5%, Women in the Workplace and Women's Suffrage −10%, Protected Class −15%), multiplies the wealth term before the means: children per woman = wealth × natural × the practices (§ Late Marriage and Birth Spacing) × (1 − means × (1 − desired)), desired carrying family policy's factor since phase 2 step 3b (§ Family Policy in the census), natural floored at 0.2 (`te_demog_tfr_natural`, stored by the step as `te_dg_natural`). The means to plan a family come from two script-only state types (`demographics_modifier_types.txt`; modifier-types spec, stage 2), read with `modifier:` in `te_demog_means`: (0.4 + `state_contraception_add`, at most 1) × (0.3 + 0.7 × literacy) + `state_fertility_means_add`, at most 1 (0.95 until 2026-10-20; § The safeguards pass). **Contraception** sits on the means techs and adds, so research order matters: vulcanization +0.20 and feminism +0.15 (INJECTs in `te_demog_tech_injections.txt`), the Contraceptive Pill +0.05 (`era_7.txt`) and Modern Pharmaceuticals +0.05 (`era_8.txt`), fitted with `demographics_harness.py fertility`. **Fertility Control** (`state_fertility_means_add`, formerly `country_fertility_means_add`) is the shift literacy doesn't scale: State-Sponsored Family Planning +0.1, and history, events and phase 2's measures. `te_demog_family_limitation` carries +0.6 (`FAMILY_LIMITATION_MEANS`), and `extra_history.txt` gives it to France, whose fertility transition began about 1800 (§2.6). That is the only line in the system that names a country. Under Full it is only France's start of a general practice (§ Phase 3: Family Limitation and Cultural Hegemony's drift); outside Full it stays France's +0.6 for good.

### Late Marriage and Birth Spacing

Two customs that lower children per woman (spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-demographics-late-marriage-design.md`, approved by the owner 2026-10-11; plan `docs/superpowers/archive/plans/2026-10-11-demographics-late-marriage.md`; fit `docs/testing/demographics-late-marriage-2026-10-12.md`). Each is a share of a state's people, 0–1 (`te_dg_pr_lm`, `te_dg_pr_bs`), and multiplies children per woman by 1 − cut × share, outside the means: children per woman = wealth × natural × (1 − 0.10 × Late Marriage) × (1 − 0.20 × Birth Spacing) × (1 − means × (1 − desired)).

- **Start (geography, not culture).** Late Marriage is 1 in western, northern and central Europe and Occitania, 0.9 in north-western Iberia, 0.8 west of the Hajnal line in the east (the Baltic, Prussia, Posen, Slovenia), 0.6 in the rest of Iberia, 0.5 in Italy, 0.4 along the gradient (Mazovia to Slovakia), 0.2 in Kola and East Karelia, 0 elsewhere. Birth Spacing is 1 in Japan (Ryukyu excepted), 0.06 in China, Manchuria and Korea (the smallest share that brings China's projected peacetime growth inside +3 to +6 per 1,000), and 0 in India and elsewhere: with no raise of the wealth curve there is nothing for India's held share to cancel. A strategic region sets a value and a state region overrides it (`te_demog_pr_start_<P>`).
- **Drift.** Each census step moves a share 2.5% of the way to its target: the start less what its conditions have eroded, plus Late Marriage's drivers, within 0–1 (`te_demog_pr_target_<P>`). Contraception beyond traditional methods erodes both (the techs' `state_contraception_add` × (0.3 + 0.7 × literacy), from 0 at 0.1 to 70% at 0.3). Health care erodes Birth Spacing by up to 30%, read as the access medicine has reached above its base (`te_dg_acc` − 0.4, full at 0.5; a default flagged for the owner, 2026-10-12). Primogeniture or Undivided Farm Succession add 0.15 × the farm share to Late Marriage's target (their `state_late_marriage_farms_add` line since 2026-10-17, a census-only type on the law and on the amendment; the amendment sits only on Forced Heirship and Customary Inheritance, so the two never add to 0.30), and women's paid work adds 0.3 × the women's job share × women's share of the workers (`te_demog_women_worker_share`, § The census, Flows) ÷ 0.5 (the women's-rights laws' own share ÷ 0.48 until 2026-10-25). Since phase 3 each step also closes 0.5% of the gap to its neighbouring states' people-weighted mean, both ways (`PRACTICE_SPREAD`; one walk a step, `te_demog_practices_neighbours`, filling a local per practice), the late-marriage spec's §4.4: an edge state moves about a fifth of the way in 50 years, and in the overnight run's saves the spread moved no state's share more than 0.09 by 1887 (0.13 with straits).
- **Seed.** A state with no share (an old save's, a new or split state's, a rule switched on mid-game) takes the people-weighted mean of the other states in its state region that hold one, else its start less what its conditions have eroded. A neighbour across a border plays no part, and a census re-seed keeps the shares. A change of owner moves the people to a new state object, which carries none of the old one's variables. So each step also copies the shares onto the state region (`te_dg_pr_<P>_r`, the last state to step), and the seed takes that copy when no sibling holds a share: a whole region taken at once, by a revolution's winner say, keeps its shares. Its ring and medicine still re-seed, as before. They run wherever the census runs (Full and Display only) and reach the engine only through M, under Full.
- **The panel.** Both children-per-woman tooltips list Late marriage and Birth spacing beside the other terms, with women's mean age at first marriage (19 + 7 × the share); the Population tab's hover adds the country's figures. Option l logs the shares, their targets and the absorbed births sum.
- **The fit (2026-10-12; Stop A).** No raise passes the regional growth gate (#904's peacetime births less deaths by region), so the wealth curve stays at 6.0 and the cuts are the ones that fit children per woman best with no raise. India, Africa, the USA and Canada, the Middle East, South America and Southeast Asia stay outside their bands, which is calibration step 3's (a geographic mortality term).

### The census's births and deaths (phase 2 step 4)

Plan: `docs/superpowers/archive/plans/2026-10-10-demographics-phase2-engine-rates.md`; evidence: the growth probe (`docs/testing/demographics-growth-probe-results-2026-10-09.md`).

- **The engine's arithmetic.** Each pop's births and deaths are its SoL curve (`bare`) × max(0, 1 + every term added together). The census's term M is M = target / bare − 1 − replaced / bare − on_top × (1 − target / bare) + q × target / bare, for births and for deaths. replaced is each pop's bare curve × the terms the engine still applies per pop that the census models (literacy's −0.1 and mild starvation's), summed by the walk into `te_dg_w_ebr` / `te_dg_w_edr` (the generated `te_demog_absorbed_walk_init` and `_pop`, under Full only). on_top is the engine's state-level lines left on top: the state read less the census's term, fast mode's and the moved lines' pairs, floored at −1, past which the engine gives no events (pollution, devastation, global warming, a decree, an event); taking it × (1 − target / bare) off M makes each act on the census's rate, as its tooltip reads (owner, 2026-10-11). A pop's own lines (severe starvation, workplace lines) stay at the bare curve's weight: one state-wide M can't scale them without moving the other pops' rates. q is the moved lines' on-top family (below), script-only, which the census adds at its rate. The refresh keeps replaced / bare as `te_dg_rep_b` / `_d`, target / bare as `te_dg_tb_*`, on_top as `te_dg_os_*` and q as `te_dg_q_*` (console option n). The target is the model's own rate (`te_dg_cbr_model`, `te_dg_cdr_model`) at today's people, in the walk's units (events a month × 100,000). M is refreshed only at each census step, so a state line that changes between steps (devastation clearing, a decaying event modifier) leaves M's share for it in force until the next step (review of #885).
- **Starvation, per pop.** The engine applies both starvation penalties × each pop's starvation value, clamp((0.4 − food security) × 2.5, 0, 1), which the save stores as `food_security={ starvation= }`: mild (`starvation_penalty`, +0.6 deaths, −0.7 births) up to 0.5, severe (`severe_starvation_penalty`, +1.0, −0.9) from 0.5 at food security 0.2 to 1 at 0. The walk took severe flat until the famine probe (2026-10-11; #894), so its famine deaths ran 1.5–1.7× the engine's and the residual booked the difference as immigrants. It now reads both in 0.05 steps of food security at each step's middle (`gen_demographics._starvation_buckets`): severe deaths +0.5625 / +0.6875 / +0.8125 / +0.9375 and births −0.50625 / −0.61875 / −0.73125 / −0.84375 at food security ≥ 0.15 / ≥ 0.10 / ≥ 0.05 / below. The model and `predict` take each pop's exact value (`demographics_model.starvation_value`). Mild is absorbed (below); severe stays on top at the bare curve's weight (owner). Evidence: `docs/testing/demographics-phase2-engine-rates-2026-10-10.md`, "The severe term".
- **The floor.** The state read less the census's, fast mode's and the moved lines' own terms, plus M, stays at or above −1, the engine's own per-pop floor (a plain pop's events reach 0 there; Q7's −3 stopped births and the growth probe's −5 deaths); when that read alone is past it, M stays at 0. A floored state sets `te_dg_rate_clamped`. The floor binds only where the absorbed per-pop lines (mild hunger's) alone pass the census's rate, or a state line takes the read past −1. M has no ceiling: target / bare is at most the model's rate over the curves' lowest, and a walk under one person at the lowest curve (`te_demog_k_rate_bare_min`, 80) leaves the terms as they are. Until 2026-10-20 the floor was −0.8 (the probes' measured −0.9 less literacy's −0.1) and M at most +3; in the owner's 2057 game the floor held about 260 late states, 1.9 billion people, at a fifth of the bare curve, so the engine killed 2.3 times the census's target (owner: "replacing something that might be wrong with something that is definitely wrong"). The engine's line from −0.9 to −1 is unmeasured: the self-check `rate_below_measured` watches it (`docs/testing/demographics-playtest.md`).
- **Applied as** a fixed-sign pair per kind, `te_demog_census_births_up`/`_down` and `te_demog_census_deaths_up`/`_down` (`te_demog_modifiers.txt`, ±1 fields, multiplier |M|, at most one of each pair), and Private Health Insurance's wealth line on `te_demog_census_wealth_up`/`_down` (multiplier |`te_dg_w`|), refreshed only by `te_demog_rates_apply`. `te_demog_rates_refresh` runs straight after the census, from the yearly state pulse and from fast mode's clock step (`te_demog_events.2`): ROOT is the state both times, as the multiplier needs. A seed leaves M alone (a seed also clears the target and the scales); Display only and Disabled clear M at the state's next step. The six carry the mod's blank `modifier_system.dds`, so the state panel hides them (by name, `gui/states_panel.gui`, and in `gui_state_hidden_modifier_count`); the birth-rate and mortality breakdowns name them "Census: Births", "Census: Deaths" and "Census: Deaths by Wealth".
- **The ring follows the engine.** Each step scales its children per woman and its five cause multipliers by how far the engine's expected events over the window ran from the target (`te_demog_on_top_scales`: bz, dz, at least −1, no events, and no ceiling since 2026-10-20, each age's probability already capped at 1; Full only, once a target exists). Births added on top are newborns. Deaths added on top fell by the model's age pattern (owner, 2026-10-10) until 2026-10-22; since, each natural cause's multiplier takes its own share of them (§ Causes of Death, "Deaths on top by cause"), so pollution's land on the old and famine's on children, and the rest (war and devastation, the census's lag, anything no tag names) still falls by the model's pattern. The step stores the model's own rates without the scales as the next target; where 1 + bz or 1 + dz is under 0.01 (the engine gave under 1% of the model's events) the last target stays, since the ring's events are too few to read it back from. Since 2026-10-20 the walk's per-pop death multiplier (`te_demog_pop_death_mult`) also takes the state's wealth line × the pop's wealth inside the floor at 0, as the engine does (probe P6), so the window's deaths, dz and the residual see what the census's pair (Private Health Insurance's line at its rate, the late game's slope) takes away; before, they ran high by the line × the mean wealth, about 0.3 of the census's rate at the slope's bound, and the residual booked the gap as immigrants. The start rate swaps the line in force for the refresh's new `te_dg_w`, on the bare deaths × wealth it reaches (`te_dg_w_edw`). A late-game state skips the calendar estimate of deaths by cause, which its own count replaces: calendar ages put an immortal state's deaths fifty times too high, which a famine's dz could take past the fixed-point range. The panel's children per woman, CBR and CDR are therefore the realized figures, and follow the window's events below; life expectancy, e65 and infant mortality stay the census's own life table, and so does the player's twenty-year outline (`te_dg_tfr_model`).
- **The window's events: the trapezoid** (owner, 2026-10-11; #894; reworked after the review of #907). The walk reads the engine's rate on the step's day, and the step books it for the whole window that ends that day. Germany's famine of 3 December 1897 was booked for all of Hannover's year to February 1898, and the residual read the deaths that never happened as 933k immigrants. Under Full the walk's tail (`te_demog_window_events`) now books the window at the mean of the engine's rate at its two ends: today's, and the rate per head the last step left in force (`te_dg_sr_b`, `_d`). The refresh stores that rate right after it sets M: the walk's rate, with its new M for the old one and without the moved lines' pairs it clears, on the bare curves those reach (`te_dg_w_eb0m`, `_ed0m`: the pops the engine doesn't floor at 0; severe starvation's births floor a pop's in a famine's lower food-security steps: below 0.10 in Germany's 1898 famine, at M about −0.28). Fast mode moves it by its own term's change. M changes only at a step and the fast term at a clock step (option k, which takes it off between steps, drops the start rate), so both ends carry them. Each end is the engine's whole rate, so every line that moved inside the window counts at the engine's own weight: severe starvation, the mild starvation M nets, a state line on every pop's bare curve, and the bare curves themselves. A first version averaged only an "on-top" share and missed the absorbed mild line and part of every state line's change. The model's own rate drifting is in neither end; it stays in dz's comparison with the target. The residual, the scales and console option n read the window (`te_dg_eb`, `te_dg_ed`). Births and deaths alike. With no start rate (the first step after a seed, a new state, an old save, fast mode's re-seed) the window is the snapshot. A refresh that sets no term (a seed) drops the start rate, so the next window takes the snapshot. A step with no births sets M like any step: `te_dg_stepped` says a step ran, not that it had births (#937's follow-up, 2026-10-16). A second pulse in one year refits M and stores the start again mid-window, as the refit itself already did. Twin: `demographics_model.window_events`; weight `WINDOW_START_WEIGHT` (0.5).
  - **Offline on the 2026-10-11 run** (first order: the run's M, pops and engine population as they were; only the booking moves; floors not modelled). Germany's 1898 residual falls from +933k to +357k, against about −300k a year before and after the famine. Over 1897–1901 together it falls from +651k to +453k: any trapezoid re-times the famine's deaths into 1899–1901 more than it removes them. Most of the rest was the walk's flat severe-starvation term ("Starvation, per pop", above): the famine probe puts its correction at −377k, −446k and −391k on Germany's 1898–1900 residuals as run (snapshot booking; first order, from 1 January snapshots), which brings the two full-famine windows to about the pre-famine baseline and leaves the 1898 steps' onset, which the trapezoid addresses.
- **The moved lines** (owner, 2026-10-11; `docs/superpowers/archive/plans/2026-10-11-demographics-engine-lines-script-only.md`). Every birth and mortality line on a law, technology or institution sits on a script-only type (`demographics_engine_line_types.txt`): vanilla's 14 lines on 9 laws by an INJECT that cancels the field and carries the type (`te_demog_engine_line_injections.txt`), the mod's 22 in place. The engine sums the types per state as it sums the fields (institution levels in incorporated states, Impact of Institutions), and `te_demog_lines_refresh` re-applies the two families' sum by a fixed-sign pair per field (`te_demog_line_<short>_up`/`_down`, generated, named Laws and Institutions, hidden from the state panel's rows) while `te_demog_lines_apply` holds: not Full, or no census term yet (`te_dg_mb`). The refresh runs on a new game (after the lobby), a law's activation, a technology, a change of owner, incorporation, a new state and every month (institution levels have no on-action), each with ROOT the state (`te_demog_events.4` for the law, technology and global hooks; `on_law_activated`'s ROOT is the law, so its states are the owner's, and the law and technology hooks wait for `has_game_started`, since history's are the after-lobby hook's), and touches a pair only when its sum changed. It first takes off a census term that is no longer the census's (a rule switched off Full, or a save from before the moved lines, which has no `te_dg_q_b`), so the term and the pairs are never both in force. Nor is a state left with neither: a state holding M's variables without the modifiers they call for (a save quirk, a state that copied its variables) gets them back from the same hooks within a month (`te_demog_rates_heal`, #937), as W's are (`te_demog_workforce_heal`), since the pairs' gate reads only `te_dg_mb`. Under Full the census's refresh clears the pairs in the effect that first sets M, and fast mode takes them off its average that step. A release, which has no rule, keeps all of it (`test_release_census_inputs.py`). `DM.engine_lines` and `DM.line_carriers` read the lines back; `TestEngineLinesMoved` pins all 36 and fails CI on a new engine line on a carrier.
- **Absorbed by the census** (the absorbed family, `state_demog_absorbed_*`): under Full the engine no longer applies these, and the census's own terms carry their effect: the SoL curves and literacy's −0.1 (per pop); the starving slope below SoL 4 (owner: the poverty term replaces it); mild starvation (per pop, its food security in the walk's 0.05 steps; owner amendment B: the poverty term was fitted without it); the health laws' mortality (access × treatment); child labour's class lines (owner: the census's smaller work term is the intended size); the women's-rights birth lines (natural fertility); the Pill's, State-Sponsored Family Planning's, Modern Vaccines', Antibiotic Mass Production's and Consumer Protection's lines (§8.4); Pro-Natalist Policy's +10% and Population Control Measures' −10% (phase 2 step 3b: the laws' force under Full is desired family size and the measures); the augmentation laws' mortality (flat chronic treatment: Medical Only +0.10, the other three +0.05; chronic cap 0.99 since 2026-10-20, 0.85 before, reaching only as far as health-care access does). Literacy's and mild starvation's per-pop terms are still engine-applied, so the walk nets them out of M. So, since calibration step 3 (owner, 2026-10-12), is one country-scope line on farm pops: the Landowners' Famine Reserves (`ig_trait_famine_reserves`, agriculture mortality −0.10, doubled while the group is powerful, as it is in 1836 India). Each pop employed in an agriculture building adds its owner's read of `building_group_bg_agriculture_mortality_mult` to the absorbed sum (`te_demog_pop_country_absorbed_deaths`, groups in `P.COUNTRY_ABSORBED_GROUPS`), the size the walk reads at the farm, so the trait moves deaths between a state's farm workers and the rest instead of out of the state. It was 4.6 per 1,000 of India's peacetime growth. Building-scope lines (working conditions, production methods, company lines, executives' traits) stay on top at the bare curve's weight.
- **Added on top.** The moved lines' on-top family (`state_demog_ontop_*`), which the census adds at its rate under Full: Communal Child-Rearing's −20% (a State Youth Center's method cancels it, call 9; Pro-Natalist Policy's and Population Control Measures' lines left this family in phase 2 step 3b); Full Equality and Protection's token births line, State Eugenics and the late-era techs (step 6); Private Health Insurance's wealth mortality, which scales by each pop's wealth (probe P6, owner, in game, 2026-10-11) and which the census applies on its own pair (`te_demog_census_wealth_up`/`_down`, Census: Deaths by Wealth) at its share of the bare curve, at least −0.005 a wealth level (owner, option b). Both reach M and `te_dg_w` at the state's yearly step, so under Full a law or technology that changes them takes effect up to a year later; outside Full the pairs follow it at once. `P.ENGINE_LINES_ON_TOP` and `P.ENGINE_FIELDS_ON_TOP` must agree with the families on the carriers (`TestEngineRateLines`). The engine still applies, on top: the Natalism decree; severe starvation (× each pop's starvation value); devastation and pollution (inside the state read: probe P1, 2026-10-10), turmoil, workplace mortality, non-homeland mortality, `low_pop_state`, unemployment, events, companies, principles and amendments. Each of those mortality lines names the cause its deaths count under in the Causes of Death section (§ Causes of Death, "Deaths on top by cause").
- **Old saves** get M at each state's next step, which takes no on-top scales (no target yet).

### Causes of Death (2026-10-11)

Plan: `docs/superpowers/archive/plans/2026-10-11-demographics-causes-of-death.md` (owner's design, 2026-10-11). Both the Demographics tab and the state subtab show a Causes of Death section after the overview (issue #1029): last year's deaths per 1,000 people, a pie of those deaths by cause with its legend (each row's hover its cause's rate against a poor country's and the factors that set it, the multipliers the section's rows used to show), and Health Care Access.

- **One factor table.** `demographics_params.CAUSE_FACTORS` names each cause's factors (infection: medicine, SoL, poverty, literacy, crowding, malaria; work: laws, safety; accidents and violence: laws, safety, turmoil; childbirth: medicine; chronic: medicine, laws, SoL). The model computes them (`cause_factors`), and the generator writes one script value per factor (`te_demog_f_<cause>_<factor>`) and each `te_demog_mult_<cause>` as their product, so the hovers and the census can't disagree. **The factors read only what the step stored** (`te_dg_acc`, `te_dg_trt_*`, `te_dg_in_*`, the last including `te_dg_in_sol` and `te_dg_in_lit`, the walk's SoL and literacy as the step used them; `te_demog_cause_inputs_store` in `te_demog_prepare` before its multipliers), so between steps the hover still multiplies to the row, even after a walk without a step (a second pulse in a year, the console's benchmark, option c), which rewrites `te_dg_sol` and `te_dg_lit`.
- **Medicine drifts.** At each step health-care access and the three treatments move a share of the gap to today's targets (`te_demog_medicine_drift` in `te_demog_step_begin`, before `te_demog_prepare`): `(target − value) × r + value`, r = 0.1 + `state_medical_diffusion_add`, at most 1; within 0.005 of its target a value takes it. The type sits on Electric Telegraph, Modern Nursing, Radio, World Wide Web and Telemedicine (+0.05 each, so 0.35 with all five), on the World Health Organization's convention (`un_pandemic_cooperation_modifier`, +0.05 times the UN's enforcement, `un_convention_multiplier`; moved off Intergovernmental Organizations) and on the Medical Outreach decree (+0.2, one state). The late game's market threshold mirrors the techs and the convention in `te_demog_lx_market_diffusion`. A seed starts at the targets (`te_demog_medicine_at_target`), as do a new state and an old save's state (the drift's `else`); a state re-seeded after a census gap or an emptied ring starts at its targets again (accepted; since 2026-10-20 no move of its people re-seeds it). The owner approved the numbers from `demographics_harness.py lag` (2026-10-11):

  ```
  Years of life expectancy behind the target after a change, at the spread's rate (the share of the gap a census step closes):
                                                           rate  e0 before  target     0y     1y     2y     3y     5y    10y    15y    20y
  1840s: Charitable Health System, Ministry of Health 1 to 3 0.10       38.8    38.8   0.04   0.04   0.03   0.03   0.02   0.01   0.01   0.00
  1870s: Modern Nursing arrives                            0.20       42.4    43.2   0.83   0.67   0.53   0.43   0.27   0.09   0.00   0.00
  1900s: Public Health Insurance at 3, before antibiotics  0.20       46.0    46.7   0.75   0.60   0.48   0.39   0.25   0.08   0.03   0.00
  1940s: antibiotics and vaccines arrive                   0.25       49.9    61.7  11.84   9.11   6.97   5.30   3.04   0.74   0.18   0.00
  1950s: a colony incorporated into that health system     0.25       47.5    58.9  11.39   8.76   6.70   5.10   2.93   0.71   0.17   0.00
  Today: Telemedicine arrives                              0.40       71.0    74.4   3.37   2.16   1.35   0.83   0.31   0.00   0.00   0.00
  ```

  A new medical technology is half felt (in e0) after about 6.6 years in 1850, 3 in 1900, 2.6 in 1950 and 1.6 today. The 1840s row is nearly empty: before Modern Nursing there is almost no treatment to spread.
- **Turmoil** raises accidents and violence ×(1 + 0.5 × turmoil), turmoil read as the 0–1 share `te_demog_crisis` reads. Vanilla's `state_mortality_turmoil_mult` ("Mortality per Turmoil", on Militarized Police, the Violent Suppression decree, the Second Amendment, `ig_trait_wounded_honor` and about 18 event modifiers) stays an engine line on top, which the walk leaves out (its scaling unknown, measured about 0): the census's term is the violence of unrest itself.
- **Policing and criminal justice** (owner, 2026-10-16): the laws factor of accidents and violence (`state_external_mortality_mult`, census-only) takes each police law a level of the **Ministry of Public Safety** (`institution_police`), on the law's `institution_modifier`, so it reaches incorporated states only and a law with the Ministry at 0 gives nothing: Local Police and Private Policing −2% a level, Dedicated and Militarized Police −3% (`te_demog_law_injections.txt`, `extra_laws.txt`; −27% at level 9). Until the PR's review the three vanilla laws carried a flat −5%, −10% and −10%, the full cut with the Ministry at level 1 (owner). Restorative Justice −4% and Rehabilitation-Focused −8% (fewer offenders return to violence; they also cap the Ministry 1 and 2 levels lower, so under a Dedicated Police Force with the Ministry at its cap each is a net −1% and −2%); Punishment-Focused carries nothing. Penal Labor Camps raise work deaths +10% (forced labour in mines and forests), as Child Labor Allowed does. No Police has no Ministry and no line. A Dedicated Police Force at level 9 under Rehabilitation-Focused criminal justice reads −35%, before the Ministry of Consumer Protection's −8% a level and the Combustion Engine's +30%; the factor's floor, 0 since 2026-10-20 (0.2 before), is far off. `test_demographics_modifiers.py` pins the carriers. The harness's 1950, 1990 and today scenarios hold the Ministry at 3, 4 and 5 (`demographics_harness.py medicine`: West 1950 e0 63.8, West 1990 73.7, Rich today 77.9 since #1045, every band in).
- **Malaria** (calibration step 3, owner 2026-10-12): infection ×(1 + the trait's excess × (1 − `state_malaria_control_add`)) in a state with vanilla's `state_trait_malaria` or `state_trait_severe_malaria` (`P.MALARIA_INFECTION`; the severe one's at vanilla's own ratio for colonists, 0.25 to 0.15). The map gives them to most of tropical Africa, three Indonesian regions and the Pacific islands. The step stores the trait's level (`te_dg_in_mal`, read with `has_state_trait`, which outlasts the technology that disables the trait's modifier, as vanilla's own quinine test assumes) and the control (`te_dg_in_malc`, 0–1). Malaria Prevention carries the control at 1 (`te_demog_tech_injections.txt`); Quinine carries none, since it protected colonists, not the people who lived there. The census's infection treatment reaches the factor through medicine, which multiplies the whole infection rate. The hover shows a Malaria line only where the factor isn't ×1. Fitted against Africa's band (spec §3).
- **Adults' infection** (#1045, owner 2026-10-18: the rich world in eras 9-10, well below it after): infection at ages 15–64 takes medicine a second time, ×(1 − 0.8 × access × treatment) on top of its multiplier (`P.INFECTION_ADULT_AGES`, `P.INFECTION_ADULT_MEDICINE`; `te_demog_infection_adult`, the local `te_dg_inf_ad` that `te_demog_enter_group` reads at those ages). The 1836 schedule's adult deaths are mostly tuberculosis, typhoid and pneumonia, which antibiotics and vaccines all but ended; infants keep the one multiplier (their rate carries the perinatal deaths and the infant anchors are fitted to it), and so do the old. Not in `CAUSE_FACTORS`' product, since it reaches only those ages: the state's infection hover lists it as a line of its own, and the Causes of Death estimate and the late sweep's count keep the adult bands' and groups' infection apart to apply it. Infection treatment's cap is 0.99 (was 0.95): the base game's carriers reach 0.94 by era 7, Personalized Medicine adds 0.03 (era 11) and Advanced Nanofabrication 0.02 (era 12, nanomedicine). On the harness's rich state the 15–44s' infection deaths are 4.7 a year per 100,000 today and at era 10 (the rich world's 3–6), 2.1 at era 11 and 0.7 at era 12; immortals at 50 years die at 1.0 per 1,000, infection 3% of it (40% before).
- **Modern safety** (owner, 2026-10-16): work and accidents and violence ×(1 − the share the safety technologies prevent, at most 0.95; era 7-9, and Autonomous Vehicles in era 11), a factor of its own beside laws, so it cuts deaths whatever the laws factor reads (that factor's floor was 0.2 until 2026-10-20 and is 0 now) (`P.SAFETY_TYPES`, `state_work_safety_add` and `state_external_safety_add`, script-only). Work: Prefabricated Construction 0.15, Industrial Robotics 0.35, Containerization 0.15, Knowledge Economy 0.25 (0.90 by era 9); accidents and violence: Modern Urban Planning 0.20, Computer-Aided Design 0.10, Cellular Networks 0.10 (0.40), and since the policing pass (below) Autonomous Vehicles 0.10 in era 11 (0.50: traffic deaths, the late-game design's §1.4 proposal, built as safety rather than a laws line because self-driving cars save lives whatever the laws). Each carrier holds its line in its own `era_N.txt` definition. The step stores each share, clamped (`te_dg_in_saf_work`, `te_dg_in_saf_ext`); a step from before stored none, so the factor reads 1 until the state's next step. It answers the late-game build's adult-mortality check (§ Phase 3: the late game): today's rich state's men die between 15 and 50 at 0.084 (band 0.03–0.09; 0.110 before, 0.126 with the Combustion Engine the harness's today had left out), its women at 0.056 (0.080; band to 0.045), whose excess was adult infection, in band since #1045's adults' infection factor (0.043; § Adults' infection above). Under immortality, where accidents and work are nearly all the deaths left, deaths fall from 2.1 to 1.5 per 1,000.
- **Nothing changes outside Full.** Drift and turmoil reach the game only through M. Under Display only they move the section's figures and the shown life expectancy, not births and deaths.
- **Medical Outreach** (`decree_medical_outreach`): +0.2 to one state's spread, 100 authority, Medical Degrees; `country_trigger = { te_demog_effects_run = yes }` hides it outside Full; valid only where it changes the state's next count (owner, 2026-10-23): some value is short enough of its target that the count, at the state's share of the gap without the decree, would leave it at least the snap behind (`te_demog_medicine_behind` on `te_demog_medicine_left_next`; a held decree is judged without its own line, `te_demog_medicine_behind_without_outreach` on `te_demog_medical_diffusion_without_outreach`, so it lasts exactly where it could be issued). Not at the targets, not for the last few thousandths the count closes anyway, not where the share of the gap is at its cap; the shortfalls count one by one (until 2026-10-23 their sum above the snap). It lapses once the state has caught up (Emergency Relief's pattern; until 2026-10-12 an issued decree stayed valid, and since the AI never revokes a decree itself, every AI one stood until the state changed hands: scripting_best_practices.md § "The AI Never Revokes a Decree"); the AI weighs it by the gap × the state's people (Road Maintenance's pattern). An AI issues it only with authority to spare: in #894's observer run East India and the USA, every state above 0.3 in 1890, had −85 to 74 authority free against the decree's 100 in the 1890–1893 saves, and East India's spare 165 in 1895 went to Promote National Values (score 1,441 against 279). **A release comments it out whole** (`comment_out_census_inputs.py` rule 3b: a decree whose `modifier` block is left with no effect line), with the six techs' lines. Its texture is a doctor's bag with a stethoscope under a red map pin, `gfx/interface/icons/decree/decree_medical_outreach.dds` (icon batch 6; vanilla Emergency Relief's until then).
- **Deaths on top by cause** (owner, 2026-10-22). The deaths the engine adds on top of the census under Full count under their own causes; until then they were a slice of their own, Added on Top, whose hover split them into the whole state's lines, severe starvation and other lines on some of its people. **Tags.** Every state-level mortality line the census leaves on top carries a tag beside it at its own value: a script-only `state_death_cause_<c>_mult` (`inf`, `chr`, `ext`, `work`, `war`; `demographics_modifier_types.txt`), which the engine sums and scales with the line. `demographics_params.DEATH_CAUSE_TAGS` classes each carrier: epidemics, famines, food relief and medicine as infection and hunger; pollution, the climate's heat, drugs, radiation and care of the old as chronic illness; disasters, massacres, crackdowns and mental health as accidents and violence; forced labour as work; devastation (the owner: its usual cause is war, natural disasters the other), raids, gas and the nuclear aftermath as war and devastation. Vanilla's carriers take generated INJECTs (`te_demog_cause_tags_generated.txt` in `static_modifiers`, `interest_group_traits` and `character_traits`); the mod's own, and pollution's INJECT (vanilla's 0.5 and the mod's 0.05), carry theirs by hand. Five vanilla lines of at most 5% stay untagged (`DEATH_CAUSE_UNTAGGED`: three companies' `prosperity_modifier`, an amendment's and two harvest conditions' `modifier`, blocks no read has shown an INJECT adds to). `test_demographics_cause_tags.py` fails CI on a mortality line with no cause, a tag off its line's value, or stale INJECTs; a release without the census comments the tags out with its other inputs. Each tag renders on its modifier's tooltip as a label, "Counted in Causes of Death under …", at the line's value. **The pops' own lines** are read by cause in the walk (`te_demog_absorbed_walk_pop`, Full only, pops the engine doesn't floor): severe starvation (`te_dg_w_sevd`) and non-homeland mortality (`te_dg_w_odh`) as infection and hunger, soldiers' and officers' class lines as war (`te_dg_w_odq`), other classes' as accidents and violence (`te_dg_w_odx`), and the rest of a pop's own lines, its multiplier less 1, the state's read, what the census absorbs, the wealth line, severe starvation's term and those two, as work (`te_dg_w_odw`: its workplace's and building groups' lines). **The window.** `te_demog_on_top_causes`, at the end of `te_demog_on_top_split`, books each cause's part at both ends of #907's window as the trapezoid books the rate. At the start, which the refresh stores beside `te_dg_ss_d` (`te_dg_sc_<c>` per head and the tag's read `te_dg_st_<c>`; removed wherever `te_dg_ss_d` is), a tagged line acts on the census's rate, the tag × `te_dg_tb_d` × the bare deaths the term reaches (`te_dg_w_ed0m`); at the end, under the M fitted at the start, the tag now less (1 − `te_dg_tb_d`) × the start's, so a line that arrived inside the window kills at the bare curve's weight. `te_dg_ot_<c>` is each cause's deaths over the window, signed (aid and relief lines are negative). A window with no start, or a start from before this build, has none, and the step spreads all of dz as one scale did. **The ring.** `te_demog_on_top_cause_scales` (`demographics_model.cause_scales`): the step's estimate now runs before the scales, at the model's rates, and each natural cause's multiplier takes 1 + rest + `te_dg_ot_<c>` × E / (the target × its own estimate), E the four's sum, the rest dz less the four's shares (`te_dg_ot_<c>` over the target): war and devastation's civilians, who die at every age, the census's lag and anything no tag names. The four add E × (1 + dz), as one scale did. A cause the model gives under one death can't take its own (`P.CAUSE_SCALE_MIN_DEATHS`), so its share joins the rest; a late-game state, whose calendar estimate can't place deaths by age, keeps one scale. **The panel.** Each cause's deaths on top on the census's count (`te_dg_dc_<c>_top` = `te_dg_ot_<c>` × the natural deaths over `te_dg_ed`) are its own; war's join the war dead (the slice War, Devastation); the rest splits by each cause's model deaths (the estimate over its scale, `te_dg_sg_<c>`). Each legend row's hover says how many were added on top (or spared) and what adds them (`te_demog_dc_top_code_<c>`). The deaths row's hover gives the census's own rate against the game's, ×(1 + dz) (`te_demog_st_ontop_rate`, `te_demog_cd_ontop_rate`), and the floor's note where the refresh's clamp bit (`te_dg_ed_clamp_d`). The old split's variables (`te_dg_ed_state`, `te_dg_ed_sev`, `te_dg_sev_share`) are still written, for the harness's ontop-fit (`scripts/analysis/demographics_ontop.py`). The pie's codes keep their numbers, 6 retired, so a save's history chart keeps its older years' Added on Top layer. Self-check `cause_tags_read` (the tags add up to the lines on top).
- **Fast mode** (console only): the fast term sits in the read, so the old split's whole-state part also carries K − 1 times a famine's share. The section isn't a fast-mode tool.
- **Severe starvation** is scaled by each pop's starvation value since #913, so infection and hunger's deaths on top follow the engine's famine deaths.
- **Deaths by cause** (issue #1029; `te_demog_cause_deaths_store`, at each step after the sweep). The sweep counts deaths, not causes, so the step splits its own: `te_demog_cause_deaths_estimate` (generated) runs the four causes' base schedules over the bands at the step's start (`te_dg_bf<b>`, `_bm<b>`, the people last counted, by rate age) times the step's multipliers, scaled by their on-top scales after it runs (`te_dg_m_<cause>`, work by sex), and their shares split the census's natural deaths (`te_dg_deaths` less childbirth). Under Full each cause's deaths on top are its own ("Deaths on top by cause" above) and the rest splits by the shares; childbirth's are the sweep's (`te_dg_mat`); the war dead and the people killed by events are the step's flows, as counted.
