So the slices sum to the year's deaths (`te_dg_dc_total`), and `te_dg_dc_lead` codes the largest (1–5, 7, 8, the pie's clockwise order; 6 was Added on Top). `te_dg_dc_fit` is the estimate over the deaths it split (about 1: 0.97 in the model's farm state, 1.00 in its rich one), the self-check `cause_deaths_estimate` (`docs/testing/demographics-playtest.md`). A state in the late game overwrites the bands' figures after its late sweep, which counts the four causes itself (`te_demog_lx_causes_at`, `te_demog_lx_cause_deaths`, generated; `demographics_model.lx_cause_deaths`), the untreated by their age group and the treated at their biological one, so its fit is 1. The bands put an immortal state's young bodies at their calendar ages: 50 years into Biological Immortality they gave chronic illness 89% of the deaths against a true 23%. A seed counts no deaths and sets them 0. The country's are its states' summed (`te_demog_cause_deaths_country_store`), with the multipliers and access weighted by people (maternal by births). The model's twin is `demographics_model.cause_deaths` (`test_demographics_cause_deaths.py`).

### The safeguards pass: medicine, floors and the life table's tail (2026-10-20)

The owner's calls of 2026-10-20, from the safeguards inventory of the 2057 EU save (every limit that binds, and why).
Each acts only through the census, so nothing changes outside Full; under Display only the figures move.

- **Chronic treatment to 0.99** (`P.TREATMENT_CAP`; was 0.85, headroom that bound nowhere). Technology alone reaches it,
  as infection's does: Modern Pharmaceuticals 0.3, Telemedicine 0.2 and Personalized Medicine 0.2 make 0.70; Genetic
  Engineering 0.05 (era 11) and 0.12 each on Molecular Assemblers and Biological Immortality (era 12) take it to 0.99.
  The augmentation laws' flat lines reach it sooner and past it only cap. The health bill counts all six carriers
  (`P.HEALTH_TECHS`, owner, 2026-10-20; the first three until then), so full technology adds +30% to the Ministry of
  Health's cost: molecular nanotech treats with expensive advanced materials, and the bill is a sink for an
  ultra-wealthy late-game country.
- **No floor on a cause's laws factor but 0** (`P.MORTALITY_MULT_FLOOR`; was 0.2). Each cause's laws, technology and
  institution factor is 1 + its types' sum, at least 0, the natural bound (a negative rate would add people). In the
  2057 save the floor held accidents and violence at 0.2 in 253 late states whose factor read 0.097 (its lines summing
  to about −0.9).
- **No ceiling on crowding's infection term** (was +50%, a guess): it follows the migration pull linearly. In 2057 it
  bound in four EU states (Île-de-France's pull 1.008 doubles its infection, against +50%).
- **The means' cap is 1** (`P.MEANS_CAP`; was 0.95, with no reason written), the natural bound of a share. 221 states
  sat at 0.95 in 2057.
- **The life table's open last interval.** The tables sum person-years over the age groups, which end at 145-149, and
  dropped the survivors at 150, so e0 stopped near 150 (65-83% of late states reached it). Now they live on at the death
  rate past 150, q a year: l150 × (1 − q/2) / q more person-years (life_table's mid-year convention), in e0 and e65
  (`demographics_model.tail_years`, `te_demog_lt_tail` from `te_demog_lt_finish`). The plain table takes its last
  group's rate; the late tables the pool's (§ Phase 3's life tables). q is at least 1 per 100,000
  (`P.LT_TAIL_RATE_MIN`, the fixed point's smallest yearly probability), so the tail is at most about 100,000 years and
  the product (radix 100,000 × 100,000) stays in the script's range. The old-age threshold still reads the table to 150
  (it is capped at 145 and reads None from 130). A table before the late game has a few survivors in ten million at
  150, so its e0 moves by under a thousandth of a year (the golden's rich case in the tenth digit). Under immortality
  e0 runs to about 1,700 years on the harness's state.
- **The display caps at 10,000** (owner: e0 shown raw). The panel, its hovers, the states list, the state row's hover
  and the history chart's hover show e0, its women's and men's figures, e65 and last census's e0 as they are up to
  10,000 and "over 10,000" past it (the list's 56-pixel column whole years from 999.95 and "10K+" from 9,999.5, so no figure rounds past its branch; the overview's reading
  drops "years" to fit): a `GreaterThan_CFixedPoint` switch at each,
  between a key holding the figure and the "over" text. The stored figures and `debug_log` lines stay exact. Past 100 the
  hover's note says what so long a figure means. The Life Expectancy chart's axis runs to the largest figure its samples
  hold, at least 100 and at most 10,000 (`te_dg_h_e0_max`, `te_demog_history_e0_axis` in the history store; the chart
  reads `te_demog_hist_e0_axis_shown`, 100 while an old save holds none), and a bar
  stops at 10,000; the hover says so.
- **Tests and checks**: `test_demographics_life_tail.py` (the script's tail in the fixed point, which rate each table
  takes, every shown figure behind the switch, the chart's axis); the model's tail and bounds in
  `test_demographics_model.py`; the golden's `SAFEGUARDS_DIGESTS`. In-game checks: `docs/testing/demographics-playtest.md`
  § The safeguards pass.

### Phase 2 step 1: the interfaces (2026-10-12)

Spec `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-12-demographics-phase2-consequences-design.md` §1; plan `docs/superpowers/archive/plans/2026-10-12-demographics-phase2-interfaces.md`. What phase 2's later steps read, computed and stored, and **no birth, death or workforce number moves in any game** (`test_demographics_golden.py`, below).

- **Two clocks.** The sweep keeps a calendar band pointer (`te_dg_cal`, the working-age start: 0 below 10, the childrens'-rights law's share at 10–14, 1 from 15; the share is the laws' `state_child_labor_participation_add` since 2026-10-17, Child Labor Allowed 0.3 and Restricted Child Labor 0.1) and a biological one (`te_dg_bio` on `te_dg_ab`, capacity and health need by the bands of `P.CAPACITY` and `P.HEALTH_NEED`), both entered in `te_demog_age_boundaries`. Until phase 3 the biological age is the calendar one. Deaths and births keep the rate age.
- **The pension age** is one country variable, `te_dg_pension_age`: the Standard position's 65 under Old Age Pension, none otherwise (`te_demog_pension_age_refresh`: game start, the yearly country census, `on_law_activated`). Every reader goes through `te_demog_pension_age` (the owner's variable, or 65 for a save from before step 1) and `te_demog_pension_kind` (1 Old Age Pension, 2 UBI or Post-Scarcity, else 0). Nothing compares an age with a pension literal.
- **The figures** (`te_demog_work_slot` on the sweep's existing accumulation, `te_demog_work_finish` where `te_dg_raw` is whole: after the seed's accumulators close, after the step's newborns join): the working-age share, the share of the working ages at work (it counts the workers past the end too, so it can pass the rates' ceiling where they far outnumber the working ages; the panel's row shows the working ages' own share, `te_demog_wk_at_work_shown`, at most 1 and in practice the ceiling, and adds those past the end as a third term, `te_demog_wk_past_pct`, so working age × at work + past the end = the workforce), the pensioners' share and the health need over 1836's. The working ages end at the pension age, at the old-age threshold under UBI and Post-Scarcity, and nowhere with no pension law (the pool then counts in them). After a late step that threshold is the state's blend the step left: `te_demog_prepare` keeps `te_dg_old_age` in a local before its plain life table writes the untreated's figure over it (`demographics_model.working_ages_old_age`; reading it after the table ended an EU state's working ages at 84 for 128). A threshold at or past `LX_OLD_AGE_NONE` (130, the panel's None) ends them nowhere, as with no pension law. Participation is start × [past the end ? the after-pension share : 1] × capacity × the sex's rate. The rates are in the game's units (owner, 2026-10-20): the historical rates × 0.7, step 2's fit of the game's count, at most `RATE_MAX` 0.7. Women's rate runs from 0.035 to the men's 0.644 by the women's-work family's sum, at least 0.14 for the lower strata's women. `te_demog_wf_target` = share × at work, step 2's target, already on the engine's scale. Until 2026-10-20 the rates were historical (men 0.92) and a hidden `WORKFORCE_SCALE` of 0.7 converted the target, so the panel read a workforce the pops never had (Paris 96% against 67%). The walk stores the lower strata's share, the pops' own ratios and the engine's workforce over people, under the cohorts only, through three gated calls (the walk runs under every rule).
- **The old-age threshold** `te_dg_old_age`: the age with 15 years of life left, women's and men's averaged, from the census's own life table (`te_demog_old_age_pass`). `te_demog_old_age_average` and `_common` both read it until phase 3.
- **Planned and unplanned births**: `te_demog_tfr_planned` and `_unplanned` split `te_demog_tfr` (they sum to it). The sweep's birth line is the generated `te_demog_slot_births`: today's single term while `P.ASFR_PLANNED_SHAPE` and `P.ASFR_UNPLANNED_SHAPE` are the same object, a two-term form when they differ (tested, not shipped).
- **The working-adult lines** (call 3) sit on two script-only families, `state_demog_womens_work_ratio_add` (the women's rights laws, Protected Class, Family Planning, Communal Child-Rearing, the Pill, second-wave feminism, personal appliances, Woman Soldiers) and `state_demog_replaced_ratio_add` (Old Age Pension's and UBI's per-level lines, Pro-Natalist Subsidies, and call 3's carriers: Restorative and Rehabilitation-Focused Criminal Justice, the two Ministries of Labour, Community Service, Mandatory Minimums, the Trade Unions' Solidarity and Bourse du Travail, Pollution Impact), each at its old value. Vanilla's are cancelled by INJECT; the mod's moved in place. A generated pair (`te_demog_line_working_adults_up`/`_down`, "Laws and Institutions") re-applies the families' sum in every game under its own gate, `te_demog_workforce_lines_apply` (not Full, or no `te_dg_mw`), and its own refresh beside `te_demog_lines_refresh`, so the births and deaths term never takes it off. Call 3's participation inputs (`state_male_labor_participation_add`, `state_labor_participation_add`, `state_work_capacity_mult`; census-only, a release comments them out) ride beside the replaced lines; the model reads them in the sexes' rates and capacity. The two rate lines are in the rates' units: the design's inventory × 0.7 (Restorative Justice +0.014 men, Rehabilitation +0.021, the Ministries of Labour +0.0035 and +0.007 a level, Community Service +0.007, Mandatory Minimums −0.007, the two Trade Unions traits +0.014); capacity multiplies and stays. Rosen's two lines stay on top (`P.LIVE_WORKFORCE_LINES`, call 12). `TestWorkforceLinesMoved` pins every line, and fails on a new live line in `common/` or a new vanilla carrier.
- **The golden** (`test_demographics_golden.py`): every census output of five fixture cases and the model's scenarios, recorded before step 1 under the interpreter's fixed point, every generated block and the walk's text; only step 1's new names may appear.
- **What changes in a game:** a state's workforce tooltip shows one "Laws and Institutions" line for the moved lines; an institution level's, an amendment's, the Trade Unions' traits', Woman Soldiers' and Pollution Impact's changes reach the pair at the next monthly refresh (an amendment's repeal or timeout the same day). The values are the old ones.
- **Self-checks** (owner, 2026-10-12, instead of an in-game gate): once a game, `workforce_amendment_type`, `workforce_ig_trait_type` and `pop_workforce_read` write a `TE_SELF_CHECK` line (`te_debug_demog_wf_selfchecks` on the country's monthly pulse, under Display only or Full). Their fallbacks and the in-game items are in `docs/testing/demographics-playtest.md` (§ Phase 2 step 1).

### Family Policy measures (phase 2 step 3a)

Spec: `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-12-demographics-phase2-consequences-design.md` §3.3-§3.7 (built from the spec, no plan; owner process, 2026-10-12). A measure is a policy choice within a Family & Reproductive Policy law, switched on and off by its button in the tab's Family Policy section, under Full only: every button and the AI pulse sit under `te_demog_effects_run`, so a release (where it reads `always = no`) never applies one.

- **The catalogue** (§3.4's starting values; step 3b's fit raised Child Allowance's and Honours' desired lines and cut Family Housing's upkeep, § Family Policy in the census): Child Allowance, Family Housing, Honours for Large Families, Restricted Contraception, Parental Leave, Free Contraception, Sex Education, Later Longer Fewer, Birth Limit (two children, one child), Rural Exemption (with Birth Limit), Crash Campaign. Which law allows which: `te_demog_ms_allowed_<measure>`. Under Communal Child-Rearing the form of government adds some (the PR's review, owner 2026-10-16): the law alone allows Child Allowance, Parental Leave, Family Housing and Free Contraception; with a Council Republic or Anarchy also Sex Education (`te_demog_ms_communal_utopia`); with a Single-Party State or Autocracy (or its variants) and Outlawed Dissent also Honours for Large Families and Restricted Contraception (`te_demog_ms_communal_dystopia`). `te_demog_ms_law_check` runs on every law activated, so a change of government ends what the new laws don't allow, with the measure's notice. While on, a country modifier `te_demog_ms_<measure>` carries its census types, its interest groups' `interest_group_ig_<group>_approval_add` and an authority upkeep (flat `country_authority_cost_add`: Honours 50, Later Longer Fewer 150, Restricted Contraception 200, Birth Limit 300 at two children and 400 at one, the Crash Campaign 300, rebalanced 2026-10-16 from 25-100 because a decree costs 100 for one state; the spec's §3.4) or the schools' cost (`country_institution_cost_institution_schools_mult`); a money upkeep sits on `te_demog_ms_<measure>_cost`, `country_expenses_add = 1` at the weekly multiplier `te_demog_ms_cost_<measure>` (a share of GDP a year ÷ 52), refreshed when it goes on and at each yearly country pulse, with its Budget Breakdown mirror (`country_te_budget_expense_family_add`: a Family Policy row under Programme Costs, `gen_budget_breakdown.py`).
- **The census's types.** Six script-only state types (`demographics_modifier_types.txt`): `state_desired_fertility_mult`, `state_urban_fertility_relief_add`, `state_means_literacy_add`, `state_maternal_mortality_mult`, `state_birth_limit_relief_add`, `state_sex_ratio_at_birth_add`, which the census reads since step 3b (§ Family Policy in the census). Free and Restricted Contraception carry the census's existing `state_fertility_means_add`. Parental Leave's women's-work line sits on phase 2 step 1's family (`state_demog_womens_work_ratio_add`, +0.02), which the moved lines' pair re-applies as a working-adult line today, as it does the women's rights laws', and step 2's participation model reads; its upkeep reads step 1's women's rate in the capital over the rates' ceiling, `te_demog_k_rate_max` (`te_demog_ms_women_at_work`), so it didn't move when the rates took the game's units. A release comments every line setting a type out (`comment_out_census_inputs.py` rule 1); each measure keeps its interest groups' lines.
- **The term.** `te_dg_ms_<measure>` holds the date it went on (`te_demog_ms_now`, the year with its months); its button can't end it for five years (`te_demog_ms_term_run`). Birth Limit's one button cycles off, two children, one child (`te_dg_ms_birth_limit_one`; the step to one keeps the term), off; its end takes the Rural Exemption along. The Crash Campaign has no off: the monthly country pulse ends it at five years (`te_demog_ms_monthly`), and `te_dg_ms_crash_campaign_end` bars it for ten.
- **Leaving the law.** `on_law_activated` (`te_demog_ms_law_check`) ends at once, with a notice (`te_demog_ms_ended_<measure>`), every measure the law in force doesn't allow; its term resets.
- **Revolutions.** The winner inherits the variables and none of the modifiers (CLAUDE.md). `te_demog_ms_repair_after_civil_war` (from `te_civil_war_on_won`) copies a revolutionary winner's measures from `scope:te_cw_loser` explicitly (`te_demog_ms_inherit`, the winner's own value kept), as `inh_repair_after_civil_war` does, and `te_demog_ms_keep_all` puts back the modifiers of every measure whose variable is set and whose law allows it, and ends the rest with a notice: at the yearly country pulse (`te_demog_ms_yearly`) and at once from `te_civil_war_on_won`. Its main modifier is added only when missing, its cost always taken off and put back (a same-name `add_modifier` stacks).
- **AI** (§3.6). The family laws' `ai_enact_weight_modifier` (every game, owner call 7): Pro-Natalist Policy when the population shrinks (the walk's `te_dg_walk_pop_prev`, every game) or, where the census runs, 15% or more are 65 and over, not in a famine; Population Control Measures in a famine, with half its people or more in states at Migration Crowding's ceiling (`migration_crowding_mult_applied` ≥ 4.5, `te_demog_ms_crowded_share`: any crowding at all held for 73-88% of countries in the 1837-1902 saves) or a youth bulge (20-29s above 18%, the census), not while the population shrinks (by more than 0.1% a year: a deadband). The measures' yearly pulse (`te_demog_ms_ai_choose`, Full): `is_ai = yes` only picks whom it acts for; each measure starts on `te_demog_ms_ai_start_<measure>` (the need and its upkeep with a margin, read from the pulse's own budget: locals `te_dg_ms_auth`, free authority less each start's upkeep, and `te_dg_ms_money`, one money measure a pulse, since a modifier added in the pulse isn't visible to it; `te_demog_ms_ai_spent`) and ends, once its term has run, when `te_demog_ms_ai_keep_<measure>` fails. Restricted Contraception, Birth Limit's one child and the Crash Campaign need the target far off and legitimacy 75 or more. Tightening Birth Limit to one child needs the further 100 upkeep plus 25 free, and takes it off the pulse's budget (`te_demog_ms_authority_birth_limit_tighten`). Birth Limit's row shows the upkeep at its setting (`te_demog_ms_authority_birth_limit_shown`). **A player's Start** is greyed, as a decree is, until the measure's authority upkeep is free (`authority >= te_demog_ms_authority_<measure>`, reason `te_demog_ms_<measure>_authority_tt`), and Birth Limit's Tighten until the further 100 is (`te_demog_ms_birth_limit_tighten_authority_tt`); ending needs none, so a country short of authority can always stop a measure once its term has run (the PR's review, owner 2026-10-16).
- **The panel** (§3.7): the law in force (`AccessActiveLawFromGroup`), a row a measure it allows (`te_demog_measure_row`: name with its modifiers on hover, running cost, term, button), then "Under Other Laws", dimmed (`te_demog_measure_row_other`), each naming its laws on hover. The rows read script values (`te_demog_ms_state_<measure>`, `_until_`, `_cost_`), never a measure's variable. Each button's tooltip lists only its failing reasons (the rule, the law, the term with its end year, the Crash Campaign's run or bar, the Rural Exemption's need for Birth Limit) and what it does. Under Display only, one line above the rows says the measures act only under Full.
- **Self-check** (`te_debug_demog_ms_selfcheck_start`, `te_debug_demog.10`): once a game, the first measure that moves desired family size to go on reads the capital's `state_desired_fertility_mult` before and a week after (`TE_SELF_CHECK OK|BROKEN|NO_VERDICT measure_country_types`; NO_VERDICT, and the check re-arms, when the measures' expected change is under 0.01): does a script-only state type on a country static modifier reach the state? The fallback: `docs/testing/demographics-playtest.md`, Self-checks.

### The urban pattern's effects and Planned Capital (phase 3)

Spec §5.1 (the table: a choice, not a penalty) and §12's phase 3 calls (owner, 2026-10-12); built from the spec, no plan. **Under Full only**: the census computes the pattern wherever it runs, and the tab shows what it would do under Display only, but the modifiers and the decision act only under Full (the release precondition). A release's gates (`always = no`) hide the decision and apply nothing.

- **The largest city and the strength.** Each country census (`te_demog_up_country`, after the label) names the census state with the most urban people (`te_dg_primate_state`, the one primacy is measured by) and flags it with the country (`te_dg_primate_of`, cleared first from every state of the country; `te_demog_up_is_primate` reads `owner = var:te_dg_primate_of`, vanilla's comparison form, so a state that changed hands reads no), counts the census states and sets the strength `te_dg_up_s` = x for x = max((primacy − 0.25) ÷ 0.25, 0) up to 1, then (x + 1) ÷ 2 (the 2026-10-22 effects design's curve; it was clamp((primacy − 0.25) ÷ 0.35, 0, 1)): none at the Dominant label's floor, so Balanced and Dispersed are the baseline, 0.6 at the Primate label's 40%, full at 50%, 1.2 at 60% (Seoul's share of Korea's urban people), 2 at 100%. Nothing steps at a label's edge. Under three census states the strength is 0: a one- or two-state country is its largest city by construction (dozens of one-state countries read 100% in the 1903 observer census).
- **The modifiers** (`te_demog_place_modifiers.txt`), one refresh site, each state's yearly pulse (`te_demog_up_state_refresh`, from the on-action after `te_demog_state_yearly`, ROOT the state; multiplier `var:te_dg_up_mult`, the owner's strength, kept): **Primate City** on the largest city, Urban Center throughput +20%, University throughput +10% and migration attraction +25% at full strength; **Provincial Neglect** on every other census state, migration attraction −15%, turmoil penalties +15% and Cultural Minority movement support +15% (the 2026-10-22 effects design). Below 0.01 neither; outside Full both come off at the next pulse. A state that changed hands keeps its modifier until its pulse, as Wealth Concentration's do. The spec's "services and Urban Center throughput" is the one throughput line: the Urban Center is where a city's services come from, and a separate `goods_output_services_mult` would count its services twice and also raise Subsistence Farms' services.
- **The panel.** The Urban Pattern rows' tooltip (Overview and Where People Live) adds the effects: the strength, the largest city by name and each field as it applies, or why there are none (a Balanced or Dispersed pattern, fewer than three states), or, under Display only, what Full would do. The Primacy tooltip names the largest city. Values in `te_demog_place_values.txt` (`te_demog_up_shown_*`); no GUI file changed.
- **Plan a New Capital** (`te_decision_plan_new_capital`, Full only; shown from Modern Sewerage). Possible with Steel-Frame Buildings, a Primate or Dominant pattern, at peace and in no diplomatic play, not under the base game's Moved Capital Recently, 50 years since the last (`te_dg_pc_year`), 100 authority and a site. A **site** (`te_demog_pc_candidate`) follows the base game's Move Capital rules (incorporated, a homeland of a primary culture), is not the capital or the largest city, and holds 1% of the country's people. The decision opens `te_demog_capital.1` and sets `te_dg_pc_pending` (365 days; checked in `possible`, cleared by every option), so one site event at a time: the three largest sites, each offered only while `te_demog_pc_site_still_open` holds (still ours and a site, at peace, no play, the cooldown run: the event can stay open for days), or Not Now (nothing spent; the default, so a lapsed event moves nothing). A site's option pays 3% of a year's GDP at once (`add_treasury`, the banking events' "huge" tier: no `country_expenses_add`, so nothing joins the Budget Breakdown), takes 100 authority for five years (`te_demog_pc_works`, `country_authority_cost_add`) and gives the new capital **Planned Capital** for 20 years (migration attraction +25%, construction +20%, infrastructure +10, government buildings' throughput +10%). The modifier ends at the state's next pulse once it is no longer the capital (`te_demog_pc_state_check`).
- **The move.** `set_capital` takes a state region's key, never a scope (effects.log gives it no Supported Targets; vanilla and every Workshop mod on disk write a literal), so `te_demog_pc_set_capital` dispatches on the site's region, a branch for each of the 675 land regions (`scripts/generators/gen_planned_capital.py`; `test_demographics_place.py` fails when it is stale). The move, the date and the self-check sit behind a click-only marker (`te_dg_pc_click`): the option's tooltip walk would test all 675 limits every frame. The option names the site in its own tooltip line.
- **AI** (`te_demog_pc_ai_wants`, the same conditions for every country, no `is_ai`): a Primate pattern of 42.5% primacy or more (strength 0.7 since the 2026-10-22 re-anchoring; it was 0.5 on the old span, the same 42.5%, which this line called 45%) in a country of eight census states or more whose largest city Migration Crowding presses at its ceiling (`migration_crowding_mult_applied` 4.5 or more, ten times the reference density, the Family Policy AI's mark; some crowding is on in 73–88% of countries, and none at the ceiling before 1902 in step 3a's saves: the congested metropolis Brasília and Abuja were built to relieve), out of default, the money in its treasury and 150 authority. It takes the largest site most often (3:2:1), never Not Now.
- **Revolutions.** `te_demog_pc_repair_after_civil_war` (from `te_civil_war_on_won`) copies a revolutionary winner's `te_dg_pc_year` from the loser and puts the building's authority cost back for the time left, rounded up to a half year (a ladder of literal durations: no `add_modifier` takes a computed one); the state modifiers are refreshed at each state's pulse.
- **Self-checks.** `primate_state_flag` (`te_debug_demog_up_selfcheck`, at the census): once a game under Full, the largest city of a country of three census states or more reads as primate and no other state does. `planned_capital_moved` (`te_debug_demog_pc_selfcheck_start`, `te_debug_demog.60`): once a game, a week after the first planned capital anywhere, whether the capital stands in the site (BROKEN only when it never moved: `at_once` 0) and whether the base game's Moved Capital Recently came with the move (`penalty=`). The fallbacks are in the play-test list.
### The metropolitan share (phase 3, 2026-10-19)

Spec §5.2 and the owner's calls of 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20 (the crowding sign; all eight terms and all five effects as the spec writes them, each effect at most 10% at the Metropolis label, a cap the 2026-10-22 effects design lifted to about 20%; computed and shown under Display only and Full, effects under Full only; the Overspill on the real share); built from the spec, no plan. A Victoria state has one city hub and no cities below it, so the **metropolitan share** (`te_dg_mt`, 0-100), the share of the state's urban people living in its largest city, is a modelled stock: seeded at its target (a new game's first yearly count, a new state, a state that regains its towns), then moved 5% of the way there at each yearly count (`te_demog_mt_state_update`, before the census step, on last year's walk). A state with fewer than 5,000 urban people (one market town) keeps no share and reads None; outside the census no variable is written. Labels (owner, 2026-10-08): Metropolis 60 or more, Leading City 40, Several Cities 20, Market Towns below (`te_demog_mt_label`). Python twin: `scripts/analysis/demographics_metro.py`, which `test_demographics_metro.py` holds the script to term by term on a grid.

- **The target** (`te_demog_mt_target`) is 40 plus eight terms in share points, within 5-95: **capital** +35 (`is_capital`); **trade and finance** (the bar's label, "Port or Finance" until 2026-10-25) +30 in a World Market Hub (`is_world_market_hub`, the state through which the market area trades with the world: the base game places it in the market's best-scoring state, often its capital, Port or none; self-check `metro_world_market_hub`) and +1 a Financial District level up to +10; **area** −5 a doubling of the state region's area past 100,000 km² (`te_region_area_km2`), three doublings at most; **farms and mines** −30 × the walk's rural share (1 − `te_dg_urban_share`: the walk's own split, everyone at a rural workplace with Peasants counted rural); **urbanisation**, the inverted U (Williamson 1965) on the owner's national urban share at its last census: +10 at half, 0 at 10% and 90%, negative past them; **infrastructure surplus** −10 × (infrastructure − usage) ÷ usage, within 0-1; **crowding** −10 × Migration Crowding's applied multiplier ÷ its ceiling 4.5; **planning**, at most −30: `state_metro_share_add` on the Ministry of Urban Planning (−1 a level, a census type, so the release script strips it), −2 a level of a Settlement Authority on Planned Towns, −10 under Planned Capital. The weights are my call, fitted by reasoning from the walk's inputs to the owner's anchors (`demographics_metro.py`'s `ANCHORS`): in 1836 Île-de-France 69, the Home Counties 95, Buenos Aires 80 (Metropolis), New York 55 (Leading City), the Rhineland 25 and Brittany 23 (Several Cities), Texas and an agrarian Russian province under 10 (Market Towns); today Île-de-France 66, New York 65, Buenos Aires 89, Texas 29, the Rhineland 26, Saxony 39. No save holds the inputs, so the play-test checks them with `event te_debug_demog.140`.
- **The effects** (Full only; `te_demog_mt_state_refresh`, the one refresh site of the three modifiers, from the state pulse with ROOT the state; multipliers `var:te_dg_mt_mult` and `var:te_dg_mt_crowd_mult`, kept). **Metropolis** (`te_demog_mt_metropolis`) grows in a straight line from nothing at 40 (Leading City's floor) to full at 60 and on at half the slope (`te_demog_mt_e_pos_strength`: 1.5 at 80, 1.875 at 95; the 2026-10-22 effects design): `state_infrastructure_from_population_mult` +20% (a compact city is cheaper to serve), Urban Center throughput +10% (agglomeration; agglomeration economies run 3-8% a doubling of city size, and a primate metropolis stacks it with Primate City's +20%, about +39% at 60% primacy and a share of 80; not the Financial District's, which produces nothing, so throughput has nothing to scale, and `building_financial_district_throughput_add` is no registered type either: the game dropped it as unknown, #1096), `state_turmoil_effects_mult` +10%. **Metropolitan Crowding** (`te_demog_mt_crowding`, hidden bookkeeping: the blank icon, a term in `gui_state_hidden_modifier_count` and the state rows' name filters) carries `state_migration_crowding_density_mult` −10% on the 0-1 ramp (`te_demog_mt_e_pos`): the type is a state's crowding capacity, `state_population_density` divides by 1 + it, so a negative value crowds sooner (the spec's denser metropolis, which then lowers the target through the crowding term; owner, 2026-10-20: the metropolis crowds sooner). A model term, so it stayed off the extended curve and the share's balance points did not move. **Dispersed Towns** (`te_demog_mt_dispersed`) from nothing at 20 (Market Towns' ceiling) to full at 5 (the target's floor): infrastructure from population −20%. Several Cities is the baseline. **Fertility**: the census's urban term (`te_demog_tfr_urban`, 0.2 × urban share × Family Housing's relief) is raised by up to a tenth at the Metropolis side's full strength (`te_demog_mt_fertility_scale`, exactly 1 outside Full or without a share), so desired fertility in a wholly urban metropolis falls by at most two points more (my call: the 10% cap read on the term the spec names). The model's `urban_term` takes it as `Inputs.metro_scale`.
- **What moves under Full.** In a new game a capital that is also its market's hub reads Metropolis and takes the full set (London, Buenos Aires), as does an urban capital (Paris); an agrarian capital or a hub alone reads Leading City and takes part of it (New York at 55: three quarters); agrarian provinces under 20% lose up to 10% of their infrastructure from population; most other states sit in Several Cities and take nothing. Nothing moves outside Full: the census-off golden is untouched (`test_demographics_golden.py`, unchanged), and under Display only no modifier is applied and the fertility scale is 1.
- **The panel.** The state subtab's pyramid section adds Settlement under Urban People: the label and share, an arrow toward the target (`te_demog_trend_mt`), and on hover (`te_demog_mt_tooltip`, a type derived from vanilla's `TooltipWidgetType`, the graph tooltips' form) the share, the target, the eight terms as bars on a shared ±35 scale with each bar's reason on a locked hover, and the effects as they apply (or what Full would do). A state below the floor reads None. Where People Live on the country tab adds Metropolises, "N of M" states, with each label's count on hover (live counts, `te_demog_mt_count_*`). The custom tooltip is unproven in the mod; its fallback is a plain tooltip, `te_demog_mt_st_tt_plain`, already written.
- **The Overspill** (`te_demog_wave.9`) fires on the spec's trigger, a Metropolis-pattern state with crowding active: a census state whose share reads Metropolis at Migration Crowding's ceiling (`te_demog_wave_overspill_state`; the ceiling is the event's own condition, kept), and lands on the most urban such state. The stand-in (the national pattern Primate or Dominant and the largest city at the ceiling) is gone; `demographics_wave.save_rows` reads the share too.
- **Fast mode** follows the urban pattern's precedent: the share moves at each state's yearly pulse, not at the clock's steps.

### Family Policy in the census (phase 2 step 3b)

Spec §3.2, §3.5, §5 (built from the spec, no plan; owner process, 2026-10-12). The census reads the measures' and the family laws' types at each state's step, in the model (`demographics_model.policy_term`, `urban_term`, `means`, `newborn_split`, the maternal cause's "laws" factor) and in the generated script, which `test_demographics_family_census.py` runs against it. With no measure on and no family law's line in force, nothing changes (`test_demographics_golden.py` holds every number, with step 3b's three block edits named).

- **Desired family size** = education × child survival × urban life × family policy, within 0.1 and 1 (`te_demog_desired`; the cap is step 3b's decision: families can't plan more children than nature gives, and without a measure desired is under 1 anyway). Family policy (`te_demog_tfr_policy`) = 1 + `state_desired_fertility_mult` (Pro-Natalist Policy +5%, Child Allowance +14%, Honours +5%, Parental Leave +5%, Later Longer Fewer −10%, Birth Limit −30% or −45%, the Crash Campaign −20%), less Birth Limit's part × the Rural Exemption's 0.5 × the state's agrarian share (`te_dg_agr_share`), at least 0. Birth Limit's part is its owner's modifier's (`te_demog_ms_birth_limit_part`), since the engine sums the type over every carrier. Planned births follow desired family size and unplanned ones don't (spec §1.6: `te_demog_tfr_planned` reads the stored `te_dg_desired`). The step stores the policy term and the urban share Family Housing leaves (`te_dg_policy`, `te_dg_urban_left`; `te_demog_family_policy_store` in `te_demog_prepare`), and the children-per-woman tooltips show those (`te_demog_tfr_policy_shown`, `te_demog_tfr_urban` through `te_demog_urban_left_stored`), as `te_demog_natural_shown` does: a measure switched on between steps shows with the figure it moves, at the next step. With `te_dg_in_mat`, three variables a census state.
- **Urban life** = 1 − 0.2 × urban × (1 − `state_urban_fertility_relief_add`, within 0–1): Family Housing's 0.5 cancels half (`te_demog_urban_relief_left`).
- **The means' access** = 0.3 + 0.7 × min(1, literacy + `state_means_literacy_add`): Sex Education's 0.2, in the generated `te_demog_means`. The practices' contraception erosion still reads plain literacy (spec §3.5 scopes Sex Education to the means).
- **Maternal deaths** × (1 + `state_maternal_mortality_mult`, at least 0; 0.2 until 2026-10-20): the maternal cause's "laws" factor (`te_demog_f_maternal_laws`, on the step's stored `te_dg_in_mat`), Restricted Contraception's +25%. The state subtab's Childbirth row lists it as Family policy, and its Causes of Death section waits for a state's next step after an update from 3a (the gate `te_demog_state_causes_sgui` needs `te_dg_in_mat`).
- **The sex ratio at birth**: with Microprocessor researched (prenatal sexing, the spec's proposal) and a positive `state_sex_ratio_at_birth_add`, the step's newborns split 100 girls to 105 + it boys (Birth Limit 110, at one child 115; `te_demog_newborn_split` sets the locals `te_dg_nb_f` and `_m`, which `te_demog_fold_slot` and `te_demog_step_finish` read). Otherwise the split is the constants, exactly (100 × 100,000 / 205 is not the constant 48,780). The seed keeps the constants.
- **The laws under Full** (§3.2): Pro-Natalist Policy's +10% births and Population Control Measures' −10% moved from the on-top family to the absorbed one (`P.ENGINE_LINES_ON_TOP` keeps Communal Child-Rearing and the late-era lines), so M cancels them under Full and the moved lines' pair re-applies the same births total outside Full. Pro-Natalist Policy gains its own `state_desired_fertility_mult = 0.05`, which a release comments out. Under Full, Pro-Natalist Policy alone now moves a rich state's children per woman by about +0.04 where its births line added 10%, and Population Control Measures alone moves nothing.
- **The fit** (`demographics_harness.py measures`, §5, one pass): §3.4's starting sizes left the full pro-natalist package (Pro-Natalist Policy with Child Allowance, Family Housing and Honours) at +0.20 to +0.23 children in rich states at 1.25–1.36. Child Allowance went to +14% and Honours to +5%: the package now gives +0.27 to +0.35 in five rich states at 1.25–1.77 (the most where families want the most), Child Allowance alone +0.11 to +0.15. The package's money upkeep then reached 3.1% of revenue in the 1.77 state (its 0–14 share is 0.2), so Family Housing's upkeep went from 0.4% to 0.25% of GDP a year × the urban share: 0.37–0.52% of GDP, 1.8–2.6% of revenue at the game's rich-country tax revenue of about 0.2 of GDP (the plain-text 1949 and 1959 saves' ten largest economies: 0.07–0.33, medians 0.18 and 0.20, the investment pool's share of construction, income slot 7, left out). The coercive measures are reported, not banded: Restricted Contraception alone +0.36 to +0.40 (Romania's Decree 770 doubled births for a year), Birth Limit −0.24 to −0.31 and at one child −0.36 to −0.47 in rich states, −0.55 to −0.63 and −0.83 to −0.94 in the two high-fertility ones (China and India, 1975). A change to the mortality or fertility calibration moves these rows (desired family size follows child survival): re-run `measures` and re-fit rather than loosen its test.
- **Self-check:** none new. The one engine fact the build rests on, a script-only state type on a country static modifier reaching the state, is step 3a's `measure_country_types`; the law's type is option l's (types on laws), and `owner = { has_technology_researched }` from a state value was the census's existing pattern (`te_demog_family_transport`'s until 2026-10-19). Console option x logs the capital's reads (`TE_DEMOG_FAMILY`).

### Phase 2 step 2: the workforce, pensions and health costs (2026-10-12)

Spec `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-12-demographics-phase2-consequences-design.md` §2 (built from the spec, no separate plan; owner process 2026-10-12). Everything acts under Full only; Display only shows the figures and greys the buttons; outside Full nothing changes (`test_demographics_golden.py` keeps its Display-only and lines cases; its two Full cases were re-recorded for the work deaths' split). Effects `te_demog_work_effects.txt`, values `te_demog_work_values.txt`, constants `te_demog_k_*` from `gen_demographics.work_step2_values`, tests `test_demographics_work.py`.

- **The workforce term W** (`te_demog_workforce_refresh`, beside `te_demog_rates_refresh` on the yearly state pulse and fast mode's clock step; one refresh site, `te_demog_workforce_apply`): the census's target on the engine's scale less the define's 0.25 (`te_demog_wf_term_target`; the pops' own bases stay on top, call 4), on the fixed-sign pair `te_demog_census_workforce_up`/`_down` ("Census: Workforce", the bookkeeping icon, hidden from the state panel's rows). After a census step only (a seed leaves it, as M, but for the region's copy below); it replaces the moved lines' pair and lands on its target at each census step, and the engine's own pull toward a pop's ratio phases the change in (owner, 2026-10-20: until then W moved at most 0.01 a step, which bound in 29% of the 2057 save's steps, 418M people, on top of the engine's own lag); a guard keeps aristocrats' 0.2 + W + the lines on top at 0.05; no cap. The pair comes off when W lands (`te_demog_workforce_lines_apply` no longer holds); outside Full W clears and the pair returns that day. `te_dg_mw`, `te_dg_wf_rem` (the read less W and the pair: Rosen's androids, the console's probe, a line added later). Each refresh copies W to the state region (`te_dg_mw_r`): a state new to its owner (a conquest, a revolution's winner: a new state object with none of the old one's variables) lands W from that copy at its first census, a seed included, so the winner continues the nation's workforce rather than starting again from the flat lines. A state that keeps `te_dg_mw` but lost the modifier gets it back within a month (`te_demog_workforce_heal`, beside the pair's refresh in the monthly and owner-change hooks).
- **The pension setting** (country `te_dg_pension_pos`, absent = Standard; `te_dg_pension_since`): Early 60, Standard 65, Raised 70, Linked to Average and to Common Longevity (five below the country's people-weighted old-age threshold, at least 65, a year a year at the yearly census only, `te_demog_pension_link_drift`; both read `te_dg_old_age` until phase 3). Five buttons beside the pension age (`te_demog_pension_<pos>_sgui`), a five-year term to the month (`te_dg_pension_since` holds `te_demog_ms_now`, as the measures' terms), interest groups while in force (`te_demog_pension_pos_*` static modifiers, re-applied at every yearly refresh so a revolution's winner has them back). Leaving Old Age Pension clears it and takes the pension bill off that day. A revolution's winner takes the loser's setting and bills and has the IG modifier and both bills back at once (`te_demog_pension_repair_after_civil_war`, from `te_civil_war_on_won`). The AI's yearly pulse (`te_demog_pension_ai`, shared weights): a bill over 30% of revenue or debt over a quarter of its ceiling picks Linked to Average where its age passes 70, else Raised; unemployment over 10% picks Early; it goes back to Standard only once the bill is under 20% (and the debt has gone) or unemployment under 5%.
- **The pension bill** (`te_demog_pension_bill`, `country_expenses_add`): GDP ÷ 52 × the pensioners' share × B a week, B = 0.06 × the Social Security level, set at the country's census (Full, Old Age Pension); its mirror lists it under Old-Age Pensions in the Budget panel's Breakdown tab (`gen_budget_breakdown.SOURCES`). **The health bill** (`te_demog_health_bill_up`/`_down`, `country_institution_cost_institution_health_system_mult`): 0.8 × (need − 1), at most +1, plus 0.05 for each of chronic treatment's six carriers, `modern_pharmaceuticals`, `telemedicine`, `personalized_medicine`, `genetic_engineering`, `molecular_assemblers` and `biological_immortality` (owner, 2026-10-20: the last three added).
- **Work deaths** split by the census's own count of women among workers aged 15-64 at the last count (`te_dg_fws_wk`), under every setting the census runs, and before a count by what the sexes' rates give equal numbers of women and men (`te_demog_women_worker_share`); the flows' labour kind and Late Marriage read the same share. Until 2026-10-25 only Full split by the count, the women's-rights laws' share split the rest, and the flows read that share everywhere. The Demographics tab's twenty-year outline splits by the people-weighted mean of its states' shares (it read the owner's law's share even under Full until then). The model's step reads the ring's last count as the script does (`Ring.fws_work`).
- **The country's figures** (`te_demog_work_country_*`, people-weighted over its census states): `te_dg_wa_share`, `te_dg_at_work`, `te_dg_pensioners`, `te_dg_need`, `te_dg_old_age`, `te_dg_wk_past`, `te_dg_wf_engine`.
- **The panel:** Work and Retirement (`te_demog_sec_work` after the overview, with the buttons; `te_state_demog_work` after Causes of Death); the overview shows Working Age and Old Age From in place of the dependency ratio (its hover keeps it). The Workforce row reads working age × at work (+ past the end) = workforce. The workforce hovers say the share is by the game's count. The state's hover names the census's aim on the pops (`te_demog_wf_engine_target`) beside the game's own count, and W, a term on the pops' own base (`te_demog_wf_pop_base`), so base + W (+ the lines on top) is what the pops are set to and base + W's target the aim.
- **The fit** (`demographics_harness.py workforce SAVE`, `pensions SAVE`; no 2000-2020 save yet): capacity 1/0.95/0.85/0.7/0.5/0.2 from 60/65/70/75/80/85, the after-pension share 0.3, women at men's rate from a family sum of 0.35, the rates × 0.7 into the game's units (fitted as `WORKFORCE_SCALE`, folded into the rates on 2026-10-20), `HEALTH_NEED_1836` 0.952, the need weight 0.8, B 0.06 a level. 1836 world 0.248 (96% of states in 0.21-0.29), Rich today 0.415, women 0.87 of men, over-65s at work 0.52 of men in 1836 and 0.13 today in the game's units (the historical 0.75 and 0.18; the bands are restated × 0.7), the bill 20-24% of revenue at 18-22% pensioners (the 1953 save's revenue over GDP, 0.27), the health term +0.42 today and −0.003 in 1836.
- **Self-checks:** `workforce_ratio_scale` (the spec §1.8's stop rule) and `workforce_follows_target` (the pull's speed), from `te_debug_demog_wf_term_checks`; `docs/testing/demographics-playtest.md` § Phase 2 step 2 has their fallbacks and the in-game list.

### Phase 2 step 4: conscription, the youth bulge and sex balance (2026-10-12)

The consequences design's step 4 (`docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-12-demographics-phase2-consequences-design.md` §4; not the engine-rates plan's step 4, the census's births and deaths, which the older text here calls phase 2 step 4). Built from the spec with no plan document (owner, 2026-10-12); the modifiers act under Full only. **All three effects are on since the migrant booking** (2026-10-12; § The census, "Flows"). Step 4 shipped them held back (controller's decision, 2026-10-12, after its review) behind three switches in `demographics_params.py`, `CONSCRIPTION_EFFECTS`, `YOUTH_BULGE_EFFECTS` and `SEX_BALANCE_EFFECTS`, generated as `te_demog_k_conscription_effects`, `_youth_effects`, `_sex_effects` (1 on, 0 held back), because the census's booking of the residual distorted the men all three read (numbers below). Off, the census still computes, stores and shows the pool, T and y, applies no modifier and no sex-balance term, and the hovers say "not applied yet". The model reads the same switches (`conscription_applied`, `youth_applied`, the sex functions), and the tests run both ways.

- **The pool** (late-game call 21): men of calendar age 20 or more and biological age 39 or less, summed in the sweep through step 1's two indexes (`te_demog_accumulate_slot`: `te_dg_age` from `te_demog_k_pool_from`, `te_dg_ab` to `te_demog_k_pool_to`), stored as `te_dg_fam` with the women of the same ages, `te_dg_faw`. They replaced the 18–40 sums. Named `fam`/`faw` (fighting-age men and women), not the spec's `te_dg_pool`: "the pool" here is already the 150-and-over pool (`te_dg_pf`, `_pm`), and `te_dg_pool` a local of the fold.
- **The war dead's window** is the pool's ages by rate age (`te_dg_r` from 20 and `te_dg_ab` to 40, the biological age after the step: 39 before it until phase 3), so the ring loses its dead where the conscription term finds its soldiers. **This moves the census's pyramid under Display only as well as Full** (the census runs under both); nothing in the game outside Full. A census from before this build divides its first step's dead by its old 18–40 sums once (`te_demog_flows`); the census then writes the pool's and removes them.
- **Conscription.** T = max(`te_dg_fam` ÷ `te_dg_people` ÷ 0.139 − 1, −1), stored under Full as `te_dg_mc`; applied to `state_conscription_rate_mult` by the fixed-sign pair `te_demog_census_conscription_up`/`_down` ("Census: Fighting-Age Men"), and only from |T| 0.01 (`CONSCRIPTION_CUT`, the review's Minor 2). **No ceiling, and hidden (owner, 2026-10-16):** the spec's +0.25 cap is gone (`CONSCRIPTION_MAX` and `te_demog_k_conscription_max` removed, so a state whose pool is half its people would take T about +2.6; in the harness a sharp 1950s transition now peaks at +0.41), and the pair takes the mod's invisible icon (`modifier_system.dds`) like the census's births and deaths terms, so it is out of the state's modifier list: both name filters in `gui/states_panel.gui` and a `has_modifier` term in `gui_state_hidden_modifier_count` carry it (`test_hidden_state_modifiers.py`), and its name still heads the state's conscription breakdown. The youth bulge and sex balance modifiers stay visible. The ceiling figures below ("134 (15%) at the +0.25 ceiling", "T within −0.13 to +0.25") were measured with the cap. In the overnight run's 1848 save 32 states sat at T −0.5 or below (2–37 men per 100 women) and 134 (15%) at the +0.25 ceiling (115–145); in 1898 the lowest ran −0.96 to −0.68 (one of 4.3M people at −0.68); 29.5–34.6% of people lived in states past ±0.05 in 1848–1904. The reference is the 1836 world's pool share: 0.1389 in the census's own bands in the overnight Full run's 1836.2.1 save, 0.1390 in the model's 1836 agrarian stable structure (`demographics_harness.py consequences`). No floor but −1 (call 21).
- **The youth bulge** (held back by step 4: 73% of the 1898 save's bulge states sat outside 90–110 men per 100 women, the old booking's young men; re-walked with the booking, no state's 20–29 share passes 0.183 to 1901). y = the share factor (the share aged 20–29 − 0.18) ÷ 0.06 × the unemployment factor unemployment ÷ 0.2, each at least 0 and extended past 1 at half the slope, the product at most 2 (the 2026-10-22 effects design; it was each clamped 0–1), stored under Full as `te_dg_yb`, unemployment the share of the workforce with no work as every mod reader takes it, `te_state_unemployment_share` (§ Unemployment as a Share of the Workforce), stored at the walk (`te_dg_unemp`, `te_demog_work_walk_store`; read through `te_demog_unemployment`, as the event wave's Youth Bulge, the pension AI and the panel's Youth row read it). Stored, not read live: a scripted GUI reads the engine's trigger as none, so the panel and the effects read the one stored figure (owner, 2026-10-17). Not the engine's `state_unemployment_rate` bare, which reads about the idle workforce over all the state's people, a quarter of the share in 1836: the self-check `unemployment_rate_read` read 0.048 against the pops' 0.195 (2026-10-17), and now tests that scale against the walk's own count (`te_dg_unemp_walk`), the census's fallback. One modifier at multiplier y from 0.02 (`YOUTH_CUT`), `te_demog_census_youth_bulge`: radicals from movements +25%, turmoil effects +15% at full, the main demographic source of general unrest. The census's 1836 share is 0.159 everywhere.
- **Sex balance** (call 10), on `te_dg_sex_balance` (men per 100 women aged 20–59; `SEX_BALANCE_EFFECTS`). Held back, no `te_dg_sxb` is stored, so the births term is 1 and the women's rate gains nothing, and neither modifier is added. Step 4 held it back because the old booking hollowed out the men of states with years of emigration (below; not famine: the residual there is emigration too). On: the census's adults run 91.5–98 in every 1836 state, so the fewer-men effects start below 90, not 100: children per woman × balance ÷ 90, at least 0.8 (`te_demog_tfr_sex`, from the balance the step began with, `te_dg_sxb`); the women's rate + up to 0.07 (in the game's units since 2026-10-20) and feminist movement support +25% (`state_pop_support_movement_feminist_mult`: the spec's `_add` form is not a percentage), both full at 80 (`te_demog_census_fewer_men`). From 110, radicals from movements and turmoil effects +15% each at 130 (`te_demog_census_more_men`). The two modifiers read the strengths `te_demog_sex_fewer_men_strength` / `te_demog_sex_more_men_strength`, extended past full at half the slope to at most 2 (70 or 150 give 1.5, 60 or 170 give 2; the 2026-10-22 effects design); the births and women's-rate terms keep the 0-1 ramps. A seed takes no births or work term. Children per woman's breakdown shows the births term as "Few men to marry".
- **Refreshed** by `te_demog_consequences_refresh` straight after `te_demog_rates_refresh` at both its sites (the yearly state pulse, fast mode's clock step), ROOT the state; one refresh site each (`te_demog_consequences_apply`). Display only, Disabled and a census from before this build clear the modifiers and `te_dg_mc`, `te_dg_yb`. The country's pool figures are set only where a census state holds a pool (the review's Minor 3).
- **The panel.** Work and Retirement gains Fighting-Age Men ("28% (×1.00)": the pool's share of the men, × 1 + T; on hover the pool's share of people, the reference read from `te_demog_k_conscription_ref`, and what the census sets, or, with the switch at 0, "not applied yet"), a type of its own (`te_demog_fam_row`, `te_state_demog_fam_row`), the last row of step 2's section on the tab and the subtab; the overview gains Youth ("21% aged 20–29") while a state has a youth bulge (the country's while any of its census states has one), its hover's effects line "not applied yet" while held back; the sex balance's hover says the same. Children per woman's terms show "Few men to marry" (×1.00 while held back; no loc line may start with a newline).
- **Harness bands** (`demographics_harness.py consequences [SAVE...]`, 2026-10-12): the 1836 world term −0.001 (band 0 ± 0.05); today's rich structure (the workforce scenario at 1.36 children) −0.257 (about −0.25); a sharp 1950s transition's 20–29 share peaks at 0.230, y 0.83 at 20% unemployment (at most full), and its pool lifts T to the +0.25 ceiling (+0.41 once the cap went, 2026-10-16); with `--effects` (judged as if the held-back effects were on) the Soviet anchor's births ×0.911, women's rate +0.08 (+0.056 in the game's units since 2026-10-20), and the 1836 save has no state at either sex-balance effect; no state has a youth bulge in 1836. **Out of band under the old booking, so step 4 held all three back:** 29.5–34.6% of people sat in states with T past ±0.05 in 1848–1904; the great powers' 1904 terms: USA +0.10, Mexico +0.14, Britain +0.08, Italy −0.08; and the saves had 37–41% of states at a sex-balance effect against under 2% (19.7–27.7% below 90, 13.7–17.7% at 110 or more), built by the labour-migrant profile (US frontier states at 130–160 men per 100 women in 1898, Hyderabad 50, the Central Provinces 28), not war. **With the booking** (`rebook` on the 2026-10-12 run): 0.6%, 0.1% and 0.0% of states at a sex-balance effect in 1848, 1898 and 1901; T within −0.13 to +0.25, 0.4–1.6% of people past ±0.15 (14–18% past ±0.05, against 0.9–1.4% with every residual booked flat); the great powers' terms by decade within −0.05 to +0.07. The 2026-10-11 run's re-walk, which reproduces that run less well and runs high, gives 0.9–2.3%. The frontier is the price: Wyoming and North Dakota re-walk to about 101–103 men per 100 women in 1898 (the results doc's § The frontier). The aged society after the era-10 ladder (about −0.4) needs phase 3's biological age; no save is later than 1904, so the 2000 band runs on the scenarios.
- **Self-checks:** `conscription_term_read` (arms only while conscription applies: on since the migrant booking) and `unemployment_rate_read` (`docs/testing/demographics-playtest.md`, Self-checks). Whether the term moves a state's potential conscripts is the play-test's item: no script reads them.

### Phase 3: Family Limitation and Cultural Hegemony's drift (2026-10-12)

The parent spec's §13 ("Family Limitation as a general practice, not France's"; owner, 2026-10-12: build it as proposed, a national practice) and its §6 row for Cultural Hegemony; no plan document. Both are census inputs **under Full only**: outside Full France keeps history's `te_demog_family_limitation` at +0.6 for good and no desired fertility moves. Results: `docs/testing/demographics-family-limitation-2026-10-12.md`.

- **Family Limitation, a national practice** (`te_demog_fl_effects.txt`): a country's share of couples who stop at the size they want by methods older than any modern one, `te_dg_pr_fl`, 0–1. A country seeds at history's modifier's 0.6 if it holds it (France: history sets it as it sets France's Forced Heirship), else 0, at its census at game start (or its first census under this build). Each census year (the yearly census, or fast mode's clock census) it rises by 2.5% of the gap up to its target and 2% of the gap up to its neighbours' share, both from last year's share and **upward only**: a practice once learned is not unlearned, and France's share would otherwise leak to its neighbours' zero.
  - **The target** (`te_demog_fl_target`): smallholders under partible inheritance, the agrarian share × 1.0 under Forced Heirship (not with Undivided Farm Succession, which switches the rural cut off too), plus literacy above 0.8 (full at 1.0) × 0.3 × the church law (State Religion and its variants 0.5, Freedom of Conscience 1, Total Separation and State Atheism 1.5: since 2026-10-17 1 + the laws' `country_family_limitation_literacy_mult`, −0.5 or +0.5, each variant carrying its parent's), within 0–1; people-weighted over its census states (`te_dg_fl_agr`, `_lit`). In 1836 only France has a target (0.73), so no other country's share moves on day one.
  - **The neighbours** (`te_dg_fl_nb`): `every_neighbouring_state` from country scope, each foreign state weighted by its people, at its owner's share; a border-weighted mean, so Spain's French frontier counts and Portugal's size doesn't.
  - **The line**: `te_demog_family_limitation` itself, re-applied at multiplier line ÷ 0.6 by `te_demog_fl_apply`, the one refresh site (every census year: a revolution's winner inherits the share but not the modifier), so one "Family Limitation" line in the country's modifiers carries `state_fertility_means_add` = the line. The line is the share × (1 − the contraception erosion Late Marriage and Birth Spacing take, at the country's people-weighted literacy): the couples who practised it move to the modern methods the means already count, so the 20th-century West isn't counted twice. Below 0.02 there is no line. The census reads it through `te_demog_means`, as before.
  - **Forced Heirship's rural birth cut is folded in** (§13: "the two should be folded together"): `inh_forced_heirship_rural`'s −15% sits on the absorbed family, as Primogeniture's +10% does, so outside Full the moved lines' pair re-applies it (Laws and Institutions) and under Full the census drops it and the target's Forced Heirship term carries it. The rural refresh fires `te_demog_events.4` for it too (no month's lag), and the Primogeniture self-check skips a state whose owner just left Forced Heirship. The means can't carry the whole cut (they close at most the gap to desired fertility, about a fifth in 1836 France), so under Full the fold raises France's children per woman while it holds Forced Heirship, about 3.5 to 3.9 in 1837 (history 3.6), as the results doc reports.
- **Cultural Hegemony's drift** (`te_demog_ch_refresh`): a country factor on its states' desired fertility, `te_dg_ch_desired`, moves 20% a year toward 1 + 0.5 × exposure × (the hegemon's desired ÷ its own before the factor − 1), within 0.9–1.1. Exposure is the hegemon's cultural lead over it as the foreign benchmark reads it (`ch_benchmark_applied` ÷ the benchmark's max 3: (the hegemon's share − its own) ÷ 100 × 1 − its ideology resistance), only while its Cultural Hegemony journal entry runs (the mass-media era); the hegemon itself has none. The hegemon's desired is its census states' women-weighted mean (`te_dg_desired` on the country, under Full). A state's step stores the factor it took (`te_dg_hegemon`), which `te_demog_desired` multiplies in. Small by design: at a 25–30-point lead and a hegemon wanting two-thirds as many children, desired falls 2–5% and children per woman 0.5–2% (`demographics_harness.py ch-drift`).
- **The panel.** Both children-per-woman tooltips list "The cultural hegemon's example ×" among desired fertility's terms and "family limitation's part +" beside the means; the Population tab's country line adds the share of couples who practise it. Option l logs `fl_line=` and `hegemon=`.
- **The neighbour spread** of Late Marriage and Birth Spacing came with it (§ Late Marriage and Birth Spacing): the same iterator from state scope, symmetric as the late-marriage spec has it.
- **Self-checks** (`docs/testing/demographics-playtest.md`): `family_limitation_scaled` (a script-only state type on a country modifier, scaled by its multiplier, reaches the states; the type-on-a-country half is already seen in saves, France's states reading history's 0.6), `fl_neighbours_read` (the country-scope iterator returns the foreign border states) and `neighbouring_state_reads` (the state-scope iterator returns a land neighbour, and whether it crosses a strait).
- **Harness**: `demographics_harness.py fl-replay SAVES --anchors A` replays every country's share through a run's saves and prints children per woman today and with the practice against Gapminder; the state-adjacency snapshot comes from `demographics_adjacency.py --refresh` (the game's `provinces.png`).

### Phase 3: the late game (2026-10-12)

The late-game design (`docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-11-demographics-late-game-design.md`, every call in its §9; built from the spec with no plan document, owner 2026-10-12). Everything that moves births or deaths acts under Full only; Display only shows the figures; outside Full nothing changes (§ What changes outside Full, below). Inert before the first carrier: a state with no ageing carrier, no ectogenesis and no stored eligibility takes the plain sweep, so `test_demographics_golden.py` holds every 1836-today number (one new name, `te_dg_mab`, and the absorbed walk's two blocks re-pinned for the wealth slope's two locals).

- **The ladder** (call 3, call 4): `state_ageing_rate_add` on mRNA Therapeutics −0.10, Personalized Medicine −0.10, Genetic Engineering −0.05, Synthetic Biology −0.05 and Biological Immortality −0.70 (r = 0.9, 0.70, 0), and `state_rejuvenation_add` +0.03 on Biological Immortality (the pull toward 35). Until 2026-10-16 Biological Immortality carried −0.75 and era 11 reached 0.75; the owner moved 0.05 to Synthetic Biology so some of the slowing arrives an era earlier (`te_demog_lx_country_carrier` lists it, though Genetic Engineering, which it needs, already starts the market). Two census-only types; a release comments them out.
- **Who is treated** (§1.2-§1.3, call 8): a treated share and their mean deficit per five-year birth band, adults only (`te_dg_s<j>`, `te_dg_d<j>`); the pool keeps its own. Each step the late sweep (`te_demog_lx_sweep`: the plain sweep's slots with each band opened before and closed after them) kills each cohort's treated part at its biological rate age (the age groups' rates precomputed as locals, a five-comparison lookup) and the rest at the calendar one; the band then takes selection, ageing (+ c × (1 − r)), the pull (3% of its mean biological age above 35), the year's joining share and the cohort turning 25 at E. A band whose adults are all gone drops both variables. Bodies out of care age at 1 from where they are (call 9).
- **Eligibility, cover and access** (§4.2, call 12): E drifts toward its target at the medical diffusion rate, both ways; when it falls cover falls in proportion, when it rises cover returns first and then the untreated join with no deficit. The target is access people-weighted over the walk's 41 wealth bands, each band the larger of the public route (the drifted health-care access × the health system's cover: Public Health Insurance 1, Charitable 0.25, Private and None 0; Mandatory Augmentation cover 1 and at least 0.9; Human Purity none) and the market route, a ramp of ±10 wealth levels around the country's threshold `te_dg_lx_w` (80 at the first carrier, falling a level a year, +100% under Private Health Insurance, +50% under the Regulated Augmentation Market, faster with the diffusion technologies, 20 lower under Unrestricted Augmentation). **The laws' parts are census-only types on the laws since 2026-10-17**, so each law's tooltip says what it does: `state_longevity_care_cover_add` and `_floor_add` (0-1 each), `state_longevity_care_market_reach_add`, `country_longevity_care_banned_bool` and `country_longevity_care_price_fall_mult`, read in `te_demog_lx_values.txt` (the health laws' lines are INJECTs in `te_demog_law_injections.txt`; a release comments them out with the other census inputs). The two price-fall laws now add, as modifiers do (×2.5 together, ×3 before, when each was a factor).
- **The life tables** (`te_demog_lx_tables`): the untreated's (the model's own rates), the treated's and the state's blend, from the sweep's own deaths by age group. Since 2026-10-20 each has an open last interval (§ The safeguards pass): its survivors at 150 live on at the rate the pool died at that step, the untreated's at the last group's rate, the treated's at their pool part's rate at its biological age, the blend's at the pool's own (both parts weighted by their people, the model's rates without the on-top scales; `te_demog_lx_fold_deaths` keeps them as `te_dg_lxp_*`). The blend replaces the step's life expectancy, e65 and Old age from (Linked to Average Longevity follows it); the untreated's threshold is `te_dg_old_age_c` (Linked to Common Longevity follows it; `te_demog_pension_link_target_common`). Living to 100 for each; the longevity gap is the treated's less the untreated's. Desired fertility's child survival keeps the untreated e0 (children are never treated).
- **Rich pops die less** (§4.3, call 14): the census fits a slope to its wealth bands (each band's multiplier 1 − its treated share × (1 − rho), its share its access scaled to the ring's), and the refresh puts it on Census: Deaths by Wealth beside Private Health Insurance's line, the richest pop held at the treated's rate so no pop's deaths go below zero, and nets it out of M with the walk's bare deaths × wealth (`te_dg_w_edw`) so the state's total stays the census's. The floor's correction the spec mentions is not needed while the hold binds (the hold keeps every pop's own rate at or above rho on the census's); a second-order miss: the trapezoid's start rate doesn't carry a slope change.
- **Fertility** (§3.1-§3.2, §3.5, call 5): planned births follow the calendar as families intend them (today's shape over the fecundity it carries) × the fecundity of the body that bears them; unplanned births follow the body. Artificial wombs (State Youth Centers' levels on Ectogenesis × 1,000 births a year, over last year's births, at most 0.9) carry that share of planned births with no fecundity loss or maternal death, from the cohort's women and men alike. The postponement shift (§3.2's mean age at childbearing) is a parameter held at 0: its historical drivers would move today's calibration, and today's shape already sits at 30.1. Every census step stores the mean age at childbirth (`te_dg_mab`); a late one the share of births to women of 50 and over.
- **Births in fixed point (fixed 2026-10-16):** `te_demog_lx_births` multiplies each term's people and schedule first and divides by 100000 last. Until then it took TFR ÷ 100000 first, which the engine's five decimals cut to 0.00001 (or 0), and a share under 1 then cut the term to 0. Every late state under a TFR of 2 recorded no births, and those above about half. Zero births also read as a seed (`te_dg_stepped`), so the refresh froze the state's births and deaths terms. A save from before keeps rings short of young people. Console option c_world (`event te_debug_demog.1`, `te_debug_demog_reseed_late`) re-seeds every state in the world whose late game has started, and takes our census at once; other countries' censuses follow at their own yearly pulses, since `te_demog_country_census` writes to ROOT. Option c re-seeds only ours. Each state seeds again at its next pulse and steps a year after that; until then its frozen terms stand, since a seed leaves them.
- **The late-era lines** (§8.4, call 19): Biological Immortality's −20%, Mental Health Awareness's −5% and Mind Backups' −5% deaths move from the on-top family to the absorbed one, so outside Full they apply flat as before and under Full M cancels them; the census carries them as the ladder, accidents and violence −10% (Mental Health Awareness) and accidents, violence and work −50% × the state's share in longevity care (Mind Backups, since 2026-10-19: § Uploaded minds). `autonomous_vehicles`' proposed −10% (§1.4) is built as modern safety instead (0.10 of accidents and violence, § Causes of Death, 2026-10-16). The ectogenesis and cloning vats' own birth lines stay on top (§3.5).
- **Bills and the AI** (§5.2, call 13; §2.2): the health bill adds 0.5 × the share on the public route (at most the share in care); the AI's pension pulse picks Linked to Common Longevity when the gap passes 20 points and goes back to Standard under 10.
- **The gap's politics** (§4.4, call 15): built behind `LONGEVITY_POLITICS`, off until a play-test sized them and **on at the spec's sizes since 2026-10-16** (owner; generated `te_demog_k_lx_politics` 1), so the play-test checks them instead: Trade Unions and Rural Folk approval −3 × the gap × the share not in care (`te_demog_lx_gap_politics`, country), Labor movement support +10% × the state's gap (`te_demog_lx_gap_labor`). The country's refresh runs inside the census, so a game switched from Full to Disabled loses its modifier through `te_demog_lx_politics_clear` on the country's yearly pulse, outside the census; the state's refresh already runs on every state pulse. The approval lines are fractional (−3 × a multiplier from 0 to 1); the game adds an interest group's approval lines before it rounds (owner, 2026-10-16; `scripting_best_practices.md` § "Interest Group Approval Sums Its Lines Before It Rounds"), so the fraction counts toward the total.
- **The biological pyramid** (§6.2's toggle): each treated part at its biological band (`te_dg_bbf<b>`, `_bbm<b>`; the country's `te_dg_cbb*`), the pyramid's scale over both; past 85 its own rows by biological age (§ The ring's 300 years).
- **The harness** (`demographics_harness.py lategame`, 2026-10-12, one pass): one rich state from today's stable structure at 1.6 children per woman, everyone within reach, to 2300. The steady tables meet the design's bands (e0 76.7 today, 81.4 at 0.9, 87.1 with era 11 medicine alone, 102 at 0.75; Living to 100 8%, 22%, 34%, 66%, 81% under immortality; Old age from 74, 82, 88, 112, none); the 60-year projections too (immortality ×1.44 at 60 years, ×1.31 at 50 against §3.3's ×1.30 with the split; the women aged 100 at 50 years bore 1.83 children; health need ×0.85; the workforce with no pension 0.72). The per-band model tracks a per-cohort truth (treated and untreated apart) within 0.1 deaths per 1,000 and 1% of the people at year 50 (immortality at 20, 50, 90% treated; era 11 at 50%). Out of band, reported and not refitted (call 20's late check): adult mortality today, 35q15 0.080 for women and 0.110 for men against about 0.02-0.045 and 0.035-0.09 (the 1836-1900 external and work schedules, with women's work deaths at men's under Protected Class), which under immortality is the whole death rate. Under immortality the population keeps growing about 1.2% a year (×9.5 by 2300 on the full ladder): births 13.8 per 1,000 (the unplanned trickle of young bodies) against deaths 2.1; the brakes are the means and the wanted size (§3.4), and the game ends in 2136. **Since modern safety (2026-10-16; § Causes of Death)** today's rich state holds the Combustion Engine and the era 7-9 safety carriers, and the command prints each sex's 35q15 by cause: men 0.084, in band (infection 0.015, work 0.003, accidents and violence 0.031, chronic 0.038), women 0.056, still out (0.015, 0.003, 0.011, 0.029: adult infection and chronic deaths, #894's follow-up after #933). **Since the policing pass and Synthetic Biology's step (also 2026-10-16)** it holds the Ministry of Public Safety at 5 under its Dedicated Police Force and era 11 reaches 0.70: men 0.082 (accidents and violence 0.029), women 0.056 (0.010), women still out. Every band passes: e0 78.4 today, 83.3 at 0.9, 89.2 with era 11 medicine, 110 at 0.70 (the sketch's 0.75 bands moved by the model's own shift, `demographics_late.STEADY`); Living to 100 9%, 24%, 35%, 73%, 87% under immortality; immortality ×1.49 at 60 years and ×1.34 at 50; deaths under immortality 1.4 per 1,000, so the full ladder reaches ×11 by 2300. **Since #1045 (2026-10-18)** the rich state holds Pharmaceuticals (it lacked the era 2 technology's infection treatment, so its infants died at twice the Rich today anchor's rate) and adults' infection takes its second factor: women's 35q15 0.043, in band at last (infection 0.002), men's 0.070; e0 80.3 today, 85.5 at 0.9, 92.4 with era 11 medicine, 114 at 0.70, Living to 100 92% under immortality, the bands moved up with them (`demographics_late.STEADY`); immortality ×1.55 at 60 years and ×1.39 at 50; deaths under immortality 0.8 per 1,000, so the full ladder reaches ×13 by 2300. **Since the safeguards pass (2026-10-20)** chronic treatment reaches 0.85 in era 11 (Genetic Engineering's 0.05 with Medical Augmentation Only) and its cap in era 12, and the tables run past 150: e0 80.3 today, 85.5 at 0.9, 96.9 with era 11 medicine (92.5), 120 at 0.70 (114.6, 0.5 of it the tail), about 1,700 under immortality (141 cut at 150); Living to 100 48% with era 11 medicine, 82% at 0.70, 94% under immortality; Old age from 96 with era 11 medicine; deaths under immortality 0.65 per 1,000, people ×1.62 at 60 years and ×1.45 at 50. The bands those figures left moved with them (`demographics_late.STEADY`), and immortality's e0 has one (1,200-2,400). The accidents floor's removal moves nothing on the harness's state.
- **Call 16's B** (`demographics_harness.py pensions SAVE`, 2026-10-12): 0.06 a level stands. The 15 largest economies' median revenue over GDP is 0.32 in 1949, 0.27 in 1953 and 0.38 in 1959 (the bill 16-23% of revenue at 20% pensioners, inside 15-30%). The one plain-text late-game save, 2062's, reads 0.10 over all 15, but seven of them raise under 10% of GDP while spending 5-34 times that (the AI's chronic insolvency); the other eight read 0.26, B 0.059 (the harness prints both). A healthy save after 2000 is the better second reading (play-test item 13).
- **Cost:** up to about 100 variables a treated state (50 for the bands, up to about 110 where people live past 150 on the 300-year ring; the pool's 2, 15 figures, 36 for the biological pyramid and, where it splits past 85, up to 27 more) against about 350; about 6 MB of a plain-text save with every state treated. A treated state's step runs about 2.9× the plain step's statements in the test interpreter (the spec estimated 2×); option d measures it in game.
- **Self-checks:** none new: every engine fact the build reads is proven (a script-only type on a technology reaching the state, #892; a pop's `wealth` as a value, the Gini walk; the wealth pair's per-pop scaling, probe P6; buildings' active methods in a state value, `te_state_railway_train_code`).
- **What changes outside Full:** the three late-era technologies' mortality lines sit on the absorbed family (the same flat values through the moved lines' pair, Laws and Institutions in the tooltip); the market threshold variable on countries with a carrier; nothing else.

### Uploaded minds (2026-10-19)

The uploaded-minds spec (`docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-16-demographics-uploaded-minds-design.md`, the owner's calls in its §7; built from the spec with no plan document). **Under Full only**: Display only shows no pool (the spec's §6: under Display the engine's deaths aren't the census's, and the scale re-ties the ring to the engine's population, so an upload the model booked from a death the engine didn't make would be counted twice), and outside Full the Nexus produces as it always has. Inert without a Nexus: a country with no Mind Backups and no Nexus never writes a `te_dg_um_*` variable, and `test_demographics_golden.py` holds (one generated block's digest moves, `te_demog_cause_inputs_store`, for call 2's two lines, which read only a late state's `te_dg_elig`).

- **What an upload is** (call 6): the engine's deaths include the uploads (their bodies are gone, so they leave the engine's pops), and the ring loses them as every death. Each state's step books the uploads among its deaths into the owner's pool. Nothing touches the ring, the 150+ pool, M (which still aims at the census's deaths with the uploads in them) or the migration residual, which is the engine's population change less the walk's natural change, war dead and kills, and never reads the pool. Uploads don't work, need no care, draw no pension, don't fight and aren't in the sex balance: nothing reads the pool for those.
- **Who** (calls 1, 4): `te_demog_um_step`, after the step's deaths by cause. The late sweep counts the treated parts' deaths by cause at their biological ages (`te_dg_lx_ce_*`), so the treated's share of the infection and of the chronic deaths gives their deaths from each; × cover (the ever-treated still in care) are the eligible (`te_dg_um_elig`). Uploads (`te_dg_um_new`) are the owner's share φ of them, at most its free capacity, which falls at once, so a year's uploads never pass it whatever order the states step in. Accidents, violence, work and childbirth stay deaths.
- **Capacity and the pool** (calls 3, 5, 7): the country's census (`te_demog_um_country`, after its deaths by cause) holds the minds by sex, active (`te_dg_um_f`, `_m`) and archived (`_af`, `_am`). Each year 0.1% of the active choose to end (`te_dg_um_end`); capacity is 1,000,000 × the Nexus levels in its states with Mind Backups (`te_dg_um_cap`, `te_demog_um_state_levels`), else 0; archived minds come back first, into the room; active minds over capacity are archived (frozen: they don't produce or end). Then the year's free capacity (`te_dg_um_free`), its share of last year's eligible deaths φ (`te_dg_um_phi`, 1 with none), the utilisation (active over capacity, `te_dg_um_util`) and the minds' share of people and minds (`te_dg_um_share`).
