Outside Full the pool stands as it was. **A revolution's rebels keep no pool** (the pool's year skips a revolutionary country), so a rebel winner holds the nation's through the engine's variable merge, and `te_demog_um_repair_after_civil_war` (from `te_civil_war_on_won`) takes each `te_dg_um_*` again from the loser where the winner holds none and puts the two country modifiers back at once (`te_demog_um_country_modifiers`, their one refresh effect, which the census also calls). A secession that wins is a new nation and starts its own. An annexed country's minds go with its variables.
- **Mind Backups' restore by care** (call 2): its two −0.5 lines are census-only types (`state_backup_external_mortality_mult`, `state_backup_work_mortality_mult`, `P.BACKUP_TYPES`) that `te_demog_cause_inputs_store` adds × last step's `te_dg_elig` (the inputs are stored before eligibility drifts: a year's lag), so the restore is 1 − 0.5 × E; Human Purity gets none. A release strips them with the census's other types; outside Full the flat −5% on the absorbed family stays.
- **The figures** (§4): deaths per 1,000 are true deaths (the state's and the country's less their uploads; the hovers add the uploads per 1,000, `te_demog_um_upload_rate`, the country's stored as `te_dg_um_rate`, and the Causes of Death pie keeps them in their causes, since the bodies did die of them); the Added on Top figures compare every body's death (`te_demog_cdr_all`, true deaths plus uploads) with the census's own rate, which counts the uploads; the History chart's deaths are true deaths, and its legend says so; Living to 100 counts an upload as living (`te_dg_um_l100`: the blended table with the treated's infection and chronic deaths × (1 − the share that uploaded), from per-group sums the late sweep keeps only while capacity is free, `te_dg_uma_tic<f|m><group>`); Biological Age was always over the ring, so over bodies; life expectancy and Old age from stay biological. Longevity gains Backed Up (E) and Uploaded Minds (the share, hosted against capacity, uploads and endings, archived minds); the state subtab Backed Up and Uploaded Last Year; the biological pyramid a Non-biological line. Gates in `te_demog_um_sguis.txt`.
- **The Nexus** (call 6): `te_demog_um_nexus_refresh`, the eight building modifiers' one refresh effect, whatever the rule: once a month from the state pulse (`te_demog_um_monthly_on_action`; a state refreshed this month skips) and at once when a construction site adds a level (`mind_upload_nexus_on_action`, after `mind_upload_nexus_construction`: each level is a new building with none of the modifiers), so a new, rebuilt or conquered Nexus, or a change of rule, is scaled within the month. Under Full each good of the method takes its own unit modifier (`te_demog_um_nexus_<out|in>_<good>`, its axis at 1; `te_demog_um_nexus_good`) at (1 + the building's other bonuses for that good, at least 0) × (utilisation × the good's factor − 1), from the state's copy `root.var:te_dg_um_k_<out|in>_<good>` (a multiplier resolves against ROOT, and buildings hold no variables). The other bonuses are the building's read of the axis less the stored multiplier, since an add and a remove aren't visible in the block that makes them. Each good therefore comes to the method's line × utilisation × factor × (1 + its other bonuses): the minds' output takes the airports' tourism, the financial cycle's services and a company's digital assets as any building's would, and an empty Nexus makes and uses nothing whatever lifts its goods. The factors: digital assets ×15, tourism and fine art ×2, services ×1 (local); electronic components and advanced materials ×8, electricity and digital access ×2 (local). A full level, 1,000,000 minds, makes about £40M a week at base prices with no other bonus (£40 a mind, between an era-12 services worker and Self-Improving AI Systems' £64), five times the method's £8.1M (the owner's choice for a late-game wonder, 2026-10-20). An owner with no minds has a Nexus that makes nothing. Its staff are the method's, fixed: an empty Nexus owes wages on no revenue and lays off staff, and re-hires slowly as minds arrive. The method's research line (+5% a staffed level, a country line no building modifier reaches) is cancelled at the census by `te_demog_um_research` × the levels × their staffing (`te_dg_um_lvo`, the building's `level` × `occupancy` read as the Strategic Reserve reads its hub) × (1 − utilisation). Three mod-good input axes are registered for it (`goods_input_electronic_components_mult`, `_digital_access_`, `_advanced_materials_`; `mod_entity_modifier_types.txt`). Once a game under Full an info line, `TE_INFO um_nexus_ownership`, logs who owns a Nexus's levels (self, country and private fractions).
- **Politics** (call 8): the Devout −3 approval while the minds pass 1% of people and minds (`te_demog_um_devout`), behind `P.UM_POLITICS`, **off** (generated `te_demog_k_um_politics` 0). `te_demog_um_clear_outside_full` takes both country modifiers off at the country's yearly pulse outside Full.
- **The harness** (`demographics_harness.py uploads`, 2026-10-19): a country of 100 million as one rich state, everyone within reach. At era 11's rates (a counterfactual: Mind Backups needs Biological Immortality) 97% of deaths are the treated's illness and old age: 1.06M uploads a year, one full Nexus (5M) full in five years, three in about fifteen; true deaths 0.3 per 1,000 while there is room, Living to 100 0.97 counting uploads against 0.73. In the transition a game makes (era 11's steady state, then Biological Immortality and Mind Backups) the old bodies still die for a decade: 1.05M uploads in the first year falling to 0.56M by the fifth, one Nexus full in about seven years, three 71% full after 60. At immortality's steady state deaths are 0.55 per 1,000 and uploads 24-53 thousand a year: one Nexus 43% full after 60 years. A lost Nexus (3 of 5 levels for ten years) archives 3M and restores them the year the levels return.
- **Self-checks:** `um_nexus_scaling` (`te_debug_demog.130`): a Nexus's digital assets output and advanced materials input axes against the refresh's expectation, their other bonuses included, within 0.05, armed at a utilisation of 0.9 or less with the advanced materials figure at 1 or more; `um_nexus_cascade` (`te_debug_demog.131`): whether a building's read of a goods axis carries its state's lines, which the offset rests on (the building's other tourism against the state's own read, armed where that is 0.3 or more) (`docs/testing/demographics-playtest.md`).
- **Files:** `scripts/analysis/demographics_uploads.py` (the model, the calibration, the scenarios), `scripts/generators/gen_demographics_um.py` (`te_demog_um_generated_effects.txt`, `te_demog_um_generated_values.txt`; called from `gen_demographics.plan_outputs`, and its `backup_inputs` from the inputs' store), `te_demog_um_effects.txt`, `te_demog_um_values.txt`, `te_demog_um_modifiers.txt`, `te_demog_um_sguis.txt`, `events/te_debug_demog_um_events.txt`; hooks in `te_demog_lx_effects.txt` (`te_demog_lx_begin`, the two treated-part sites), `te_demog_effects.txt` (the step's finish, the seed, the state's figures, the country census and yearly pulse) `te_demog_on_actions.txt` (the monthly refresh), `extra_on_actions.txt` (a new level's refresh) and `te_civil_war_on_actions.txt` (the repair); `test_demographics_uploads.py`.

### Phase 3: the event wave (2026-10-12)

The parent spec's §9 candidates, all ten, built from the spec with no plan document (owner, 2026-10-12: the owner judges
the text and balance in the play-test). Each fires when the census crosses its threshold, at most once a generation per
country, under Full only (`te_demog_wave_runs`: Full and a census taken from steps, so an 1836 game's first chance is a
year or more after the start). Each threshold is a constant in `te_demog_wave_values.txt` pinned to `demographics_wave.py`.

| Event | Fires when | Choices |
|---|---|---|
| The Demographic Dividend (`.1`) | the share aged 15-64 reaches 0.623, a tenth above the 1836 agrarian reference's 0.566 (design rule 5) | schools (education access, a costlier Ministry of Education), industry (construction, manufacturing), savings (cheaper loans, tax capacity); ten years each |
| The Baby Boom (`.2`) | a war period of two years or more whose dead passed a hundredth of the men of fighting age ends | births +15% for ten years, decaying (§9), with homes (standard of living, a one-off cost), or +20% with the women sent home (fewer workers), or +10% with the women kept at work (more) |
| The Lost Generation (`.3`) | a war period's dead pass a twentieth of the men of fighting age when it began | a harm menu: mourning, empty workbenches, widows and orphans; memorials, women into industry or widows' pensions each spare one |
| The Greying of the Nation (`.4`) | under Old Age Pension the pensioners (past the pension age) reach a fifth of the people; without one, the people past the old-age threshold reach 0.14 | raise the pension age (the Raised position, its term binding), cut benefits or raise contributions (weekly income at a fifth or a seventh of the pension bill, ten years), open the borders, keep the pension; without one, the borders, almshouses or the family |
| The Youth Bulge (`.5`) | more than a fifth of the people aged 20-29 while a tenth of the workforce has no work | public works, national service, emigration, or the youth bulge's own effects for five years |
| Missing Girls (`.6`) | 110 boys born per 100 girls or more in the capital's census (Birth Limit after Microprocessor) | a ban (-5 for twenty years, enforcement authority), payments for daughters (-3), relax the limit (one child to two at once, or end it once its term has run), or look away |
| Bare Branches (`.7`) | 110 men per 100 women aged 20-59 or more (step 4's stored figure) | assisted passages for women, service, police, or the held-back more-men effect for ten years |
| The Empty Villages (`.8`) | a state with a quarter of its people Peasants or Farmers, a median age of 40 or more, that lost half a percent of its people over the year | a harm menu on that state: idle fields, closed services, the old alone; farm subsidies, keeping the school and clinic open or moving the old into town each spare one |
| The Overspill (`.9`) | a Primate or Dominant pattern whose largest city (most urban people) is at Migration Crowding's ceiling (`migration_crowding_mult_applied` 4.5) | new towns (the city's pull -15%; Settlement Authorities switch to Planned Towns where the country runs any and knows Modern Urban Planning), a green belt, or sprawl |
| The Last Generation? (`.10`) | Biological Immortality, at once (`on_acquired_technology`), once a game | birth licences (desired family size -30%), children a right, or payments for the next generation (+10%); twenty years each |

- **The dispatcher** (`te_demog_wave_yearly`, after the country's yearly census): the eight yearly events in a fixed
  order, at most one a year, so two thresholds crossed together don't arrive as two popups; the next is still due the year
  after. The hold is `te_dg_wv_<event>`, a 25-year timed variable set as the event fires. The events carry no trigger of
  their own: a trigger is evaluated on `trigger_event` and would block the console's test firing, so each event's
  `immediate` picks what it names (the village state, the city) with a fallback.
- **The war tracker** (`te_demog_wave_war_monthly`, monthly, Full): a war period runs from the first month at war to the
  first month at peace. Its dead are the rise in the dead of all its wars month by month, from its own snapshot (the
  census's yearly total is reset at the yearly country pulse and the on-actions' order isn't guaranteed); its yardstick is the census's
  pool (`te_dg_fam`) when it began, nineteen in twenty of the dead counted as men.
- **Decisions where the spec left room:** the Greying reads the pension age or the old-age threshold, not 65 (late-game
  §2.2): pensioners under Old Age Pension at the parent's 20%; without a pension law the share past the old-age threshold
  at 0.14, what it is when 65+ first passes a fifth in the harness's fast transition (0.144). Missing Girls fires at 110 or
  more, so Birth Limit's two children (110) counts, not only one child (115). Bare Branches and the Youth Bulge read step
  4's stored figures although step 4's effects are held back; Bare Branches reads the census's 20-59 balance (§9 said
  20-39). The Overspill's "Metropolis-pattern state" (§5.2) isn't built: the national pattern and the largest city's
  crowding stand in. The Baby Boom's "mass mobilisation" is dead of a hundredth of the men of fighting age. Two default
  options never share an event: the Greying's default names itself by the pension law.
- **Census levers:** the Greying's raise uses `te_demog_pension_choose` (gated on the term, greyed when it runs); Missing
  Girls' relax steps Birth Limit back or ends it (`te_demog_ms_apply`, `te_demog_ms_end`; ending needs its term run);
  the Overspill's new towns switch Settlement Authorities to Planned Towns. Every variable write sits in a
  `custom_tooltip`.
- **Money:** one-off payments are a share of the yearly gross income (`te_demog_wave_cost_small/_medium/_large`: 2%, 5%,
  10%). The Greying's cut and contributions are weekly `country_tax_income_add` at a share of the pension bill in force,
  mirrored under Pension Reform in the Budget Breakdown.
- **Census types on event modifiers:** Missing Girls' ban and payments carry `state_sex_ratio_at_birth_add`, The Last
  Generation?'s licences and payments `state_desired_fertility_mult`, on timed country modifiers; each keeps a line of its
  own for a release, which comments the types out. The self-check `wave_timed_country_type` reads the capital a week after
  the first of them (`docs/testing/demographics-playtest.md`, Self-checks). Women's work (the Baby Boom's women sent
  home or kept at work, the Greying's family care) is on phase 2 step 1's women's-work family
  (`state_demog_womens_work_ratio_add`, as Parental Leave's), never the engine's working-adult field
  (`TestWorkforceLinesMoved`): under Full the participation model reads it as women's rate. It rides the same timed
  country modifiers, so the self-check's verdict covers it too.
- **Revolutions:** the winner keeps the holds and the tracker (variables), not the event modifiers, as for any event.
- **The fit** (`demographics_harness.py events`): no threshold crossed in the 1836 reference structures; a fast
  transition opens the Dividend in year 27 and the Youth Bulge in year 32 at 20% unemployment, a slow one neither; the
  Greying fires for today's oldest structure and not the average rich one (65+ 18%). In the overnight run's 1900 and
  1904 saves (94 and 96 census countries of a million people or more) only Bare Branches is due in more than one: 12 and
  9, the settler societies (USA, Canada, Argentina, Chile, Cuba) with some of the migrant booking's artefacts (Mexico,
  Bolivia, Colombia) that held step 4's effects back; the Dividend once (South Africa, 1904).

### Internal Resettlement in the census, and the US frontier (2026-10-19)

The master spec's §2.5 "Known kills" and §2.6, on the owner's calls of 2026-10-19. It runs under Display only and Full. Under Display only it moves nothing outside the census's figures; under Full the census's consequence modifiers (§ Phase 2 step 4: Census: More Men and Fewer Men, the conscription term, which has no ceiling, and the youth bulge) follow the new structures, so a programme's states and the US frontier take them (figures in the master spec §2.5 and §2.6). A country with no Settlement Authority runs exactly as before (`test_demographics_golden.py`), apart from the US's frontier states at the 1836 seed.

- **Profiles** (`demographics_params.RESETTLE_PROFILES`, `RESETTLE_KINDS`): each programme moves people by its own age and sex profile, the same at the source and the destination. Land Grants and Organized Colonization move families (the residual's family kind); Military Colonies half the labour kind at 80% men and half families; Penal Transportation mostly 15–35 at 85% men (12% aged 15–17, 78% 18–35, 10% 36–59: the controller's class split, confirmed by the owner on 2026-10-20); Special Settlements the refugee kind (whole families); the Development Program 60% families and 40% labour, the labour's women's share set by the destination's jobs as the residual's is (`te_demog_rs_labour_f`, before the balance ramp); Rustication ages 15–24 evenly, booked by single year over the people of those ages (the bands 15–19 and 20–24), since 15–24 straddles the migrant classes; Managed Retreat the refugee kind with its 60+ weight doubled.
- **Counters** (`te_demog_resettle_effects.txt`). While the census runs, the Authority's monthly walk books each source's move (`te_demog_rs_note_move`, called in `resettlement_take_from_source`) and its transit dead (`te_demog_rs_note_dead`, in `resettlement_source_consequences`) at both ends that hold a census: `te_dg_rs_in` and `te_dg_rs_i_<s><c>` (by migrant class and sex; `_y<s>` Rustication's ages) on the destination, `te_dg_rs_out`, `te_dg_rs_dead` and `te_dg_rs_o_*` on the source (the generated `te_demog_rs_add`). A census-off save holds none.
- **The step** (`te_demog_rs_take`, from `te_demog_flows`) takes the counters gathered since the state's last step, the same months its population change covers (the war dead's `te_dg_war_in` pattern), so a state stepped in October takes the moves since last October, and a walk after the step starts new counters; then it removes them, and a seed clears them (`te_demog_rs_clear`). Each class and sex gains or loses its movers over its last-year people (`te_demog_rs_known_rates`, `te_demog_rs_enter_class`, generated), **with no cap**: a known move is a count, not an estimate (the sweep's guard, half of what is left of a cohort, stays). That is put to the owner as a choice; the alternative books known moves through the residual's caps and balance ramps. The residual is the change less natural change, war dead, kills and the known moves, so its own profile and caps book only the rest; `te_dg_mig_raw` keeps the whole, and the panel's net migration (`te_dg_net_migration`) adds the known moves back, which the step also stores apart (`te_dg_rs_net`) so `demographics_rebook.py` re-books only the rest. A frontier filling by resettlement keeps its census however fast it grows: the census has no size test since 2026-10-20 (the old one left the known moves out).
- **Deaths in transit** go through `te_demog_note_kills` at the source, as the nuclear strikes' and Violent Hostility's do (they leaked into the residual before, the 2026-10-09 note), so the Causes of Death section counts them as killed; the step's every-age kill rate leaves them out and they leave by the programme's profile. The resettlement events' own kills (`resettlement.3.b`'s hard winter, 1,000; `resettlement.6.b`'s famine, 5,000) are noted as known kills too.
- **The US frontier at the 1836 seed** (history data, as France's Family Limitation is): `common/history/extra_history.txt` marks the US's states in Michigan, Indiana, Illinois, Missouri, Arkansas, Iowa and Wisconsin, and since 2026-10-20 (owner) in the Old Southwest and Florida, Mississippi, Alabama, Louisiana and Florida (`te_dg_frontier`, `te_demog_frontier_listed`): every state the US holds in 1836 whose 1840 free white men per 100 women aged 15–49 were 110 or more (the params give every state's figure). Their 1836 seeds (`te_demog_frontier_begin`, the generated `te_demog_frontier_slot`) set each age group's men from 15 to its women × the 1840 census's free white men per woman, mixed with the state's other 1836 pops at one to one by the settlers' share of its people (`FRONTIER_1836`, `frontier_mix`; source in the params). The seed's normalisation keeps the state's people; the first pulse's re-seed applies it again and takes the mark off, and with the census off the game start takes it off. Wisconsin opens at 178 men per 100 women aged 20–59, Florida 144, Illinois and Louisiana 134, Iowa 130, Missouri 128, Mississippi 127, Michigan 126, Arkansas 123, Alabama 114, Indiana 113: under Full all eleven take Census: More Men and a conscription term of +7% to +61%, and Wisconsin the youth bulge where work is short. In the Old Southwest the enslaved are a third to nearly half of the people, so the settlers' share, and the mixture, is lower there.
- **Self-check** `resettle_moves_booked` (once a game; § Self-checks in `docs/testing/demographics-playtest.md`). **Console:** `event te_debug_demog.120` logs the player's states' counters (`TE_DEMOG_RESETTLE`). **Harness:** `demographics_harness.py frontier` (the seeds, then ageing) and `resettle` (each programme's ten years at both ends); `demographics_resettle.py` is the twin; `test_demographics_resettle.py` runs the script against it.

### The ring's 300 years and the pyramid past 85 (issue #1075, 2026-10-27)

In the owner's France → European Union game (autosave of 2057-11-01) 54% of the EU's 2.17 billion people sat in the pyramid's 85+ bar, and 98 million people world-wide sat in the ring's pool past 150, with no ages at all (Franche-Comté: 9.4 million at a mean age of 165). The owner (2026-10-20): show those ages, gated on there being people in them.

- **The pyramid's rows past 85** (`demographics_params.OLD_ROWS`): 85–99, 100–124, 125–149, 150–199, 200–249, 250–299 and 300 and over (the pool). The census keeps 85 and over as its last band for every figure (median, shares, the outline, the deaths-by-cause estimate); only the pyramid splits it. The sweep notes the last band's people at each row start (`te_demog_old_row_mark`, on the band boundary's own comparison, so no extra test per slot) and the close stores the people past each start, `te_dg_o<f|m><i>`, only where anyone is (`te_demog_old_rows_close`). **The gate** (`te_demog_old_rows_show`, `OLD_ROW_GATE`): a row past 85–99 shows while the people of its age and over are 1% of the people or more, and the highest row shown holds everyone older, labelled "125+"; with none, nothing is stored and the pyramid ends at 85+ as before, so an 1836–2000 pyramid is unchanged (people past 100 are a few in ten thousand there). **Drawn per five years of age** (`OLD_ROW_DRAW`, my call): a row of 15, 25 or 50 years draws its people × 5 ÷ its width, so its bar compares with the five-year rows below and the pyramid's shape stays readable; the hover gives the row's people, and the pool's open row draws its count, as 85+ does. The pyramid's scale (`te_demog_pyramid_max`, `_state_pyramid_max`, the biological stores) takes the rows as drawn in 85+'s place, and the outline's 85+ leaves it, since the split rows have no outline. States, countries (their states' rows summed, `te_demog_country_old_rows_store`) and the biological pyramid (each treated part moved between the rows by its calendar and biological ages, `te_demog_lx_bio_move`) alike; the GUI gates each view's rows on `te_demog_pyr_split_sgui` and its three siblings.
- **The ring: 300 years** (`RING_YEARS`), so nobody a player can reach falls into the pool (someone born in 1836 is 264 in 2100). The sweep, the slot trees, the late game's birth bands (`LX_BANDS` 30 → 60) and the debug lines regenerate. **Kept:** the age groups (`GROUPS`) still end at 145–149: every base rate is flat from 110, so the last group's rates hold at every older rate age, as they did for the pool, and the life tables still close at 150 on their open last interval (§ The safeguards pass), which now reads the table's own last group in the late game, the pool being empty in play. Extending the groups would have doubled the rate trees for identical leaves. **Changed:** the last migrant class runs to 298, so people past 150 move with the rest of the old (they never moved in the pool), and the hand-written 150s are 300s (`test_demographics_ring.TestRingYears` pins them to `RING_YEARS`).
- **A save from before** (`te_demog_ring_migrate`, at the start of a state's next step, `te_demog_ring_check`; twin `demographics_model.ring_migrate`): a census with no `te_dg_ring` is re-filed once. Each cohort of age a moves from slot (Y − a) mod 150 to (Y − a) mod 300 (Y its last count's year): where Y mod 300 is under 150 the slots above the open slot move up 150, else the open slot and those below it. The late game's birth bands move with their slots, the open slot's band with its oldest cohorts (its others are children). The pool goes to its mean age rounded, with its treated share and deficit merged into that age's band by people (owner, 2026-10-20: something simple; Franche-Comté's 9.4 million all become 165); a pool of mean age 300 or more stays. The age-149 cohort and the pool's people join the last migrant class's sums; the conscription pool's sums wait for the step's count. The console's replay and benchmark re-file before they turn the census year back. `demographics_rebook.ring_from` re-files a save's ring the same way.
- **Cost:** in an ordinary game slots 150–299 stay empty, and each still costs its guards in the sweep. In the test interpreter (statements and trigger tests counted on one state with nobody past 150) a plain step rises from about 16,200 to 20,900 (+29%) and a late step from 50,500 to 58,400 (+16%), the rows past 85 included. At the spec's 1836 rate (about 1 ms a plain step) that is about 0.3 ms more per state, a fifth of a second per game year world-wide; option d measures it in game. A late-game state with people past 150 runs up to twice the occupied slots. Variables: up to 12 rows (6 pairs) per state where people pass 100, 14 shown rows and a top where the pyramid splits, as many again for the biological pyramid; up to about 300 more ring variables in a state with people past 150.

### Generator and harness

- `python3 scripts/generators/gen_demographics.py` (`--check` exits 1 when stale) writes the ring's sweeps, the age-group rate tables, the engine's growth curves as per-pop values, the cause multipliers, the migrant profiles and the booking's cap (`te_demog_migrant_rates`), the normalisation effects and the debug replay lines from `demographics_params.py`, `extra_defines.txt`, `00_buy_packages.txt` and the land-reform laws. The cause multipliers are products of one script value per factor (`P.CAUSE_FACTORS`), on the step's stored inputs (§ Causes of Death); their inputs come from the census's seven mortality modifier types, not the owner's techs and laws: medicine is `1 − access × treatment` (`state_health_care_access_add` from the health laws' per-level `institution_modifier`, incorporated states only, on a base of 0.4; `state_<cause>_treatment_add` from the medical techs, which every state inherits from its country), and police, child labour, pensions, the combustion engine, Workplace Safety and Consumer Protection are `1 + their types' sum`, floored at 0.2; work and accidents and violence also take modern safety's factor, `1 −` the era 7-9 technologies' share (§ Causes of Death). The values live on those carriers in the game files; `scripts/analysis/demographics_modifiers.py` resolves them for the model and the harness (modifier-types spec, stage 1; fit in `docs/testing/demographics-fast-run-2026-10-09.md`). Since phase 2 step 1 it also writes the working-adult pair's three files (`te_demog_workforce_line_*_generated.txt`) beside #892's. It is not a post-load regenerator: run it after changing any input, and commit both files with the change. `docs/auto_generated_files.md` has the row.
- `python3 scripts/analysis/demographics_harness.py` has `sketch` (the equilibrium of §2.2/§2.3's cases), `inputs`, `gini`, `seed`, `natural-change`, `replay` (below), `wc`, `medicine` (the mortality anchors with the game files' values), `fertility` (children per woman against §2.3's bands), `measures` (phase 2 step 3b: the Family Policy measures' effect on children per woman and the pro-natalist package's upkeep against the design's §5 bands; `--save` reads a plain-text save's tax revenue over GDP), `workforce` (phase 2: participation, need and the old-age threshold on the census's structures, step 2's bands on Rich today, the participation inputs against their flat lines, and with a save the 1836 world's engine-scale totals, its measured workforce and its health need), `pensions` (phase 2 step 2: the pension bill against a save's revenue over GDP, the health bill), `adopters` (health-law countries against their peers and without their law), `fidelity` (the model's cause multipliers against the ones the census stored in a save, state by state), `practices-replay` (Late Marriage's and Birth Spacing's drift through a run's saves), `practices-fit` (the wealth curve's raise, the cuts and step 1's mortality fitted to the anchors, with #904's peacetime births less deaths projected by region and judged against history's bands, widened by half the two-run spread, at least 0.5: `demographics_regions.TWO_RUN_SPREAD`), `ontop-fit` (calibration step 3: the deaths on top by state-year from the Causes of Death split, Famine Reserves absorbed, the malaria factor fitted and the gate before and after; `demographics_ontop.py`), `consequences` (phase 2 step 4's bands on the model's structures and a save's census), `events [SAVE...]` (phase 3: the event wave thresholds against model structures and saved census countries); `frontier` and `resettle` (2026-10-19: the US frontier's 1836 seeds ageing, and each Internal Resettlement programme's ten years at both ends; `demographics_resettle.py`), `rebook` (the migrant booking: a run's census re-walked with its own residual, booked by today's rules and by the profile alone, and step 4's bands judged; plain-text saves or the overnight analysis's per-save JSON; `demographics_rebook.py`), `predict` (the engine's growth once the census sets its rates, from a save: the gate's offline half, reporting what the absorbed lines and the starving slope did) and `history` (each country's model rates beside history's life expectancy, infant mortality and growth, from `scripts/analysis/fetch_history_anchors.py`'s CSV; phase 2's calibration, `docs/testing/demographics-history-check-2026-10-10.md`; `--shares`, `--incorporated-only` and `--no-practices` for the practices); `docs/guides/python_tools.md` has the full list. Everything numeric except the mortality types' carrier values lives in `demographics_params.py`: change it, regenerate, and `test_gen_demographics.py` and `test_demographics_registry.py` (which interprets the script against the model) check that script and model still agree.
- `event te_debug_demog.1` (game console; `events/te_debug_demog_events.txt`): **a** replay one year of the capital's census to `debug.log` for `demographics_harness.py replay`; **b** census log on (`TE_DEMOG_CENSUS:` lines at each yearly country census; **b_off** turns it off) for `demographics_observer_report.py`; **c** re-seed every state; **d** benchmark the walk and the step (`full=` on the start line); **e** war-dead accounting; **f**/**g** the working-adult skew probe (`te_demog_debug_working_adults`); **h**/**i**/**j** fast mode at 4×, 6× or 12×, **k** back to normal speed (below); **l** the census's modifier types as the capital reads them, and the practices' shares and targets, with a second line, `TE_DEMOG_WORK` (phase 2 step 1's figures, the owner's pension variable, the pension kind, the 10–14s' share, the working-adult families, the pair and call 3's inputs); **m** every devastated or polluted state's mortality and birth reads (probe P1); **n** the capital's census terms, the terms in force, the on-top scales and their target, the trapezoid's start rates per head for the next window (`sr_b`, `sr_d`), and the Causes of Death section's split of the window's deaths: `ed_state=` (less the pops' own lines), `ed_sev=` (severe starvation's part), `sev=` (the share severely starving at the count), `clamp_d=` (whether the floor bit the measured window: 0 no, 1 yes) and the next window's start parts `sp_d=`, `ss_d=` per head (`TE_DEMOG_RATES`, probe P3); **o** the late-marriage plan's engine-scaling probe: a script-only births type on the capital's state modifier at multiplier 0.62, logged before and a day after (`TE_DEMOG_PROBE`); **q** the owner-change probe: one of our states alone in its region, stamped and given to a neighbour, logged before, inside `on_state_owner_change` (only while its global flag is set) and a day after (`TE_DEMOG_PROBE_OWNER`): does the hook's ROOT still hold the old state's variables? Throwaway games only. **x** family policy in the census (phase 2 step 3b): the capital's six Family Policy types, the policy term and Birth Limit's part, the sex ratio's add in force and the stored desired, means, children per woman with its planned and unplanned parts, the maternal input and rate (`TE_DEMOG_FAMILY`). **p** call 3's carriers (phase 2 step 1): Community Service on Punishment-Focused Criminal Justice, Woman Soldiers at half strength and the Trade Unions pushed past loyal, the capital logged now, a day and a month later (the hidden `te_debug_demog.3`); **r** the capital's workforce term (`TE_DEMOG_WF`) and the country's pension setting and bills (`TE_DEMOG_PENSION`, phase 2 step 2); **s** ends the pension setting's five-year term now. **t** phase 2 step 4's figures: the capital's pool, conscription term, youth bulge and sex-balance terms beside the fields they move (`TE_DEMOG_CONSEQ`), and the country's (`TE_DEMOG_CONSEQ_COUNTRY`); its keys are `te_debug_demog.1.t_opt` (`.t` is the event's title). **w** opens `te_debug_demog.80`, a chooser that fires any of the event wave's ten events on the player now, whatever its condition and hold (phase 3).. The hidden `te_debug_demog.30` is the self-check `conscription_term_read`'s second half. Under the census log (b) each country also writes a `TE_DEMOG_WORKC` line, which `demographics_observer_report.py --work` reads. `demographics_observer_report.py --phase2` checks phase 2's gate. With `--saves` it judges the world's multiple by every state's people in the saves, against `--band` (default ×1.4–×1.65, #894). The census log's own figure counts only countries of a million people or more, so it runs high as colonized land joins the census. Details are in `docs/guides/python_tools.md`.

### Fast mode

A test tool for iterating on the census: `event te_debug_demog.1` option h, i or j runs demography, research and construction at 4×, 6× or 12× (`te_demog_fast_effects.txt`). It isn't for play, and nothing starts it but the console. Wars, diplomacy, laws, literacy and pop wealth keep the calendar's pace, so a fast game differs from a real one; check a result in a normal game once it looks right.

- **The clock.** `te_demog_year` reads `global_var:te_demog_clock` once the first switch creates it. The global monthly pulse advances it a year every N months (3, 2 or 1) and steps every state's census at once through the hidden state event `te_demog_events.2`; each country takes its census a day later (`te_demog_events.3`). Every window is whole calendar months, so it holds exactly N of each pop's monthly growth updates and the walk's expected births and deaths (`te_demog_step_months`) cover it. The states' own pulses are 30-day timers, which a one-month window can miss.
- **The speed-up.** `te_demog_fast_births`/`_deaths` (state, `state_birth_rate_mult`/`state_mortality_mult`) are sized at each step to (K − 1) × the state's average multiplier from the walk, less the term already applied, so its engine births and deaths run at K× rather than diluting its other terms. From phase 2 step 4 the census's last term comes off that average too and its new term goes in, both from `te_demog_rates_refresh`'s locals (it runs first in the clock step), so the engine runs K × (the census's target plus the terms on top); the term is clipped at 0. `te_demog_fast_speed` (country) adds K − 1 to research speed, technology spread and construction.
- **The trapezoid** (§ The census's births and deaths, the window's events) books the clock's window at the mean of the engine's rate at its two ends, as a yearly step books its year. The fast term is set at a clock step, where the start's rate moves by the term's change, so both ends carry the same one; and both cover the walk's months (`te_demog_step_months`), so a switch between two fast speeds is booked at the months it covered. Option k takes the term off at once, between two steps: `te_demog_fast_clear_rates` then drops the start's rate, which held the term (about K times the engine's rate after k), and that window takes the snapshot, as before.
- **Use.** In a new game on day 1: option b (census log), then h, then `observe`; archive the logs, then run `demographics_observer_report.py`. Census lines carry the clock's year, `date=` (the calendar date, which `--closed-borders` matches to saves) and `lag=` (states not at the census year; the report flags any).
- **Caveats.** The first switch re-seeds every census at the clock's first step. A later switch keeps the rings. Normal speed (k) takes the rate modifiers off at once, so the next step misreads migration once. The clock never stops, so the census year stays ahead of the calendar. Wealth Concentration and inheritance stay on the yearly pulse.

### Owner checks in game

1. Natural change: two plain-text saves a month apart in a new 1836 game, `demographics_harness.py natural-change OLD NEW`; the ratio should be near 1 before modifiers.
2. Replay: `event te_debug_demog.1` option a, then `demographics_harness.py replay debug.log` prints `OK` for the capital (worst slot error under 1%).
3. The 1836 census: the tab and subtab show a pyramid on day one; Britain's median about 20, children per woman 5.5–6, life expectancy about 40; China's lower. This is also the check that the seed's large products (`state_population × 100000` in the normalisation, about 2.5×10^11 for a large state) evaluate in the engine, as vanilla's products of that size do: a garbled pyramid or a population far off the state's means they don't.
4. An observer run to 2100 with the census log on: fertility falls with standard of living, literacy and the Pill; life expectancy rises with medicine; Gini about 0.55 shown in 1836 Britain. This is phase 1's gate (§12). Keep some plain-text autosaves (debug mode) and run `demographics_observer_report.py <logs> --closed-borders <saves>`. Closed Borders countries' net migration before the noise band (the census line's `mig_raw`) should have a median within ±1 per 1,000 a year of 0. It was −6 before the per-pop rates. The floored figure can't settle this: each state's residual under 3 per 1,000 reads 0, so its median stays at 0 for any smaller error.
5. Benchmark (option d) in a late-game save: the yearly cost stays near the 1836 figure per occupied slot.
6. War dead (option e) during a war, and whether battle dead come out of home-state pops (§14 Q4).
7. Skew (options f, g): how fast a working-adult modifier changes a pop's workforce share (§14 Q11).
8. The bareword reads: the census line's `crisis` moves with `devastation` and `turmoil`. The census reads a state's devastation as a 0–1 share, as vanilla's trigger comparisons do (`devastation >= 0.2`, `> 0.1`, `>= 0.5`; `add_devastation` takes points): the check confirms that `crisis` rises by the `devastation` the line prints, and by its `turmoil` (0–1) too.
9. Wealth Concentration: #822's law tooltip and the concept still show the score and its target; the inheritance events still move it; a banking crash lowers it; a few countries' 1836 figures against the law targets.
10. Save size: a 1900 save with the census against one with the rule Disabled (the owner's §13 cohort-width call; about 26 MB of an 1836 plain-text save as built).
11. Causes of Death: the state subtab shows the section after its figures, open, with no label or value cut short; Health Care Access is 40% in an unincorporated colony; one hover's factors multiply to its row; an old save reads "after its next count" until the state's step.
12. Medicine drifts: a health law or Modern Nursing (console) shows "×a → ×b" at once and moves a tenth to a fifth of the way at the next count; Medical Outreach is offered under Full only, where medicine is behind, and raises the hover's share of the gap by 20 points (option l's `diff=`).
13. Deaths Added on Top: absent outside Full, a figure from a state's second Full count, red from ×1.25 (a famine state); the hover's three parts multiply to the row; option n's `ed_state=`, `ed_sev=` (above 0 in a famine: the walk's severe sum parses), `sev=` and `clamp_d=` match it.
14. Late Marriage and Birth Spacing: the late-marriage plan's in-game list (Task 12, Step 4), the engine-scaling probe (option o) first.
15. Phase 2 step 1: `docs/testing/demographics-playtest.md` § Phase 2 step 1 (nothing moves; the 1836 figures and `wf_engine`, step 2's stop rule; option p's carriers; the skew probe and the benchmark). Since 2026-10-12 that file holds the play-test lists; none gates a merge.
16. Family Policy measures: `docs/testing/demographics-playtest.md`, "Family Policy measures (step 3a)".
17. The urban pattern and Planned Capital: `docs/testing/demographics-playtest.md`, "Phase 3: the urban pattern and Planned Capital".
17. Phase 2 step 2: `docs/testing/demographics-playtest.md` § Phase 2 step 2 (the section and its buttons, a position moving the bill and the workforce, the AI, the observer gate with `--work`, a late save for the fit).
18. Phase 2 step 4: `docs/testing/demographics-playtest.md` § Phase 2 step 4 (option t's 1836 figures; the war dead land in the pool's ages; the panel's rows and their "not applied yet"; the conscription, youth-bulge and sex-balance effects are on since the migrant booking, 2026-10-12).
19. Phase 3's event wave: `docs/testing/demographics-playtest.md` § Phase 3: the event wave (each event from the console's option w: text, art and options; the war tracker in a real war; the self-check).

### Compatibility (§11.5)

The Demography mod models ages too, so running both applies two sets of corrections (no detection; the rule is the way out) and it replaces `states_panel.gui`. The Population panel is a new full-file override (`pops_overview.gui`), so any other mod that replaces it collides with this one. The state panel already collided with Demography; the subtab adds nothing new.

## Penal Labor Camps (`law_penal_labor_camps`)

The authoritarian end of `lawgroup_criminal_justice` (`common/laws/extra_laws.txt`), beside Punishment-Focused (progressiveness 0, the default), Restorative (25, `behaviorism`) and Rehabilitation-Focused (50, `mental_health_awareness`).

- **Gate:** `mass_surveillance` plus one of `law_autocracy` / `law_bakufu` / `law_neo_absolutism` / `law_single_party_state` / `law_outlawed_dissent`. The two Autocracy variants are listed because `unlocking_laws` matches exact keys. A country that loses every gate is moved to Punishment-Focused by the generated `te_fix_inconsistent_lawgroup_criminal_justice` (closest progressiveness; the law is -50). The sweep runs from `on_law_activated`, so when the replacing Distribution of Power or Free Speech law activates, and on the monthly country pulse. `cultural_hegemony.16` never presses the camps on a country: its `activate_law` would skip the gate.
- **Modifier:** +100 authority, -10 legitimacy, -0.10 suppression attraction factor (Shinsengumi's value; vanilla multiplies a suppressed movement's attraction by -0.5 plus the factor, so under Outlawed Dissent, itself -0.5, suppression goes from -1.0 to -1.1 × base), +10% civil-rights movement support, and a flat +5% throughput for mines, logging camps, plantations and rubber plantations. The throughput is deliberately flat (owner call): nothing scales it with radicals, turmoil or prisoners. There is no activism cut: repression feeds the opposition as a cost, so the movement levers are the civil-rights support and the movement stances below.
- **Interest groups:** by ideology stance only (`ideology_modifications.py`; the six custom-religion society ideologies in `extra_ideologies.txt`). Liberal, progressive and moderate criminal-justice ideologies strongly disapprove (so the Intelligentsia and Trade Unions); regressive ones approve, one step below their Punishment-Focused stance, so they don't push for camps. The ideologies that rank the camps above Punishment-Focused, and so push for them, are the fascist leader and movement (strongly approve) and the authoritarian leader (approve); none has a Punishment-Focused stance. The totalitarian society strongly approves both laws, and the imperial-cult and theocratic societies approve both, so they are indifferent between them. The liberal, radical and anarchist movement ideologies strongly disapprove, which is how the law feeds those movements. `test_penal_labor_law.py` pins that every ideology with a Criminal Justice stance has one on the camps.
- **Where else it is listed:** the UN human-rights violator test (`un_regime_human_rights_violator`) and the human-rights vote lean, refusal and withdrawal weights beside Outlawed Dissent; the Mental Health JE's fail condition and the punitive AI weights beside Punishment-Focused (`mental_health_events.3`, `social_tensions_events.5`).
- **Not listed** in the reform-debate enactment events (`extra_law_events.12/.30/.48/.72`) or either Criminal Justice amendment, which are written for the reform laws and Punishment-Focused.

## On-Actions Reference

The mod uses 55 on-action files under `common/on_actions/`; the index below lists the main ones. These wire mod logic into engine hooks — either **pulse-based** (fires periodically for all relevant scopes) or **immediate** (fires the instant a specific game event occurs).

### File Index

| File | Purpose | Hook Type |
|------|---------|-----------|
| `extra_on_actions.txt` | Central hub: pulse wiring, dynamic modifiers, immediate triggers, company cleanup | Mixed |
| `te_construction_market_on_actions.txt` | Construction-market site re-placement on diplomatic/territorial and building-lifecycle changes, plus its yearly heartbeat | Mixed |
| `headlines.txt` | "World first" tech notifications (`on_acquired_technology`) | Immediate |
| `law_events_on_actions.txt` | Law enactment checkpoint events (advance/debate/stall) | Immediate |
| `amendment_on_actions.txt` | Temporary-amendment expiry follow-up events (`on_amendment_timeout`) | Immediate |
| `amendment_petition_on_actions.txt` | Amendment petitions on laws in force, one yearly roll per petition (§ Amendment Petitions) | Pulse |
| `langreform_events_on_actions.txt` | Language reform yearly random events | Pulse |
| `minor_events_on_actions.txt` | Miscellaneous yearly random events | Pulse |
| `repeatable_events_on_actions.txt` | Generic repeatable yearly events | Pulse |
| `resettlement_on_actions.txt` | Internal resettlement: the monthly country pulse (transfer, politics, Declaration, events) and the monthly state pulse (modifier refresh: destination bonuses and readouts) | Pulse (monthly) |
| `social_tensions_on_actions.txt` | Social/political tension yearly events | Pulse |
| `space_race_on_actions.txt` | Space race in-progress and cross-system yearly events | Pulse |
| `te_monetary_on_actions.txt` | Monetary policy: world reference rate and (phase 3) the world rate, the monthly country update, the yearly growth snapshot, the country-creation hooks (see **Monetary Policy (phase 1)**), and — phase 5 — the anchored-GDP refresh on the global pulse, the yearly arrangement scan + seigniorage re-sum, `on_country_default` (the guarantee is called) and `on_become_subject` (currency boards) | Mixed |
| `te_unemployment_on_actions.txt` | Each state's yearly walk for its workforce share, which `te_state_unemployment_share` divides the engine's unemployment by (§ Unemployment as a Share of the Workforce), a monthly fill for a state with none yet, and the self-check `unemployment_share_read` | Pulse |

See Space Race → *Orbital debris* | Pulse (monthly) |

### Pulse Wiring (`extra_on_actions.txt`)

All pulse-based on_actions are routed through `extra_on_actions.txt`:

**`on_monthly_pulse_state`** (Root = State):
- `space_elevator_on_action` — wonder construction progress
- `solar_collector_on_action` — wonder construction progress
- `orbital_battlestation_on_action` — wonder construction progress
- `mind_upload_nexus_on_action` — wonder construction progress
- `antimatter_facility_on_action` — wonder construction progress
- `pollution_on_action` — state pollution modifier update
- `war_propaganda_on_action` — wartime propaganda effects
- `state_yearly_cultural_acceptance_add_on_action` — cultural acceptance
- `tourism_on_action` — tourism output/throughput modifier refresh (sole owner; the multipliers read monthly-varying `city_size_rank` and the live infrastructure balance and building levels)
- `ministry_of_thought_control_on_action` — monthly loyalists from `state_monthly_loyalists_add`, per incorporated state

**`on_monthly_pulse`** (Root = global):
- `city_rank_on_action` — city tier updates
- `global_warming_events_on_action` — GW threshold & recurring events

**`on_monthly_pulse_country`** (Root = Country):
- `remove_invalid_buildings` — space program placement validation
- `cheaty_on_action` — debug modifier (disabled)
- `combined_arms_update_on_action` — military doctrine bonuses
- `investment_pool_setup_on_action` — investment pool management
- `international_relations_events_on_action` — diplo events
- `decolonization_events_on_action` — decolonization narrative
- `movement_events_te_on_action` — political movement events
- `society_technology_events_on_action` — society tech events
- `world_war_events_on_action` — world war events
- `overbuild_protection_on_action` — prevents wonder overbuilding
- `aptitude_traits_cleanup_on_action` — strips aptitude traits from characters the game rules don't allow them on

**`on_yearly_pulse_state`** (Root = State):
- `global_warming_update_on_action` — GHG emissions calculation
- `te_homeland_monthly` — dynamic homeland progress (monthly state pulse)
- `violent_hostility_on_action` — cultural violence
- `migration_crowding_on_action` — migration pull reduction
- `religious_mission_conversion_on_action` — treaty-based conversion

**`on_yearly_pulse_country`** (Root = Country):
- `tech_spread_on_action` — technology diffusion
- `excess_private_construction_on_action` — Excess Private Construction (per-project construction cap raise with an efficiency penalty, removed the year it is no longer needed) and Overinvestment
- `fix_incompatible_laws` — auto-fix illegal law combos
- `construction_cost_scaling_on_action` — GDP-based construction costs
- `colonial_collapse_on_action` — tiny, poor AI countries absorbed or decentralized
- `assign_aptitude_traits_on_action` — character trait assignment

### Immediate Triggers (`extra_on_actions.txt`)

These fire instantly when the engine event occurs, providing same-tick responsiveness:

**`on_company_disbanded`** (Root = Country, scope:company = disbanded company):
- Calls `remove_disbanded_company_buildings_effect` on every state to remove buildings belonging to the disbanded company. Uses a 64-entry if/else_if mapping in `common/scripted_effects/company_building_cleanup_effects.txt`.

**`on_building_built`** (Root = Building):
- When a barracks is built, recalculates `apply_combined_arms_bonuses` for the owning country (new combat unit type enters a formation). Only fires if `country_combined_arms_bonus_enabled_bool` is true.
- Also used by the construction market (`te_construction_market_on_actions.txt`) to remove a finished state's construction site.
- Grand Monuments: `monument_events.1` (a construction site's level: the AI's dedication ceremony, a refresh). It missed a monument whose five queued levels finished on the same day, so the AI's ceremony also has a check in the monthly refresh and the site's levels are counted, with their vanity backlash, by the state pulse (§ Grand Monuments). A player's ceremony comes from the Dedicate button.

**`on_character_recruitment`** (Root = Character):
- Calls `update_characters` on the owner to immediately apply tech-based traits (immortality, logistics) to newly recruited characters instead of waiting for monthly pulse.
- Recalculates `apply_combined_arms_bonuses` for the owner (new general may change formation composition).

**`on_military_formation_created`** (Root = Military Formation):
- Recalculates `apply_combined_arms_bonuses` for the formation's country. Uses `country` accessor (not `owner`) to reach country scope from formation scope.

**`on_state_owner_change`** (Root = state):
- Removes `building_space_program` if the state has one and is not the new owner's market capital. Catches conquest scenarios same-tick instead of waiting for monthly `remove_invalid_buildings`.

**`on_acquired_technology`** (Root = Country):
- `add_arable_land_effect_on_action` — arable land from agricultural techs
- `fix_incompatible_laws` — law compatibility check
- `cultural_hegemony_tech_first_on_action` — world-first tech prestige (`cultural_hegemony_on_actions.txt`)
- `agricultural_diffusion_on_action` — broadcasts the first researcher of each diffusion-eligible tech

**`on_country_formed`** (Root = the new country), **`on_country_released_as_{independent,own_subject,overlord_subject,company_subject}`** (scope:target = the released country):
- `agdiff_backfill_on_country_formed` / `agdiff_backfill_on_released_country` — give the new country every agricultural-diffusion modifier whose world-first has already fired (`agdiff_backfill_diffusion_for_country`, stateless). The broadcast only reaches countries that exist at the time. Unlike the broadcast (recognized countries only), this backfill ignores country type; that predates #460 and is left as it was.

**Civil wars** (the shared hooks in `te_civil_war_on_actions.txt`, #467). `te_civil_war_on_won` runs `te_civil_war_resolve_sides`, then nuclear custody and the #460–#465 repairs (`agdiff_repair_after_civil_war`, `un_repair_after_civil_war`, `te_monetary_repair_after_civil_war`, `cr_repair_after_civil_war`, `sr_repair_after_civil_war`), then `te_civil_war_clear`. The agricultural-diffusion ones:
- `agdiff_on_uprising`, from `te_civil_war_on_start` at `on_revolution_start` / `on_secession_start` (Root = the original, scope:target = the uprising country) — gives the rebels each diffusion modifier the original holds (`agdiff_copy_diffusion_from_root`), and nothing the nation lacked, and marks them with `agdiff_cw_copied`. The rebel object is the one that survives a rebel victory, and a revolution's winner inherits no modifier from the loser.
- `agdiff_repair_after_civil_war`, from `te_civil_war_on_won` at `on_civil_war_won` (Root = the winner) — the backfill again, only when the revolutionaries won a revolution (`var:te_cw_rebels_won = 1`), the winner carries no `agdiff_cw_copied` (a backstop for wars begun before the rebels got the copy), and it is recognized; the marker is removed here. On a rebel win only (`te_cw_rebels_won = 1`), it also restores what is left of a lost `agdiff_first_mover_prestige`, read from `agdiff_first_mover_month` (recorded with the title) off a ladder of whole years left, and not restored for titles won before that variable existed, and re-points `first_<tech>_country` from the dead loser to the winner.

**`on_law_activated`** (Root = Law scope):
- `fix_incompatible_laws_from_law_scope` — law compatibility
- `te_fix_inconsistent_laws_from_law_scope` — generated per-lawgroup consistency cleanup
- `language_reform_law_on_action` — language reform init/cleanup
- `radical_law_backlash_on_action` — backlash events for radical laws
- `banking_law_cascade_on_law_activated` — command economy force-enacts state-owned banking

**`on_law_enactment_started`** (Root = Law scope):
- Fires `minor_events_timelineextended.2` (law enactment notification)

**`on_amendment_timeout`** (Root = Country, scope:amendment = expired amendment, scope:law = its law):
- `te_amendment_timeout_on_action` — routes to the sunset-clause expiry events (`amendment_on_actions.txt`; see § Temporary Amendments)

**`on_merge_markets`** (Root = dissolving market, scope:market = absorbing market):
- `gw_market_join_on_action` removes the dissolving leader's fossil-fuel tariff-rate modifier without writing native tariff levels. National climate policies remain with the country. Monthly `gw_refresh_tariff_policies_effect` clears lost customs authority; it never synchronizes national policies.


### Construction-Market Immediate Triggers (`te_construction_market_on_actions.txt`)

The construction market hooks many engine events to keep its construction sites placed on the current map:
- `on_merge_markets`, `on_create_market` — market changes
- `on_country_released_as_independent/own_subject/overlord_subject` — country releases
- `on_country_formed`, `on_capitulation`, `on_enemy/ally_capitulated_notification` — country events
- `on_diplo_play_back_down`, `on_war_end` — diplomatic resolutions
- `on_revolution_start`, `on_secession_start` — internal conflicts
- `on_wargoal_enforced` — war results
- `on_start_expanding_building`, `on_building_expanded`, `on_building_built` — building events
- `on_production_method_changed` — removes `pm_retooling` in games whose rule setting waives it (§ Market settings without retooling or maintenance)

### Scope Chain Limitation (Important)

Building, institution and law scopes **do not support variables or modifiers**. The state modifier refresh effects in `extra_effects.txt` use `add_modifier = { multiplier = script_value }`, which evaluates the script value through the parent scope chain, so calling them from building-scope hooks like `on_building_built` / `on_production_method_changed`, from `on_law_activated`, or from `on_acquired_technology` causes cascading errors. Those hooks have all been removed (a plain `remove_modifier` on the building itself is fine: `te_remove_waived_pm_retooling` runs from `on_start_expanding_building` and `on_production_method_changed`) — the **periodic state pulses are the only refresh sites**: `pollution_on_action` and `tourism_on_action` on `on_monthly_pulse_state`, `migration_crowding_on_action` and `free_port_tariff_update_on_action` on `on_yearly_pulse_state`. Pick the pulse whose cadence matches how fast the multiplier's inputs move, and give each modifier exactly one refresh site.

## AI Weights Guidelines

- **Journal entries:** `weight` determines priority in the JE list. Global issues use 1000+, personal/national issues use 10.
- **Scripted buttons:** `ai_chance = { value = 0 ... }` — base value with conditional `add` modifiers.
- **Diplomatic actions:** Key fields: `evaluation_chance`, `will_propose`, `propose_score`, `will_break`.
- **Treaty articles:** Key fields: `article_ai_usage = { offer request none }`, `evaluation_chance`, `inherent_accept_score`.
- Always look at **vanilla files** for AI pattern reference.

## Company AI

The engine picks one company at a time for the AI to work toward: among the types whose `ai_will_do` holds (and at least `attainable`), weighted by `ai_weight` (engine default 1) times its `NAI` `COMPANY_TYPE_*` factors (stickiness ×3 for 60 months, a formable bonus, predicted productivity, competition with companies already held). While planning it builds toward the type's `ai_construction_targets`. Numbers live in `common/script_values/te_company_ai_values.txt`.

- **Weights.** Vanilla gives its flavored companies 3 and generic ones nothing (1). The mod's 82 flavored companies get `te_company_ai_weight_flavored` (10), plus `te_company_ai_weight_home` (10) while the country holds one of the company's `preferred_headquarters` states; its 11 new generic companies get `te_company_ai_weight_generic` (3). `REPLACE:`/`INJECT:` entries are vanilla's companies and keep vanilla's weight.
- **Construction targets need a `state_trigger`.** Vanilla's `companies.md`: a target with an empty state trigger does nothing. Every mod target now names the company's preferred HQ states, the capital, or a state that already has the building (that last one covers mines and rigs whose resource the capital lacks). `test_company_ai.py` fails on a target without one, a mod flavored company without `ai_weight`, or a buildable flagship without `ai_value`.
- **Flagships** (`common/buildings/company_buildings.txt`) carry `ai_value = te_company_flagship_ai_value` (50000, vanilla's top tier). Their only max level comes from the company's prosperity bonus (on at 100, off below 75), so only a prosperous company's flagship can be built at all. Only the state's owner builds one (`te_company_flagship_builder_owns_state` in `possible` and `can_build_government`), so investment rights abroad never reach another country's flagship. Before the `ai_value`, the AI built 9% (2029 observer save) to 14% (2073 save) of its prosperous companies' flagships. If `ai_value` doesn't move that, the fallback is a decision that places the flagship (the Strategic Reserve hub and Space Program precedent).
- **Failing companies.** The engine's AI never disbands a company by choice (observer run 1972–2029: no surviving country dropped one company for another), so its slots fill before the mod's late-era companies unlock. `te_company_failing_monthly_effect` (`te_company_effects.txt`, on `on_monthly_pulse_country`) counts each company's consecutive monthly checks that fail either test (`te_company_fails_this_month`): prosperity below `te_company_failing_prosperity` (10), or owned levels (`company_owned_levels`) below `te_company_small_share` (0.1%) of the country's `building_levels`, saved as `scope:te_company_min_levels` before the iteration. The count lives in the company variable `te_company_months_failing`; an AI country removes one company a check once a count reaches `te_company_failing_months` (60, about 4.9 years), then runs the flagship cleanup. The size test catches a prosperous company too small to matter to a large economy; since the engine dissolves companies under 5 levels anyway, it only bites above 5,000 country levels. Together they stand in for "profit below 0.1% of GDP for five years", which script cannot read (no company profit trigger or link): on the 2073 save, of 406 AI companies with five years of history, 102 fell under the profit rule; prosperity alone flags 50 (41 of the 102), both tests 83 (52 of the 102, the rest earning a median 0.34% of GDP). Players are exempt; it models the AI choosing what a player chooses in the companies panel.
- **Flagship subsidies.** The engine's AI almost never changes a subsidy itself. It keeps the ones a building gets by default (ports, railways, power plants) and adds none: on the 2073 save it subsidized 0 of its 23 company buildings (the player 20 of 20), 0 of 140 shipyards, and 0 of 250 airports and highways outside the laws that force them. 12 of the 23 were under half staffed, some losing workers to subsidized buildings nearby, since a building that is not subsidized stops hiring below `BUILDING_DEFAULT_MIN_EARNINGS_TO_HIRE_EMPLOYEES`. `te_company_ai_subsidy_monthly_effect` (`te_company_effects.txt`, same monthly on-action) subsidizes every `bg_company_buildings` building of an AI country that is not in default, and removes those subsidies in default, because the AI never drops one on its own (in default it still paid for 60 of 61 railways). A subsidy only tops a building up to `SUBSIDIES_MIN_GAIN` (0), so a profitable flagship costs nothing. Players are exempt, as for dissolution. The mod's `country_building_*_require_subsidies_bool` forced-subsidy modifiers (airports and highways under Interventionism and Command Economy) held on only 35 of 52 such AI buildings in that save, so this uses `set_subsidized` on each building instead.
- **Verifying in an observer run:** company counts per country and companies lost while the country survived, from saves (the 2026-10-06 study's decoders: company records key `company_type` 0x5c80, prosperity 14193, `prosperous` 24210), and flagship counts with `scripts/analysis/save_world_report.py buildings`. Flagship subsidies: in a plain-text save each building record under `building_manager` carries `subsidized=yes` when subsidized; an AI flagship should have it unless its country is `in_default`.

## Decolonization System (`je_colonial_empire`)

### Overview

The decolonization system models the decline of colonial empires through a journal entry with a stability progress bar, scripted buttons for colonial policies, and a series of events. The system is designed so that **most colonial powers except the top 2-3 GPs will lose most of their colonies** after the `decolonization` tech is researched (era 6).

### Architecture

Three layers:
1. **Gate & Progress Bar:** `je_colonial_empire` activates when a country has colonial states and `decolonization` tech. The `colonial_stability_bar` (0-100, starts at 50) tracks how stable the empire is. At 0 the empire collapses; at 100 it solidifies.
2. **Player Interaction:** the **Colonial Stability widget** (`gui/journal_entry_widgets/colonial_empire_widget.gui`) is the human surface, laid out to `docs/guides/gui_style_guide.md`: an overview at the top (the stability bar with where it is heading in 12 months at this month's rate, green while rising and red while falling, and a thin line at the next band's edge; four of Banking's cells: the band and where the next begins, the great powers' escalation and net weight, what holds the entry (the colonies and colonial subjects, defined once as concepts), the programmes running; in the top band the months held at 100 and the months Solidified against their targets; the condemners' and supporters' shares of great-power prestige), then **Colonial Holdings** (every territory, largest GDP first, with each one's primary-culture share, standard of living and GDP against the colony tests and a Release button; every colonial subject with its kind, liberty desire, GDP and Release and Dominion buttons; Planned Full Decolonization), why stability is moving (each term a pillar bar over its range), international pressure (a row per great power with what it does to stability a month), the three programmes (each a level, 0-3, with a minus and a plus), two history charts and a collapsed How the Colonial Empire Works. The 3 decision buttons behind it carry `is_ai = yes` and are the **AI's** path to the decisions; the AI steps the programmes in a monthly review (§ Colonial Programmes below). Every surface calls the same `colonial_empire_possible_*` / `colonial_empire_effect_*` helpers; the per-target buttons are the player's alone (§ Colonial Holdings below). Full reference: `journal_entry_systems.md` § Colonial Stability Widget.
   **Timeline Extended window (2026-09-30; not yet seen in game).** The same panels also show on the *Colonial Empire* tab of the mod's own window (`gui/te_systems_window.gui`), under `datacontext = "[GetPlayerJournalEntry('je_colonial_empire')]"`, then a link back to the entry. The tab is greyed until the entry runs; its tooltip lists `ce_entry_unlocked` (the entry's technology and `possible`).
3. **Events:** 21 events fire from `decolonization_events_on_action` (monthly pulse), covering colonial negotiations, crackdowns, releases, GP stance choices, post-independence transitions, and the Suez Crisis model. `.70`-`.80` are the wars of independence (§ Wars of Independence below). `decolonization_events.400` / `.401` are the confirmation popups the three decisions open — each previews candidates and offers a "Reconsider" option, so nothing is released by pressing a button. `.402` / `.403` / `.404` are the per-target ones: one territory's release (grant or Round Table), one subject's independence, one colony's dominion status, each with Reconsider as its default.
