(b) **cover** — `covert_op_refresh_detection` stages the target network's strength on the operator as `iw_net_strength_staging` (0 without one), and `covert_operation_detection_chance` subtracts `covert_net_detect_reduction` = strength × 0.05 raw points (−5 at full) after the funding terms and before efficiency. The staging happens inside `covert_ops_sync_all`, before the monthly network pass, so detection uses last month's strength — a one-month lag, accepted. (c) **burn** — `covert_op_burn` takes `covert_net_burn_loss` = 25 off the target's network (unscaled — about a year of single-operation rebuilding).
- **Counterintelligence (2026-10):** a network also works against its target's operations. `covert_op_refresh_detection` looks in the *target's* `iw_nets` for the network whose `iw_target` is the operator (zeroed first, the write done inside the `random_in_list`, like the cover lookup), stages its strength on the operator as `iw_tgt_net_strength_staging`, and `covert_operation_detection_chance` adds `covert_net_catch_penalty` = strength × `covert_net_catch_factor` (0.1, so +10 at full) raw points after the target's counterintelligence penalty and before efficiency. Twice the cover factor on purpose: a penetrated service is the decisive counterintelligence advantage, and +10 is the one term that lifts a fully funded operation (raw −9 against an equal) off the 0.1 floor; two services holding full networks inside each other each run +5 on balance. A target without the journal entry has no networks (they come from its own operations, which need funding ≥ 1, or from a retaliation seed, which option b gates on the entry), so the lookup misses. The network row's country hover shows the figure (`je_iw_net_row_catch` inside `je_iw_net_row_tt`, `covert_net_catch_display` in network scope); the operator's row tooltip only says a network of theirs may sharpen their counterintelligence and prints no number for it. The row's `iw_detect` does include the term, so a player who works the published formula against the inputs the tooltip and overview print can infer the leftover — a weaker side channel to the defender rule than the tier-2 count, accepted (owner, 2026-10-07: a vague line, no number). AI: `covert_warfare.2` option c (expel) takes ×0.2 when the defender's network inside the perpetrator has reached intelligence tier 1 (`iw_net_intel_tier >= 1`, strength 50), because the expulsion is answered in kind and would cost it 25 of that network. Console: `event te_debug_covert.2` option k (every target gets a full network inside us).
- **Lookup rule:** every "network for target X" lookup does its work **inside** the `random_in_list` (`limit = { var:iw_target ?= X }`), never through a saved scope afterwards. Several run inside loops, where an unmatched pick would leave the previous iteration's network in a saved scope, and several sit on paths the engine also walks to render tooltips (the steppers' `covert_refresh_funding_state`, `covert_warfare.1`'s `after`), where a saved scope may be unset. `iw_net_head_start_offer` is restated by `covert_net_clamp` after every strength write, so a burn shrinks the head start a same-day relaunch gets.
- **Projection** (months from 0): strength 25 in 12.5 / 8.3 / 6.3 months with 1 / 2 / 3 operations; 50 in 25 / 16.7 / 12.5; 75 in 42 / 28 / 21; 90 in 65 / 44 / 33. Decay from 50 with no operations: 33 months (67 at funding ≥ 3).
- **Console:** `event te_debug_covert.2` options i (every network to full strength) and j (one network pass now).

### Network intelligence (2026-09, covert slice 7)
- **What:** a network strong enough reports on the service it has penetrated — display only, nothing in script reads the report back. Tier 1 (strength ≥ `covert_net_intel_tier_1_strength`, 50): the target's intelligence capacity and technology count, each printed beside our own. Tier 2 (≥ `covert_net_intel_tier_2_strength`, 75): also how many covert operations the target is running against us. With one operation a network reaches tier 1 in ~25 months and tier 2 in ~42; cultivate assets alone in ~17 / ~28.
- **The defender rule's one exception:** nothing else tells a country about hostile operations it has not caught (`covert_op_burn`'s header). The tier-2 count is that exception on purpose — it is earned by holding a strong network inside the other service, not given to the defender — and it says how many, never which operations or what they do.
- **Tier code:** `covert_net_intel_tier_value` (network scope) is the only place the two thresholds are compared; `covert_net_clamp` writes it to `iw_net_intel_tier` (0 / 1 / 2) after every strength write, beside the head-start offer, so a burn that drops a network below 75 or 50 hides that part of the report the same day. `covert_net_create` seeds 0. The widget reads only the code.
- **Report:** `covert_net_refresh_intel` (network scope, needs `scope:iw_net_operator`), called from `covert_nets_sync` step 3 straight after the strength write and from the console harness — never from a tooltip-walked path, because it uses saved scopes. At tier ≥ 1 it writes `iw_net_intel_ic` (the target's `intelligence_capacity_total`) and `iw_net_intel_techs` (`techs_researched`); at tier 2, `iw_net_intel_ops`, counted by accumulation over the target's hostile covert pacts (`is_hostile_covert_operation_pact`: Counterintelligence Support is not an operation against us) with `first_country` = target and `second_country` = us. Pacts, not the target's `iw_ops`: the containers only sync while the target's own journal entry is active. Every phase counts. Below a tier its values stay stored but hidden. Strength only rises in the monthly pass (or the harness), which refreshes right after, so a tier is never shown with values that were not written at it. Our own figures are live (`intelligence_capacity_total`, `covert_techs_researched_display`); theirs are last month's report.
- **Network row, not operation row:** the spec said "operation/network row". The report sits on the network row because the network outlives its operations. The operation row's detection line already printed the target's capacity (`iw_tgt_ic`) as a detection input before this slice, and still does, but only while an operation is running there.
- **Old saves:** a network from before this slice has no `iw_net_intel_tier` until its first monthly pass; every report line is gated on `ScriptContainer.HasVariable('iw_net_intel_tier')`, so for that month the row shows none.
- **Console:** `event te_debug_covert.5` — a: every network to 50; b: to 80; c: every network's target starts cultivate assets against us (target funding floored at 1) and the reports refresh, so a tier-2 row's count goes up by one. `te_debug_covert.2` option i (strength 100) now refreshes the report too.

### Tradecraft — agency experience (2026-09, covert slice 5)
- **What:** one country variable on the operator, `iw_tradecraft`, 0 – `covert_tradecraft_max` (100), seeded 0 by `covert_tradecraft_init` (from the JE's `immediate` and again at the top of every monthly pass, because `immediate` does not re-run for an entry already active in a loaded save). Its **only writers** are `covert_tradecraft_gain` / `covert_tradecraft_loss` (`covert_warfare_effects.txt` § TRADECRAFT), both no-ops while the variable is missing and both written with `set_variable = { value = { value = var:… add = … } }` + `clamp_variable` rather than `change_variable` (which does not reliably resolve a script-value operand). `iw_tradecraft_last_reason` records why it last moved: 1 operations maturing; 20 / 21 / 22 / 23 a mild / moderate / severe / wartime operation burned; 24 idle decay.
- **Gain:** `covert_tradecraft_monthly`, called **only** from the JE pulse, right after `covert_ops_age_all_durations` (never from `covert_ops_sync_all` / `covert_refresh_funding_state`, which run on every stepper click). Each hostile operation at establishing or better counts 1 and each still preparatory counts `covert_tradecraft_prep_gain_fraction` (0.5); the total, capped at `covert_tradecraft_ops_counted` (4), is `iw_tradecraft_ops` (shown in the tooltip), times `covert_tradecraft_gain_per_op` (1), scaled by `covert_tradecraft_gain_scale` = (100 − x) / 50 clamped [0.1, 1], the UN-standing shape. **Decay:** `covert_tradecraft_decay` (0.25) a month while no hostile operation runs. Counterintelligence Support earns nothing and does not hold the decay off: a service that only protects a friend is idle for this purpose (reason 24 says so).
- **Loss:** `covert_tradecraft_burn_loss`, called from `covert_warfare.1`'s `after` inside the same `exists = scope:detected_by_country` guard as `covert_op_burn`, and **before** `iw_burned_type_code` is removed (it branches on that variable through the `covert_code_tier_*` triggers): mild 3, moderate 6 (also any unrecognised code), severe 9, war 3 — unscaled. Both options' `covert_op_burned_tt` print the amount through `covert_tradecraft_burn_loss_value`. Standing an operation down costs nothing.
- **Balance:** detection rolls from month 0 and a burned operation is relaunched preparatory; the spec's closed form ignored both, and with preparatory operations earning nothing one moderate op at 10 % per-op detection averaged ~31. Preparatory operations therefore earn half (`covert_tradecraft_prep_gain_fraction`). Simulated long-run averages (600 months; network head start 0 / 5) and median months to Established: at 10 % one moderate op 57 / 69 (131 / 81 months), two 62 / 72 (62 / 39), four 67 / 74 (31 / 18), one severe 25 / 44 (208 / 138); at 5 % one moderate op 82 / 85 (62 / 51); at 2 %, 94 / 95. 10 % is funding 1 with no covert efficiency. Table: `covert_warfare_script_values.txt` § TRADECRAFT.
- **Tiers** (`covert_tradecraft_tier_1` … `_4`, the only place the floors are compared; `covert_tradecraft_tier` counts them 0–4): **Untested** < 20 ≤ **Fledgling** < 40 ≤ **Established** < 60 ≤ **Seasoned** < 80 ≤ **Veteran**. Names are loc only (`iw_tradecraft_tier_name_0..4`, via the `covert_tradecraft_tier_name` custom loc). The spec's fifth name, "Storied", was dropped: its unlock lines bind Established = 40, Seasoned = 60, Veteran = 80.
- **Bonuses:** `iw_tradecraft_bonus` (`country_intelligence_capacity_mult` +0.05) on `je:je_covert_warfare` with `multiplier = covert_tradecraft_bonus_mult` (= tier, via `owner = { }`), refreshed only by `covert_tradecraft_refresh_bonus` at the end of the monthly pass — +20 % capacity at Veteran. Networks grow ×(1 + `covert_tradecraft_net_gain_per_tier` 0.15 × tier), ×1.6 at Veteran: `covert_nets_sync` stages `iw_tc_net_mult_staging` on the operator and each network copies it into `iw_net_tc_mult` just before `covert_net_tick_gain` reads it (nominal gain, before `covert_net_gain_scale`). Networks tick earlier in the pulse than Tradecraft, so they grow at **last month's** tier.
- **Unlocks** (one trigger each, so each gate is one `custom_tooltip`; none ever ends something already running): `covert_tradecraft_unlocks_priority_3` (Established) — the step *to* priority 3 in `covert_possible_priority_up`, so it binds the row stepper and `covert_ai_manage_priorities` alike; an operation already at 3 stays there and stepping down is never gated. `covert_tradecraft_unlocks_severe_ops` (Seasoned) — read by regime change's and nuclear programme sabotage's `possible` (slice 6): launching only, so a running one survives the score falling. `covert_tradecraft_unlocks_extra_per_type` (Veteran) — +1 in `covert_ops_max_per_type`, which only gates launching.
- **Limitation:** Tradecraft accrues only while the journal entry is active (its pulse is the only clock) — the same limitation the detection roll has.
- **Console:** `event te_debug_covert.3` — set 45 (Established), set 85 (Veteran), one monthly pass now.
- **Naming:** funding level 2 used to be called "Tradecraft"; it is now **Professional**, so the word means only this score.

### New operations (2026-09, covert slice 6)
- **Regime change** (`covert_regime_change_action`, code 9, severe, ideological defence): needs a rivalry (launch and maintain), a non-subject target and **Seasoned** Tradecraft (launch only). Target modifier `covert_regime_change`: coup resistance −1, legitimacy −5, movement radicalism +5 %, all × phase × priority (up to ×3.2). Once fully operational, `je:je_ip4_coup ?= { add_progress = { value = covert_regime_change_coup_push … } }` (+5 a month) — no DLC gate: coups are base game. The coup bar moves weekly by commander strength − coup resistance, so each point of resistance removed is ~+4.3 progress a month; against a legitimacy-50 government a fully operational priority-1 operation adds ~+18 a month (table: `docs/superpowers/archive/plans/2026-09-23-covert-new-operations.md`).
- **Nuclear programme sabotage** (`covert_nuclear_sabotage_action`, code 10, severe, military defence): target must satisfy `nuclear_program_is_proliferating` (funded, running, not paused or disarming — a stockpiling nuclear power qualifies) and **Seasoned** Tradecraft to launch; it is maintained on `nuclear_program_is_standing` instead (the programme exists and is not paused by treaty or disarmed — funding is not read), so a target stepping its funding to 0 for a week cannot end the operation for free. Target modifier `covert_nuclear_sabotage`: `country_nuclear_program_progress_mult −0.25` × phase × priority — progress ×0.75 … ×0.2, never zero.
- **Space programme espionage** (`covert_space_espionage_action`, code 11, mild, economic defence): target must have completed a milestone we have not (`covert_target_ahead_in_space`, over all eight; milestone completion is public). Self modifier `covert_space_espionage` (+10 % milestone progress, −10 % risk, × phase × priority, from the strongest such operation); target marker `covert_space_espionage_detected` (authority −3, like the other espionage markers).
- **Cultivate assets** (`covert_cultivate_assets_action`, code 12, mild, ideological defence): **no effect on the target or the operator**. `covert_nets_sync` flags the network it feeds (`iw_net_cultivating`), and `covert_net_tick_gain` multiplies that network's growth by `covert_net_cultivate_mult` (1.5; stacks with the extra-operation factor and Tradecraft) — alone against a target, strength 50 in ~17 months and 75 in ~28 (25 and 42 for any other operation). Always counts towards Tradecraft at the preparatory fraction. **Priority is fixed at 1**: `covert_possible_priority_up` refuses it (binding the AI too) and its widget row hides the stepper and the phase and priority lines behind one line of its own. A burn still reaches the defender through `covert_op_burn`'s exposure record, like every other type's. The AI proposes it against a rival or an antagonised country where its network is below `covert_cultivate_ai_net_ceiling` (50), more keenly where it already runs another operation.
- **Secure loose material** (`covert_secure_material_action`, code 13, mild, military defence; 2026-09-26, `nuclear_crisis_design.md` §0.10 step 5): needs the `nuclear_weapons_enabled` rule too, and a target whose arsenal line has warheads unaccounted for (`nd_loose_has_line`), which is also its `requirement_to_maintain` — it ends by itself when nothing is left to find. **No modifier on anyone.** Its own block in `covert_ops_apply_all_phase_effects`: once established, each month a `covert_secure_material_chance` (`covert_secure_material_base_chance` 3 × `covert_op_effect_mult`: 3 % established, 6 % fully operational, 9.6 % at priority 3) of `nd_loose_recover_from_line` on the target — the warhead is destroyed and leaves the pool — and `nuclear_loose.9` for the operator; the target is never told. `test_covert_op_registry.ACTS_WITHOUT_MODIFIER` lets it act without a marker. AI: a major power or above proposes it against any target with a loose line (score 5, +5 for a neighbour; evaluation 0.05).
- **Console:** `event te_debug_covert.4` — plant all four (fully operational; rivalry declared for regime change; nuclear and space only if a qualifying target exists) and set Tradecraft to Seasoned.

### Colony operations (2026-10-26, solar colonization slice 5)
Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-26-solar-colonization-free-colonies-design.md` § 6. Both act on the target's colonies in the solar system, which under the Space Race rule's Simple and Full Colonies settings carry an autonomy figure (0–100; at 100 a colony breaks away as a free colony). Both need that rule (`sr_colonies_contested_enabled` in `potential`, so the actions are absent otherwise) and a target that holds a colony (`sr_has_space_colony`, `iw_target_holds_space_colony_tt`), in `possible` and as a `requirement_to_maintain`, so an operation ends by itself when the target's last colony goes. Neither leaves a modifier: each is in `test_covert_op_registry.ACTS_WITHOUT_MODIFIER` and has its own block in `covert_ops_apply_all_phase_effects`, which once established hands the operation's `covert_op_effect_mult` (1 establishing, 2 fully operational, × 1 / 1.35 / 1.6 by priority, so 1 to 3.2) to the space race's colony effect as `local_var:sr_cov_mult`, in the target's scope, guarded on `is_country_alive`. The colony effects and their constants live with the space race (`sr_cov_*`). No technology gate (they have their own: a colony to act on).
- **Incite colonial autonomy** (`covert_incite_autonomy_action`, code 15, moderate, ideological defence): `sr_cov_incite_autonomy` — every colony the target holds gains `sr_cov_incite_autonomy_base` (0.5) × the multiplier autonomy a month: 0.5 establishing at priority 1, 1 fully operational, 1.6 at priority 3. Operations from several countries add up.
- **Sabotage colony** (`covert_sabotage_colony_action`, code 16, severe, military defence): `sr_cov_sabotage_colony` — the target's most populous colony loses `sr_cov_sabotage_share` (1 %) × the multiplier of its people a month (1 % to 3.2 %) and gains `sr_cov_sabotage_autonomy` (0.25) × the multiplier autonomy (0.25 to 0.8). **Seasoned** Tradecraft to launch (`possible` only, as nuclear programme sabotage).
- **AI:** incite proposes against a target holding a colony while we hold one or run a milestone (`sr_has_space_colony` or `sr_has_running_milestone`), not a friend, with influence to spare; score 5, +5 against a rival; evaluation 0.02. Sabotage adds a rivalry or a war with the target; score 5, +10 at war, +5 aggressive ruler; evaluation 0.02 (+0.03 aggressive, ×0.25 cautious). Both are called off once settled when we have no stake in space left (no colony, no milestone running) or influence is in deficit; sabotage also when the hostility has gone (`covert_ai_hostility_gone`). Like the other severe operations, sabotage needs Seasoned Tradecraft, so the AI rarely launches it.
- **Survey colony defences** (`covert_survey_defences_action`, code 17, moderate, military defence; solar colonization slice 6, Full Colonies only: `sr_colonies_full_enabled` in `potential`): no modifier. `covert_ops_apply_all_phase_effects` calls `sr_cov_survey_reset` on the operator, then `sr_cov_survey_defences` in each established target's scope: the operator's `sr_cov_survey_targets` list, `sr_cov_survey_mult` (the strongest operation's multiplier) and the 35-day `sr_cov_survey_live`, read by `sr_cov_surveys_<key>`: +0.2 × the multiplier on our fleets' fire at the target's colony defences (`sr_cb_edge_<key>`), and the Fleets row's target hover shows the world's Defences, integrity and marines exactly (*Fleets, Space Command and combat*, Space Race). AI: a fleet power (`sr_fleet_power`) against a rival or an enemy holding a colony, not a friend; it breaks when no longer a fleet power, when hostility is gone outside a war, or in an influence deficit.
- **Icons:** byte copies, ideological subversion's art for incite, infrastructure sabotage's for sabotage and military espionage's for the survey, in both `diplomatic_action_icons/` and `lens_toolbar_icons/`.

### Technology theft (2026-10)
- **What:** every industrial espionage operation (production technologies) and military espionage operation (military technologies) that is established steals each month on its own, from its own target: `covert_ops_steal_tech_all` (`covert_warfare_effects.txt`, called from `covert_ops_apply_all_phase_effects`). Progress goes to our current research if it is in the category and the target has it, else to a random technology in the category that the target has, we lack and `can_research`, else nowhere. It replaced the +15 % production and military technology-spread modifiers (`covert_industrial_espionage`, `covert_military_espionage`: kept defined so saves load cleanly and stripped monthly by `legacy_modifier_cleanup.txt`, PENDING REMOVAL one release after 2026-10-06). Design: `docs/superpowers/archive/specs/2026-10-06-covert-tech-theft-design.md`.
- **Theft only, while there is something to steal (2026-10-07, owner's call):** the theft is all either type gives its operator; the target still carries its −3 authority marker. Industrial espionage's +5 weekly innovation (`covert_espionage_base`) and military espionage's +5 % unit offense and defense (`covert_military_espionage_unit`, which helped against every enemy, not only the target) are retired the same way as the spread modifiers (PENDING REMOVAL one release after 2026-10-07). Both types launch (`possible`) and run (a `requirement_to_maintain`, as space programme espionage does with its target's lead) only while `covert_tech_stealable_<category> = { TARGET = scope:target_country }` holds, so an operation ends by itself once the target has nothing left we could take, the player's and the AI's alike; the AI's `will_break` is `always = no`. Before this only industrial espionage had a launch gate, and neither had a keep gate (the AI's `will_break` was the only one), so a player could launch military espionage anywhere and keep either running with nothing to steal.
- **Amount:** `covert_tech_theft_share` (0.05) × the technology's era cost (`common/technology/eras/00_eras.txt`) × the operation's phase × priority multiplier: 5 % at base, 10 % fully operational, 16 % at priority 3. `add_technology_progress` takes a literal only, so `scripts/generators/gen_covert_tech_theft.py` writes the amounts: twelve `covert_tech_grant_era_N`, each branching on phase × priority the way `covert_op_add_scaled_modifier` does.
- **Generated** (rewritten on full `/reload`; `test_gen_covert_tech_theft.py` fails CI when stale): `covert_tech_steal_production` / `_military` (the current-research ladder, then a `random_list` with one gated entry per technology, behind the stealable check), `covert_tech_stealable_production` / `_military = { TARGET = … }` (the steal guard, and both types' `possible`, `requirement_to_maintain` and `will_propose`; it also accepts the technology being researched, as the steal's current-research branch does, so the keep gate can't end an operation that is still stealing), and `covert_stolen_tech_name` (`type = container` custom loc: technology number → its name key). Technologies with `can_research = no` are left out.
- **Record:** each operation's container keeps `iw_stolen_total` (progress stolen) and `iw_stolen_last` (the latest technology's number: its position in the generator's key-sorted list, so adding a technology shifts later numbers and an old save's row can name another technology until that operation's next theft); the row prints both (`je_iw_op_row_tech_stolen`, "nothing yet" before the first theft). The name comes from `type = container` custom loc called as `[ScriptContainer.GetCustom('covert_stolen_tech_name')]`, the mod's first use of either; confirmed rendering in game on 2026-10-06 (owner's check after #780).
- **Console:** `event te_debug_covert.6` runs one theft pass now.

### Friends and domestic backlash (2026-10-16)
- **Friend** (`covert_is_friend = { TARGET = X }`, `covert_warfare_triggers.txt`): the one definition every rule below asks. Relations with X at least cordial (20) **and** a tie (treaty alliance, defensive pact, the same power bloc, guarded by `is_in_power_bloc = yes` so two blocless countries don't match, or one the other's overlord or subject, through `is_subject_of`, which also counts a subject's subject), **or** relations at least amicable (50) with no tie. A tie never counts alone: two members of one bloc who dislike each other are not friends. Relations are read as `X.relations:this`, not `:root`, so the trigger answers from any country scope and the same from either side (the defender's backlash calls it with ROOT the attacker). Consumers: the attacker's backlash, the defender's backlash scaling, the AI's watch odds, Counterintelligence Support's `possible` and `requirement_to_maintain`, and the AI's launch and break checks.
- **The relations block is a cost.** The gates that refused six operations at good relations are gone: amicable on election interference, financial subversion, infrastructure sabotage, communications disruption and ideological subversion (`iw_no_good_relations_tt`), cordial on destabilization (`iw_no_cordial_relations_tt`, and its second `requirement_to_maintain`, which ended it at cordial). Any operation may be run against a friend, and a catch costs the attacker at home and abroad. The intelligence-sharing treaty gate (`iw_no_intel_sharing_tt`) stays on every hostile operation: it is a treaty obligation, not the relations block. Each hostile action's launch preview adds `covert_friend_target_warning_tt` when the target is a friend (an `if = { limit = { covert_is_friend … } custom_tooltip }` in `accept_effect`, after the detection warning). The AI side is under § AI Behavior.
- **Attacker's home backlash:** `covert_backlash_home = { SHARE = full|half }` is the last line of each `covert_warfare.1` option: Acknowledge pays the full share, Deny half. A gate, then a dispatch (`covert_backlash_home_$SHARE$`) onto two internals that hold the literals. It does nothing unless `iw_burned_friend = 1` (copied in `.1`'s `immediate` from `covert_is_friend` against the target, with the other `iw_burned_*` copies, removed in `after`) and the exposure is not costless (`covert_exposure_is_costless`). Tier columns are mild / moderate / severe; a war-tier code that is not costless (caught in the run-up to war) takes the severe values, and an unrecognised code the moderate:

  | share | appeasement | legitimacy (`covert_friend_spying_scandal` multiplier) |
  |---|---|---|
  | full (Acknowledge) | −3 / −5 / −8 | −3 / −5 / −8 |
  | half (Deny) | −2 / −3 / −4 | −2 / −3 / −4 |

  Appeasement: every `lobby_pro_country` with the target as its `target`, or `lobby_pro_overlord` when the target is the overlord of the lobby's country (`covert_backlash_pro_lobby_of`, the one definition both halves use), through `change_appeasement` with the factor `appeasement_covert_spying_exposed` ("Caught Spying on Them", `common/political_lobby_appeasement/te_covert_appeasement.txt`). The factor is `is_always_usable = yes`, because vanilla's lobby types list their own factors and an unlisted, not-always-usable one is rejected (`Appeasement change failed`); `appeasement_special_events_negative` is the fallback. The lobby's interest groups lose approval through the lobby itself, so there is no separate approval hit. With no such lobby `covert_backlash_no_lobby_tt` replaces the appeasement line and the legitimacy hit still lands. Legitimacy is the static modifier `covert_friend_spying_scandal` (`country_legitimacy_base_add = -1`, decaying, `days = short_modifier_time`, 913, about 2.5 years) with a **literal** multiplier per branch: `multiplier` is re-evaluated against ROOT on later ticks and `iw_burned_type_code` is gone by then, so a value reading it would fall to zero (`modifier_multiplier_var_audit`). Abroad, the existing infamy and relations costs apply, with the relations hit ×1.5 when the target was a friend (`covert_exposure_friend_relations_mult`, applied once in `covert_exposure_relations_deny`; Acknowledge's half derives from it, so applying it in both would give ×2.25).
- **Defender's public reaction:** `covert_backlash_public`, called in `.1`'s `after` as `scope:detected_by_country = { covert_backlash_public = yes }`, after the burn chain and before `covert_tradecraft_burn_loss` and `.2`. Every exposure passes it, whoever chose it (the target's `.3` or panel click, an AI, or a target with no service), and it sits there rather than in `.2`, whose 24-month cooldown would skip it. Each member of each lobby that favours the attacker (`covert_backlash_pro_lobby_of` with `TARGET = ROOT`, ROOT being the attacker) takes `covert_foreign_ties_discredited` (`interest_group_pol_str_mult = -0.05`) with a literal multiplier 1 / 2 / 3 by tier (severe or non-costless war tier takes 3), ×1.5 when the attacker was a friend (1.5 / 3 / 4.5), for `short_modifier_time`, decaying. Nothing when the exposure is costless or the defender has no such lobby. It sets `iw_last_exposed_public = 1` on the defender when it applied, and removes it otherwise (nothing else clears the exposure record, so a stale flag would print the line on a later burn), for `.2`: a second `first_valid` child of `desc` (`covert_warfare.2.d_public` / `_unnamed`, "At home, public anger has turned on X's friends."). The `probe_result_events.txt` shape it copies has no in-game confirmation; the flavor chain is the fallback (play-test list). `.2` after an exposure the defender itself ordered still opens "Our counterintelligence services have uncovered evidence…" although it has known for months: text only, left as is. A watched operation causes none of this until it is exposed.

### Watching a caught operation (2026-10-16)
- **Flow.** `covert_ops_roll_detection_all` (the operator's JE pulse) saves the catch as `scope:iw_burned_op`, its target as `scope:iw_catch_target` and the operator as `scope:iw_catcher_attacker` (operations carry no operator, and the target's event needs one). Then by target: with `covert_can_watch` (the game rule on and `je_covert_warfare` active, the test `covert_warfare.2`'s Retaliate in kind applies) and a **player**, the operation gets `iw_catch_pending = 1` (the roll skips it) and `covert_warfare.3` fires on the target (`duration = 3`, which is months, so a player may leave it open that long): **Expose them** (default) or **Let it run, and watch**; with an **AI**, `covert_watch_ai_decide` watches by chance, else the operation is exposed at once; with **no service**, exposed at once, today's flow. **Exposing** is `covert_exposure_fire` on the attacker, which opens `.1` (the attacker's Acknowledge or Deny, `after` burns the operation and fires `.2` on the target). Costs are computed from the operation's phase at the time of exposure, so a long-watched operation pays the ×1.5 fully operational factor. **Watching** is `covert_watch_start` on the target: `iw_known = 1` on the operation (the attacker's panel never shows it and it gets no event), `covert_net_create` for a network inside the attacker if there is none (no seed amount), and a record. `.3`'s options read the operation inside `hidden_effect` under a `custom_tooltip` and guard every use with `exists`, since the operation can end while it is open.
- **One exposure in flight per attacker.** `.1` keeps its burned operation on the attacker (`iw_burned_type_code` and siblings), so two open at once would overwrite each other. `covert_exposure_fire` is **the only trigger site of `.1`** (the roll, the AI's catch, `.3` Expose and every later exposure call it, so each pays the backlash, infamy and Tradecraft loss `.1` resolves). It takes the lock, `iw_expose_inflight = 1` on the attacker, before `trigger_event` (the event's `immediate`, which sets the lock's other half `iw_burned_type_code`, may not run inside the calling effect); `.1`'s `after` clears it. `covert_exposure_in_flight` is either variable. While held, the roll skips that attacker for the month, the Known Foreign Operations Expose greys with a reason, `.3` Expose while locked watches the operation with `iw_expose_ordered = 1` and fires `covert_warfare.4` four days later, a retry: a player attacker may leave `.1` open for up to its month, so the target's monthly pass retries any order still waiting. Failsafe (`covert_watch_attacker_monthly`): a pass that finds the lock with no `.1` open raises it, and the second such pass removes it, so a `.1` that never ran costs one to two months. A `.1` that opened and never closed is caught the same way: a revolution that wins while it is open hands its copies to the winner, whose lock would then hold for good, since the loser's event and its `after` die with the loser. Each pass that finds `iw_burned_type_code` counts itself on `iw_burned_seen` (which `.1`'s `after` removes with the copies); the pass that brings the count to `covert_open_event_stale_passes` (5) removes the copies, the lock and the count. An event's `duration` is in months: `.1` is `duration = 1` (a longer event would let a player attacker stall its own detection roll by leaving it unanswered; at one month a stall skips at most one roll per catch), `.3` is 3, and five passes come four months after either opened at the soonest. A panel click is never queued: the button stays greyed until `.1` has closed, which a player attacker may take weeks over; `.3`'s Expose is the one that waits.
- **Records.** One container per watched operation, on the **defender**: tags `iw_known_rec` + `iw_known_<TYPE>`, parent the defender, listed in its `iw_known_ops`; variables `iw_attacker`, `iw_attacker_capital` (restated monthly, for the row's flag and name), `iw_type_code`, `iw_watch_months`, `iw_watch_net` (our network's strength inside the attacker, restated monthly, which the AI's expose chance and the row hover read), `iw_expose_ordered` (an exposure is ordered or waiting) and `iw_expose_sent` (`.1` has been opened for it). A record names its operation by (attacker, type code), not by a reference to the attacker's container: the no-duplicate rule makes the pair unique per operator, and `covert_watch_op_matches` (`iw_known`, target, type code, the code compared through a staged country variable, never `PREV` or the container's own `var:`) finds the live operation. A relaunch of the type carries no `iw_known`, so an old record never adopts it. **Reaping:** `covert_op_destroy` and `covert_op_sync`'s direct reap call `covert_watch_forget = { ATTACKER TYPE }` for an `iw_known` operation (burn, stand-down, a broken pact and a relaunch clear all remove the row the same day); `covert_watch_monthly` reaps what is left (a dead attacker's culled containers). `covert_watch_attacker_monthly` also clears an `iw_catch_pending` that reaches `covert_open_event_stale_passes` (four months after the roll, past `.3`'s three: `.3` never ran) and an `iw_known` whose target holds no matching record, so a revolution (the winner inherits neither lists nor containers: a government overthrown loses what it watched, owner's call) makes the operation catchable again. Old saves: every read of `iw_known_ops` sits behind `has_variable_list`.
- **The target's monthly pass** (`covert_watch_monthly`, from the JE pulse straight after `covert_nets_sync`, which has just counted the records into the networks: growth has no other clock, so a defender who loses the entry keeps its records and stops growing): reap, age (`iw_watch_months`) and restate, retry waiting exposures, and the AI's exposure roll.
- **Network growth.** Each watched operation not already ordered for exposure adds `covert_net_watch_gain_p1` / `_p2` / `_p3` = 4 / 5.4 / 6.4 a month (4 × the priority effect multipliers 1.35 and 1.6, read from the attacker's live operation) to `iw_net_watch_gain` on our network inside the attacker, summed in `covert_nets_sync` step 2. It reaches the strength through `covert_net_watch_tick_gain` (× our Tradecraft and the UN host's multipliers, not the cultivate-assets factor) and `covert_net_gain` (so the diminishing return above half strength applies). Compare 2 a month for an operation of our own and 25 once for the Retaliate-in-kind seed: one watched operation outgrows the seed in about six months, and the price of watching is the harm the operation keeps doing, at full strength, meanwhile. A watched network does not decay. The figures are starting values, to tune in play.
- **AI odds** (`covert_ai_watch_chance`, percent, at the catch): watch 60 for a mild, moderate or war-tier operation, 15 for a severe one (`covert_code_tier_severe`), +20 when the attacker is a friend, flat 10 once our network inside the attacker has reached 75 (the other terms drop out). Each month, per record with no exposure ordered (`covert_ai_watch_expose_chance`): expose with 2 + 0.1 per point of network strength, 25 once it reaches 75, +5 for a severe operation. The choice is the AI-specific part only; no outcome branches on `is_ai`.
- **Known Foreign Operations panel and Expose button:** `journal_entry_systems.md` § Covert Warfare → Panels. The button only orders the work (sets `iw_expose_ordered`, fires `covert_warfare.4`); `.4` is hidden, copies every ordered record to a temporary list (an exposure can forget a record) and calls `covert_watch_expose_record` on each, which forgets a record whose operation or attacker is gone, leaves one waiting while the attacker is locked, and otherwise opens `.1` from inside the attacker's lookup. The exposure is not in the scripted GUI's effect because the engine walks those to render tooltips (the trophies pattern, `monument_trophy_events.10`–`.13`).
- **Self-checks** (`TE_SELF_CHECK OK|BROKEN <name>` in `debug.log`, once a game each, separate OK and BROKEN flags): `covert_catch_decision` (OK in `.3`'s `immediate`: the roll's saved scopes crossed attacker to defender; BROKEN from the attacker's pending watchdog), `covert_exposure_lock` (BROKEN only, from the stale-copy failsafe above: a `.1`'s `after` never ran) and `covert_watch_expose` (OK in `.1`'s `immediate` when the operation had `iw_known`: the target's order crossed defender to attacker; BROKEN from the target's monthly pass when an exposure was sent, its operation lives and its attacker is not locked). Fallbacks and the other in-game unknowns (the Expose button's `AddScope` container link, several `.1` fired from one effect each binding its own `iw_burned_op`) are in `docs/testing/covert-counterintel-playtest.md`.

### Counterintelligence Support (2026-10-16)
- **What:** `covert_counterintel_support_action`, type 14 (registry row `("counterintel_support", 14, "ideological", "mild", "covert_counterintel_support")`; mild is nominal). Our officers lent to a friend's counterintelligence: the static modifier `covert_counterintel_support` (+8 on each of `country_covert_defense_economic_add`, `_military_add` and `_ideological_add`) lands on the **target** through `covert_op_apply_target_effect`, so phase and priority scale it: nothing while preparatory, ×1 from month 6, ×2 from month 12, × the priority effect 1.35 / 1.6 (8 to 25.6 per axis). `is_hostile = no`, `should_notify_third_parties = no`, `requires_approval = no` (the ally is notified: "has begun supporting our counterintelligence services"). It costs an operation slot, upkeep (a priority share), a pact cost of 25 influence (the mild tier) and counts against the per-type cap. Ungated by technology (`UNGATED`). `possible`: funding ≥ 1, a free slot, under the cap, no duplicate, `covert_action_valid_target` (not decentralized), `covert_is_friend`, and no other protector. `requirement_to_maintain`: funding ≥ 1 and `covert_is_friend`, so it lapses with the friendship. No truce check and no `iw_no_intel_sharing_tt`: that gate is for hostile operations. It has a priority stepper, a Stand down button and no Detection Risk figure (the row says "Detection Risk: none, an open arrangement").
- **One protector per ally.** A named modifier on one country doesn't stack with itself, so a second protector could only overwrite the first. `iw_cis_protector` (country variable on the **target**) is set by `covert_op_create`'s non-hostile branch, cleared by `covert_op_destroy` and `covert_op_sync`'s direct reap when it still names the operator, and dropped when stale by `covert_warfare_monthly_country` on the target's own monthly pulse (a dead protector's pulse never runs; it needs no journal entry): `NOT = { var:iw_cis_protector ?= { has_diplomatic_pact = { who = ROOT type = covert_counterintel_support_action is_initiator = yes } } }`, the shape of `un_lobby_runs_campaign_on` (`un_lobby_triggers.txt`: the target's side did not see the initiator's one-sided pact in play). `possible` accepts a target with no mark or one that is ours. Unproven in game (play-test items 9 and 10: the mark surviving a month, and whether the shared no-duplicate gate, which passes no `is_initiator`, blocks mutual protection).
- **The protector gets nothing** (owner). Every consumer that treats an operation as a threat or a foothold reads `covert_op_is_hostile` (container) or `is_hostile_covert_operation_pact` (pact), which exclude the type by tag: the detection roll (never caught, never watched, never burned: `.1`'s chain keeps a row for code 14 that is unreachable, like `covert_caught_type_name`); `covert_nets_sync` steps 1 and 2 (no network inside the ally, no growth); `covert_op_create` (no head start and no network: it sets the protector mark instead); the tier-2 count of operations against us (`covert_net_refresh_intel`); `covert_tradecraft_monthly` (no gain, and no help against idle decay); `covert_ai_manage_priorities` (the war and rivalry escalation sits behind `covert_op_is_hostile`, so it stays at priority 1); cultivate assets' AI `propose_score` bonus for another operation against the target; and the console harness's detection and hostile-network helpers. Unchanged on purpose: the slot and upkeep (`covert_operations_active` and the funding floor count it), the per-type cap, phases, `covert_op_add_scaled_modifier`, priority (it scales the boost and the upkeep) and Stand down. The UN dossier and docket, election confidence and the backlash read exposure records or type codes only, which it never produces.
- **Intelligence-sharing shield:** `update_intel_sharing_defense` reads the parties' defence modifiers. The ally's +8 counts once in its own base defence, and a partner of the ally can take up to half the gap through the shield at the next yearly pulse. No loop (shields are stripped before comparing) and no double count on the ally.
- **AI** (`will_propose`): the target is a friend **and** (a power bloc member of a bloc we lead, our subject, or a treaty ally); our `intelligence_capacity_total` is greater than the target's; we run no other Counterintelligence Support; a free slot; funding ≥ 1; not in default; `covert_ai_can_spare_influence`. Evaluation 0.05; score 5, +5 for our own subject; `will_break = { always = no }` (the maintain check ends it). The AI's funding rule is unchanged, so an AI with no rivals, no war and no operations holds funding 0 and never launches it.
- **Icon:** a black glove holding up a round steel shield (icon batch 6, 2026-10-27), `covert_counterintel_support_action.dds` with its lens copy; the widget row draws the same file.

### Election Interference & Electoral Confidence
- **Gate:** Election interference (`covert_election_interference_action`) requires the target to have an elected legislature (Landed/Wealth/Census/Universal Suffrage). If the target abolishes elections, the operation auto-cancels via `requirement_to_maintain`.
- **Electoral Confidence Effect:** On `on_election_campaign_end`, the system checks if any country has an active election interference operation against the country holding the election. Based on the **worst** (most advanced) operation among all attackers:
  - **Preparatory phase** (<6 months): No effect.
  - **Establishing phase** (6–11 months): `-0.05` electoral confidence.
  - **Fully Operational** (12+ months): `-0.1` electoral confidence.
  - Both are halved while the country hosts a UN electoral observer mission with any strength (`un_mission_hosts_with_strength`): a Moribund UN's mission has none and halves nothing.
- **Operation matching:** For each attacker with an election-interference pact against ROOT, reads the attacker's `iw_ops` container tagged `iw_op_election_interference` whose `iw_target` is ROOT, and takes its phase.
- **On-action:** `covert_warfare_on_actions.txt` → `on_election_campaign_end` → `on_actions = { covert_warfare_election_end }` → calls `covert_op_election_confidence_effect` scripted effect.
- **Notification:** `iw_election_interference_confidence` message sent to the affected country.

### AI Behavior
- **Evaluation chance:** Low (0.02–0.05) to prevent spammy toggling. Aggressive rulers get +0.02–0.03, cautious rulers get ×0.25–0.5.
- **Will propose guards:** `in_default = no`, `country_rank >= rank_value:major_power` (peacetime ops), rivalry/antagonistic/domineering attitude required, IC advantage check for some ops.
- **Target size (2026-10):** upkeep scales with the operator's GDP (`covert_operations_cost_scale`), not the target's, so against a much smaller country an operation costs more than it returns. Every operation whose payoff scales with the target's size carries `covert_ai_target_worth_the_upkeep = { TARGET = scope:target_country }` (`covert_warfare_triggers.txt`) in `will_propose`: the target passes unless our GDP is at least `covert_ai_much_weaker_gdp_factor` (10) times its own (`covert_ai_target_much_weaker`), and a much weaker target still passes when we have money to burn (`covert_ai_has_money_to_burn`: gold reserves at least `covert_ai_spare_reserves_ratio` (0.5) full — a tenth of a year's GDP, since the limit is 20 % — and `net_fixed_income > 0`). Gated: election interference, financial subversion, influence campaign, ideological subversion, destabilization, regime change, cultivate assets, and the two wartime operations, which skip the test while `is_losing_war_against` the target. Exempt, because the payoff is our own progress or a threat removed: industrial, military and space programme espionage, nuclear programme sabotage, secure loose material; and the two colony operations, whose payoff is the target's colonies, not its size. Launch only — a running operation never lapses for it, and humans never see it. `test_covert_ai_targets.py` makes every type sit on one list.
- **Friends (2026-10-16):** the six operations the old relations block covered (election interference, financial subversion, infrastructure sabotage, communications disruption, ideological subversion, destabilization) carry `NOT = { covert_is_friend = { TARGET = scope:target_country } }` in `will_propose`, so the AI does not start them against a friend; so do the two colony operations (2026-10-26), written that way, though the AI does not call them off when the target turns friend. The other hostile operations have no friend test (regime change and nuclear programme sabotage need a rivalry or a hostile attitude to launch): the AI can still run espionage, an influence campaign, cultivate assets or secure loose material against a friend, and pays the backlash when caught.
- **Watching (2026-10-16):** an AI target with a covert service decides at the catch in script (`covert_watch_ai_decide`) and exposes watched operations by a monthly chance; figures in § Watching a caught operation. Counterintelligence Support's AI rule is in § Counterintelligence Support.
- **Propose score:** Scales with rivalry (+10), great power rank (+5–7), aggressive ruler (+5–8).
- **Calling an operation off (2026-10):** an operation does nothing for six months and reaches full strength at twelve, while upkeep runs from the first month, so every covert action spells out its AI `will_break` rather than leaving it to the engine's default. Before this, none had one, and the launch tests in `will_propose` (a free slot, intelligence capacity, target size, `in_default`) were the only AI test an operation had: if the engine falls back to "break once `will_propose` fails", filling the last slot made every running operation breakable. Now the AI keeps an operation until it is fully operational, `covert_ai_op_settled = { TYPE TARGET }` (`covert_warfare_triggers.txt`, on `covert_op_is_fully_operational`; a pact without its container yet reads as not settled). After that it ends it only once its reason has gone, judged more loosely than at launch. Election interference, financial and ideological subversion, destabilization, regime change and nuclear programme sabotage stop at `covert_ai_hostility_gone`: no rivalry either way, no antagonistic, belligerent or domineering attitude, and relations above poor, where launch needs only our rivalry or one of two attitudes. The first four (election interference, financial and ideological subversion, destabilization) also stop once the target is a friend (`covert_is_friend`, a third branch of the `OR` in `will_break`, behind the same settle wait); infrastructure sabotage and communications disruption keep `always = no`. Space programme espionage stops when we run no milestone of our own; the two colony operations when we have no stake in space left (no colony and no milestone running), and sabotage colony also at `covert_ai_hostility_gone`. Cultivate assets stops once its network reaches `covert_cultivate_ai_net_done` (75, intelligence tier 2), whatever its age, since it pays from its first month; a network decays back to the launch ceiling of 50 in ~17 months. It also stops once settled if the hostility has gone. The wartime operations, influence campaign, secure loose material and industrial and military espionage carry `will_break = { always = no }`: their `requirement_to_maintain` already ends them when their purpose does. Launch-only tests never break anything. `test_covert_ai_targets.py` makes every type take one of these rules.
- **AI Funding Management:** The JE monthly pulse sets `iw_funding_level` outright for every `is_player = no` country — this, not a button, is the AI's path into funding. Branches, in order: in default or bankrupt → 1 if it has operations (dropping to 0 would lapse them all and waste the setup), else 0; otherwise, if major power or above **and** (rivalled or at war) → at war: `iw_funding_level_max` for a great power, else 3; at peace: 3 for a great power (whether or not it already runs 3+ operations), else 1; otherwise 1 if it has any operation running, else 0. A human's level comes from the widget's stepper and is never overwritten.
- **AI Priority Management (2026-09, covert slice 3):** `covert_ai_manage_priorities`, run for every `is_player = no` country immediately before `covert_ops_sync_all` in the monthly pulse (so the sync sees the new priorities the same tick). In default or bankrupt, the wanted level is 1 (never raises while the treasury is in that state); otherwise a great power at war with the operation's own target wants 3, a country with a rivalry pact against the target wants 2, and everything else wants 1. Each operation's `iw_priority` steps toward its wanted level at most twice per direction per month, through the same `covert_possible_priority_up`/`_down` gates the human stepper uses, so slice 5's Tradecraft requirement for priority 3 binds the AI too.
- **Wartime ops:** Higher eval chance (0.05), no rank requirement, `in_default = no` guard only. `propose_score` 15, +10 rivalry pact with the target, +5 GP, +5 when `is_losing_war_against = { ENEMY = scope:target_country }` (battlefield read from `common/scripted_triggers/nuke_triggers.txt`; see § War Support Feeds).
- **Slice-6 operations (2026-09):** regime change — rivalry plus an antagonistic or domineering attitude, major power or above; score 5, +5 great power, +8 aggressive ruler; evaluation 0.02. Nuclear programme sabotage — target proliferating, we are a nuclear power or a great power, and rival or antagonistic; score 5, +10 when the target's programme is at 75 % or more, +5 great power. Space programme espionage — target ahead in space and we are pursuing a milestone; score 10, +5 great power. Cultivate assets — rival or antagonistic, and our network there below `covert_cultivate_ai_net_ceiling` (50); score 5, +5 when we already run another operation there; evaluation 0.05. **The AI will rarely launch the two severe operations:** `possible` binds it, so it needs Seasoned Tradecraft, and one moderate operation at 10 % detection averages 57.

### Cancellation Conditions
- **All 14 peacetime ops** (election interference, financial subversion, industrial espionage, military espionage, influence campaign, ideological subversion, destabilization, slice 6's regime change, nuclear programme sabotage, space programme espionage and cultivate assets, secure loose material, and the two colony operations) have truce checks in both `possible` and `requirement_to_maintain`, so they auto-cancel if a truce with the target begins. None of them has a war guard (the actions say "Allowed during war"): a war with the target does not end them.
- **Slice-6 operations also lapse** when their own condition goes: regime change when the rivalry ends; nuclear programme sabotage when the target's programme is paused by treaty, given up or gone (`nuclear_program_is_standing` — not when its funding merely drops to 0); space programme espionage once the target is no longer ahead; cultivate assets when the target becomes decentralized; secure loose material when the target's line has no warhead left unaccounted for; the two colony operations when the target holds no colony.
- **Counterintelligence Support** has no truce check and no intelligence-sharing gate; it lapses when funding drops below 1 or its target stops being a friend (`covert_is_friend`). Relations end no operation (Destabilization does not lapse at cordial); the AI alone calls the four breakable formerly blocked ones off once the target is a friend (§ AI Behavior).
- **Wartime ops** (infrastructure sabotage, communications disruption) require active war with the target **or** a diplomatic play against them under way (2026-09, covert slice 2, Task 8 — see § Graduated exposure blowback); they auto-cancel once neither holds, e.g. the play resolves without war, or peace is achieved.
- **Script value scope:** All covert warfare SVs use `owner = {}` wrapping to access country-scope data from JE scope (the `on_monthly_pulse` context). This is required because the JE monthly pulse runs in journal entry scope, not country scope.
- **Stand down:** `covert_effect_stand_down` (called only from the widget's seventeen `covert_stand_down_<type>_sgui` handlers) ends one operation on demand: `remove_diplomatic_pact` plus `covert_op_destroy`. That reaches the same end state as a manual break in the diplomacy outliner, whose `manual_break_effect` is `covert_op_end` → the same `covert_op_destroy`; the effect's `any_in_list` guard makes it idempotent, so it is correct whether or not `remove_diplomatic_pact` also fires the break hook. No infamy and no relations hit — those belong to being caught, not to calling an operation off.

### Known Behaviours (not bugs to fix in passing)
- **Detection was a single country-level roll until 2026-09 (covert slice 1).** It rolled once against the worst target's intelligence capacity combined with an arbitrary target's type defence, then burned a *random* operation, and the `random_list { 1 = { add = c } 99 }` form made the odds (1 + c) / (100 + c) rather than c %. It now rolls per operation (see **Detection** above). Two script values from the old roll's display layer, plus the unused `covert_ops_detected_infamy` constant, were deletion candidates and have since been deleted (`covert_detection_chance_display`, `covert_detection_target_ic_display`, `covert_ops_detected_infamy`) — none remain anywhere in the mod. `covert_detection_base_display`, `covert_detection_efficiency_pct_display` and `covert_ops_funding_detection_reduction_display` are a different set: they feed the JE's detection-factors tooltip (`je_iw_detection_factors` in `te_journal_entries_l_english.yml`) and remain live. `covert_detection_efficiency_reduction` is the one old-roll value still defined and unreferenced (`covert_warfare_script_values.txt`) — remaining deletion candidate for a later slice.
- **Losing a slot deactivates the entry but does not stop the operations.** The JE's `possible` gate wants one slot above the rank baseline; no `requirement_to_maintain` checks slots, so operations already running continue (and stay visible in the outliner) while the journal entry and both widgets disappear.
- **`covert_warfare.2` keyed infrastructure sabotage on its state modifier until 2026-09 (covert slice 6)**, so a burned sabotage operation never reached the defender; slice 6 keyed it on the country-scope `covert_infra_sabotage_morale`.
- **`covert_warfare.2` never reached the defender of an operation burned during preparation until #430 (2026-09-25).** Its trigger listed the modifier each type leaves on its target, and those are applied only from the establishing phase. It now keys on the exposure record `covert_op_burn` writes for every burn (`iw_last_exposed_type`, with `iw_last_exposed_phase` for the text), and it names a burn stopped in preparation as one that never took effect. Its option b, **Retaliate in kind**, used to take 3 infamy off the defender and retaliate against nobody: it now seeds the defender's own network inside the perpetrator (`covert_retaliation_seed_network`, `covert_net_retaliation_seed` = 25, the size of the burn's own network loss), open to a country whose covert journal entry is active. The infamy relief became option c, **Make the evidence public**; since #448 option c is **Expel their diplomats** instead: `covert_net_expel` takes `covert_net_expulsion_loss` (25) off the perpetrator's network inside the defender, the same off any network of the defender's inside the perpetrator (expulsions are answered in kind), and relations fall by 25. It needs the perpetrator, like b.
- **`covert_warfare.2` names the perpetrator and the operation (2026-09-26).** Until then its text said only "agents of a foreign power", although option b already named the country. The `_named` descs (`covert_warfare.2.d_named`, `.d_preparatory_named`) print `#b [SCOPE.sCountry('iw_exposed_by').GetName]#!` — vanilla's own country link, flag and hover tooltip included — and are chosen only while `scope:iw_exposed_by` exists; the plain `.d` / `.d_preparatory` are the fallback for a record whose country is gone. All four name the operation through `$covert_exposed_op_link$`: bold, hoverable, with `covert_exposed_op_tt` as its tooltip — the operation's name over `covert_last_exposed_type_desc`, what that type does to its target. The journal entry's last-exposed line (`je_iw_last_exposed_named` / `_unknown`) uses the same link and bolds the country, so the snippet reads the defender through `GetPlayer`, not `ROOT`: that line is built by `ExecuteTooltip`, where the existing text reached the defender only through `GetPlayer`. The event's flavor is chosen the same way: `covert_warfare.2.f_election` (the ballot-box vignette) only for code 0, the general `.f` for every other type, `.f_preparatory` for a burn in preparation. `test_covert_op_registry.py` pins the block's codes, the texts' shape and the flavor choice.
- **The defender's side of an exposure aged only in `je_covert_warfare`'s pulse until 2026-09-26.** `iw_last_exposed_age` and `covert_warfare.2`'s cooldown (`iw_defender_event_cooldown` / `_age`) sit on the target of an operation, which need not run a service of its own, so such a country saw `covert_warfare.2` once per game and kept an exposure "recent" for ever (`surveillance_events.5` worked around it with a once-only flag, now removed). Both age in every country's monthly pulse now (`covert_warfare_monthly_country`, `common/on_actions/covert_warfare_on_actions.txt`), the single site. The same event's option a, **Shore up our counterintelligence**, added `intelligence_capacity_defense` at country scope, where `legacy_je_modifier_cleanup_effect` strips it within a month; it adds `covert_counterintelligence_alert` instead: the same separatism and coup resistance, plus 2 intelligence capacity (owner decision, PR #510), all ×3 and decaying.

## War Support Feeds (1.14 hook)

Vanilla 1.14 computes each country's weekly war support change in `common/script_values/war_support_values.txt`; its last term, `war_support_from_journal_entries`, is the only slot that accepts a per-line `desc` key. The mod injects into it from **`common/script_values/zz_te_war_support_injections.txt`** (`INJECT:war_support_from_journal_entries`; the `zz_` prefix was a hedge: directives apply after every bare definition, so an INJECT needn't sort after its target, `scripting_best_practices.md` § Load Order (probed 2026-10-26), fact 4). `root` = country, `scope:war` = the war being evaluated; no randomness; it runs per country per war per beat, so conditions are `has_modifier` / pact / war-participant checks only. Labels live in `te_miscellaneous_l_english.yml` (`WAR_SUPPORT_TE_*`).

| System | Condition (root = country) | Per beat |
|---|---|---|
| World War | `je:je_world_war ?= { has_modifier = ww_home_front_strain_modifier }` (2+ years) — the phase modifiers sit on the **journal entry**, not the country | −0.5 |
| World War | same for `ww_prolonged_war_exhaustion_modifier` (4+ years; stacks with the line above) | −0.5 |
| United Nations | `un_condemned_modifier` on root (`else_if` `un_non_binding_rebuke_modifier`, −0.25) | −0.5 |
| United Nations | an enemy in `scope:war` carries `un_condemned_modifier` ("the world is with us") | +0.25 |
| Covert Warfare | root is `second_country` of a `covert_comms_disruption_action` pact whose attacker fights in `scope:war` (flat — operation phase lives on the attacker's containers) | −0.25 |
| Wars of independence | root holds `var:decol_iw_metropole` (a territory's rebels, a colonial subject or secessionists fighting the metropole) and the metropole fights in `scope:war`: "Fighting for independence"; while a great power arms them (`decol_iw_foreign_arms_modifier`), "Foreign arms" +0.25 | +0.5 |
| Wars of independence | an enemy in `scope:war` names root as its metropole: "A war to keep a colony"; "The world condemns it" −0.25 when the condemners hold a third of great-power prestige, −0.5 at two thirds (`decol_iw_condemner_share`, stored by the monthly settle); "Settlers to defend" +0.25 when that enemy carries `decol_iw_settlers` (our people were a tenth of the territory) | −0.25 |
| Nuclear | root lacks `nuclear_power`, an enemy in `scope:war` has it, and root has no armed guarantor (`nd_has_armed_guarantor_against`: an in-force `nuclear_guarantee` from a country believed armed, or an overlord's nuclear umbrella, removes the "Enemy nuclear arsenal" line — that is what extended deterrence is for). Strikes themselves already drain through devastation and the one-off in `nuclear_industrial_strike` | −0.25 |

Scale: vanilla's per-beat factors run from −5 (fully occupied) to about +2; the rival boost / taking loans are ±0.25. War support is 0–100, drifts toward 50, red band ≤ 25.

**Battle war-support modifiers** (`country_war_support_battles_increase_mult` / `_decrease_mult`, vanilla 1.14; every grant sums into `1 + Σ`, floored at 0, no upper clamp). Mod grants — laws in `common/laws/extra_laws.txt`, techs in `common/technology/technologies/era_7.txt` / `era_9.txt`:

| Entity | increase | decrease |
|---|---|---|
| `law_ministry_of_propaganda` (spin machine; always stacks on `law_outlawed_dissent`) | +0.15 | −0.15 |
| `law_state_controlled_internet` (mirrors `law_censorship`) | −0.10 | −0.20 |
| `law_unregulated_internet` / `law_net_neutrality` | +0.20 / +0.15 | same |
| `law_state_secrets` / `law_freedom_of_information` / `law_open_government` | −0.05 / +0.05 / +0.10 | same |
| `law_total_war` / `law_limited_war` (how much of society is invested) | +0.25 / −0.20 | same |
| `television_broadcasting` / `satellite_communications` / `social_media` (the living-room war) | +0.10 / +0.05 / +0.15 | +0.15 / +0.10 / +0.20 |

The worst-case mod-added negative `decrease` sum is −0.60 (`/modifier-grants/country_war_support_battles_decrease_mult?scope=mod`), so with vanilla `law_outlawed_dissent` (−0.4) it just reaches the floor (Limited War, State-Controlled Internet, State Secrets and the Ministry of Propaganda under Outlawed Dissent); vanilla's `war_propaganda` + `mass_propaganda` techs (−0.2 each) can then floor it, which is intentional — a fully censored state never hears about its defeats. `decrease_mult` is `color=bad`, so a beneficial negative renders red (vanilla's propaganda techs share the quirk). The casualties axis (`country_war_support_casualties_mult`) is deliberately untouched: the mod already saturates it (`law_total_war` −0.50 alone is twice vanilla's largest law value; it was −0.75 before the 2026-10-09 Rules of War redesign).

**Battlefield "losing" reads** — `is_losing_war_against = { ENEMY = scope:x }` in `common/scripted_triggers/nuke_triggers.txt`: most size-weighted battles in the shared war lost (`size_weighted_won_battles_fraction < 0.35` after `num_significant_battles >= 5`) or `enemy_occupation >= 0.25`. Used by the nuke AI `will_propose` (strategic and tactical; the previous war-support proxy also fired for merely unpopular wars) and as the +5 desperation term in the wartime covert ops. The nuke `propose_score` is ×1.5 in a war where `is_at_war_with_rival = ROOT`. `enemy_side_occupation` is the share of the *enemy* we hold (high = winning) and is not a losing read.

**World War stalemate event** `world_war_events.31` (weight 5 in the `je_world_war` monthly pulse): `ww_years_elapsed >= 2` (world-war-wide counter) **and** a war with `war_duration_months >= 24`, `num_significant_battles >= 10`, `has_stalled_wargoal_held_by = ROOT`. Options use one-off `add_war_war_support` (+5 hold the line / −10 armistice talks); `add_war_support_change` is avoided because it accumulates for the war (see `docs/guides/scripting_best_practices.md`).

**Not moved into the hook:** `war_propaganda_on_action` (`extra_on_actions.txt`, monthly per-state `add_war_war_support` driven by the state-scoped `state_war_support_monthly_add`, which does not cascade to a country-scope read) stays a one-off level change; a phase-scaled covert line would need a country variable written by the covert JE pulse.

## Wartime Munitions Demand

**Peacetime armies train with half of vanilla's ammunition. A mobilized battalion burns four times that, which is twice vanilla's peacetime figure.** Ammunition is the good a war uses up rather than wears out, so its demand should swing hard between peace and war. That swing is what makes a munitions industry, imports and the Strategic Reserve matter. In vanilla, mobilization raised ammunition only to 1.5× peacetime, or 2× with extra and luxurious supplies.

- **Peacetime side:** a unit's `upkeep_modifier` is what its barracks buys every week, whether or not it is mobilized. Mod units in `common/combat_unit_types/extra_combat_units.txt` carry half their former ammunition. Vanilla units take an `INJECT` diff of minus half vanilla's value, summed with vanilla's own (squad infantry: 3 − 1.5), so a vanilla patch to any other good flows through untouched. `REPLACE:combat_unit_type_heavy_tank` carries the halved value directly.
- **Wartime side:** `common/mobilization_options/te_wartime_munitions_injections.txt` raises `mobilization_option_basic_supplies`, which no army can switch off, from +50% to +300% ammunition while mobilized. It also cancels the +25% that extra and luxurious supplies each added, so ammunition has a single wartime knob. The per-battalion additions of the mod's own options (Entrenchment +5, Missile Defense +10, Exoskeleton Suits +40) come on top and were not changed.
- **Why ×4:** with `BUY_SELL_DIFF_AT_MAX_FACTOR = 4` and `GOODS_SHORTAGE_PENALTY_THRESHOLD = 0.25`, four times the demand pushes a good whose demand is almost all military to its maximum price, and shortage penalties start only beyond that. A war therefore strains the munitions market without, by itself, starving barracks, whose input shortages cut formation supply and organization.
- **Mobilization is not war.** The spike starts when an army mobilizes, including in a diplomatic play that never becomes a war, and it tapers over the 90-day demobilization.
- **The Strategic Reserve is the buffer.** Its hub is nearly free (`construction_cost_very_low`, 100 points), the AI values it at 2000 in peacetime for a major power and 10 000 more above 10 million GDP, and AI reserves run every good on Stabilize Prices, buying below −20% up to full capacity and releasing above +30% down to empty, on an 8-week average. A war's ammunition spike therefore draws AI stockpiles into the market (`docs/systems/strategic_reserve_system.md` §7).
- **Drift guard:** `test_wartime_munitions.py` checks every diff against `vanilla_parsed/`. It fails when a vanilla unit's ammunition changes, when a new vanilla unit starts using ammunition without a diff, or when a supplies option's vanilla value moves.
- **Not yet read in play:** whether an `INJECT` sums on combat unit types and mobilization options (it does for ranks, techs and static modifiers). The tells are a squad-infantry barracks buying 1.5 ammunition per battalion in peace, and basic supplies' tooltip showing +300% Ammunition next to +50% for the other goods. Two more things to read in the same launch: how formation supply consumption, which 1.14 derives from goods costs, responds; and whether the multiplier touches only the mobilized battalions' own upkeep or the whole barracks.

## Legacy narrative event integration

Law-enactment bank runs (`extra_law_events.2` / `.38`) now apply a small
confidence shock (-5 cycle, -1 momentum) when the banking JE exists, including
simplified banking. With banking disabled they remain enactment flavor.
`finreg_banking_stability` retains its company-throughput benefit and also
reduces banking crash probability by 10% of base; deposit guarantees in `.62`
share that protection.

The discretionary bailout (`banking_cycle_events.45`) requires a non-defaulting
donor at cycle 40+ and a non-hostile, diplomatically relevant trading partner
with a smaller GDP than the donor's, in downturn/panic with an active banking JE.
One of the two markets must rely on the other for at least 5% of its trade
(`market_trade_reliance`, `banking_bailout_min_trade_reliance` — the banking
contagion's first tier). The partner is asked first: the
donor's banking pulse picks it with the same gate and sends it
`banking_cycle_events.68` ("appeal to [donor]?", −5% prestige for asking), and
only its appeal option sends `.45` to the donor; whatever the donor answers
reaches the partner as `.69`, naming the sum. Rescue options transfer equal treasury amounts (the donor's
old weekly expense multiplied by duration / 14, approximating its former
linearly decaying total), capped by the recipient's GDP — the rescue package at
0.2× (vanilla's gold reserve limit), the smaller grant at 1/8 of that — and grant
temporary banking stability to the recipient.
This is a grant, not a new swap-line or lender-of-last-resort treaty. The latter
continues to use its own default-driven event. Protected recipients cannot draw
another discretionary bailout while the stability modifier lasts.

`international_relations_events.6` and `.7` are disabled-system fallbacks only.
Enabled covert warfare owns detection and exposure; enabled space race owns
milestone celebrations. The first-colony charter story (`society_technology_events.18`)
is dispatched seven days after a country's first tracked colony, after its
location-specialization event. Governance (`.19`) requires a tracked colony and
the charter story to have fired. Both retain their building-based flavor gates
when space race is disabled; enabled-system governance no longer needs an
unrelated space-elevator building or era-12 technology (colonization begins in
era 11). The monthly first-colony draw backfills existing saves, with a short
pending flag preventing it from racing the delayed establishment event.
